tracks.legalName: Request to Exclude Case from Online Public Index (CourtView), AS 22.35.030; Alaska Administrative Rule 40(a)
tracks.publicName: Getting a closed case off the public court index
tracks.mechanism: The Alaska Court System may not publish a court record of a criminal case on a publicly available website if 60 days have elapsed from acquittal or dismissal and a statutory condition is met. Removal is automatic; TF-810 exists only for when the court system made an error, which the form says in terms.
dispositions: the defendant was acquitted of all charges filed in the case

the defendant was acquitted of some charges and the remaining charges were dismissed
all charges were dismissed after a suspended entry of judgment under AS 12.55.078

the additional Administrative Rule 40(a) grounds, including the underage alcohol offenses and a conviction for possessing less than one ounce of marijuana where the person was at least 21 and was not convicted of any other charge in the case

tracks.publicName: Expunge a misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: All seven statutory conditions must be met. Discretionary on the § 15-27-5(b) factors. CR-65 Section II. Reaches a youthful offender adjudication where the underlying charge is a misdemeanor, violation, traffic violation or municipal ordinance violation.
authority: Ala. Code § 15-27-1(b), as amended by Act 2024-407 (SB 153), effective 1 October 2024
recordTypes: conviction for a misdemeanor offense, violation, traffic violation, or municipal ordinance violation
youthful offender adjudication where the underlying charge is one of those
exclusions: A violent offense as provided in § 12-25-32.
A sex offense as provided in § 15-20A-5.

An offense involving moral turpitude as provided in § 17-3-30.1, unless the crime was classified as a felony at conviction but has been reclassified as a misdemeanor under Act 2015-185 and the person has not been arrested for any offense, excluding minor traffic violations, in the 15 years before filing.
A serious traffic offense as provided in Article 9 of Chapter 5A of Title 32, which is where DUI sits.

If the conviction is for an offense enumerated in 49 C.F.R. § 383.51, the person must not have been operating a commercial motor vehicle and must not have held a CDL or CLP at the time of the offense.
Case-count limitation: two, shared with the diversion route.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge Marijuana Records, limited jurisdiction court, A.R.S. § 36-2862
tracks.publicName: Marijuana Record Expungement
tracks.mechanism: The only true expungement in Arizona. Effectively mandatory: under § 36-2862(B)(3) and Rule 36(d)(3) the court must grant unless the prosecuting agency proves by clear and convincing evidence that the offense is not eligible, or the court finds the identified offense is not eligible.
dispositions: all dispositions, including acquittal and dismissal. Sentence completion is not required.
exclusions: Any marijuana offense outside the three statutory descriptions, including sale.
Any conduct occurring on or after July 12, 2021.
One petition per case number. Multiple eligible offenses under more than one case number require separate petitions.
tracks.venue: Statewide Arizona law; file in the municipal or justice court that concluded the case.

packetInstructions: Automatic record relief is not a dismissal, sealing or expungement. The record stays on the state summary criminal history and a notation is added, which controls whether the record is disseminated to employers and agencies conducting fingerprint background checks under PC 11105(k) through (p).
The absence of a notation does not mean ineligibility. The DOJ evaluates millions of records monthly back to 1973 and says no additional action is needed to receive relief.

Commercial background check companies do not access DOJ records at all and may hold stale data. Law enforcement, the Commission on Teacher Credentialing, school districts and their contractors continue to see conviction history.
scopeRestrictions: Route participants to CA-1 through CA-6 where a petition adds something the notation does not, most obviously a 17(b) reduction. The DOJ says a petition is still the route for resentencing, dismissal, sealing or reduction of charges.

tracks.legalName: Erasure After a Nolle, and Motion to Nolle a Continued Charge, C.G.S. § 54-142a(c)
tracks.publicName: Records erased after a case was nolled
tracks.mechanism: Where a charge has been nolled, records shall be erased once thirteen months have elapsed since the nolle. Separately, where a charge was continued at the prosecutor's request and thirteen months have passed with no prosecution or other disposition, the charge shall be nolled on motion of the arrested person, and erasure then follows the nolle rules. The second is an affirmative motion the participant can make; it is the one part of this track that is not passive.

tracks.legalName: Clean Slate Automatic Erasure, C.G.S. § 54-142a(e)(1)(A)(i)(I) and (ii)(I)
tracks.publicName: Clean Slate erasure for offenses from 2000 onward
tracks.mechanism: Erasure by operation of law for offenses occurring on or after 1 January 2000. Seven years for a misdemeanor, unclassified misdemeanor or motor vehicle violation with a maximum of not more than one year, with § 14-227a excepted from that bucket. Ten years for a Class D or E felony, an unclassified felony with a maximum of not more than five years, a motor vehicle violation above one year and not more than five, or any violation of § 14-227a. The clock runs from the date the court entered the person's most recent judgment of conviction for any crime, not the conviction being erased.
authority: C.G.S. § 54-142a(e)(1)(B), classification under the law in effect when the offense was committed
C.G.S. § 54-142a(e)(4), cannabis carve-out from the clock
C.G.S. § 54-142a(i)(1), the multi-count and multi-defendant bar
recordTypes: classified or unclassified misdemeanor, or motor vehicle violation with a maximum term of not more than one year, on the seven-year clock

Class D or E felony, unclassified felony with a maximum term of not more than five years, motor vehicle violation above one year and not more than five years, or any violation of § 14-227a, on the ten-year clock
dispositions: conviction for an offense occurring on or after 1 January 2000
exclusions: Any conviction on or after 1 January 2000 designated a family violence crime under § 46b-38a. § 54-142a(e)(2)(A). The exclusion is limited to convictions on or after that date; it is not a flat categorical bar.
Any nonviolent sexual offense or sexually violent offense as defined in § 54-250. § 54-142a(e)(2)(B).

The enumerated sections at § 54-142a(e)(2)(C): 29-33, 53a-60a, 53a-60b, 53a-60c, 53a-61a, 53a-64bb, 53a-64cc, 53a-72a, 53a-90a, 53a-103a, 53a-181c, 53a-191, 53a-196, 53a-196d, 53a-196f, 53a-211, 53a-212, 53a-216, 53a-217, 53a-217a, 53a-217c, 53a-322, 53a-323, 54-251, 54-252, 54-253, 54-254, and § 53a-189a(a)(1). This must be screened section by section, not by category label: it includes several firearms sections but also assault variants, sexual assault in the fourth degree, voyeurism, burglary and home invasion variants, harassment, cruelty to animals and registration offenses.

A § 14-227a conviction where the person was convicted of another § 14-227a violation within the ten years following. § 54-142a(e)(2)(D). This is the only DUI bar; DUI is otherwise eligible on the ten-year clock.
Records referencing more than one count, or a police record referencing more than one defendant, unless and until all counts and all referenced defendants are entitled to erasure. § 54-142a(i)(1).

waitingPeriods.condition: Classified or unclassified misdemeanor, or motor vehicle violation with a maximum term of not more than one year, excepting § 14-227a
waitingPeriods.duration: Seven years from the date the court entered the person's most recent judgment of conviction for any crime

waitingPeriods.duration: Ten years from the date the court entered the person's most recent judgment of conviction for any crime

packetInstructions: The offense class and the maximum sentence that could have been imposed are determined based on the law in effect at the time the offense was committed, not current law. § 54-142a(e)(1)(B).

If a case has more than one count and any count is not erasable, nothing on that record is erased. The same rule appears at § 54-142a(i)(1), § 54-142u(b) and § 54-142v(b). This is the most common practical defeat in Connecticut.

DUI is not excluded from Clean Slate. § 14-227a is carved out of the seven-year misdemeanor bucket and placed in the ten-year bucket. The only DUI bar is a second § 14-227a conviction within the ten years following.
Firearms offenses are not a category exclusion. § 54-142a(e)(2)(C) is an enumerated list of statute sections and must be screened section by section, not by category label.

Erasure does not terminate the obligation to pay an unremitted fine imposed as part of the sentence, and it does not end sex offender, deadly weapon offender or felony-for-a-sexual-purpose registration obligations, or a standing criminal protective order. Nothing in the erasure provisions requires the DMV to erase criminal history information on a driving record, which matters to any CDL holder.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Erasure of Cannabis Conviction Records, C.G.S. § 54-142v
tracks.publicName: Petition to erase an older or larger cannabis conviction
tracks.mechanism: There is no official form. The Clean Slate portal states plainly that a petition must be filed under § 54-142v or § 54-142d and that no official form exists, and the statute specifies exactly what the petition must contain. Relief is mandatory once the papers are in order.
authority: C.G.S. § 54-142v(a)(1), the three eligible conviction categories
C.G.S. § 54-142v(a)(2), required content: a copy of the arrest record or a supporting affidavit
C.G.S. § 54-142v(a)(3), the court shall direct erasure if the petition is in order
recordTypes: a § 21a-279 conviction for possession of a cannabis-type substance where the amount was four ounces or less, entered on or after 1 October 2015 and before 1 July 2021, or before 1 January 2000
a § 21a-267(a) conviction before 1 July 2021 for use or possession with intent to use drug paraphernalia to store, contain, conceal, ingest, inhale or otherwise introduce cannabis into the body

a § 21a-277(b) conviction before 1 July 2021 for manufacturing, distributing, selling, prescribing, compounding, transporting with intent to sell or dispense, possessing with intent to sell or dispense, offering, giving or administering a cannabis-type substance, where the amount was four ounces or less or six plants grown inside the person's own primary residence for personal use
dispositions: conviction falling within one of the three § 54-142v(a)(1) categories
exclusions: Records referencing more than one count unless every count is entitled to erasure. § 54-142v(b).
The petition does not apply while the criminal case is pending.
Convictions outside the three listed subsections.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Physical Destruction of Records of a Decriminalized Offense, C.G.S. § 54-142d
tracks.publicName: Ask the court to destroy records of an offense that is no longer a crime
tracks.mechanism: Where a person was convicted of an offense that has since been decriminalized, the person may petition the Superior Court and the court shall direct the records to be physically destroyed. The remedy is destruction rather than erasure, and the trigger is decriminalization generally rather than the specific cannabis categories. No official form was located, so the filing vehicle is a custom pleading.
recordTypes: police and court records and records of the state's or prosecuting attorney pertaining to a conviction for an offense that has since been decriminalized
dispositions: conviction for an offense since decriminalized
exclusions: The current scope of "decriminalized" after State v. Menditto is unresolved, so the eligible offense set is not stated here.
State v. Dudley held that § 54-142d did not compel erasure of a violation of probation finding premised on a later-decriminalized offense. Neither case was read in full.

tracks.legalName: Erasure After an Absolute Pardon, C.G.S. § 54-142a(d)
tracks.publicName: Records erased after an absolute pardon
tracks.mechanism: Two branches turning on the pardon date. An absolute pardon received before 1 October 1974 requires a petition to the Superior Court, which shall direct erasure. An absolute pardon received on or after 1 October 1974 results in erasure without a petition: such records shall be erased. The original track must be split because one branch requires a participant petition and the other does not.
recordTypes: records of a conviction for which an absolute pardon has been received
dispositions: conviction followed by an absolute pardon
exclusions: A provisional pardon or a certificate of employability is not an absolute pardon and does not erase anything.

waitingPeriods.condition: After the absolute pardon is received
waitingPeriods.duration: None

units.label: Absolute pardon received before 1 October 1974: participant petition
units.description: The pardon was received before 1 October 1974, so erasure requires a petition to the Superior Court, which shall direct erasure. No official form was located, so the vehicle is a custom pleading or an expressly approved petition format. This branch exists because the automatic branch does not reach a pre-1974 pardon.

units.label: Absolute pardon received on or after 1 October 1974: automatic erasure
units.description: The pardon was received on or after 1 October 1974, so such records shall be erased without a petition. Explain that no filing is needed and how to confirm the erasure happened. No participant filing.

tracks.venue: Superior Court on the pre-1974 petition branch. No venue on the post-1974 automatic branch.

destination.name: Superior Court, and the State Police Bureau of Identification for the state record
destination.detail: The pre-1974 branch is a petition to the Superior Court, which shall direct erasure. The post-1974 branch requires no filing at all.

components.conditionDescription: Only on the pre-1 October 1974 branch, where a petition is required.
Only on the on-or-after 1 October 1974 branch, where erasure happens without a petition.

packetInstructions: Note the October 1, 2027 gate in product copy from day one.

Motion content, § 16-806(c)(1): the motion must state all of the movant's unsealed and unexpunged citations, arrests, charges, and convictions as reasonably known, the grounds for eligibility, and facts in support. If the motion does not comply, the movant has 30 days after notice to amend, or the motion is dismissed without prejudice.

Scope relief, § 16-806(h): the movant need not satisfy the waiting periods for all records and need not seek relief for every eligible record. Packets can be scoped to what the person actually wants cleared.

The prosecutor is not required to respond. Under § 16-806(d) the motion is served on the prosecutor, but the prosecutor need not respond unless the court orders it. Do not tell users to expect an opposition by default.

Repeat-motion limits: under § 16-806(i)(6), after a denial the court entertains a second motion no sooner than one year, and a third and final motion no sooner than one year after that. A temporary provision, § 16-806(i)(7), exempts motions dismissed between March 1, 2025 and July 14, 2025 from the one-year wait.

Completion of the sentence, § 16-801(2), is unconditional discharge from incarceration, commitment, probation, parole, or supervised release, whichever is latest, and nonpayment of fines, restitution, or other monetary assessments does not prevent completion.

tracks.legalName: Mandatory Expungement by Application to the State Bureau of Identification, 11 Del. C. § 4373
tracks.publicName: Mandatory Expungement through the State Bureau of Identification
tracks.mechanism: On an appropriate request the Bureau shall expunge. No court discretion. Tier A under § 4373(a)(1) is not barred by prior or subsequent ineligible convictions provided every other charge in the case is eligible; Tier B under § 4373(a)(2) requires no prior or subsequent convictions that bar eligibility.
authority: 11 Del. C. § 4373(d) and (e), authorizing the SBI to promulgate procedures, forms, regulations, and a fee schedule
dispositions: Tier A: the case was terminated in favor of the accused, as defined in § 4372(b)
Tier A: one or more violations in the same case and three years since conviction
Tier A: marijuana possession under 16 Del. C. § 4764 or paraphernalia under § 4771, or both in the same case
Tier A: underage possession or consumption of alcohol under 4 Del. C. § 904(e) or (f)
Tier B: one or more misdemeanors, or misdemeanors combined with violations, in the same case, five years since conviction
Tier B: drug possession under 16 Del. C. § 4756, five years since conviction
Tier B: the six listed felonies, ten years since conviction or release from incarceration, whichever is later
exclusions: § 4372(f) plus the § 4373(b) list: crimes of domestic violence as defined there, offenses with a child victim, offenses with a vulnerable adult victim, any misdemeanor in subparts A, B, C, or F of subchapter VI of chapter 5, a long enumerated misdemeanor list, and a § 4373(a)(2)c. felony where the victim falls in the first three categories.
No expungement while criminal charges are pending, except that pending charges do not include an alleged violation of 4 Del. C. § 904(e) or (f), 16 Del. C. § 4764(c), or a Title 21 offense.

Five convictions may never be expunged: vehicular assault in the second degree (§ 628A), incest (§ 766), unlawful sexual contact in the third degree (§ 767), coercion (§ 791), and unlawfully dealing with a child (§ 1106).
No expungement while the person is serving incarceration, parole, or probation.

researchSbiProcess.process: The SBI page distinguishes the expungement/pardon enrollment code 27S23V from the personal-use history code 27RVGT; its linked 'Expungement Application' is a one-page service-code/enrollment instruction sheet, not a standalone court petition or an eligibility determination. Initial fee $72. After review, a mandatory-eligible applicant returns signed paperwork within 30 days of receipt with a $75 money order payable to Delaware State Police; otherwise SBI sends discretionary-process information. The second fee is conditional, never presented as unconditional; automatic-relief screening is preserved. The sheet describes online enrollment and a telephone alternative, 1-866-761-8069, requires valid unexpired photo identification and addresses name-change documentation; no unverified mail-in destination is hardcoded; a date in the sheet's URL is not a printed revision.
researchSbiProcess.participantText: For the SBI expungement application process, enroll through the State Police's linked fingerprint service using code 27S23V. The initial application fee is $72. Follow the registration instructions for the appointment or permitted mail-in option and identification. After SBI reviews the application, read its eligibility notice. If SBI says you qualify for mandatory expungement, return the signed paperwork within 30 days after you receive it, together with a $75 money order payable to Delaware State Police. If SBI instead sends discretionary-expungement information, follow that separate court process. Do not use the personal-background-check code 27RVGT as a substitute.

tracks.publicName: Discretionary Expungement in Superior Court
tracks.mechanism: Discretionary expungement on petition where the petitioner shows manifest injustice from the continued existence and possible dissemination of the record, by a preponderance. The State is a party defendant. Filed in Superior Court where any charge or conviction was disposed of outside Family Court.
authority: 11 Del. C. § 4374, most recently amended at 85 Del. Laws, c. 142, § 10
dispositions: one or more misdemeanors not listed in § 4373(b), same case, at least 3 years since conviction or release from incarceration, whichever is later, and no prior or subsequent convictions
one or more misdemeanors listed in § 4373(b), same case, at least 7 years, and no prior or subsequent convictions
a felony, at least 7 years, and no prior or subsequent convictions, subject to the (b) exclusions

one or more violations or non-§ 4373(b) misdemeanors in more than one case, at least 5 years since the most recent conviction or release, and no other prior or subsequent convictions that would not be mandatory-eligible standing alone
exclusions: § 4374(b), on top of § 4372(f): a Title 11 felony listed in § 4201(c); 16 Del. C. § 1136; 31 Del. C. § 3913; and a felony conviction involving physical or sexual assault crimes as defined in 31 Del. C. § 309, the Beau Biden Child Protection Act.

Title 21 bar under § 4374(i): no Title 21 motor vehicle offense, or a county or municipal equivalent, except driving after judgment prohibited (21 Del. C. § 2810), reckless driving (§ 4175), and operation of a motor vehicle causing death (§ 4176A). A DUI under 21 Del. C. § 4177 is not expungeable on this route.
No expungement while criminal charges are pending, except the three carve-outs.
No expungement while the person is serving incarceration, parole, or probation.

tracks.publicName: Expungement After a Pardon
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of any crime other than the six excluded, who has since been unconditionally pardoned by the Governor, may petition. Per the enacting synopsis a § 4375 expungement is not restricted by the eligibility requirements or exclusions in § 4374, and crimes ineligible under § 4372(f) become eligible after an unconditional pardon. This is the only route for a § 4201(c) violent felony and for most of the permanent exclusions.
authority: Procedure under 11 Del. C. § 4374(c) through (h) and (j)
dispositions: a conviction for any crime other than the six excluded, followed by an unconditional pardon by the Governor
exclusions: § 4375(b): manslaughter (§ 632), murder in the second degree (§ 635), murder in the first degree (§ 636), rape in the second degree (§ 772), rape in the first degree (§ 773), and sexual abuse of a child by a person in a position of trust, authority, or supervision in the first degree (§ 778(1), (2), or (3)).

tracks.legalName: Record Restriction of a Non-Conviction Arrest Cycle Arising from an Arrest on or after July 1, 2013
tracks.publicName: Restricting an arrest that did not end in a conviction (2013 or later)
tracks.mechanism: Access to the arrest cycle shall be restricted by the center for the non-conviction dispositions listed in subsection (h). Restriction is mandatory and there is no application: the clerk, the arresting agency or the prosecuting attorney reports the qualifying disposition and the center restricts. Where the restriction has not in fact been entered, the participant's route is a written request to the prosecuting attorney for the county of arrest — the Attorney General, district attorney or solicitor-general under § 35-3-37(a)(5) — who enters the restriction code in the CCH interface or forwards the approved paperwork to GCIC. GCIC then notifies the arresting agency within 30 days and the arresting agency restricts its own records within 30 days under § 35-3-37(k)(1).
exclusions: Dismissal or nolle prosse entered as part of a plea agreement that resulted in conviction on an offence arising from the same transaction (§ 35-3-37(i)).
Dismissal because the prosecuting attorney was barred from introducing material evidence (§ 35-3-37(i)).
Dismissal because the conduct was part of a pattern of criminal activity prosecuted in another jurisdiction (§ 35-3-37(i)).
Dismissal because of diplomatic or consular immunity (§ 35-3-37(i)).
Partial acquittal, where some charges resulted in acquittal and some did not (§ 35-3-37(i)).
An acquittal later shown to have resulted from jury tampering or judicial misconduct (§ 35-3-37(i)).
An acquittal within the ten days the prosecuting attorney has after the verdict to defeat restriction by clear and convincing evidence on either ground in § 35-3-37(h)(2)(E).

waitingPeriods.condition: All charged offences dismissed, nolle prossed, reduced to a local ordinance violation, or acquittal of all charges
waitingPeriods.duration: none

units.label: Automatic restriction on the qualifying disposition
units.description: Subsection (h) says access shall be restricted. There is no application and no form. The participant obtains their own Georgia criminal history, reads it for whether each charge shows a final disposition and whether the cycle is already marked restricted, and if it is, stops here and moves to the clerk-sealing and jail routes. LegalEase supplies the diagnosis, the reading guide for the report, and the confirmation step of pulling the criminal history again.

units.label: Written request to the prosecuting attorney where the restriction was not entered
units.description: Where the criminal history does not show the cycle as restricted, the participant asks the prosecuting attorney for the county of arrest to enter the restriction. LegalEase identifies the correct prosecuting office and generates the participant-signed written request setting out the arrest date, the arresting agency, the charges, the disposition and the statutory ground. Where the county prosecutor's office publishes its own intake form, that local form governs and the generated request is the covering request. LegalEase does not make the prosecutor's decision and does not enter anything in the GCIC CCH interface.

provenance.sourceStatement: **"The person may state the record does not exist" is wrong for restriction.** Nothing in § 35-3-37 gives a person the right to deny a restricted arrest or conviction. ... tracks.mechanism: For arrests before July 1, 2013 the eligibility criteria are those of subsection (h), but the procedure is an application. Section 35-3-37(p) requires that any application to the center be made in writing on a form approved by the center, so the GBI Request to Restrict Arrest Record is mandatory and a custom document may not be substituted for it.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Restrict and Seal Records of a Misdemeanor Conviction under the Georgia Second Chance Act
tracks.publicName: Restricting a misdemeanour conviction (Second Chance Act)
tracks.mechanism: An individual convicted of a misdemeanour, or of a series of misdemeanours arising from a single incident, may petition the court in which the conviction occurred to restrict access to the criminal history record information. The court shall grant the order if the individual has completed the terms of the sentence, has not been convicted of any crime in any jurisdiction excluding nonserious traffic offences for at least four years immediately preceding the filing, has no pending charged offences, and the harm to the individual clearly outweighs the public's interest in the information being publicly available. Section 35-3-37(w) applies the paragraph to sentences imposed before, on or after July 1, 2020.
exclusions: Family violence simple assault, § 16-5-20(d), unless the individual was a youthful offender under 21 at the time of arrest.
Family violence simple battery, § 16-5-23(f), unless the individual was a youthful offender.
Family violence battery, § 16-5-23.1(f), unless the individual was a youthful offender.
Family violence stalking, § 16-5-90.
Violating a family violence order, § 16-5-95.
Child molestation, § 16-6-4.
Enticing a child for indecent purposes, § 16-6-5.
Improper sexual contact by employee or agent, by a foster parent, or by a person in a position of trust, § 16-6-5.1.
Public indecency, § 16-6-8(b).
Keeping a place of prostitution, § 16-6-10.
Pimping, § 16-6-11.
Pandering by compulsion, § 16-6-12.
Sexual battery, § 16-6-22.1.
Obstructing or hindering a person making an emergency telephone call, § 16-10-24.3.
Peeping Toms, § 16-11-61.
Any offence related to minors generally under Part 2 of Article 3 of Chapter 12 of Title 16.
Theft under Chapter 8 of Title 16, except misdemeanour shoplifting or refund fraud under § 16-8-14 or § 16-8-14.1.
Any serious traffic offence under Article 15 of Chapter 6 of Title 40, which is where DUI sits.
A lifetime maximum of two convictions restricted under § 35-3-37(j)(4) has already been reached.
A petition on the same conviction denied less than two years ago, measured from the final order.

a separate and additional requirement: every term of the sentence, including probation, fines and restitution, must be complete

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. tracks.publicName: Sealing the court file
tracks.mechanism: An individual who has a record restricted under § 35-3-37 may petition to have the clerk of court's criminal history record information, including any index, sealed and unavailable to the public. The court shall order sealing if it finds by a preponderance of the evidence that the record has been restricted under the Code section and that the harm otherwise resulting to the privacy of the individual clearly outweighs the public interest in the information being publicly available. Notice by registered mail, certified mail or statutory overnight delivery is sufficient. After the order the clerk has 60 days to restrict every document in its custody, possession or control.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Restrict Access to Criminal History Record Information Following a Pardon
tracks.publicName: Restricting a conviction after a pardon
tracks.mechanism: An individual whose Georgia conviction has been pardoned by the State Board of Pardons and Paroles may petition the court in which the conviction occurred to restrict access to the criminal history record information. The offence must not have been a serious violent felony as defined in § 17-10-6.1 or a sexual offence as defined in § 17-10-6.2, the individual must not have been convicted of any crime in any jurisdiction, excluding nonserious traffic offences, since the pardon was granted, and must have no pending charged offences. The court shall grant the order if the harm otherwise resulting to the individual clearly outweighs the public's interest in the information being publicly available.
exclusions: A serious violent felony as defined in O.C.G.A. § 17-10-6.1.
A sexual offence as defined in O.C.G.A. § 17-10-6.2.
Any conviction of any crime in any jurisdiction, excluding nonserious traffic offences, since the pardon was granted.
Any pending charged offence.
A participant who is still seeking the pardon. The pardon application itself is outside scope; this route begins once a pardon exists.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Restrict Access to Criminal History Record Information for a Felony Charge Resolved Without Conviction
tracks.publicName: Restricting a felony charge where you were convicted only of a separate misdemeanour
tracks.mechanism: Where an individual had a felony charge dismissed or nolle prossed, or was found not guilty of it, but was convicted of a misdemeanour offence that was not a lesser included offence of the felony charge, the individual may petition the court in which he or she was accused or convicted — or, if the charge was dismissed, the superior court in the county where the arrest occurred — to restrict access to criminal history record information for the felony charge, within four years of the arrest. The relief restricts the felony charge only. The court shall grant if it determines the misdemeanour conviction was not a lesser included offence of the felony charge and the harm clearly outweighs the public interest.
exclusions: A misdemeanour of conviction that was a lesser included offence of the felony charge.
A petition filed more than four years after the arrest. This is a limitations period, not a waiting period.
The misdemeanour conviction itself, which this route does not reach — only the felony charge is restricted.

waitingPeriods.duration: the petition must be filed within four years of the arrest. This is a hard deadline running from arrest, not a waiting period, and it is the opposite of every other Georgia route. An eligibility engine that treats it as a waiting period will silently produce false positives.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.
The certificate of service must name both the arresting law enforcement agency and the prosecuting attorney. This notice set is broader than the other § 35-3-37(j) routes.
The packet must say that the relief restricts the felony charge only and does not reach the misdemeanour conviction.
participantQuestions: Ask which court handled the case and carry the court level as data. The engine must not default to Superior Court: a state-law offence may have been tried in a State, Superior, Magistrate, Probate or Municipal court.

scopeRestrictions: LegalEase prompts for and formats the participant's own account of what has changed and how the record has been a barrier. provenance.sourceStatement: **"The person may state the record does not exist" is wrong for restriction.** Nothing in § 35-3-37 gives a person the right to deny a restricted arrest or conviction. ... Worse, § 35-3-37(u) says expressly that a restriction or sealing may be used to disqualify a person from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. This is a consumer-harm-grade error and must be removed from all Georgia copy and from Wilma.

provenance.sourceHeading: READ THIS FIRST: CORRECTIONS TO THE INTERNAL GEORGIA REFERENCE / 9
provenance.sourceStatement: **The internal petition replica has the wrong caption and the wrong court.** It uses "IN THE SUPERIOR COURT OF ___ COUNTY / IN RE: [name] / Civil Action No." An SB 288 petition is filed in the court in which the conviction occurred, which is frequently a State Court, and it is filed in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled *State of Georgia v. Defendant*. The court retains jurisdiction over that case for this limited purpose. Filing it as a new civil action in Superior Court is likely to be rejected or misrouted.

tracks.mechanism: Where an individual's charged offence has remained on the dead docket for more than 12 months, the individual may petition the court in which the charged offence is pending to restrict access to criminal history record information for that charged offence. tracks.legalName: Petition to Restrict Access to Criminal History Record Information for a Vacated or Reversed Conviction Not Retried
tracks.publicName: Restricting a conviction that was thrown out and never retried
tracks.mechanism: Where an individual was convicted of an offence and sentenced to a punishment other than the death penalty, the conviction was vacated by the trial court or reversed by an appellate or other post-conviction court, that decision became final by the completion of the appellate process, and the prosecuting attorney has not retried the case within two years of the date the vacating or reversing order became final, the individual may petition the court in which he or she was convicted to restrict access to criminal history record information for the offence. The court weighs why the judgment was reversed or vacated, why the prosecuting attorney has not retried it, and the public interest.
exclusions: A conviction carrying a sentence of death.
A case the prosecuting attorney has retried within two years of the vacating or reversing order becoming final.
A vacating or reversing decision that has not yet become final by completion of the appellate process.

waitingPeriods.condition: Finality of the vacating or reversing order

tracks.mechanism: An individual who has had criminal history record information restricted pursuant to § 35-3-37 may submit a written request to the appropriate county or municipal jail or detention center to have all records for the restricted offence maintained by that jail or detention center restricted. tracks.publicName: First Offender records restricted and sealed when you are sentenced
tracks.mechanism: As amended by Act 403 and effective July 1, 2026, § 42-8-62.1(b)(1) provides that at the time of sentencing the court shall limit public access to the defendant's first offender sentencing information by ordering that dissemination of the first offender records be restricted; that the criminal file, docket books, criminal minutes, final record, all other records of the court and the defendant's criminal history record information in the custody of the clerk, including within any index, be sealed and unavailable to the public; and that law enforcement agencies, jails or detention centers restrict the criminal history record information of arrest including any fingerprints or photographs. The former discretionary language and the former written-findings requirement in (b)(2) were struck; (b)(2) is now Reserved. The clerk seals within 60 days under (e)(1) and the agencies comply within 30 days under (f). Under (g), restriction and sealing are removed if the court revokes the First Offender Act sentence and adjudicates the defendant guilty.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Restrict and Seal First Offender Records for a Sentence Imposed Before July 1, 2026 That Has Not Been Revoked
tracks.publicName: Restricting and sealing an active First Offender case
tracks.mechanism: As amended by Act 403, § 42-8-62.1(c) provides that an individual who was sentenced pursuant to Article 3 of Chapter 8 of Title 42 prior to July 1, 2026 and has not had their sentence revoked and adjudicated guilty may petition the court that ordered such sentence to limit public access to his or her case information pursuant to subsection (b). Notice of the petition shall be sent to the clerk of court and the prosecuting attorney, and notice sent by registered or certified mail or statutory overnight delivery is sufficient. Under (d), within 90 days of the filing the court shall order restriction and sealing. Act 403 struck the former requirement that the court find by a preponderance of the evidence that a discharge had been granted and that privacy harm outweighed the public interest, so relief on a properly filed petition is now mandatory and no balancing showing is required.
exclusions: A First Offender sentence imposed on or after July 1, 2026, which the court restricts and seals at sentencing instead.
A case where the First Offender sentence was revoked and an adjudication of guilt entered.
A participant who was never sentenced under the First Offender Act, who is on the separate retroactive first offender route under § 42-8-66.
A participant who was exonerated and discharged before July 1, 2026, who is routed to the § 42-8-62.2(c) petition under the adopted crosswalk.

packetInstructions: The prosecuting attorney receives notice of the petition. Notice is not a request for consent, there is no advance-consent gate on this route, and the packet must not describe one.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.

The packet must say that the court shall order restriction and sealing within 90 days of filing, that the clerk then seals every document in its custody within 60 days, and that law enforcement agencies, jails and detention centers must restrict within 30 days of receiving a copy of the order.

scopeRestrictions: No objection-triggered statutory hearing branch is modelled, because current law does not create one. A prosecutor objection may trigger the general LegalEase handoff policy, but it does not create a different statutory relief track or an opposition branch.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Restrict and Seal First Offender Records Where the Participant Was Exonerated and Discharged Before July 1, 2026
tracks.publicName: Restricting and sealing a completed First Offender case
tracks.mechanism: Section 42-8-62.2, enacted by Act 403 and effective July 1, 2026, provides at (b) that at the time a defendant sentenced under the article has been exonerated and discharged without court adjudication of guilt, the court records shall be restricted. Subsection (c) provides that an individual who was exonerated of guilt and discharged, as a matter of law or pursuant to a court order, prior to July 1, 2026 may petition the court that granted such discharge for an order to seal and make unavailable to the public the criminal file, docket books, criminal minutes, final record, all other records of the court and the defendant's criminal history record information in the custody of the clerk of court, including within any index. Notice of the petition shall be sent to the clerk of court and the prosecuting attorney, and notice by registered or certified mail or statutory overnight delivery is sufficient. Under (d) the court shall order sealing within 90 days of the filing, with no findings required. The clerk seals within 60 days under (e), and under (f) the court shall also order law enforcement agencies, jails and detention centers to restrict, with compliance within 30 days.
exclusions: A First Offender sentence imposed on or after July 1, 2026, which the court restricts and seals at sentencing instead.
A case where the First Offender sentence was revoked and an adjudication of guilt entered, so that no exoneration and discharge occurred.
A participant who was never sentenced under the First Offender Act, who is on the separate retroactive first offender route under § 42-8-66.
A participant who has not yet been discharged or whose case remains operationally active, who is routed to the § 42-8-62.1(c) petition under the adopted crosswalk.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Retroactive First Offender Treatment, Exoneration and Discharge under O.C.G.A. § 42-8-66
tracks.publicName: Asking for First Offender treatment you should have been given
tracks.mechanism: An individual who qualified for first offender sentencing but was not informed of that eligibility, or who was sentenced between March 18, 1968 and October 31, 1982 to incarceration not exceeding one year and would otherwise have qualified, may petition the court in which they were convicted for retroactive first offender treatment. The petition may be filed only with the consent of the prosecuting attorney, obtained before filing. A hearing is held if requested by the petitioner or the prosecuting attorney or if the court desires one. The court may grant if it finds by a preponderance that the defendant was eligible at the time of the original sentencing, or qualifies under the 1968 to 1982 provision, and that the ends of justice and the welfare of society are served. There is no filing fee. On a grant the conviction becomes a first offender discharge, which is not a conviction, and the court sends the order to the petitioner, the prosecuting attorney, the Georgia Crime Information Center and the Department of Driver Services, both of which must modify their records.
exclusions: A participant who was in fact sentenced under the First Offender Act, who is on the § 42-8-62.1 or § 42-8-62.2 routes instead.
A sentence entered before March 18, 1968, since § 42-8-66(g) applies the Code section to any sentence entered on or after that date.
A sentence that may be modified under O.C.G.A. § 17-10-1, to which § 42-8-66(f) says this Code section does not apply.
A filing without the prosecuting attorney's advance consent. Prosecutor silence is not consent.

waitingPeriods.condition: Where proceedings on a § 712-1200 charge were actually deferred under Chapter 853 and the person was discharged and the charge dismissed
waitingPeriods.duration: Three years following discharge, under HRS § 712-1200(4)(c). Calculated from the discharge date; the ordinary Chapter 853 one-year period is not added. items: Fill the current legal name, other names, date of birth, addresses and contact details only from the participant's supplied facts; preserve the form's actual field identities.
SSN is optional on the issuer form: never a required application field, never an invented value.

The form asks the person to initial the applicable application statement: use the non-conviction treatment for this route, not the first-time drug/property/DUI conviction statement; draw no fabricated checkbox over an initials field; never execute initials, signature or date for the participant.
Never assert the person is not a fugitive because the route is a deferred disposition; the person reviews and executes the statement.
The current form has no arrest/case table: collect disposition and timing facts upstream; invent no table on the issuer form.

The form's demand for a court order granting expungement of a conviction belongs to its conviction branch and is not applied to this non-conviction application; attaching the discharge-and-dismissal order is a clearly labelled LegalEase safeguard, not an issuer certification requirement.

Fees as the form states them: $35 first-time expungement, $50 non-first-time, including a $10 nonrefundable portion; valid government-issued photo-ID copy, self-addressed stamped envelope, United States-issued money order or cashier's check payable to the State of Hawaii; destination HCJDC, Attn: Expungement, 465 South King Street, Room 102, Honolulu, HI 96813. No invented waiver process, no guarantee about every court or private copy.

tracks.publicName: Conviction expungement, first-time drug offender
tracks.mechanism: Two stages, both settled. Stage one is a written motion in the participant's own existing penal case, filed in the court that sentenced or convicted them, seeking a court order expunging the record of conviction; stage two is the HCJDC 159(b) Expungement Application submitted to the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center with a copy of that order attached. The stage-one vehicle is fixed by Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a), which provides that "An application to the court for an order shall be by motion", so Hawaii penal practice does not distinguish an application from a motion however the statute words it; the Rules of Penal Procedure govern because Rule 54(a) applies them to all penal proceedings and none of these provisions supplies its own procedure. Mandatory. 'the court shall issue a court order to expunge'. The proviso states conditions, not a discretion. The court has no listed ground to refuse a qualifying application. No official statewide Hawaii Judiciary expungement form exists for stage one in any circuit, so a controlled custom pleading is permitted and is the only available strategy. Venue follows the offence and is a participant input rather than a track constant. Nothing here makes the Hawaii implementation ready.

tracks.publicName: Conviction expungement, first-time property offender
tracks.mechanism: Two stages, both settled. Stage one is a written motion in the participant's own existing penal case, filed in the court that sentenced or convicted them, seeking a court order expunging the record of conviction; stage two is the HCJDC 159(b) Expungement Application submitted to the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center with a copy of that order attached. The stage-one vehicle is fixed by Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a), which provides that "An application to the court for an order shall be by motion", so Hawaii penal practice does not distinguish an application from a motion however the statute words it; the Rules of Penal Procedure govern because Rule 54(a) applies them to all penal proceedings and none of these provisions supplies its own procedure. {"subsection3":"Mandatory. 'the court shall issue', subject to the proviso.","subsection4":"Mandatory once the findings are made — 'shall issue ... provided that (a) through (d)' — but two of the four are findings the court makes, so the outcome is not mechanical. There is then an express discretionary fallback: where the court cannot make the paragraph (b) finding, it 'may nevertheless' order expungement provided it finds the person successfully completed a substance abuse treatment programme. This is the only discretionary grant in any of the five statutes, and the packet copy must not describe subsection (4) relief as automatic."} No official statewide Hawaii Judiciary expungement form exists for stage one in any circuit, so a controlled custom pleading is permitted and is the only available strategy. Venue follows the offence and is a participant input rather than a track constant. Nothing here makes the Hawaii implementation ready.

tracks.legalName: Conviction Expungement, DUI under 21, HRS § 291E-64(e)
tracks.publicName: Conviction expungement, DUI under 21
tracks.mechanism: Two stages, both settled. Stage one is a written motion in the participant's own existing penal case, filed in the court that sentenced or convicted them, seeking a court order expunging the record of conviction; stage two is the HCJDC 159(b) Expungement Application submitted to the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center with a copy of that order attached. The stage-one vehicle is fixed by Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a), which provides that "An application to the court for an order shall be by motion", so Hawaii penal practice does not distinguish an application from a motion however the statute words it; the Rules of Penal Procedure govern because Rule 54(a) applies them to all penal proceedings and none of these provisions supplies its own procedure. Not established as mandatory. This subsection is drafted differently from the other four: it says the person 'may apply to the court for an expungement order' if the conditions are met, and it does not say the court shall grant it. No source read here resolves whether a qualifying application must be granted. Recorded as an open point below. It does not block the build — the vehicle, the venue and the allegations are all settled — but the packet copy must not tell a participant the order is guaranteed. No official statewide Hawaii Judiciary expungement form exists for stage one in any circuit, so a controlled custom pleading is permitted and is the only available strategy. Venue follows the offence and is a participant input rather than a track constant. Nothing here makes the Hawaii implementation ready.

exclusions: Persons in possession of a commercial learner's permit or a commercial driver's license.
A conviction sustained while operating a commercial motor vehicle.

tracks.mechanism: Where an acquittal was entered for all criminal charges, or all criminal charges were otherwise dismissed, the court shall enter an order expunging the district court record. Expunge means the record becomes a confidential record exempt from public access under § 22.7; nothing is destroyed.
exclusions: Dismissals related to a deferred judgment under § 907.9, which route to the deferred-judgment track.
Cases dismissed because the defendant was found not guilty by reason of insanity.
Cases in which the defendant was found incompetent to stand trial.
Matters that are not public offenses as defined in § 692.1.
Appellate records, other than appeals of simple misdemeanors to district court, under Rule 2.84(5).
Partial dispositions. All charges in the separately numbered case must be acquitted or dismissed.

tracks.legalName: Application to Expunge Misdemeanor Court Records under Iowa Code section 901C.3
tracks.publicName: Expunging one misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: One misdemeanor conviction may be expunged per lifetime, more than eight years after the date of conviction, where financial obligations are paid, no criminal charges are pending, and the defendant has not previously been granted two deferred judgments. The court shall enter the order as a matter of law on proof; the burden is expressly on the defendant.
exclusions: Section 901C.3(2) excludes twenty-four categories, which must be built from the statute rather than from the form's note: (a) § 123.46; (b) a simple misdemeanor under § 123.47(3) or a similar local ordinance; (c) §§ 321.218, 321A.32, 321J.21; (d) § 321J.2; (e) a sex offense as defined in § 692A.101; (f) involuntary manslaughter under § 707.5; (g) assault under § 708.2(3); (h) § 708.2A; (i) harassment under § 708.7; (j) stalking under § 708.11; (k) removal of an officer's communication or control device under § 708.12; (l) trespass under § 716.8(3) or (4); (m) chapter 717C; (n) chapter 719; (o) chapter 720; (p) § 721.2; (q) § 721.10; (r) § 723.1; (s) chapter 724; (t) chapter 726; (u) chapter 728; (v) chapter 901A; (w) a comparable offense listed in 49 C.F.R. § 383.51(b) table 1 or § 383.51(e) table 4; (x) a conviction under prior law of an offense comparable to an offense enumerated in this subsection.
Paragraphs (w) and (x) are absent from the official form's note and from both internal references.
Section 235B.20 appears on the official form's note but is not in the Iowa Code 2026 text; screen it out and refer until resolved.
One expungement under this section per lifetime.
Any pending charge of a public offense as defined in § 692.1.
Two previously granted deferred judgments, counted per Rule 2.83(5).

tracks.legalName: Expungement of a Deferred Judgment Record on Discharge from Probation
tracks.publicName: Clearing a deferred judgment after probation
tracks.mechanism: On discharge from probation where judgment was deferred under § 907.3, the court's criminal record with reference to the deferred judgment shall be expunged, together with dismissed counts in the same charging instrument and other related dismissed charges arising from the same transaction or occurrence or a common scheme or plan. The record is not expunged until financial obligations in that case are paid. The deferred judgment itself remains on the state court administrator's deferred judgment docket and is not expunged. This mechanism sits outside Rules 2.80 through 2.86 and has no Rule 2.86 form.
exclusions: A revoked deferred judgment. Revocation makes the case ineligible under chapter 907; the resulting conviction may then be eligible under § 901C.3 if it is a misdemeanour.
Cases where financial obligations in the case containing the deferred judgment remain unpaid.

waitingPeriods.condition: Discharge from probation, with all financial obligations in that case paid
waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond discharge and payment

units.label: Verify that the automatic expungement happened, and diagnose it if it did not
units.description: For a discharge after July 1, 2013 there is no participant filing: the expungement is expected to occur without an application. The product is diagnostic. Confirm the disposition was a deferred judgment rather than a conviction or a dismissal, confirm discharge and its date, confirm every financial obligation in that case is paid, check whether the case still appears on the public online docket, and if it does, contact the clerk of the district court for that county. The usual blocker is an unpaid balance in that case, which is actionable.

units.description: For a discharge before July 1, 2013 an application is required, but no statewide form exists, no rule governs it, and the statutory mechanics are thin. The filing vehicle is legally unresolved, so no packet is generated and no strategy is invented.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Shield Records from Public Disclosure, I.C. § 67-3004(11)
tracks.publicName: Shielding a Record from Public Disclosure
tracks.mechanism: Shielding hides a court record from the public but does not destroy it. The court shall order shielding if it finds eligibility, that the petitioner has been held accountable, and that shielding would not compromise public safety or the safety of any victims. Paragraph (l) makes the procedures subject to the rules of the Idaho Supreme Court.
authority: I.C. § 67-3004(11), added by 2023 chapter 108, effective January 1, 2024
Idaho Supreme Court, Petition to Shield Records from Public Disclosure, 01/01/2024
dispositions: arrested for, prosecuted for, or convicted of a misdemeanor that is not on the assaultive or violent list
arrested for, prosecuted for, or convicted of felony possession of a controlled substance under § 37-2732(a), (c), or (e)
exclusions: The thirteen assaultive or violent misdemeanors under § 67-3004(11)(b): assault (§ 18-901); battery (§ 18-903); domestic battery (§ 18-918); stalking in the second degree (§ 18-7906); violation of a protection order or no contact order (§§ 18-7907 and 18-920); telephone harassment (§ 18-6710); vehicular manslaughter (§ 18-4006(3)(c)); excessive driving under the influence (§ 18-8004C); domestic assault (§ 18-918(3)(a)); battery upon law enforcement (§ 18-915(1)(b)); injury to children (§ 18-1501); sexual battery (§ 18-924); and indecent exposure (§ 18-4116).
One petition granted per lifetime, covering one eligible crime, or more than one eligible crime if committed in a single incident or transaction, § 67-3004(11)(k).

waitingPeriods.condition: Completion of the sentence in full, including all ordered probation, parole, fines, and restitution. Unpaid fines or restitution stop the clock from starting.

tracks.legalName: Application for Set-Aside, Dismissal and Discharge, I.C. § 19-2604(1)
tracks.publicName: Set aside your conviction and have the case dismissed
tracks.mechanism: Where sentence was imposed but suspended, or was withheld, on the defendant's application and a satisfactory showing of compliance with probation, or graduation from an authorized drug court or mental health court program, the court may terminate the sentence or set aside the plea or conviction and finally dismiss the case and discharge the defendant. Final dismissal restores civil rights. It does not hide the record and it is not an expungement.
dispositions: graduation from an authorized drug court or mental health court program with compliance during any subsequent probation
exclusions: An offense requiring sex offender registration under § 18-8304 is not subject to dismissal or reduction under this section. "Conviction" here includes a plea or finding of guilt notwithstanding the form of the judgment or a withheld judgment.

tracks.legalName: Request to Expunge Criminal Records of an Arrest or Charge Not Resulting in Conviction
tracks.publicName: Expunging an arrest or charge that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Arrests and charges not initiated by arrest that ended in acquittal, dismissal, release without charging, or a vacated or reversed conviction may be expunged on petition. Expunge means the records are destroyed or returned and the name is obliterated from official indexes; the circuit court file is impounded rather than destroyed.
exclusions: Minor traffic offenses under § 5.2(a)(3)(B), meaning a petty offense, business offense, or Class C misdemeanor under the Illinois Vehicle Code or a similar local ordinance, unless the petitioner was arrested and released without charging.
The (a)(3)(A) and (a)(3)(C) exclusion lists are keyed to supervision or conviction and do not reach this track.

waitingPeriods.duration: none

tracks.venue: Section 5.2(d)(1) requires filing with the clerk of the court where the arrests occurred or the charges were brought, not the county of residence. Where arrests occurred or charges were brought in more than one jurisdiction, a separate petition is filed in each. Cook County filings go to the district matching the case.

tracks.legalName: Request to Expunge Criminal Records After Successful Termination of Court Supervision
tracks.publicName: Expunging a case that ended in court supervision you completed
tracks.mechanism: Court supervision is not a conviction under § 5.2(a)(1)(C), so a successfully terminated order of supervision routes to expungement rather than sealing. The waiting period runs from satisfactory termination of the supervision itself, not from the last sentence.
exclusions: Supervision for a sexual offense committed against a minor, for DUI under Vehicle Code § 11-501, or for reckless driving under § 11-503 outside the under-25 exception, all under § 5.2(a)(3)(A).
Minor traffic offenses under § 5.2(a)(3)(B) unless the petitioner was arrested and released without charging.

Supervision terminated unsatisfactorily is a conviction under § 5.2(a)(1)(C) unless the unsatisfactory termination is reversed, vacated or modified and any judgment of conviction is reversed or vacated.

waitingPeriods.condition: Supervision under Illinois Vehicle Code §§ 3-707, 3-708, 3-710 or 5-401.3, or a similar local ordinance, or under Criminal Code §§ 11-1.50, 12-3.2 or 12-15, or a similar local ordinance
waitingPeriods.duration: 5 years after satisfactory termination

waitingPeriods.condition: Supervision on a misdemeanor violation of Vehicle Code § 11-503(a) or a similar local ordinance that occurred before the petitioner reached 25, where the petitioner has no other conviction under § 11-501 or § 11-503
waitingPeriods.duration: Until the petitioner reaches age 25
2 years after satisfactory termination

tracks.legalName: Request to Expunge Filed in Anticipation of Successful Completion of a Problem-Solving Court or Diversion Program
tracks.publicName: Filing early as a problem-solving court or diversion graduate
tracks.mechanism: Added by the Clean Slate Act effective June 1, 2026. In anticipation of successful completion of a problem-solving court program, a pre-plea diversion program or a post-plea diversion program, a petition for expungement may be filed 61 days before the anticipated dismissal of the case, or any time after. On successful completion and dismissal the court reviews the petition and shall grant expungement if the petitioner meets all requirements of any applicable statute.
exclusions: The filing does not ripen if the program is not completed successfully.
Minor traffic offenses under § 5.2(a)(3)(B) unless arrested and released without charging.

waitingPeriods.condition: Anticipated dismissal on successful program completion
waitingPeriods.duration: None. The filing window opens 61 days before the anticipated dismissal and remains open at any time after.

tracks.legalName: Request to Seal Criminal Records, Two-Year Category
tracks.publicName: Sealing supervision, qualified probation, probation or a misdemeanor conviction after two years
tracks.mechanism: The Clean Slate Act created a two-year sealing bucket effective June 1, 2026, covering successfully completed supervision, qualified probation, conditional discharge or probation completed without revocation, and misdemeanor convictions. The period runs from termination of the petitioner's last sentence in any jurisdiction.
exclusions: Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(i): offenses in Article 11 of the Criminal Code, or a similar local ordinance, except § 11-14 and a misdemeanor violation of § 11-30.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(ii): §§ 11-1.50, 12-3.4, 12-15, 12-30, 26-5 or 48-1, or a similar local ordinance.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(iii): §§ 12-3.1 or 12-3.2, or Stalking No Contact Order Act § 125, or Civil No Contact Order Act § 219, or a similar local ordinance.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(iv): Class A misdemeanors or felony offenses under the Humane Care for Animals Act.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(v): any offense or attempted offense that would subject a person to registration under the Sex Offender Registration Act.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(A): a sexual offense committed against a minor, DUI under Vehicle Code § 11-501, and reckless driving under § 11-503 outside the under-25 exception.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(B): minor traffic offenses unless the petitioner was arrested and released without charging.

tracks.legalName: Request to Seal Criminal Records, Three-Year Category
tracks.publicName: Sealing a felony conviction after three years
tracks.mechanism: Felony convictions not captured by the two-year subparagraph, plus the remaining conviction records, may be sealed three years after termination of the petitioner's last sentence. Convictions requiring public registration under the Arsonist Registry Act, the Sex Offender Registration Act or the Murderer and Violent Offender Against Youth Registration Act may not be sealed until registration ends.
exclusions: Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(i): offenses in Article 11 of the Criminal Code, or a similar local ordinance, except § 11-14 and a misdemeanor violation of § 11-30.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(ii): §§ 11-1.50, 12-3.4, 12-15, 12-30, 26-5 or 48-1, or a similar local ordinance.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(iii): §§ 12-3.1 or 12-3.2, or Stalking No Contact Order Act § 125, or Civil No Contact Order Act § 219, or a similar local ordinance.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(iv): Class A misdemeanors or felony offenses under the Humane Care for Animals Act.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(v): any offense or attempted offense that would subject a person to registration under the Sex Offender Registration Act.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(A): a sexual offense committed against a minor, DUI under Vehicle Code § 11-501, and reckless driving under § 11-503 outside the under-25 exception.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(B): minor traffic offenses unless the petitioner was arrested and released without charging.

Section 5.2(c)(3)(C): convictions requiring public registration under the Arsonist Registry Act, the Sex Offender Registration Act, or the Murderer and Violent Offender Against Youth Registration Act, until the petitioner is no longer required to register.

waitingPeriods.condition: Termination of the petitioner's last sentence, in any jurisdiction
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years

tracks.legalName: Request to Seal Criminal Records Under the Educational-Credential Waiver
tracks.publicName: Sealing sooner because you earned a diploma, GED, degree or certificate while serving your sentence
tracks.mechanism: Records eligible under (c)(2)(C), (D), (E) or (F) may be sealed upon termination of the last sentence with no waiting period where, during the sentence or mandatory supervised release, the petitioner earned a high school diploma, associate's degree, career certificate, vocational technical certification or bachelor's degree, or passed the high-school-level Test of General Educational Development. If a petition under this subparagraph is denied, the ordinary (c)(3)(B) or (c)(3)(C) periods apply to any subsequent petition.
exclusions: Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(i): offenses in Article 11 of the Criminal Code, or a similar local ordinance, except § 11-14 and a misdemeanor violation of § 11-30.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(ii): §§ 11-1.50, 12-3.4, 12-15, 12-30, 26-5 or 48-1, or a similar local ordinance.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(iii): §§ 12-3.1 or 12-3.2, or Stalking No Contact Order Act § 125, or Civil No Contact Order Act § 219, or a similar local ordinance.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(iv): Class A misdemeanors or felony offenses under the Humane Care for Animals Act.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(v): any offense or attempted offense that would subject a person to registration under the Sex Offender Registration Act.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(A): a sexual offense committed against a minor, DUI under Vehicle Code § 11-501, and reckless driving under § 11-503 outside the under-25 exception.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(B): minor traffic offenses unless the petitioner was arrested and released without charging.
The credential must have been earned during the sentence or mandatory supervised release period, not before and not after.
The subparagraph applies only to a petitioner who had not completed the same educational goal before the sentence or MSR period.

waitingPeriods.condition: Qualifying educational credential earned during the sentence or mandatory supervised release
waitingPeriods.duration: None. Sealing is available upon termination of the last sentence.

tracks.legalName: Immediate Sealing at Disposition
tracks.publicName: Asking for immediate sealing on the day your case is dismissed or you are acquitted
tracks.mechanism: Arrests or charges not initiated by arrest resulting in acquittal or dismissal with prejudice on or after January 1, 2018 may be sealed immediately. The petition must be filed with the circuit clerk on the same day and during the same hearing in which the case is disposed, and the presiding trial judge rules during that hearing. Section 5.2(g)(5)(A) frames the filing as made by the defendant's attorney on the defendant's behalf.
exclusions: Records of offenses occurring before January 1, 2018.
Minor traffic offenses under § 5.2(a)(3)(B).
A dismissal without prejudice, which is not within the subsection.

tracks.publicName: Expunging a conviction after a pardon that authorizes expungement
tracks.mechanism: Where the Governor has issued a pardon that specifically authorizes expungement, a verified petition may be filed with the Chief Judge of the circuit of conviction, a judge of that circuit designated by the Chief Judge, or in counties under 3,000,000 inhabitants the presiding trial judge. No objection to the petition may be filed. The effect is hybrid: the arrest record is expunged from the arresting authority's records while the circuit clerk's and ISP's records are sealed until further order.

tracks.legalName: Expungement or Sealing Following a Prisoner Review Board Certificate of Eligibility
tracks.publicName: Using a Prisoner Review Board certificate to clear a record that is otherwise excluded
tracks.mechanism: Two stages before two different bodies. The petitioner first applies to the Prisoner Review Board for a certificate of eligibility for sealing under § 5.2(e-5) or for expungement under § 5.2(e-6); that is discretionary agency relief outside the circuit court. With the certificate attached under § 5.2(d)(2), the petitioner then files in the circuit court under the same venue formula as the pardon route.
exclusions: Stage 2 cannot proceed without the certificate issued at stage 1; the Board's decision is discretionary and outside LegalEase's control.

waitingPeriods.condition: Issuance of a Prisoner Review Board certificate of eligibility
waitingPeriods.duration: None stated for the court stage. The Board controls its own timing.

units.label: Prisoner Review Board certificate application stage
units.description: The participant applies to the Board for a certificate. Which certificate depends on the branch below. Board discretion, the rehabilitation narrative, notarisation, supporting documents and a possible Board hearing are filing instructions and post-generation conditions, not reasons to withhold a packet.

units.label: Certificate of Sealing application, § 5.2(e-5)
units.description: Generate the Board's Certificate of Sealing Acknowledgement and Certificate of Sealing Application from the participant's answers. Both are fillable AcroForms published by the Board, revised 09/18/2024. The acknowledgement must be completed first and included with the petition or the petition is rejected and returned. Rehabilitation, personal-history and reasons narratives are participant-authored through structured prompts, and the perjury declaration is sworn before a notary.

units.label: Certificate of Expungement for Military application
units.description: Generate the Board's Certificate of Expungement for Military Eligibility Acknowledgement and application, v9.18.24. This branch is military-specific and is offered only where the participant's eligibility rests on military service. It is not a general certificate-of-expungement application.

units.label: Non-military certificate of eligibility for expungement, § 5.2(e-6)
units.description: Section 5.2(e-6) refers to a certificate of eligibility for expungement. The Board publishes a Certificate of Sealing and a military-specific Certificate of Expungement; no general non-military expungement-certificate application was located on the Board's site. The filing vehicle for this branch is unverified, so no packet is generated and no form mapping is asserted.
units.unavailableReason: No official non-military certificate-of-eligibility-for-expungement application has been located on the Prisoner Review Board site. The Certificate of Sealing application does not cover it and the military application is expressly military-specific.

tracks.legalName: Clean Slate Automatic Sealing
tracks.publicName: Automatic sealing starting in 2029, and why you may still want to file now
tracks.mechanism: Added by the Clean Slate Act, subsection effective June 1, 2026 and operative January 1, 2029. From that date, records created on or after January 1, 1970 meeting the (k)(3) eligibility and (k)(4) or (k)(5) timing criteria are sealed without a petition, with pre-2029 records phased in through January 1, 2034. Section 5.2(k)(1) subjects both the ISP and circuit clerk duties to appropriations, so even the 2029 date is conditional.
exclusions: Section 5.2(k)(3) is broader than the petition exclusions: ineligible while serving a sentence, supervision or qualified probation, or with pending filed charges.
Convictions under Article 9 or Article 11 of the Criminal Code, Class X felonies, and SORA-registration felonies, except that § 11-14 offenses are eligible.
A crime of violence as defined in Drug Court Treatment Act § 20.
Trafficking in persons, involuntary servitude, involuntary sexual servitude of a minor, organized retail crime, robbery, vehicular hijacking, Class 1 or 2 burglary, and residential burglary.
Arsonist Registration Act and Murderer and Violent Offender Against Youth Registration Act convictions until registration ends.
Any record sharing a case number with an excluded conviction.
Felony records generally, until all of the person's automatic-sealing-eligible felony records meet the timing test.

tracks.publicName: Checking whether your old cannabis arrest was already cleared automatically

Records associated with an arrest, conviction or other disposition for a violent crime as defined in Rights of Crime Victims and Witnesses Act § 3(c).
Offences committed on or after June 25, 2019.

waitingPeriods.duration: One year or more since the arrest or law enforcement interaction. All statutory expungement deadlines have now passed.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Vacate and Expunge a Cannabis Conviction
tracks.publicName: Vacating and expunging a cannabis conviction
tracks.mechanism: Any individual may move to vacate and expunge a conviction for a misdemeanor or Class 4 felony violation of Cannabis Control Act § 4 or § 5. This is broader than the minor-cannabis-offense definition and is not limited to 30 grams. The motion may be filed after completion of any non-financial sentence or non-financial condition; unpaid financial obligations do not block it. The State's Attorney may object within 60 days and the standard is discretionary.
exclusions: Convictions under drug statutes other than Cannabis Control Act § 4 or § 5.

waitingPeriods.condition: Completion of any non-financial sentence or non-financial condition imposed by the conviction

rules.filing: File the verified petition, order, appearance where self-represented, Notice of Exclusion and Confidential Information Form with a circuit or superior court in the county where the charges were filed, or where the arrest occurred if none were filed.
rules.fees: None. Section 1 petitions carry no filing fee.
rules.feeWaiver: Not applicable. There is no fee.
rules.notice: The court serves a copy of the petition on the prosecuting attorney under § 35-38-9-1(f). The court shall grant unless the subsection (a) conditions are unmet or criminal charges are pending, and may summarily deny a petition that shows on its face that the person is not entitled to relief.
rules.service: The court serves the prosecuting attorney. The CCA appearance form nonetheless carries a certificate of service to the county prosecutor; follow the form.
rules.participantSignature: The petition is verified and signed by the petitioner.

Put only the last four digits of the Social Security number on the petition. The full number goes on the Confidential Information Form, filed as a confidential document, accompanied by the Notice of Exclusion of Confidential Information from Public Access. Do not persist the full number.
