On granting a conviction expungement the court shall also order the related arrest records expunged under §§ 35-38-9-6(g) and 35-38-9-7(e). Tell the participant they do not file separately for those.
scopeRestrictions: One petition per lifetime under § 35-38-9-9(i). Petitions filed in separate counties count as one only if they land inside a single 365-day window. Build the eligibility calendar and the 365-day window optimiser before the petition generator; in Indiana the scheduling decision is worth more than the document.

Put a hard gate in front of any conviction filing: where the participant has any conviction not yet eligible, surface Chastain v. State and the consequence of filing early before letting them proceed. Under Chastain a petitioner cannot use the liberal amendment rule to add records that were not yet eligible when the initial petition was filed, so filing now can permanently cost a record that ripens later. This is a delivery gate, not a generation blocker.

packetInstructions: Never say records are destroyed. In Indiana expungement means records are sealed or restricted under § 35-38-9-1(k). The Office of Judicial Administration states plainly that court records are not deleted or destroyed under I.C. 35-38-9.

Put only the last four digits of the Social Security number on the petition. The full number goes on the Confidential Information Form, filed as a confidential document, accompanied by the Notice of Exclusion of Confidential Information from Public Access. Do not persist the full number.
Disclose that the expungement case file is public until the order is granted.

Explain the Section 7 effect honestly: court and public records stay public but must be clearly and visibly marked expunged, and the listed agencies add an entry noting the expunged status. This is weaker than Section 6 sealing.
scopeRestrictions: One petition per lifetime under § 35-38-9-9(i). Petitions filed in separate counties count as one only if they land inside a single 365-day window. Build the eligibility calendar and the 365-day window optimiser before the petition generator; in Indiana the scheduling decision is worth more than the document.

Put a hard gate in front of any conviction filing: where the participant has any conviction not yet eligible, surface Chastain v. State and the consequence of filing early before letting them proceed. Under Chastain a petitioner cannot use the liberal amendment rule to add records that were not yet eligible when the initial petition was filed, so filing now can permanently cost a record that ripens later. This is a delivery gate, not a generation blocker.
The grant is discretionary. Route to a legal-review gate before offering this track, per the build order in the review.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge a Serious Felony Conviction, I.C. 35-38-9-5
tracks.publicName: Clearing a serious felony conviction with the prosecutor's written consent
tracks.mechanism: A felony resulting in serious bodily injury, elected-official offences and other serious felonies may be expunged at the later of ten years from conviction or five years from completion of the sentence, shortened by written consent. The prosecuting attorney's written consent is required to file at all. The grant is discretionary. Effect is Section 7. Section 5 was amended by P.L.77-2025.
exclusions: Sex or violent offenders as defined in I.C. 11-8-8-5.
Persons convicted of a felony that resulted in the death of another person.
Persons convicted of official misconduct under I.C. 35-44.1-1-1, unless the person is not an elected official or an elected or appointed judicial officer.
Persons convicted of any homicide offence or attempt under I.C. 35-42-1.
Persons convicted of any human or sexual trafficking offence or attempt under I.C. 35-42-3.5.
Persons convicted of any sex crimes offence or attempt under I.C. 35-42-4.
Persons convicted of unlawful possession of a firearm by a serious violent felon.
Persons convicted of two or more felony offences involving the unlawful use of a deadly weapon not committed as part of the same episode of criminal conduct, as defined in I.C. 35-31.5-2-46.5.
Filing without the prosecuting attorney's written consent.

waitingPeriods.condition: The later of the date of conviction or completion of the sentence
waitingPeriods.duration: 10 years from conviction or 5 years from completion of the sentence, whichever is later, shortened by the prosecuting attorney's written consent

tracks.legalName: Request to Expunge a Collateral Action, I.C. 35-38-9-9.5
tracks.publicName: Clearing a related case, forfeiture or driving-privileges matter after your expungement
tracks.mechanism: After an original expungement order is issued, a person may request expungement of an action or proceeding, including an administrative proceeding, factually or legally related to the arrest, charge, allegation, conviction or adjudication. This expressly includes a seizure, a civil forfeiture and a petition for specialized driving privileges. The court notifies the prosecuting attorney of that county and sets a hearing, or may grant without one where the record conclusively establishes entitlement.

tracks.legalName: Infraction Non-Disclosure under I.C. 34-28-5-15
tracks.publicName: Keeping an infraction off background checks
tracks.mechanism: The court must order the clerk and any case management system operator not to disclose infraction information to a non-criminal-justice organisation or individual where the person is not prosecuted, the charge is dismissed, the person is adjudged not to have committed the infraction, or an adjudication is later vacated. This does not apply where prosecution was deferred. Where the court failed to act, a petition branch applies with earliest filing dates. A deferral or satisfied judgment supports a verified petition no earlier than five years after satisfying the conditions.
exclusions: Cases where prosecution was deferred, for the automatic branch. Those use the five-year deferral branch instead.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Kansas District Court Conviction under K.S.A. 21-6614
tracks.publicName: Expunging a Kansas conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted in Kansas of a traffic infraction, cigarette or tobacco infraction, misdemeanour, class D or E felony, nongrid felony, nondrug grid severity level 6 through 10 felony, drug grid severity level 4 felony for crimes committed between July 1, 1993 and June 30, 2012, or drug grid severity level 5 felony for crimes committed on or after July 1, 2012, may petition the convicting court to expunge the conviction and related arrest records once the applicable period has elapsed since satisfying the sentence imposed or being discharged from probation, a community correctional services programme, parole, postrelease supervision, conditional release or a suspended sentence. Longer periods apply under (c) and (d). At the hearing the court shall order expungement if it makes the four findings in (h). The clock runs from sentence satisfaction or discharge from supervision — not from arrest and not from conviction.
authority: State v. Anderson, 12 Kan. App. 2d 342, 744 P.2d 143 (1987)
exclusions: Rape, K.S.A. 21-5503 or former 21-3502.
Indecent liberties or aggravated indecent liberties with a child, K.S.A. 21-5506 or former 21-3503 or 21-3504.
Criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504(a)(3) or (a)(4) or former 21-3505(a)(2) or (a)(3).
Aggravated criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504 or former 21-3506.
Indecent solicitation or aggravated indecent solicitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5508 or former 21-3510 or 21-3511.
Sexual exploitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5510 or former 21-3516.
Internet trading or aggravated internet trading in child pornography, K.S.A. 21-5514.
Aggravated incest, K.S.A. 21-5604 or former 21-3603.
Endangering or aggravated endangering a child, K.S.A. 21-5601 or former 21-3608 or 21-3608a.
Abuse of a child, K.S.A. 21-5602 or former 21-3609.
Capital murder, K.S.A. 21-5401 or former 21-3439.
Murder in the first degree, K.S.A. 21-5402 or former 21-3401.
Murder in the second degree, K.S.A. 21-5403 or former 21-3402.
Voluntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5404 or former 21-3403.
Involuntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5405 or former 21-3404.
Sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3517, where the victim was under 18 at the time of the crime.
Aggravated sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3518.
A violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, including any diversion for such violation.

Any conviction for any offence in effect at any time prior to July 1, 2011 that is comparable to any offence in K.S.A. 21-6614(e). This reaches convictions under repealed pre-2011 offence definitions.
An attempt to commit any of the above.

Any conviction or any part of the criminal record of a person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f), except through the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route.

waitingPeriods.condition: Traffic infraction, cigarette or tobacco infraction, misdemeanour, or class D or E felony
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the latest of satisfying the sentence imposed or discharge from probation, a community correctional services programme, parole, postrelease supervision, conditional release or a suspended sentence, K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1)

waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the same triggering events, K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1)

waitingPeriods.condition: Drug grid severity level 5, offence committed on or after July 1, 2012
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the same triggering events, K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1)

waitingPeriods.condition: Class A, B or C felony; off-grid felony; nondrug grid severity levels 1 through 5; drug grid levels 1 through 3 for offences from July 1, 1993 to June 30, 2012, or levels 1 through 4 for offences on or after July 1, 2012

Vehicular homicide; driving while cancelled, suspended or revoked; perjury under K.S.A. 8-261a; fraudulent application under K.S.A. 8-142 Fifth; any felony in which a motor vehicle was used; failing to stop at an accident scene; no motor vehicle liability insurance under K.S.A. 40-3104; a violation of former K.S.A. 21-3405b
waitingPeriods.duration: 5 years, K.S.A. 21-6614(c)(1) through (c)(8)

waitingPeriods.condition: First violation of K.S.A. 8-1567, driving under the influence
Second or subsequent violation of K.S.A. 8-1567
waitingPeriods.duration: 10 years, K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(2). Subsection (d) applies to violations committed on or after July 1, 2006.

waitingPeriods.condition: Second or subsequent violation of K.S.A. 8-1567 committed on or after July 1, 2014 but before July 1, 2015
waitingPeriods.duration: 7 years. K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(3) disapplies the 10-year rule to that window, and the shorter period follows from the law in effect at the time of the offence under State v. Anderson.

What sex, race and date of birth should the petition state?
In which Kansas county and which court was the case, and what is the case number?
Which law enforcement agency arrested you?
What offence were you convicted of, and under which Kansas statute?
On what date was the offence committed? This is not the same as the conviction date, and it decides which version of the law applies to you.
On what date were you convicted?
How was the offence classified — a traffic, cigarette or tobacco infraction, a misdemeanour, or a felony? If a felony, what class or grid severity level?
Was the conviction for driving under the influence under K.S.A. 8-1567, and if so was it a first violation or a second or subsequent violation?

Having read the list of offences that cannot be expunged, do you assert that your conviction is not one of them and is not comparable to one of them under a pre-July-2011 offence definition?
In your own words: what has changed in your circumstances and behaviour since the case, and why does expungement matter to you now?

selfHelpBoundaries: The prosecutor opposes the petition.
The court sets a contested evidentiary hearing or a person appears to testify against the petition.
The offence classification or severity level is disputed.
The State v. Anderson time-of-offence analysis is in play beyond the DUI rows in the Judicial Council chart.
The participant may currently be required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act.
The record may be comparable to a K.S.A. 21-6614(e) offence under paragraph (19).
The participant needs to build a real showing on the (h)(2), (h)(3) or (h)(4) findings.
The petition seeks expungement of a felony conviction, because of the firearms-safety finding at (h)(4).
The participant is seeking firearms restoration as the primary goal, which is a federal and state law question beyond the order.
Immigration consequences are in play.
The arrest county and the convicting county differ.

Generation is complete when the packet is produced. Self-help stops when the prosecutor opposes, the court sets a contested evidentiary hearing, the offence classification is disputed, or the participant asks for individualized advocacy on the discretionary findings.
postGenerationHandoffs: Generation is complete when the packet is produced. Self-help stops when the prosecutor opposes, the court sets a contested evidentiary hearing, the offence classification is disputed, or the participant asks for individualized advocacy on the discretionary findings.
packetInstructions: The packet carries a hearing-preparation document putting the four K.S.A. 21-6614(h) findings in plain language and prompting the participant to assemble their own account of the intervening years and their own supporting documents. Three of the four findings are unpleaded by the official petition. LegalEase does not write the participant's account of their own life and does not predict the outcome.

The packet must tell the participant exactly who completes what and in what order: which documents are for the clerk, which are brought to the hearing for the judge, and which goes to the KBI. A packet that hands someone five documents without saying so fails at the counter.
The required number of copies varies by county and there is no statewide answer. The packet instructs the participant to confirm the copy count with the clerk before filing.

Consumer copy must carry the disclosure carve-outs. After expungement the participant is treated as not having been arrested, convicted or diverted and may say so, but K.S.A. 21-6614(i)(2) lists twelve contexts where the arrest, conviction or diversion must still be disclosed, including law enforcement employment, a commercial driver's licence, bar admission, private detective and private patrol work, KDADS institutions, the Kansas lottery, racing and gaming, expanded lottery act positions, state and tribal gaming, securities registration, bail enforcement licensure, and insurance producer or public adjuster licensure for a fraudulent insurance act. Subsection (l) lists eighteen categories of requestor to whom the custodian may still disclose.

The packet must state the firearms-restoration effect. Under K.S.A. 21-6614(k)(2) a person whose expunged record had prohibited firearm possession is deemed to have had the right to keep and bear arms fully restored, and this applies to all orders of expungement including those issued before July 1, 2021; under (m)(2) the KBI reports to the FBI that the record be withdrawn from the national instant criminal background check system. LegalEase states the statutory effect and does not advise on federal firearms law.

The packet must say that the hearing is required and real: the prosecutor appears, any person with relevant information may testify, and the court may inquire into the participant's background with access to Department of Corrections and Prisoner Review Board records.
The docket fee of $176, plus any non-judicial personnel charge, accompanies the petition at filing.
participantQuestions: Capture the date the offence was committed, not only the conviction or diversion date. Under State v. Anderson the law in effect when the offence was committed governs eligibility unless current law is more beneficial to the defendant, and the waiting-period lanes turn on offence-date windows.
Ask for the offence severity level and grid classification, and refer where it is disputed. The 3-year and 5-year lanes turn on it and the participant owns the classification.

Ask whether the participant has been convicted of a felony in the past two years and whether any felony proceeding is pending or being instituted, because K.S.A. 21-6614(h)(1)(A) requires the court to find neither.
scopeRestrictions: A person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act may not expunge any conviction or any part of their criminal record while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f). That freezes every case in the record, not only the registrable offence. The sole exception is the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route; sex offender and violent offender registrants are barred with no exception.

The Kansas Judicial Council states its forms are for non-commercial use and may not be sold, republished or transferred for value without express permission. Every Kansas official-form route is source-gated on that licence until permission is confirmed.

LegalEase does not assert that the participant is eligible, does not classify the offence into a grid severity level for them, and does not assert that an old conviction is or is not comparable to a K.S.A. 21-6614(e) offence under paragraph (19).

provenance.sourceStatement: **The Criminal Cover Sheet versus (g)(3) docketing tension.** The statute requires docketing in the original criminal action; the cover sheet exists to initiate a criminal docket sheet.

unresolvedQuestions.question: The amount of the non-judicial personnel charge actually imposed. 2026 Senate Bill 430 carries the supreme court's authority to impose a charge not exceeding $19 per case from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2030, but the amount currently imposed must be confirmed before a total is quoted.

provenance.sourceStatement: **The current non-judicial personnel charge.** The Revisor's text ends the authority June 30, 2025; 2025 HB 2393 extends it to June 30, 2030. Confirm the amount currently imposed.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Whether a poverty affidavit will be accepted against the $176 expungement docket fee. 2026 House Bill 2724, which would have authorised judges to waive it on a poverty affidavit, died without enactment, and K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(2) says the docket fee is the only fee collected for the case. Some Kansas district court clerks nonetheless publish a poverty affidavit alongside the expungement forms.

provenance.sourceStatement: **Whether any general poverty-based fee waiver reaches a 21-6614 petition.**

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Capture the date the offence was committed, not only the conviction or diversion date. Under State v. Anderson the law in effect when the offence was committed governs eligibility unless current law is more beneficial to the defendant, and the waiting-period lanes turn on offence-date windows.

provenance.sourceStatement: Under *State v. Anderson*, the law in effect when the offense was committed governs eligibility unless current law is more beneficial to the defendant. The Judicial Council chart works this through for DUI. It applies more broadly, and it means the engine must capture the **date the offense was committed**, not only the conviction date.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: A person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act may not expunge any conviction or any part of their criminal record while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f). That freezes every case in the record, not only the registrable offence. The sole exception is the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route; sex offender and violent offender registrants are barred with no exception.

provenance.sourceStatement: Except as provided in K.S.A. 22-4908, an offender required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act may not expunge **any** conviction or any part of the criminal record while the registration requirement is in effect. Not just the registrable offense. Every other case is frozen too.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The packet carries a hearing-preparation document putting the four K.S.A. 21-6614(h) findings in plain language and prompting the participant to assemble their own account of the intervening years and their own supporting documents. Three of the four findings are unpleaded by the official petition. LegalEase does not write the participant's account of their own life and does not predict the outcome.

provenance.sourceStatement: **What LegalEase can prepare:** a preparation sheet that puts the four findings in plain language, prompts the participant to assemble their own evidence of the intervening years, and tells them the prosecutor will be there and that any person with relevant information may testify. **What LegalEase must not do:** write the participant's account of their own life, or predict the outcome.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The Certificate of Service and Mailing on the Notice of Hearing is left blank and visibly labelled for clerk completion. It reads in the first person but its signature line is "(Clerk of the Court) (Deputy Clerk)", K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(1) puts notice on the court, and the Judicial Council instructions have the participant file the original plus copies and the clerk send them. LegalEase must never prefill it or have the participant sign it.

provenance.sourceStatement: **LegalEase must leave that block blank and label it for clerk completion.** Do not prefill it, do not have the participant sign it.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The hearing date, time, courthouse, division and room are left blank on the Notice of Hearing. The participant obtains them from the clerk or the assigned judge's administrative assistant after filing, and writes them in. The packet generates before the court supplies them.

provenance.sourceStatement: **What the participant must obtain:** a date, a time, the courthouse, and the division or room number.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Judge, clerk, prosecutor and court blocks are left blank. LegalEase completes paragraphs 1 through 4 of the granting and denying orders, which recite the participant's own identity and case facts, and never drafts the findings language or paragraph 8 of the denial order, which is the court's reason.

provenance.sourceHeading: LEGAL-DESIGN DECISION / Can LegalEase generate a participant-facing form or packet ... / 2
provenance.sourceStatement: **Never assert on the participant's behalf a fact only the other actor can establish.** LegalEase may prepare paragraphs 1 through 4 of both orders because those recite the participant's own identity and case facts. It may not draft paragraph 8 of the denial order, which is the court's reason, or the finding language the judge must make.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The packet must tell the participant exactly who completes what and in what order: which documents are for the clerk, which are brought to the hearing for the judge, and which goes to the KBI. A packet that hands someone five documents without saying so fails at the counter.

provenance.sourceHeading: LEGAL-DESIGN DECISION / Can LegalEase generate a participant-facing form or packet ... / 3
provenance.sourceStatement: **Tell the participant, in the packet, exactly who completes what and in what order.** A packet that hands someone five documents without saying that two are for the clerk, two are for the judge, and one goes to the KBI is a packet that fails at the counter.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The required number of copies varies by county and there is no statewide answer. The packet instructs the participant to confirm the copy count with the clerk before filing.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK A / GEOGRAPHY AND VENUE / Local practice
provenance.sourceStatement: the instructions tell the participant to check with the clerk for the required number of copies. That varies by county and there is no statewide answer.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Race, ethnicity and Social Security number on the Criminal Cover Sheet and the order cover sheet are left for the participant to complete by hand, pending the data-protection review. The Criminal Cover Sheet states the Social Security number is not mandatory, is not a public record, is stored separately and is destroyed within a reasonable time.

provenance.sourceStatement: **Race and ethnicity are collected as checkbox fields.** Route to the data-protection review before build, and consider whether LegalEase should collect them at all or leave them for the participant to complete by hand.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Consumer copy must carry the disclosure carve-outs. After expungement the participant is treated as not having been arrested, convicted or diverted and may say so, but K.S.A. 21-6614(i)(2) lists twelve contexts where the arrest, conviction or diversion must still be disclosed, including law enforcement employment, a commercial driver's licence, bar admission, private detective and private patrol work, KDADS institutions, the Kansas lottery, racing and gaming, expanded lottery act positions, state and tribal gaming, securities registration, bail enforcement licensure, and insurance producer or public adjuster licensure for a fraudulent insurance act. Subsection (l) lists eighteen categories of requestor to whom the custodian may still disclose.

provenance.sourceStatement: **It omits the disclosure carve-outs, which are the core consumer message.** ... Telling a Kansas participant they can say it never happened, without the carve-outs, is the same class of error as the Georgia reference's "may state the record does not exist."

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The packet must state the firearms-restoration effect. Under K.S.A. 21-6614(k)(2) a person whose expunged record had prohibited firearm possession is deemed to have had the right to keep and bear arms fully restored, and this applies to all orders of expungement including those issued before July 1, 2021; under (m)(2) the KBI reports to the FBI that the record be withdrawn from the national instant criminal background check system. LegalEase states the statutory effect and does not advise on federal firearms law.

provenance.sourceStatement: **It omits the firearms restoration effect, which is in the statute's own title.** K.S.A. 21-6614(k)(2) provides that a person whose expunged record had prohibited firearm possession "shall be deemed to have had such person's right to keep and bear arms fully restored," and says this applies to all orders of expungement including those issued before July 1, 2021.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The Kansas Judicial Council states its forms are for non-commercial use and may not be sold, republished or transferred for value without express permission. Every Kansas official-form route is source-gated on that licence until permission is confirmed.

provenance.sourceHeading: Kansas source-package import record, source_gated treatment of the Kansas Judicial Council order form
provenance.sourceStatement: Commercial distribution is source-gated because the Kansas Judicial Council states its forms are for non-commercial use and may not be sold, republished, or transferred for value without express permission.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Generation is complete when the packet is produced. Self-help stops when the prosecutor opposes, the court sets a contested evidentiary hearing, the offence classification is disputed, or the participant asks for individualized advocacy on the discretionary findings.

provenance.sourceHeading: Controlling Batch 2 packet-only amendment / Scope restrictions and handoffs do not erase packet identity
provenance.sourceStatement: An active sentence, required hearing, discretionary standard, evidentiary burden, local filing practice, or likely objection is represented as a scope restriction, packet instruction, or handoff condition—not automatically as process_guidance.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Ask for the offence severity level and grid classification, and refer where it is disputed. The 3-year and 5-year lanes turn on it and the participant owns the classification.

provenance.sourceStatement: Offense severity level and grid classification | **Participant question**, with attorney referral where disputed

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Ask whether the participant has been convicted of a felony in the past two years and whether any felony proceeding is pending or being instituted, because K.S.A. 21-6614(h)(1)(A) requires the court to find neither.

provenance.sourceStatement: Prior felony conviction within two years | **Participant question**

legalDesignLimitations.statement: LegalEase does not assert that the participant is eligible, does not classify the offence into a grid severity level for them, and does not assert that an old conviction is or is not comparable to a K.S.A. 21-6614(e) offence under paragraph (19).

provenance.sourceStatement: Fee: $176 docket fee, plus a supreme court charge of up to $19 per case to fund non-judicial personnel.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Fulfilled Kansas Diversion Agreement under K.S.A. 21-6614
tracks.publicName: Expunging a Kansas diversion you completed
tracks.mechanism: A person who has fulfilled the terms of a diversion agreement may petition the district court to expunge the diversion agreement and related arrest records if three or more years have elapsed since the terms of the diversion agreement were fulfilled. The five-year lanes in (c) and the five-year first-violation DUI lane in (d)(1) reach diversions by their own terms; the 10-year lane in (d)(2) speaks only of satisfying a sentence or discharge from supervision and does not reach a diversion, which is why the Judicial Council chart shows not-applicable in the diversion column for the 7-year and 10-year DUI rows. The triggering event is fulfilment of the diversion terms, and nothing else.
authority: State v. Anderson, 12 Kan. App. 2d 342, 744 P.2d 143 (1987)
exclusions: Rape, K.S.A. 21-5503 or former 21-3502.
Indecent liberties or aggravated indecent liberties with a child, K.S.A. 21-5506 or former 21-3503 or 21-3504.
Criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504(a)(3) or (a)(4) or former 21-3505(a)(2) or (a)(3).
Aggravated criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504 or former 21-3506.
Indecent solicitation or aggravated indecent solicitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5508 or former 21-3510 or 21-3511.
Sexual exploitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5510 or former 21-3516.
Internet trading or aggravated internet trading in child pornography, K.S.A. 21-5514.
Aggravated incest, K.S.A. 21-5604 or former 21-3603.
Endangering or aggravated endangering a child, K.S.A. 21-5601 or former 21-3608 or 21-3608a.
Abuse of a child, K.S.A. 21-5602 or former 21-3609.
Capital murder, K.S.A. 21-5401 or former 21-3439.
Murder in the first degree, K.S.A. 21-5402 or former 21-3401.
Murder in the second degree, K.S.A. 21-5403 or former 21-3402.
Voluntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5404 or former 21-3403.
Involuntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5405 or former 21-3404.
Sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3517, where the victim was under 18 at the time of the crime.
Aggravated sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3518.
A violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, including any diversion for such violation.

Any conviction for any offence in effect at any time prior to July 1, 2011 that is comparable to any offence in K.S.A. 21-6614(e). This reaches convictions under repealed pre-2011 offence definitions.
An attempt to commit any of the above.

Any conviction or any part of the criminal record of a person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f), except through the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route.
A diversion agreement whose terms have not been fulfilled.
A second or subsequent DUI lane. K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(2) speaks only of satisfying a sentence or discharge from supervision, so the 10-year lane and the 7-year window do not reach a diversion.
A diversion for a violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, which K.S.A. 21-6614(e)(18) excludes expressly including any diversion for such violation.

waitingPeriods.condition: A diversion for a first violation of K.S.A. 8-1567, driving under the influence
waitingPeriods.duration: 5 years from fulfilment of the terms of the diversion agreement. K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(1) reaches a first DUI violation including any diversion for such violation.

waitingPeriods.condition: A diversion for a second or subsequent DUI
waitingPeriods.duration: not applicable. K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(2) is written in terms of satisfying a sentence or discharge from supervision and does not reach a diversion; the Judicial Council chart records this as not applicable in the diversion column.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name?
What was your full name at the time of the arrest, conviction or diversion, if different from your name now?
What sex, race and date of birth should the petition state?
In which Kansas county and which court was the case, and what is the case number?
Which law enforcement agency arrested you?
What offence was the diversion agreement for, and under which Kansas statute?
On what date was the offence committed? This is not the same as the date you entered the diversion, and it decides which version of the law applies to you.
On what date did you enter into the diversion agreement?
On what date did you fulfil all the terms of the diversion agreement? This is the date the waiting period runs from.
Which prosecuting authority or court granted the diversion?
How would the diverted offence have been classified — an infraction, a misdemeanour, or a felony? If a felony, what class or grid severity level?
Was the diversion for driving under the influence under K.S.A. 8-1567, and if so was it a first violation?
Have you been convicted of a felony in the past two years, or is any felony proceeding pending or being instituted against you?
Are you currently required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act?
Having read the list of offences that cannot be expunged, do you assert that your diverted offence is not one of them?
In your own words: what has changed in your circumstances and behaviour since the case, and why does expungement matter to you now?
What documents do you have that show what you have been doing since the case — employment, education, treatment, service, letters of support?

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Prostitution Conviction or Diversion Where the Petitioner Was Acting Under Coercion, K.S.A. 21-6614(b)
tracks.publicName: Expunging a prostitution case where someone was coercing you
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of prostitution as defined in former K.S.A. 21-3512, or of a violation of K.S.A. 21-6419, or who entered into a diversion agreement in lieu of further criminal proceedings for such a violation, may petition the convicting court to expunge the conviction or diversion agreement and related arrest records if one or more years have elapsed since satisfying the sentence, fulfilling the diversion terms or discharge from supervision, and the person can prove they were acting under coercion caused by the act of another. Coercion is defined in the subsection as threats of harm or physical restraint against any person; a scheme, plan or pattern intended to cause a person to believe that failure to perform an act would result in bodily harm or physical restraint against any person; or the abuse or threatened abuse of the legal process.
exclusions: A case that is not a conviction of, or diversion for, prostitution under K.S.A. 21-6419 or former K.S.A. 21-3512.
A petitioner who cannot prove they were acting under coercion caused by the act of another. The coercion element is a proof burden at the hearing, not a formality.
A person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act, K.S.A. 21-6614(f).
The K.S.A. 21-6614(e) offence list, which continues to apply.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Immediate Expungement After Completing a Specialty Court Programme, K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3)
tracks.publicName: Expunging a conviction right after you finish a specialty court programme
tracks.mechanism: Notwithstanding the three-year rule in K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1), and except as provided in subsections (b), (c), (d), (e) and (f), a person who has completed the requirements of a specialty court programme established under K.S.A. 20-173 may petition the district court to expunge the conviction and related arrest records. There is no waiting period. The court may waive all or part of the docket fee imposed for filing a petition under this subsection. At the hearing the court need only find that no felony proceeding is presently pending or being instituted against the petitioner under (h)(1)(B); the two-year no-felony-conviction lookback in (h)(1)(A) does not apply to this lane. The other three findings continue to apply.
exclusions: Rape, K.S.A. 21-5503 or former 21-3502.
Indecent liberties or aggravated indecent liberties with a child, K.S.A. 21-5506 or former 21-3503 or 21-3504.
Criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504(a)(3) or (a)(4) or former 21-3505(a)(2) or (a)(3).
Aggravated criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504 or former 21-3506.
Indecent solicitation or aggravated indecent solicitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5508 or former 21-3510 or 21-3511.
Sexual exploitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5510 or former 21-3516.
Internet trading or aggravated internet trading in child pornography, K.S.A. 21-5514.
Aggravated incest, K.S.A. 21-5604 or former 21-3603.
Endangering or aggravated endangering a child, K.S.A. 21-5601 or former 21-3608 or 21-3608a.
Abuse of a child, K.S.A. 21-5602 or former 21-3609.
Capital murder, K.S.A. 21-5401 or former 21-3439.
Murder in the first degree, K.S.A. 21-5402 or former 21-3401.
Murder in the second degree, K.S.A. 21-5403 or former 21-3402.
Voluntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5404 or former 21-3403.
Involuntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5405 or former 21-3404.
Sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3517, where the victim was under 18 at the time of the crime.
Aggravated sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3518.
A violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, including any diversion for such violation.

Any conviction for any offence in effect at any time prior to July 1, 2011 that is comparable to any offence in K.S.A. 21-6614(e). This reaches convictions under repealed pre-2011 offence definitions.
An attempt to commit any of the above.

Any conviction or any part of the criminal record of a person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f), except through the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route.

Any offence that would sit in the five-year lane under K.S.A. 21-6614(c), the five-year or ten-year DUI lanes under (d), or the one-year prostitution lane under (b). The exceptions in (b), (c), (d), (e) and (f) all continue to apply, so the immediate route reaches only offences that would otherwise sit in the three-year lane.
A programme that was not a specialty court established under K.S.A. 20-173, including ordinary diversion and locally run programmes that do not qualify.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Kansas Arrest Record under K.S.A. 22-2410
tracks.publicName: Expunging an arrest that did not lead to a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Any person who has been arrested in Kansas may petition the district court to expunge the arrest record. There is no waiting period. On filing, the court sets a hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency, and the official court file is separated from other court records and disclosed only to a judge, designated court staff, the prosecuting attorney, the arresting agency or others by court order. At the hearing the court shall order the arrest record and subsequent court proceedings expunged on finding that the arrest occurred because of mistaken identity, that a court found there was no probable cause for the arrest, that the petitioner was found not guilty, or that expungement would be in the best interests of justice and charges have been dismissed or no charges have been or are likely to be filed. This is the correct route for an arrest-only record: K.S.A. 21-6614 expunges a conviction or a diversion and related arrest records, so with neither there is nothing for it to attach to.
authority: State v. Yrigolla, 38 Kan. App. 2d 1029, 175 P.3d 276 (2008)
exclusions: A case in which the person was charged with and convicted of a crime, or entered into and completed a diversion agreement, which runs under K.S.A. 21-6614 instead. State v. Yrigolla holds that K.S.A. 22-2410 does not apply where a person was arrested and subsequently entered into and completed a diversion agreement to avoid a conviction.
An arrest on a violation of a city ordinance, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516a in the municipal court.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The K.S.A. 22-2410(a)(2) mandatory expungement category is not a participant filing. Where a person was arrested as a result of mistaken identity or because another person used their identifying information and the charge is dismissed or not prosecuted, the prosecuting attorney or the judicial officer who ordered the dismissal or declined to prosecute provides notice to the court and petitions for expungement, and the court shall order it. LegalEase explains that route and does not file it or represent that it can.

provenance.sourceStatement: the prosecuting attorney or other judicial officer who ordered the dismissal or declined to prosecute shall provide notice to the court of such action and petition the district court for the expungement of such arrest record, and the court shall order the arrest record and subsequent court proceedings, if any, expunged and purged from all applicable state and federal systems pursuant to subsection (d).

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The packet must state the fee position accurately. No surcharge or fee at all is imposed on a petitioner under (a)(1) who was arrested as a result of identity theft, or who has had charges dismissed because a court found no probable cause, or who was found not guilty, or whose charges have been dismissed. That reaches most arrest-only petitioners, and the $176 docket fee is charged only where none of those applies.

provenance.sourceStatement: No surcharge or fee shall be imposed to any person filing a petition pursuant to subsection (a)(1), who was arrested as a result of being a victim of identity theft under K.S.A. 21-4018, prior to its repeal, or K.S.A. 21-6107(a), and amendments thereto, or who has had criminal charges dismissed because a court has found that there was no probable cause for the arrest, the petitioner was found not guilty in court proceedings or the charges have been dismissed.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Ask whether the participant was convicted or completed a diversion in the case. If either happened, K.S.A. 21-6614 governs and this route does not apply, as the form's own Notes on Use and State v. Yrigolla record.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Kansas Municipal Court Conviction or Diversion under K.S.A. 12-4516
tracks.publicName: Expunging a city ordinance conviction or diversion
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of a violation of a city ordinance may petition the convicting municipal court to expunge the conviction and related arrest records once three or more years have elapsed since satisfying the sentence imposed or discharge from probation, parole or a suspended sentence; a person who has fulfilled the terms of a diversion agreement based on a city ordinance violation may petition once three or more years have elapsed since those terms were fulfilled. Longer five-year and ten-year periods apply to the offences listed in (d) and to DUI-equivalent ordinance violations under (e), and a one-year period applies under (c) to a prostitution-equivalent ordinance violation where the petitioner can prove coercion. The court sets a hearing and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency, and shall order expungement on three findings: no felony conviction in the past two years with no such proceeding pending or being instituted, that the petitioner's circumstances and behaviour warrant expungement, and that expungement is consistent with the public welfare. There is no firearms finding, because a municipal ordinance conviction is not a felony.
exclusions: A conviction or diversion for a city ordinance violation that would also constitute a violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, K.S.A. 12-4516(f).
A district court conviction or diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 21-6614.
An arrest with no municipal conviction and no municipal diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516a.
A petitioner convicted of a felony within the past two years, or against whom such a proceeding is pending or being instituted, K.S.A. 12-4516(h)(1).

waitingPeriods.condition: Conviction of a city ordinance violation
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the latest of satisfying the sentence imposed or discharge from probation, parole or a suspended sentence, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(1)

waitingPeriods.condition: Fulfilled diversion agreement based on a city ordinance violation
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the date the terms of the diversion agreement were fulfilled, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(2)

waitingPeriods.condition: An ordinance violation prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) and adopted before July 1, 2014
waitingPeriods.duration: none. K.S.A. 12-4516(b) states no elapsed period for this category.

waitingPeriods.condition: An ordinance violation that would also constitute prostitution under K.S.A. 21-6419 or former K.S.A. 21-3512, where the petitioner can prove coercion caused by the act of another
waitingPeriods.duration: 1 year from satisfying the sentence, fulfilling the diversion terms or discharge from supervision, K.S.A. 12-4516(c)

waitingPeriods.condition: An ordinance violation that would also constitute vehicular homicide, driving while cancelled, suspended or revoked, perjury under K.S.A. 8-261a, a fraudulent application under K.S.A. 8-142 Fifth, a felony in which a motor vehicle was used, failing to stop at an accident scene, no motor vehicle liability insurance under K.S.A. 40-3104, or a violation of former K.S.A. 21-3405b
An ordinance violation that would also constitute a first violation of K.S.A. 8-1567, driving under the influence
An ordinance violation that would also constitute a second or subsequent violation of K.S.A. 8-1567
waitingPeriods.duration: 10 years, K.S.A. 12-4516(e)(2). Subsection (e) applies to all violations committed on or after July 1, 2006, and the municipal statute has no equivalent of the K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(3) seven-year window.

tracks.venue: Statewide statute available in every Kansas municipal court, executed court by court. K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(1) directs a conviction petition to the convicting court, which is the municipal court of the city whose ordinance was violated, and (a)(2) directs a diversion petition to the court. Kansas has hundreds of municipal courts and no unified municipal forms regime, so the instrument is court-specific even though the mechanism is statewide.

The municipal findings are three, not four. K.S.A. 12-4516(h) requires no felony conviction in the past two years with no such proceeding pending or being instituted, that the petitioner's circumstances and behaviour warrant expungement, and that expungement is consistent with the public welfare. There is no firearms-safety finding, because an ordinance conviction is not a felony conviction.

The disclosure carve-outs apply here too. K.S.A. 12-4516(i) tracks the district court effect: the petitioner is treated as not having been arrested, convicted or diverted, subject to an enumerated list of contexts in which the arrest, conviction or diversion must still be disclosed.

scopeRestrictions: Kansas municipal courts publish their own expungement instruments and some govern by charter ordinance rather than by K.S.A. 12-4516 directly. Wichita Municipal Court proceeds under Charter Ordinance No. 224, §§ 12 and 13 and publishes a Motion and Order rather than a petition; Topeka Municipal Court cites K.S.A. 12-4516 and publishes its own petition and order forms. Where the municipal court publishes a current form or requires its own process, that local instrument governs and the statewide controlled pleading is not used.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a City Ordinance Arrest Record under K.S.A. 12-4516a
tracks.publicName: Expunging an arrest on a city ordinance charge
tracks.mechanism: Any person who has been arrested on a violation of a city ordinance may petition the court to expunge the arrest record. When the petition is filed the court sets a hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency, and the official court file is separated from other court records and disclosed only to a judge, designated court staff, the prosecuting attorney, the arresting agency or others by court order. A municipal court may prescribe a fee as costs, except that no fee may be charged to a person arrested as a result of being a victim of identity theft. At the hearing the court shall order the arrest record and subsequent court proceedings expunged on finding mistaken identity; that a court found no probable cause for the arrest; that the petitioner was found not guilty; that the arrest was for a violation of an ordinance prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) adopted before July 1, 2014; or that expungement would be in the best interests of justice and charges have been dismissed or no charges have been or are likely to be filed.
exclusions: A municipal conviction or a fulfilled municipal diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516.
An arrest on a state law violation, which runs under K.S.A. 22-2410 in the district court.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Relief from Drug Offender Registration under K.S.A. 22-4908, Combined with Expungement under K.S.A. 21-6614
tracks.publicName: Getting off the drug offender registry so your record can be expunged
tracks.mechanism: K.S.A. 21-6614(f) bars expungement of any conviction or any part of the criminal record of a person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act while registration is required, except as provided in K.S.A. 22-4908. Under that section a drug offender who has registered for at least five years after the date of parole, discharge or release, or five years from the date of conviction if not confined, may file a verified petition for relief from registration in the district court of the county of conviction. The Judicial Council has developed the petition form the statute requires. On relief the court orders removal from the registry and notifies the KBI within 14 days. Subsection (i) permits the offender to combine the petition for relief with a petition for expungement under K.S.A. 21-6614 where the offence requiring registration is otherwise eligible for expungement. Sex offenders and violent offenders are not authorised to seek relief.
exclusions: Sex offenders and violent offenders required to register. K.S.A. 22-4908 authorises relief for drug offenders only, and K.S.A. 21-6614(f) bars expungement for the rest with no exception.

An offender who has registered for less than five years after the date of parole, discharge or release, or less than five years from the date of conviction if not confined. Time in jail or prison, and time when the offender was not in substantial compliance with registration requirements, does not count.
An offender required to register under K.S.A. 22-4906(k) because of an out-of-state conviction who would still be required to register under the law of the state where the conviction occurred.
A further petition within three years of a denial, unless the court orders a shorter period.
A registrable offence that is not otherwise eligible for expungement, for the combined expungement unit.

Any period during which the offender is incarcerated, or does not substantially comply with registration requirements, does not count toward the five years.
three years, unless a shorter period is ordered by the court

units.label: Verified petition for relief from offender registration
units.description: The Kansas Judicial Council Petition for Relief from Offender Registration, 06/2022, filed in the district court of the county where the offender was convicted of the offence requiring registration, with the Order of Relief from Offender Registration Cover Sheet for the KBI. Items 1 through 9 are the participant's own identity, conviction, registration, compliance and treatment-provider facts, all of which LegalEase completes from their answers. Item 10, the showing that circumstances, behaviour and treatment history demonstrate sufficient rehabilitation and that registration is no longer necessary to promote public safety, is a participant-authored narrative that LegalEase prompts for and formats and never writes. The court sets the hearing and notifies the county or district attorney, who notifies victims; the court may order a risk assessment at the offender's expense; relief requires clear and convincing evidence.

units.label: Companion or combined expungement petition under K.S.A. 21-6614
units.description: The K.S.A. 21-6614 expungement packet for the registrable conviction, permitted by K.S.A. 22-4908(i) to be combined with the registration-relief petition where the offence is otherwise eligible for expungement. This unit is the conviction packet already modelled at ks-21-6614-conviction and is not duplicated here: the same Judicial Council petition, cover sheet, notice of hearing, order cover sheet and both proposed orders are used, on the same waiting-period and findings rules. It is a separate legal filing from the registration petition, with a different statute, a different notice set and a different standard of proof, which is why the route is composed rather than a single packet.

tracks.publicName: Get the certification you need before asking to clear a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Every petition or application seeking expungement of a conviction must include a certification of eligibility issued by the Administrative Office of the Courts. The participant requests it on the AOC Records Unit form, pays the statutory fee, and the AOC produces the certification after a Kentucky State Police records check. The certification is an evidentiary attachment: it decides nothing, and an adverse certification does not stop the clerk from accepting a petition.
exclusions: Not required for a non-conviction petition under KRS 431.076. The Clerks' Manual states the certification requirement applies to conviction expungements.
Not required for void-and-seal relief under KRS 218A.275 or KRS 218A.276.
Not required for juvenile expungement under KRS 610.330.
Not required for protective-order record expungement under KRS 403.745 or KRS 456.070.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Misdemeanor, Violation or Traffic Infraction Conviction (KRS 431.078)
tracks.publicName: Clear a Kentucky misdemeanor, violation or traffic conviction
tracks.mechanism: On petition, the court expunges a misdemeanor, violation or traffic infraction conviction, together with any misdemeanor, violation or traffic charges dismissed or amended in the same criminal action, five years after the later of sentence completion or successful completion of probation. Relief is mandatory for a single offence or a series arising from a single incident and discretionary for a series that did not. Once expunged the proceedings are deemed never to have occurred and the participant need not disclose them.
exclusions: A sex offence, or an offence committed against a child.
An offence subject to enhancement for a second or subsequent offence, unless the enhancement window has expired.
Any felony or misdemeanor conviction in the five years before filing.
Any felony or misdemeanor proceeding pending or being instituted against the participant.
Offences against a jurisdiction other than the Commonwealth of Kentucky. KRS 431.078(10) confines the relief to Kentucky offences.

waitingPeriods.duration: five years from the later of completion of the sentence or successful completion of probation

waitingPeriods.condition: Conviction voided under KRS 218A.275(8) or KRS 218A.276(8)
waitingPeriods.duration: none. KRS 431.078(2) removes the five-year wait where the conviction was voided, which is the only route in Kentucky to same-year misdemeanor expungement

tracks.legalName: Application to Vacate and Expunge a Class D Felony Conviction (KRS 431.073)
tracks.publicName: Ask the court to vacate and clear a Kentucky Class D felony
tracks.mechanism: On a verified application filed in the original criminal case, the court may vacate an eligible Class D felony conviction, dismiss the charges with prejudice and order the record expunged. Relief is discretionary. The record is expunged only on full payment of the $250 expungement fee, which may be paid in instalments under KRS 534.020. Vacatur does not revive an expired limitations period, is not a finding of legal error or innocence, and does not nullify findings of fact or law.
exclusions: Class A, B and C felonies, and any felony not within KRS 431.073(1).

For the KRS 431.073(1)(d) branch: KRS 189A.010 impaired driving, KRS 508.032, KRS 519.055, abuse of public office, sex offences, offences against a child, and any offence that resulted in serious bodily injury or death.
Any conviction in the five years before the application.
Any felony or misdemeanor proceeding pending or being instituted against the applicant.

The eligibility list must be date-parameterised before release, and the controlling review's statement that no future amendment exists is incorrect.

tracks.legalName: Application to Vacate and Expunge a Felony Conviction After a Full Pardon (KRS 431.073(1)(c))
tracks.publicName: Clear a Kentucky felony the Governor has pardoned
tracks.mechanism: Where the Governor has granted a full pardon, the pardoned conviction is eligible for vacatur and expungement on the same verified application as any other KRS 431.073 case. The Class D limitation and the enumerated-offence list do not apply on this branch: the pardon itself is the eligibility ground. The five-year wait in KRS 431.073(2)(a) is not branch-specific and still applies.
exclusions: Anything less than a full pardon. A partial pardon, a conditional pardon or a commutation is not this branch.
Any conviction in the five years before the application.
Any felony or misdemeanor proceeding pending or being instituted against the applicant.

rules.filing: File AOC-496.3, Application to Vacate and Expunge Felony Conviction (printed revision 6-23), as a motion in the original criminal case with the Circuit Court Clerk of the court of conviction, using the full-pardon election only under KRS 431.073(1)(c). One operative filing per original criminal case; related underlying District Court case information is included where the form asks for it. The applicant appears pro se unless represented; attorney signature language is never used for a pro-se filer.
rules.fees: Ordinary branch: $40 certification, $50 application fee at filing, and $250 upon issuance of relief, subject to the statutory instalment mechanism under KRS 534.020. IFP branch: AOC-026 with AOC-496.3 and the pardon; the clerk accepts the application without the fee or the certification while the IFP motion is considered; the judge decides; an express ruling on the later $250 is sought and no waiver is promised by the filing.
rules.feeWaiver: AOC-026 (revision 10-22) filed with the application; the Clerks' Manual expressly permits acceptance without fee or certification when an IFP motion is filed. The judge decides the request; the actual waiver order governs fee relief.
rules.notice: The clerk performs statutory notice to the prosecuting Commonwealth's or county attorney and to the county attorney where judgment was entered, as applicable; the prosecutor handles victim notification. AOC-496.3's clerk-use notice certification is left blank and is not assigned to the applicant.
rules.service: None by the applicant: effected by the clerk. No certificate of service is prepared by the applicant.
rules.participantSignature: The applicant signs before a notary or the circuit court clerk.
rules.serviceTiming: None required of the applicant; the prosecutor's 60-day response period runs from the clerk's service, with any extension and the statutory 120-day provisions tracked after filing.
rules.filingMethod: Deliver to the proper Circuit Court Clerk by a channel that office accepts. Official guidance permits attorney electronic filing; universal pro-se eFiling or mail acceptance is not inferred from that statement.
rules.filingDeadline: No special outer deadline running from the pardon was identified in KRS 431.073(1)(c). In the ordinary certification branch the application is filed while the certification remains valid; court guidance says it expires in 30 days.
rules.coverSheet: None: no statewide civil cover sheet is identified for this original-case filing, and none is inserted by default; genuinely applicable local administrative requirements are checked.
rules.proposedOrder: The statewide clerk workflow uses AOC-496.4; the applicant supplies a proposed order only when the particular court requires it.
rules.affidavitOrVerification: The official application's own sworn verification, signed before a notary or the Circuit Court Clerk; no separate duplicative affidavit.
rules.schedulesOrContinuationPages: Labeled continuation sheets where needed; unrelated captions never combined; no charge omitted for not being a felony.
rules.postFilingInstructions: Track the prosecutor's 60-day response period from service, any extension and the statutory 120-day provisions. The court may grant without a hearing after a no-objection response or after 120 days with no response from prosecutor or victim; this is not automatic relief on day 120. Obtain the actual order and complete its payment or waiver and distribution steps.
rules.uncontestedHearingTreatment: The court may grant without a hearing after a no-objection response or after the statutory 120 days with no response from the prosecutor or victim; relief is never presented as automatic on day 120.
rules.contestedHearingOrOppositionHandoff: Self-help stops on prosecutor or victim opposition, a disputed pardon or identity, or a contested evidentiary proceeding (product policy recorded from the research).
rules.eligibilityAnchor: Full pardon covering the conviction under KRS 431.073(1)(c); five years after sentence completion or successful completion of probation or parole, whichever is later; no felony or misdemeanor conviction during the preceding five years; no pending or newly instituted felony or misdemeanor proceeding. The pardon is not itself an expungement and its date is never substituted for the anchor without records establishing that it ended the sentence.
rules.formMappingCorrections: AOC-496.3's full-pardon category is separate from the discretionary Class-D category; Section 7's rehabilitation narrative is expressly limited to KRS 431.073(1)(d) and is never required of a pardoned applicant. The pardon is attached as the selected category directs; mutually exclusive alternatives are never both checked. Applicant execution signature and date, notarial attestation and clerk notice date and signature remain completion fields; the applicant's printed identifying facts may be filled from supplied information. AOC-496.3's ordinary certification instruction is never erased or falsified; the Clerks' Manual IFP exception is explained in companion instructions and the branching contract.
rules.statuteCurrency: The statute consulted is labeled effective until April 30, 2027; this version is not silently reused for filings governed by a later version.

researchParticipantText.text: Use the full-pardon selection on the official application and attach your pardon. Do not sign the sworn application in advance. For an ordinary paid filing, include the current certification and application fee. If you are asking to proceed without paying costs, submit AOC-026 with the application and pardon; the clerk's statewide instructions permit acceptance without the fee or certification while that request is considered. Ask for an express ruling on the later expungement fee. Filing a waiver request does not mean the judge has granted it.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Expungement of Acquittals and Dismissals With Prejudice (KRS 431.076(1)(a))
tracks.publicName: Check whether your dismissed or acquitted Kentucky case already cleared itself
tracks.mechanism: Where a person is acquitted, or an order dismisses with prejudice all criminal charges in a case and the dismissal was not in exchange for a guilty plea to another charge, the court enters an order of automatic expungement thirty days after the judgment becomes final. The statute states that the order shall not require any action by the person. All criminal records in the custody of the court and of any other agency, including law enforcement records, are expunged and the proceedings are deemed never to have occurred. KRS 431.076(8) makes the section retroactive except for subsection (1)(a), so the automatic route does not reach dispositions before 15 July 2020.
exclusions: Dispositions before 15 July 2020, which KRS 431.076(8) excludes from the automatic subsection.
Any dismissal in exchange for a guilty plea to another offence.
Traffic infractions not otherwise classified as misdemeanors.
Cases where fewer than all charges were resolved this way. The statute reaches an order dismissing all criminal charges in a case.
Cabinet for Health and Family Services records, which KRS 431.076(4) does not reach.

Standard distribution is to the defendant or their attorney, the county or Commonwealth's attorney, the Kentucky State Police, the arresting agency, the local jail and the local pretrial office; any other agency must be asked for within sixty days of the expungement.

tracks.publicName: Clear a Kentucky case that ended without a conviction
tracks.mechanism: On petition, the court expunges the records of an acquittal or a dismissal not already expunged automatically, and of felony charges originally filed in District Court on which no grand jury indicted and no Commonwealth's attorney filed an information. For the acquittal and dismissal branch the court shall grant the petition. All criminal records in the custody of the court and of any other agency, including law enforcement records, are expunged and the proceedings are deemed never to have occurred. The section is retroactive except for the automatic subsection.
exclusions: Any dismissal in exchange for a guilty plea to another offence.
Records already expunged under the automatic subsection.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Void a First Controlled-Substance Possession Conviction and Seal the Records (KRS 218A.275)
tracks.publicName: Void and seal a first Kentucky drug possession conviction
tracks.mechanism: After satisfactory completion of treatment, probation or other sentence on a first conviction for possession of a controlled substance, the court may void the conviction and shall then order the records sealed. A voided conviction is not a first offence for later Chapter 218A purposes and is not a conviction for disqualifications or disabilities imposed by law. Voiding may occur only once for any person. Records excepted by KRS 27A.099 are not sealed.
exclusions: Anything other than a first conviction for possession of a controlled substance.
Trafficking offences.
Any person who has already had a conviction voided under KRS 218A.275, which may occur only once.

Any person who has previously had a possession charge dismissed after completing a deferred prosecution under KRS 218A.14151. KRS 218A.275(12) makes that an absolute bar, and the controlling decision owner recorded it on 2026-08-29 (LWD-2026-08-29-KY-218A-275).

tracks.publicName: Work out what your diverted Kentucky case counts as
tracks.mechanism: On successful completion of pretrial diversion the charges are listed as dismissed-diverted and do not constitute a criminal conviction. The person need not disclose the disposition on an application for employment, licensure or otherwise unless federal law requires it, and diversion records may not be introduced as evidence without the defendant's consent. The designation is not expungement: the record still exists until it is expunged, so this node reads the disposition and routes to the automatic or petition track.

awaitingCounselClassification.question: Whether a dismissed-diverted disposition is a dismissal with prejudice for the purposes of the automatic expungement subsection. KRS 533.258(1) is silent on prejudice. Two points bear on it that the controlling review does not make: the diversion plea is to the same charge, so the KRS 431.076(1)(a) carve-out for a dismissal in exchange for a guilty plea to another charge is not triggered; and the Clerks' Manual records a distinct disposition code for dismissed-diverted, so diverted cases will not be swept into the automatic queue as a matter of system behaviour whatever the legal answer. The routing node is buildable today because it routes on the face of the order and escalates on silence, so this changes which branch is common rather than what is built.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Vacate and Expunge a Juvenile Record (KRS 610.330)
tracks.publicName: Clear a Kentucky juvenile record
tracks.mechanism: On petition, the court vacates the adjudication and expunges all records in the custody of the court and of any other agency, including law enforcement records and public and private elementary and secondary school records. The proceedings are deemed never to have occurred and all index references are deleted. Relief covers status offences and public offences that would be felonies, misdemeanors or violations if committed by an adult, adjudicated under KRS Chapters 630, 635 or 645. There is a separate automatic branch under KRS 610.330(7) where a petition is dismissed or the child is found not delinquent, which requires no action by the child.
exclusions: Proceedings pending or being instituted against the child.
A sex crime as defined in KRS 17.500.
An offence that would classify a person as a violent offender under KRS 439.3401.
Adjudications under KRS Chapter 620 or Chapter 640, which the section does not cover.

waitingPeriods.duration: two years from termination of the court's jurisdiction, or two years from unconditional release from commitment, waivable on a finding of extraordinary circumstances

tracks.legalName: Motion for Expungement of an Emergency Protective Order or Temporary Interpersonal Protective Order Record (KRS 403.745, KRS 456.070)
tracks.publicName: Clear the record of a protective order case that was dismissed
tracks.mechanism: Where a protective-order petition did not result in the issuance of a domestic violence order or a non-temporary interpersonal protective order and the case was dismissed, the court may for good cause shown order expunged all records in the case in the custody of the court and any such records, including law enforcement records, in the custody of any other agency or official. The respondent moves six months after dismissal, provided no order of protection has been issued against them in the preceding six months.
exclusions: Any case in which a domestic violence order or a non-temporary interpersonal protective order was issued.
Any respondent who has been bound by, or had issued against them, an order of protection for the protection of any person in the six months before the request.
Criminal records, which this route does not reach. Those go to the criminal tracks.

tracks.legalName: Segregation of Arrest Records After Acquittal, Dismissal or Withdrawal of Charges (KRS 17.142)
tracks.publicName: Ask agencies to file away the record of an arrest that went nowhere
tracks.mechanism: A law enforcement or other public agency holding arrest records, fingerprints, photographs or other data must, on the written request of the arrestee, segregate those records into a file separate from those of convicted persons where the person was found innocent or all charges relating to the offence were dismissed or withdrawn. The person may instead apply to the court, which shall forthwith issue an order to all law enforcement agencies. Each agency must notify every agency it shared the records with, and the segregated record must show the disposition. Records subject to KRS 431.076 or KRS 431.078 are sealed under those statutes instead.
exclusions: Records subject to KRS 431.076 or KRS 431.078, which KRS 17.142(4) directs be sealed under those statutes instead. In practice this is most acquittals and dismissals, so segregation is a fallback.
