tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge Record of Arrest That Did Not Result in a Conviction (La. C.Cr.P. art. 976)
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Article 976(A) lets a person move to expunge a record of arrest for a felony or misdemeanour that did not result in conviction where the person was not prosecuted and the time limitation has expired, the district attorney declined to prosecute every offence arising out of the arrest including because a pretrial diversion programme was completed, the proceedings were finally disposed of by dismissal, sustaining of a motion to quash or acquittal, or the person was judicially determined to be factually innocent and entitled to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8. Article 976(B) bars expungement of an arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, or a parish or municipal equivalent, where the person was placed in a pretrial diversion programme, until five years have elapsed since the date of arrest. Article 975 bars filing by a person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour. Relief is effectively mandatory: under Article 980 the court grants where no timely objection is filed and the mover is legally entitled.
exclusions: A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file the motion (Art. 975). This is a status bar that lifts when custody status changes, not a permanent eligibility bar.

An arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated under R.S. 14:98, or a parish or municipal ordinance equivalent, where the person was placed in a pretrial diversion programme, until five years have elapsed from the date of arrest (Art. 976(B)).
A conviction arising out of the arrest. Any charge on the arrest that resulted in a misdemeanour or felony conviction is outside this Article and belongs to Article 977 or Article 978.

waitingPeriods.condition: Arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, or a parish or municipal ordinance equivalent, where the person entered a pretrial diversion programme
waitingPeriods.duration: Five years from the date of arrest for that offence (Art. 976(B)). The Article 989 form carries a dedicated check-box for it.
None. There is no waiting period; where prosecution was never instituted the ground is the expiry of the time limitation for prosecution itself.

tracks.venue: The court with trial jurisdiction over the offence in the parish of arrest, under Article 972.1: district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts.

destination.name: Clerk of court for the parish of arrest
destination.detail: File the Article 989 motion with the proposed Article 991 and Article 992 orders. The clerk collects the Article 983 fees at filing unless a returned Article 988 fee exemption is appended, and thereafter serves the district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting agency under Article 979.

components.conditionDescription: Generated wherever the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) exemption, which on this track is common.
Used only where the arrest carries more charges or counts than the Article 989 motion's own fields hold.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days. Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Bill of information or indictment for each charge. Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Minute entry showing the final disposition. Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "How did each charge on this arrest end — never prosecuted and the time limit ran out, the district attorney refused the charges, you completed a pretrial diversion programme, the case was dismissed, a motion to quash was sustained, you were acquitted, or a court found you factually innocent?" against Minute entry showing the final disposition, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain District attorney certification letter verifying that the charges were refused. The Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing for a letter verifying that the charges arising out of this arrest were refused. The packet includes a cover request naming exactly which certifications your chosen eligibility basis needs.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the eligibility basis is that the district attorney declined to prosecute.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain District attorney certification letter verifying no participation in a pretrial diversion programme. Ask the district attorney's office in writing for a letter verifying that you did not participate in a pretrial diversion programme on this arrest. The Article 989 attachment checklist lists it, and the Article 988 fee exemption turns on the same fact.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the eligibility or fee-exemption basis depends on the absence of pretrial diversion.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Court order of factual innocence and entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8. Ask the clerk of the court that made the determination for a certified copy.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The court that made the determination
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only where the eligibility ground is factual innocence under Art. 976(A)(4).

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency. This is the agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form, and only they can execute it. If you can obtain one from each named agency and attach them to the motion, the Article 991 Order provides that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Optional. Pursue it only where the agencies will execute one; the track does not depend on it.

participantActionRequired.description: Every finding, ruling, date, place and signature on the Article 991 Order — Article 991 Order — the ordering paragraphs, the date and place line and the judge's signature line.

Every granting or denying paragraph, finding, date, place and signature on the Article 992 Order of Expungement — Article 992 Order of Expungement — the decretal paragraphs, the date and place line and the judge's signature line.
Race and gender — Article 989 Motion, Part I Defendant Information.
The participant's signature and the date of signing — Article 989 Motion, unrepresented-mover signature block on the final page.
Every certification box and the district attorney's signature on the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption — Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, the certification section and signature block.
The whole of the Article 990 Affidavit of Response — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The clerk's service of the motion and of the order and judgment — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.

Article 983(A) caps the total cost of obtaining a court order of expungement at five hundred fifty dollars. The clerk collects at the time of filing and Article 983 makes the fees non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Article 983(F) waives all fees where a district attorney certification verifies no felony convictions and no pending felony charge under a bill of information or indictment, together with one of the listed non-conviction grounds — acquittal of all charges after trial including lesser and included offences, no prosecution within the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, dismissal or refusal before the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, factual innocence with entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8, or a juvenile who completed a juvenile drug court programme and is exempt under Article 983(G). The exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after.

Article 983(F), claimed through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption. The form goes to the district attorney before filing and comes back within fifteen days. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge a Record of Arrest and Conviction of a Misdemeanor Offense (La. C.Cr.P. art. 977)
tracks.publicName: Clear a misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: Article 977(A) lets a person move to expunge a record of arrest and conviction of a misdemeanour on either of two grounds. Under (A)(1) the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 894(B), which is the separate Article 987 mechanism. Under (A)(2) more than five years have elapsed since the person completed any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, the person has not been convicted of any felony offence during that five-year period and has no felony charge pending; the motion must include a certification obtained from the district attorney verifying, to his knowledge, no felony convictions during the five-year period and no pending felony charges under a bill of information or indictment. Article 977(C) bars expungement where the misdemeanour conviction arose from circumstances involving or resulting from an arrest for a sex offence as defined in R.S. 15:541 — expressly preserving interim expungement under Article 985.1 — and where the conviction was for domestic abuse battery or for stalking under R.S. 14:40.2. rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles.
rules.feeWaiver: Article 983(F) through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, but its grounds are non-conviction grounds, so it is rarely available on a conviction track. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.

The conviction was for domestic abuse battery or for stalking.
The district attorney declines to give the Article 977(A)(2) certification.

Self-help limits: any sex offense connection, which is a hard stop into Track E instead; domestic abuse battery or stalking; DA declines to certify; unclear sentence completion date.
packetInstructions: Where Art. 894(B) has not been done and appears available, the participant must obtain the Art. 987 set-aside and dismissal first, and return to this track with the order of dismissal. Track J is not duplicated inside Track B.

DA certification letters and returned Art. 988 forms are required before filing. They are not generation blockers: the packet is produced, and the certifications are named, requested and scheduled by the instructions.

tracks.legalName: Motion for Expungement for Misdemeanor Conviction for a First Offense Possession of Marijuana (La. C.Cr.P. arts. 977(D), 998)
tracks.publicName: Clear a first-offense misdemeanor marijuana possession conviction
tracks.mechanism: Article 977(D) provides that notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, a person may file a motion to expunge his record of arrest and conviction of a misdemeanour conviction for a first offence possession of marijuana, tetrahydrocannabinol or chemical derivatives thereof after ninety days from the date of conviction. It replaces both the Article 894(B) set-aside requirement and the five-year wait that Article 977(A) would otherwise impose. Article 986 makes Article 998 the form to be used, and Article 998 is a dedicated motion form for this category, separate from Article 989. Article 977(D) carries no sunset of its own and remains in the current official text with the Article 977 source notes running through Acts 2023, No. 342.
exclusions: A conviction that is not a first offence for possession of marijuana, tetrahydrocannabinol or chemical derivatives thereof. A second or later possession offence falls back to Article 977(A).
A felony marijuana conviction, which is Article 978 territory and subject to the Article 978(B)(3) controlled dangerous substance exclusions and their exceptions.
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).

rules.filing: File the Article 998 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of conviction, at any time after ninety days from the date of conviction. Article 986 makes Article 998 the form to be used for this category; the Article 989 form is not used here.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: The ordinary Article 983(A) cap of five hundred fifty dollars now applies. The three-hundred-dollar cap formerly in Article 983(M) — fifty dollars each to the Bureau, the sheriff and the district attorney and one hundred fifty to the clerk — was null, void and without effect and terminated on 1 August 2026 under Article 983(M)(5), and is now historical only. The clerk collects at filing and the fees are non-refundable even if the motion is denied.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge Record of Arrest and Conviction of a Felony Offense (La. C.Cr.P. art. 978)
tracks.publicName: Clear a felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: Article 978(A) lets a person move to expunge a record of arrest and conviction of a felony where the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 893(E); or where more than ten years have elapsed since the person completed any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, the person has not been convicted of any other criminal offence during that ten-year period and has no criminal charge pending, with a district attorney certification; or where the person is entitled to a first offender pardon for the offence, provided it is not a crime of violence or a sex offence. Article 978(B) bars expungement, and bars filing, where the person was convicted of the commission or attempted commission of a crime of violence under R.S. 14:2(B) unless Paragraph E applies; a sex offence or a criminal offence against a victim who is a minor under R.S. 15:541, with a narrow carnal-knowledge exception; a violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law, except five listed categories that may be expunged; or domestic abuse battery. Article 978(E) permits the court, after a contradictory hearing, to order expungement for aggravated battery, second degree battery, aggravated criminal damage to property, simple robbery, purse snatching, or illegal use of weapons or dangerous instrumentalities on the ten-year clean-period conditions. Read against the current official text, whose source notes now run through Acts 2024, No. 580.
exclusions: A crime of violence as defined by or enumerated in R.S. 14:2(B), unless the offence is one of the six named in Article 978(E) and the court grants relief after a contradictory hearing (Art. 978(B)(1)).

Notwithstanding any provision of Article 893, a sex offence or a criminal offence against a victim who is a minor as each is defined by R.S. 15:541, or any offence occurring before 18 June 1992 that would be so defined had it occurred on or after that date (Art. 978(B)(2)(a)).

A violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law (Art. 978(B)(3)), except any of the following, which may be expunged: possession of a controlled dangerous substance under R.S. 40:966(C), 967(C), 968(C), 969(C) or 970(C); possession with intent to distribute; a violation punishable by a term of imprisonment of not more than five years; a violation that may be expunged under Article 893(E); and a violation for which the person is entitled to a first offender pardon under La. Const. art. IV, § 5(E)(1).
A conviction for domestic abuse battery (Art. 978(B)(4)).
A first offender pardon route is unavailable where the offence is a crime of violence or a sex offence (Art. 978(A)(3)).
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).

waitingPeriods.condition: Article 978(A)(1) — the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 893(E)
waitingPeriods.duration: None. The set-aside and dismissal is the qualifying event, and it is obtained on the separate Article 987 track.

More than ten years from completion of any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, with no conviction of ANY OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENCE during that ten-year period and no criminal charge pending. This is not the misdemeanour test with a larger number: the misdemeanour clean period bars felony convictions only, and this one bars any criminal offence.

waitingPeriods.condition: Article 978(A)(3) — the first offender pardon route
waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond entitlement to the pardon itself. Under R.S. 15:572 a first offender never previously convicted of a felony is automatically pardoned on completion of sentence without a Board of Pardons recommendation or gubernatorial action, but no pardon issues unless the court costs for the conviction are paid.

waitingPeriods.condition: Article 978(E) — the violent-offence lane for aggravated battery, second degree battery, aggravated criminal damage to property, simple robbery, purse snatching, or illegal use of weapons or dangerous instrumentalities
waitingPeriods.duration: More than ten years since completion of sentence, deferred adjudication, probation or parole, with no criminal conviction during that period and no pending charge, and only after a contradictory hearing at which the court may grant relief in its discretion.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days. Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain District attorney certification verifying no conviction of any other criminal offence during the ten-year period and no pending criminal charge. Article 978(A)(2) requires it and the Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing; the packet includes a cover request naming the exact certification and the ten-year window. LegalEase cannot produce it, and its absence is a filing requirement rather than a generation blocker.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish of conviction
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(2) ten-year route and on the Article 978(E) lane.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution. Ask the clerk for a certified copy. Where no such order exists and Article 893 relief appears available, obtain it first on the separate Article 987 track and then return here.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the order
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Has a court already signed an order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution under Article 893(E)?" against Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the first offender pardon. Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Under R.S. 15:572 the pardon is automatic for a first offender on completion of sentence, but it does not issue while court costs for the conviction remain unpaid. If costs are outstanding, pay them and then request the pardon; this is the most common and most fixable obstacle on this route.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana Board of Pardons and Committee on Parole, or the Department of Public Safety and Corrections
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(3) first offender pardon route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Bill of information or indictment for each charge. Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Minute entry showing the final disposition. Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles under Article 984. Article 984 requires a person convicted of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to supplement the motion with a certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles proving compliance with that Article, and it is attached to the motion. A further fifty-dollar court cost is assessed and paid to the Office of Motor Vehicles for storage and retrieval.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only to a conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Optional, and not available on the Article 978(E) lane, where a contradictory hearing is required by the Article itself.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte. On the Article 978(E) lane a contradictory hearing is required by the Article itself, so the ex parte route is not available there and the objection window is not the operative constraint.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles. On the first offender pardon route the participant must also have paid the underlying court costs of the conviction, which is a precondition of the pardon rather than an expungement fee.
rules.feeWaiver: Article 983(F) through the Article 988 form in principle, but Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony. On a felony conviction track the exemption will almost never be available, and the packet says so rather than implying a waiver that will be refused.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.

participantFilingRequirements.name: District attorney certification verifying no conviction of any other criminal offence during the ten-year period and no pending criminal charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(2) ten-year route and on the Article 978(E) lane.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Article 978(A)(2) requires it and the Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing; the packet includes a cover request naming the exact certification and the ten-year window. LegalEase cannot produce it, and its absence is a filing requirement rather than a generation blocker.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the order
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy. Where no such order exists and Article 893 relief appears available, obtain it first on the separate Article 987 track and then return here.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the first offender pardon
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Louisiana Board of Pardons and Committee on Parole, or the Department of Public Safety and Corrections
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(3) first offender pardon route.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Under R.S. 15:572 the pardon is automatic for a first offender on completion of sentence, but it does not issue while court costs for the conviction remain unpaid. If costs are outstanding, pay them and then request the pardon; this is the most common and most fixable obstacle on this route.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Bill of information or indictment for each charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Minute entry showing the final disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles under Article 984
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only to a conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Article 984 requires a person convicted of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to supplement the motion with a certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles proving compliance with that Article, and it is attached to the motion. A further fifty-dollar court cost is assessed and paid to the Office of Motor Vehicles for storage and retrieval.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the order waiving the sex offender registration and notification requirements under R.S. 15:542(F)
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that issued the waiver
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only to the narrow Article 978(B)(2)(b) carnal-knowledge exception.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Article 978(B)(2)(b) makes such an order sufficient to meet the mover's burden of showing that a pre-15-August-2001 carnal knowledge conviction would today be misdemeanour carnal knowledge of a juvenile.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Optional, and not available on the Article 978(E) lane, where a contradictory hearing is required by the Article itself.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.

manualCompletionItems.why: The final order is the court's judgment. LegalEase supplies the caption and the participant's identifying and charge information only.

tracks.legalName: Interim Motion to Expunge a Felony Arrest from Criminal History (La. C.Cr.P. art. 985.1)
tracks.publicName: Clear a felony arrest that ended in a misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: Article 985.1(A) permits an interim motion to expunge a felony arrest from the criminal history of a person who was convicted of a misdemeanour offence arising out of that original felony arrest; only the original felony arrest is expunged. Article 985.1(B) makes the interim motion separate and distinct from expungement of a final conviction under Articles 976, 977 and 978. Article 985.1(C) applies the Article 979 et seq. procedures and fees except as provided in (D), and Article 985.1(D) provides that the motion is not subject to the time limitations of Article 977(A)(2) or 978(A)(2) and permits more than one interim expungement. Article 977(C)(1) expressly preserves interim expungement even where the misdemeanour conviction itself is barred by the sex-offence exclusion. Article 986 makes Article 994 the motion form and Article 995 the order form. Confirmed against the current official text; Article 985.1 has not been amended since Acts 2014, No. 145.
exclusions: The misdemeanour conviction itself is not expunged by this track. Only the original felony arrest entry is removed from the criminal history; the misdemeanour conviction remains on the record unless it is separately cleared under Article 977.
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).
There is no case-count limitation. Article 985.1(D) expressly permits more than one interim expungement.

rules.filing: File the Article 994 Motion for Interim Expungement with the proposed Article 995 Order of Expungement of Interim Arrest Record with the clerk of court. Article 985.1(C) applies the procedures of Article 979 et seq. Article 986 makes Articles 994 and 995 the forms to be used.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 994 Motion in the block for an unrepresented mover. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: Article 985.1(C) applies the ordinary Article 983 fee provisions, so the five-hundred-fifty-dollar cap applies, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
rules.feeWaiver: Article 983(F) through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption where its grounds are met.

tracks.legalName: Expungement by Redaction of Records with References to Multiple Individuals (La. C.Cr.P. art. 985)
tracks.publicName: Remove your name from a record you share with someone else
tracks.mechanism: Article 985(A) provides that if a record includes the name of more than one individual and one or more of them is entitled to an expungement of an arrest or conviction under Title XXXIV, any individual so entitled may petition the court to have records related to that individual's arrest or conviction expunged by redaction. Article 985(B) provides that if the court grants expungement by redaction, the name of the individual and all other identifying information regarding that individual shall be redacted from all records regarding the arrest and conviction, and the redacted records remain available for public access. Article 985(C) relieves the clerk of liability where the order does not specifically identify all locations of the records to be expunged or specify the information to be redacted. Article 972(3) defines the term. The relief runs on the Article 989 motion and the Article 992 order, whose text contains the dedicated redaction paragraph. Confirmed against the current official text; Article 985 has not been amended since Acts 2014, No. 145.
exclusions: A person who is not independently entitled to an expungement of the arrest or conviction under Title XXXIV. Article 985 is a form of relief for someone already entitled under Article 976, 977 or 978; it is not an independent eligibility ground.
A record that names only the petitioner. Where no other individual appears in the record there is nothing to redact and the ordinary expungement track applies instead.
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).

waitingPeriods.duration: None of its own. The waiting period is whichever of Articles 976, 977 or 978 gives the petitioner the underlying entitlement to expungement.

rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
rules.feeWaiver: Article 983(F) through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption where the underlying basis meets its grounds.

tracks.legalName: Expedited Expungement of Arrest Records for Certain Individuals (La. C.Cr.P. arts. 999, 999.1)
tracks.publicName: Free expedited clearing of an arrest from when you were seventeen
tracks.mechanism: Article 999(A) provides that a person shall be entitled to the expedited expungement of his arrest, at no cost to him, if the person meets all of the following: (1) the person is seventeen years of age when arrested or charged with any criminal offence under Title 14 or Title 40 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes of 1950; (2) the district attorney, for any reason, declined to prosecute all offences arising out of that arrest, including because the person successfully completed a pretrial diversion programme; and (3) prosecution was instituted and such proceedings have been finally disposed of by dismissal, sustaining of a motion to quash, or acquittal. Article 999(B) provides that the Article does not apply to any misdemeanour or felony conviction arising from the incident of arrest. Article 999(C) provides that the expedited expungement shall be served under Article 982. Article 972(1) defines expedited expungement as an order of expungement that a judge may sign pursuant to Article 999 WITHOUT THE INDIVIDUAL FILING A MOTION TO EXPUNGE WITH THE CLERK OF COURT. Article 999.1 supplies the order form to be used, which recites the three Article 999(A) conditions, provides the defendant-information fields and a six-entry service list, and carries the judge's signature line. Both Articles were added, and Articles 972 and 983(G) amended, by Acts 2024, No. 270, effective 1 August 2024.
exclusions: Any misdemeanour or felony conviction arising from the incident of arrest (Art. 999(B)).

A person who was not seventeen years of age when arrested or charged. The age element is objective and narrow: it is a legacy of Louisiana's raise-the-age transition and is not a general youthful-offender provision.
An arrest or charge for an offence outside Title 14 or Title 40 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes of 1950.

Applied as written, Article 999(A) requires all three conditions together, which means the route reaches only a person who was seventeen at arrest AND whose offences the district attorney declined to prosecute AND whose instituted prosecution was finally disposed of by dismissal, quashal or acquittal. This memo applies the statute as written because that is the narrower reading; the internal contradiction between (2) and (3) is preserved as an open question rather than resolved by construction.

releaseBlockers.question: Article 999(A) says the person must meet 'all of the following' and then lists (2) a declination to prosecute all offences arising out of the arrest and (3) an instituted prosecution finally disposed of by dismissal, quashal or acquittal. Read literally the two are mutually exclusive, because a declination means no prosecution was instituted, and almost nobody could qualify. The Acts 2024, No. 270 résumé digest repeats 'all of the following', and the Article 999.1 order form recites the same three conditions under the heading 'wherein all of the following applies', so both the statute and the prescribed order carry the cumulative formulation. Whether (2) and (3) are cumulative as written or alternative as they must sensibly be is unresolved, and it materially decides who the eligibility engine returns.

tracks.legalName: Automated Expungement of Qualifying Records (La. C.Cr.P. art. 985.2)
tracks.publicName: Louisiana's automated expungement process
tracks.mechanism: Article 985.2(A) directs the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information to identify within its criminal repository database all records with a Case Management Information System number and final dispositions for individuals eligible for expungement under Articles 976, 977 and 978. Article 985.2(B) provides that beginning 1 January 2025 a defendant may submit a request through the Bureau for expungement through the automated process, the request containing the defendant's name, date of birth, last four digits of the Social Security number, arrest date and case number, and requires the Bureau to expunge any eligible records within thirty days of receipt and send them to the Louisiana Supreme Court Case Management Information System. Paragraphs (C) and (D) govern clerk verification and notice to the district attorney, sheriff and arresting agency. Article 985.2(G) provides that the Article shall be subject to the appropriate funding necessary for implementation and provided for in the executive budget for Fiscal Year 2025-2026. The current official text at legis.la.gov carries the operative note 'Article 985.2 eff. upon appropriation of monies by the Legislature. See Acts 2023, No. 454.' Section 4 of Acts 2023, No. 454 conditions the effectiveness of its substantive Sections on an Act or Acts originating in the 2023 Regular Session containing specific appropriations of monies for the office of state police, the Louisiana Supreme Court and the Louisiana Clerks' Remote Access Authority for the implementation of the Act. The route reaches only records already eligible under Articles 976, 977 and 978 and expands eligibility for no one.
exclusions: The Article is not established as effective. The current official text of the Code carries the note that Article 985.2 is effective upon appropriation of monies by the Legislature, citing Acts 2023, No. 454, and that note is still present on the Legislature's own current publication of the Article as of 3 August 2026.

The route does not expand eligibility. It reaches only records already eligible for expungement under Articles 976, 977 and 978, so a person not already eligible under those Articles gains nothing from it.
Records predating the automation window described in the Article are outside it.
The enacting legislation provided that no person shall have a cause of action resulting from the omission of their records from automated expungement.

waitingPeriods.duration: None of its own. Whatever waiting period Article 976, 977 or 978 imposes on the underlying record still governs, because the Article reaches only records already eligible under those Articles.

tracks.legalName: Immediate Expungement; Judicial Discretion (La. C.Cr.P. art. 985.3)
tracks.publicName: Immediate clearing by the court after you finish probation or a program
tracks.mechanism: Article 985.3(A) provides that the court MAY ORDER the immediate expungement of the record of the arrest and conviction of the violation that necessitated participation in the probation or programme, by a person who is otherwise eligible for an expungement, upon the successful completion of a court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing programme. Article 985.3(B) provides that ONLY THE FORM PROVIDED IN ARTICLE 992 shall be used to expunge the record of such a person. Article 985.3(C) provides that the immediate expungement shall be served pursuant to Article 982 and shall include the court record with the signed order together with the bill of information, the sentencing minutes, and any documents or records relevant to the arrest incident and plea agreements, if available. The Article was enacted by Acts 2024, No. 560 (2024 H.B. 416), whose digest describes it as providing for a court-ordered automatic expungement in certain cases. The full text was obtained and read for this normalization; the review had identified the Article but not read it.
exclusions: A person who is not otherwise eligible for an expungement. Article 985.3(A) reaches only a person 'who is otherwise eligible for an expungement', so the underlying eligibility rules of Articles 976, 977 and 978, including every Article 977(C) and Article 978(B) exclusion, continue to govern. The Article shortens the path, not the eligibility test.
A record other than the record of the arrest and conviction of the violation that necessitated participation in the probation or programme. Other cases are outside it.
A person who did not successfully complete the court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing programme.
The relief is discretionary. Article 985.3(A) says the court 'may order', so no participant is entitled to it.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. The triggering event is the successful completion of the court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing programme, and the expungement is immediate on the court's order. Whether it displaces the Article 977(A)(2) five-year and Article 978(A)(2) ten-year waiting periods for an otherwise-eligible person is the open question below; the Article does not say so expressly, unlike Article 985.1(D), which disapplies them in terms.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether a defendant may move for Article 985.3 relief, and if so by what vehicle. Article 985.3(A) says the court 'may order' the immediate expungement and prescribes no motion, application or request; Article 985.3(B) names only the Article 992 order form; Article 986's mandatory-form list assigns no motion form to the Article; and the Acts 2024, No. 560 digest describes it as a court-ordered automatic expungement. Whether in practice the court acts on its own at the completion or discharge proceeding, or whether the defendant presents an ordinary Article 989 motion and asks the court to exercise Article 985.3 discretion, is not answered by any official source. If the latter, the participant-facing packet is the Article 989 and 992 pair already modelled on the Article 977 and 978 tracks, and this track would become a routing node into them rather than an independent packet.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether Article 985.3 displaces the Article 977(A)(2) five-year and Article 978(A)(2) ten-year waiting periods for a person who is otherwise eligible and has successfully completed a court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing programme. The word 'immediate' and the completion trigger suggest it does, but unlike Article 985.1(D) — which disapplies those time limitations in terms — Article 985.3 says nothing about them, and 'otherwise eligible for an expungement' can be read either as eligible but for the waiting period or as eligible including the waiting period. The difference decides who the eligibility engine returns.

Open question blocks release (output_strategy): Whether a defendant may move for Article 985.3 relief, and if so by what vehicle. Article 985.3(A) says the court 'may order' the immediate expungement and prescribes no motion, application or request; Article 985.3(B) names only the Article 992 order form; Article 986's mandatory-form list assigns no motion form to the Article; and the Acts 2024, No. 560 digest describes it as a court-ordered automatic expungement. Whether in practice the court acts on its own at the completion or discharge proceeding, or whether the defendant presents an ordinary Article 989 motion and asks the court to exercise Article 985.3 discretion, is not answered by any official source. If the latter, the participant-facing packet is the Article 989 and 992 pair already modelled on the Article 977 and 978 tracks, and this track would become a routing node into them rather than an independent packet.

Open question blocks release (waiting_period): Whether Article 985.3 displaces the Article 977(A)(2) five-year and Article 978(A)(2) ten-year waiting periods for a person who is otherwise eligible and has successfully completed a court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing programme. The word 'immediate' and the completion trigger suggest it does, but unlike Article 985.1(D) — which disapplies those time limitations in terms — Article 985.3 says nothing about them, and 'otherwise eligible for an expungement' can be read either as eligible but for the waiting period or as eligible including the waiting period. The difference decides who the eligibility engine returns.

Open question blocks release (filing_process): Whether the Article 983 fee schedule applies to an expungement ordered under Article 985.3, given that the Article prescribes no fee and no exemption and that Article 983 is drafted around obtaining a court order on a motion.
One or more official sources have no recorded SHA-256, so staleness cannot be detected.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Set Aside Conviction and Dismiss Prosecution; Rule to Show Cause; Order of Dismissal (La. C.Cr.P. art. 987)
tracks.publicName: Set aside a conviction and dismiss the prosecution after a deferred sentence
tracks.mechanism: Article 987 supplies the forms to be used for a motion to set aside a conviction and dismiss the prosecution, the rule to show cause, and the order of dismissal. It is not an expungement. It is the predicate filing that converts a completed deferred sentence into a set-aside conviction and a dismissed prosecution under Article 894(B) for a misdemeanour or Article 893(E) for a felony, which in turn unlocks Article 977(A)(1) or Article 978(A)(1). As pleaded on the statutory form, eligibility is that the period of the deferred sentence has run and the petitioner has successfully completed the terms of probation. The instrument is in three parts: the Motion; a Rule to Show Cause ordering the district attorney to show cause why the motion should not be granted; and the Order of Dismissal. The motion's own prayer asks for relief after a contradictory hearing with the district attorney's office. Service is on the district attorney and on the attorney for the defendant or the defendant. The form carries parallel signature blocks for counsel and for an unrepresented mover, so it is drafted for pro se use. Source note Acts 2014, No. 145.
exclusions: A conviction that was not the subject of a deferred sentence under Article 893 or Article 894. Where no deferred sentence was imposed there is nothing to set aside, and the participant goes directly to the Article 977 or Article 978 waiting-period route instead.
A case where the period of the deferred sentence has not yet run.
A case where the terms of probation were not successfully completed.

researchTwoFieldResolution.finding: The 'Conviction offense wording' and 'Conviction statute' lines are not held facts: the builder's canonical and boundary FACTS objects omit both, the field map assigns both to REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, and primaryBody always prints dotted lines. They are participant-supplied case facts, collected before filing, written into the statutory instrument as neutral case fields when actually supplied, and truthfully tracked as missing when not. No value is guessed and no absent value is reported as written.
researchTwoFieldResolution.largerDefect: The builder's primaryBody does not reproduce the Article 987 motion, rule to show cause and order: it substitutes a questionnaire, omits the statutory identifying and service elements (DOCKET NUMBER, CHARGE, DATE OF ARREST, ARRESTING AGENCY, CITY/PARISH OF ARREST; pro-se address, city/state/ZIP and telephone; PLEASE SERVE recipients), paraphrases the motion and replaces the order's preprinted operative wording with blank findings and decretal lines, and prints machine metadata inside the filed text. Article 986 restricts filing to the prescribed forms; Article 987 supplies the text; the LA-STATUTORY-FORMS determination (COMPOSE_FROM_AUTHORITY) already authorises composition from the codified article. One bounded repair per the contract, not a two-field patch.
researchTwoFieldResolution.sourceRequirement: The current codified text of La. C.Cr.P. arts. 986 and 987 is not held in any custody (the Master Library's Louisiana review describes the three-part instrument but does not quote it; 05_SOURCE_GATED holds arts. 990, 993, 995, 998 and 999.1 only), and legis.la.gov is blocked from the build container. The repair cannot reproduce the statutory text faithfully until the official article text is acquired and bound.

tracks.publicName: Sealing your record through Probation
tracks.mechanism: On a form furnished by the Commissioner of Probation and signed under the penalties of perjury, the Commissioner shall seal a record once the statutory period has run. Relief is mandatory and ministerial: no judge is involved, the Commissioner has no discretion to refuse, and no reasons are given. The 2018 Criminal Justice Reform Act cut the waits from five and ten years to three and seven.
exclusions: Convictions under G.L. c. 140, §§ 121 to 131H (firearms), except as part of a delinquency record.
Convictions under G.L. c. 268 or c. 268A, except resisting arrest, which may be sealed.
A person who has at any time been classified as a level 2 or level 3 sex offender under G.L. c. 6, § 178K may not seal sex offences at all.

A guilty finding in Massachusetts within the applicable lookback, or a conviction or imprisonment in another state, a United States possession or a federal court in that window, excepting motor vehicle offences punishable by a fine of not more than $50.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal Criminal Records for Nolle Prosequi or Dismissal under G.L. c. 276, § 100C ¶2
tracks.publicName: Asking a judge to seal a dismissed case
tracks.mechanism: A nolle prosequi entered by the prosecutor, or a dismissal entered by the court, may be sealed on petition where the court finds that substantial justice would best be served, which Pon construes as good cause against six factors. There is no waiting period; passage of time is instead one of the Pon factors. Form TC0057 is standardised across the Boston Municipal, District, Juvenile and Superior Court departments.
exclusions: None by offence. This route is not offence-limited, which makes it the fallback for records the administrative sealing route excludes.
An open case is not sealable; for a CWOF the probationary term must be complete and the case actually dismissed.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Passage of time is a Pon factor rather than a threshold, so a recent case is harder but not ineligible.

tracks.venue: Statewide form, court-specific filing. District Court cases are filed at the clerk's office where the case started. Boston Municipal Court cases are filed in the BMC division where the person lives, or, if they no longer live in BMC territory, the BMC division where the most recent eligible record is from. That residence-based venue rule is unique in the state.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge under G.L. c. 276, §§ 100F, 100G and 100H
tracks.publicName: Expunging a record from before you turned 21
tracks.mechanism: Time-based expungement requires all offences to have occurred before the person's 21st birthday, a record of not more than two convictions or two non-conviction records, and three years for a misdemeanour-only record or seven where any felony is involved. The architecture is genuinely staged: the Commissioner of Probation certifies eligibility under §§ 100I and 100J, and only then does the matter reach a judge with the district attorney on notice.
exclusions: The § 100J list: offences resulting in death or serious bodily injury; offences committed with intent to cause death or serious bodily injury; offences involving a dangerous weapon; offences against an elderly or disabled person; sex offences, child sex offences and sexually violent offences; operating under the influence under c. 90 § 24; firearms offences under c. 140 §§ 121 to 131Q; violations of abuse prevention and harassment prevention orders; and domestic assault and battery under c. 265 § 13M.
Any offence occurring on or after the person's 21st birthday. All offences must have occurred before it.
More than two records. Multiple offences arising from the same incident count as one.

Any other Massachusetts criminal or juvenile appearance or disposition, and any out-of-state, United States possession or federal appearance or disposition, excepting minor motor vehicle offences and the records being expunged.
Being the subject of an active criminal investigation.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement under G.L. c. 276, § 100K
tracks.publicName: Expunging a record created by mistake, fraud, or identity theft
tracks.mechanism: Section 100K reaches a record created by false identification or identity theft, an offence that is no longer a crime, demonstrable errors by law enforcement, by civilian or expert witnesses, or by court employees, or demonstrable fraud on the court. It operates notwithstanding §§ 100I and 100J, so the under-21 rule, the two-record cap and the § 100J exclusion list do not apply. The court must find on clear and convincing evidence that the record was created on one of the grounds, then exercises discretion on the best interests of justice.
exclusions: None. Section 100K operates notwithstanding §§ 100I and 100J, so the under-21 rule, the two-record cap and the § 100J exclusion list do not apply. This is the most important structural fact about the track and the internal reference does not state it.

waitingPeriods.condition: A record created on one of the eight statutory grounds

tracks.legalName: Consolidated Multi-Record Sealing Petition in the Boston Municipal Court Department
tracks.publicName: Sealing several dismissed cases at once in Boston
tracks.mechanism: The Boston Municipal Court Department permits a single consolidated petition to seal three or more criminal records from two or more BMC divisions, under a Standing Order revised after Pon to conform to the new legal standard. It is a local implementation of the ordinary § 100C judicial-sealing remedy, not a separate statewide remedy. Below the threshold, the ordinary route applies with one form per case.
authority: Boston Municipal Court Department Amended Standing Order No. 1-09
exclusions: Records outside the Boston Municipal Court Department. This does not reach District Court, Juvenile Court or Superior Court records.
Fewer than three criminal records, or records from fewer than two BMC divisions. Below that threshold the ordinary judicial sealing route applies with one form per case.

Records that ended in a finding of no probable cause or a not-guilty finding are outside this consolidated procedure: the May 10, 2024 amended Standing Order 1-09 limits it to dismissal and nolle prosequi records under the second paragraph of G.L. c. 276, § 100C. Those other dispositions arise under a different paragraph of § 100C and their separate procedural and case-law treatment is not decided here; they are not called ineligible for every form of relief (recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research).

waitingPeriods.condition: Dismissal, nolle prosequi, no probable cause or not guilty
waitingPeriods.duration: None, the same as the ordinary judicial sealing route.

rules.notice: The petitioner sends a copy of the petition to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office at least 30 days before the final hearing unless that office waives the full notice period, and keeps proof of what was sent and when; the court's own notice to the Commonwealth does not remove that obligation. researchConsolidationScope.statement: The May 10, 2024 amended Standing Order 1-09 limits this consolidation procedure to at least three dismissal or nolle-prosequi criminal records from at least two BMC divisions under § 100C's second paragraph; the Judiciary guide recommends rather than universally requires criminal records or certified dockets. The guide's stop when any hearing is set is a product boundary and is retained; supporting an ordinary uncontested hearing is a separate decision from correctly explaining the published process.

researchFormIdentity.statement: The Standing Order authorizes one petition and says a form is available, but an exact current dedicated consolidated form was not retrieved by the research. Neither unsupported universal assertion is perpetuated: that no such court form exists, or that a TC0057 must accompany every case. The accepted instrument, and whether any per-case forms are required for the selected court, remain to be confirmed with the issuing court; the existing release blocker on form identity stays.

researchParticipantText.text:
Scope. Use this consolidated route for at least three criminal records ending in dismissal or nolle prosequi across at least two BMC divisions. Other dispositions require their own treatment. Confirm the proper filing division and list each applicable docket.

Fee and notice. There is no filing fee to request sealing. Send a copy of this petition to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office at least 30 days before the final hearing unless that office waives the full notice period. Keep proof of what you sent and when. Court notice to the Commonwealth does not eliminate your separate obligation. Follow the hearing notice; a separate preliminary hearing is not always held.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records under Md. Code, Criminal Procedure § 10-105
tracks.publicName: Expungement of a case that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Police, court and other State or local records may be expunged on petition for the § 10-105(a) favorable dispositions. Absent a timely State's Attorney objection § 10-105(d)(2) directs the court to pass the order; Maryland appellate law holds a court has no discretion to deny where statutory entitlement is shown. As amended by the Expungement Reform Act of 2025, effective October 1, 2025.
exclusions: A PBJ entered on a charge under Transportation § 21-902(c), (d), (h) or (i), Criminal Law Title 2 Subtitle 5, or Criminal Law § 3-211, is not eligible at all under § 10-105(a)(3).

The § 10-105(a-1) carve-out for a pre-October 1, 2020 sodomy conviction or a pre-October 1, 2023 § 3-322 violation committed without consent, with a minor under 16, with a person the individual could not marry under Family Law § 2-202, or with a mentally incapacitated, physically helpless or substantially cognitively impaired individual.
Non-incarcerable vehicle-law and traffic violations, per the form's own affirmation.
The unit rule under § 10-107(b)(1), subject to the minor-traffic and cannabis-possession carve-outs in § 10-107(a).
Ineligible while a defendant in a pending criminal proceeding, § 10-105(e)(4)(iii).

For a PBJ, a conviction within 3 years of the PBJ other than a minor traffic violation or an act no longer a crime, § 10-105(e)(4)(i); extended to 15 years for a § 21-902(a) or (b) PBJ under § 10-105(e)(4)(ii).

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Conviction under Md. Code, Criminal Procedure § 10-110
tracks.publicName: Expungement of an eligible conviction
tracks.mechanism: Convictions on the § 10-110(a) enumerated list may be expunged after the applicable period from completion of the sentence. Absent objection § 10-110(e)(3) makes the order mandatory. On a timely objection by the State's Attorney or a victim, § 10-110(f)(2) requires a hearing and five findings on the record. SB 432 (2025) overrode In re Expungement Petition of Abhishek I., so a probation violation no longer automatically disqualifies.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement After a Full and Unconditional Pardon
tracks.publicName: Expungement after a pardon from the Governor
tracks.mechanism: Where the person is convicted of only one criminal act, that act is not a crime of violence as defined in Criminal Law § 14-101(a), and the Governor grants a full and unconditional pardon, the record may be expunged. The petition may not be filed later than 10 years after the Governor signed the pardon.
exclusions: Crimes of violence as defined in Criminal Law § 14-101(a).
Persons convicted of more than one criminal act.
Petitions filed more than 10 years after the Governor signed the pardon.

waitingPeriods.condition: The Governor signs a full and unconditional pardon
waitingPeriods.duration: None, but the petition may not be filed later than 10 years after the pardon signature. This is a deadline, not a waiting period.

tracks.publicName: Shielding a conviction from public view
tracks.mechanism: Twelve enumerated convictions may be shielded from public view three years after the sentence for all convictions for which shielding is requested is satisfied, including parole, probation or mandatory supervision. One shielding petition will be granted per lifetime, in one court in one county, and must include every eligible conviction from that court. Under § 10-305 a shielded conviction is not a conviction for the subsequent-conviction rule.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Expungement of Qualifying Non-Conviction Cases under § 10-105.1
tracks.publicName: Automatic clearing of a case that ended without a conviction
tracks.mechanism: For a civil offence under Criminal Law § 5-601(c)(2)(ii) or a crime other than a Transportation Article violation for which the defendant is not required to appear, where no charge in the case resulted in a disposition other than acquittal, dismissal, not guilty or nolle prosequi excluding nolle with a treatment requirement, the record shall be expunged three years after disposition, beginning October 1, 2021. No petition, no fee, no filing. The court notifies the Central Repository, custodians and the person, and under § 10-105.2 must notify the defendant of the right at disposition with a General Waiver and Release form.
exclusions: Cases where any charge resulted in a disposition other than the four qualifying outcomes.
Nolle prosequi entered with a drug or alcohol treatment requirement.
Transportation Article violations for which the defendant is required to appear.

tracks.legalName: Request to a Law Enforcement Unit for Expungement of a Pre-2007 Arrest Record, with District Court Application on Denial
tracks.publicName: Clearing police records from an arrest before October 2007
tracks.mechanism: For arrests, detentions or confinements occurring before October 1, 2007, the person requests expungement directly from the law enforcement unit within 8 years after the incident. The unit investigates and, if the facts are verified, expunges within 60 days. On written denial, or on failure to act within 60 days, the person may apply to the District Court with proper venue within 30 days of the denial, on DC-CR-071, which prints Rules Forms 4-503.3 and 4-503.4. The agency has 30 days after service to answer with specific grounds.
exclusions: Incidents occurring on or after October 1, 2007, which use the automatic police-record route.
Requests made more than 8 years after the incident. Because the incident must predate October 1, 2007, that window closed no later than October 2015.
