tracks.legalName: Motion to Seal Criminal History Record Information (15 M.R.S. ch. 310-A, §§ 2262-2264)
tracks.publicName: Sealing a Maine criminal conviction
tracks.mechanism: Chapter 310-A permits a person to move, in the underlying criminal proceeding, to seal the criminal history record information relating to one specific eligible criminal conviction. Under § 2262 the conviction must be an eligible criminal conviction; at least four years must have passed since the person fully satisfied each of the sentencing alternatives imposed under 17-A M.R.S. § 1502(2); the person must not have been convicted of another crime in Maine and must not have had a criminal charge dismissed as the result of a deferred disposition since satisfying the sentence for their most recent eligible criminal conviction; must not have been convicted of a crime in another jurisdiction in that period; and must have no presently pending criminal charges in Maine or elsewhere. Former § 2262(6), an age condition, was repealed by PL 2023, c. 666, § 3. 'Eligible criminal conviction' under § 2261(6)(A) means a current or former Class E crime other than one under 17-A M.R.S. ch. 11, and under § 2261(6)(B) five specifically listed marijuana offences committed before 30 January 2017. Relief is mandatory once proven: § 2264(5) directs that the court shall grant the motion where the person establishes each prerequisite by a preponderance of the evidence. A hearing is required and the Maine Rules of Evidence do not apply (§ 2264(4)). The current text reflects PL 2021, c. 674 as amended by PL 2023, cc. 409, 639 and 666 and PL 2025, c. 513, which became law without the Governor’s signature on 11 January 2026 and took effect on 29 July 2026.
exclusions: Every Class A, Class B and Class C crime. Chapter 310-A does not reach them.
Every Class D crime other than the five listed marijuana offences committed before 30 January 2017.
A current or former Class E crime under 17-A M.R.S. ch. 11 (sexual assaults), excluded by § 2261(6)(A).

A conviction of another crime in Maine, a criminal charge dismissed as the result of a deferred disposition under 17-A M.R.S. former ch. 54-F or ch. 67 subch. 4, or a conviction in another jurisdiction, in each case since the person fully satisfied the sentence for their most recent eligible criminal conviction (§ 2262(3) and (4)).
Any presently pending criminal charge in Maine or in another jurisdiction (§ 2262(5)).

A non-conviction disposition. § 2262 reaches a specific criminal conviction only, and filing this motion on a non-conviction is affirmatively wrong; those records are handled by operation of law under 16 M.R.S. § 703(2).
The exclusion set is the defining fact about Maine: the ordinary adult route reaches almost nothing, and the product's most valuable function here is to say no accurately and quickly.

waitingPeriods.duration: Four years from the date the person fully satisfied EACH of the sentencing alternatives imposed under 17-A M.R.S. § 1502(2) — imprisonment, probation, administrative release, licence suspension, fine payments, restitution and community service. The clock does not start at conviction and does not start at release, and an unpaid restitution or fine balance means it has not started at all.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 3 of CR-218 — the assertion of no other adult criminal convictions in Maine
manualCompletionItems.why: Paragraph 3 of CR-218 Rev. 7/24 reads in full: 'Defendant has no other adult criminal convictions in Maine and has not had a case dismissed as the result of a deferred disposition since completing their sentence for this offense.' The trailing time limit governs the deferred-disposition clause but not the convictions clause, so the form asks the participant to swear to an unbounded absence of Maine convictions while § 2262(3) bars only a conviction SINCE the person fully satisfied the sentence for their most recent eligible criminal conviction. A participant with an old prior that predates the completion date is not disqualified by the statute but reads as disqualified on the form. LegalEase does not answer this paragraph either way: it prints it blank, sets out both readings in plain terms, and tells the participant to complete it themselves and to take advice before filing if they have an older prior.

A hearing is mandatory on this track and there is no consent or default path. The clerk sets it, the court holds it, the Maine Rules of Evidence do not apply, and the movant bears a preponderance burden on each prerequisite. That is a packet instruction and a post-generation handoff, not a reason to withhold the packet.
postGenerationHandoffs: A hearing is mandatory on this track and there is no consent or default path. The clerk sets it, the court holds it, the Maine Rules of Evidence do not apply, and the movant bears a preponderance burden on each prerequisite. That is a packet instruction and a post-generation handoff, not a reason to withhold the packet.
packetInstructions: Maine seals; it does not expunge. The Judicial Branch says in terms that Maine does not have expungement and the record is not completely erased. Never use 'expungement' in Maine participant copy.

Treat as no fee, confirm with the clerk, and do not promise a refund. Do not send the participant to CV-067 or CV-191: the $60 line applies to motions under the Maine Rules of Civil Procedure, and a sealing motion is filed in the underlying criminal proceeding.

Participant-facing copy must say that sealing restricts what criminal justice agencies may disseminate and what appears on a State Bureau of Identification background check, and must not say or imply that the court case disappears.

Build the § 2264(7) self-reporting duty into post-grant participant instructions. Any new criminal conviction after the sealing order requires the record to be unsealed, and the person shall promptly file a written notice in the underlying criminal proceeding identifying the new conviction, its jurisdiction, court and docket number. If they do not and the court learns of it, the burden flips to clear and convincing evidence, and failing to request that hearing results in automatic unsealing. This duty applies to this track only; PL 2025 c. 513 exempted § 2262-A and § 2262-B records from it entirely.
Set expectations honestly on eligibility: most Maine convictions do not qualify, and the product should be able to tell someone no quickly and clearly.
Offense class at the time of conviction must be established from documents. The certified judgment is obtained by the participant and brought to the hearing; it does not delay generation.
participantQuestions: The 4-year clock runs from full satisfaction of every sentencing alternative, including fines and restitution.
scopeRestrictions: Automatic sealing did not happen. LD 1911 passed both chambers on April 14, 2026, Governor Mills vetoed it on April 24, and the Senate override failed 20-11 on April 29. Four narrower sealing bills also failed in the same session. Maine has no clean-slate mechanism. If any Maine copy anywhere in the product hints at automatic adult sealing, it is wrong.
Eligible convictions are Class E only, excluding Title 17-A chapter 11, plus five listed pre-2017 marijuana offenses.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether the movant must serve the prosecutorial office, or whether the court performs all notice. 15 M.R.S. § 2264(3) directs notice to the prosecutorial office that represented the State but does not assign the act to the movant, and none of CR-218, CR-289 or CR-307 carries a certificate-of-service block — unlike the juvenile form JV-043, which states on its face that the petitioner must provide a copy to the prosecuting attorney. The packet fails closed: it tells the participant that the court is understood to give notice, and that they should confirm with the clerk at filing and deliver a courtesy copy if the clerk asks.

provenance.sourceStatement: Whether the movant must serve the district attorney, or whether the court handles all notice. Neither the statute nor CR-218 says. Build blocker for the packet instructions.
provenance.counselQuestion: Does 15 M.R.S. § 2264(3) place notice on the court alone, or must the movant also serve the prosecutorial office? If the latter, a certificate of service must be added to every chapter 310-A packet.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether any clerk assesses a fee for a chapter 310-A motion in practice. Administrative Order JB-05-26 (A. 3-26) lists no fee for a criminal post-judgment motion; the $60 post-judgment figure is tied by its own terms to M.R. Civ. P. 55(b)(2), 59, 60(b), 62 and 66, which are civil rules, and the schedule separately provides 'Filing a Criminal Action, Traffic Infraction, or Civil Violation: No fee'. The packet therefore states that no fee is expected, tells the participant to confirm with the clerk, and promises no refund.

provenance.sourceStatement: Whether any clerk charges a fee for CR-218 in practice. Unresolved.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether a chapter 310-A sealing order removes the case from Maine's public court record search. 15 M.R.S. § 2265 makes the conviction confidential criminal history record information and restricts dissemination by a criminal justice agency, and § 2264(6) makes the State Bureau of Identification amend its records. But 16 M.R.S. § 708(3)(A) provides that the Criminal History Record Information Act does not apply to criminal history record information contained in the records of public judicial proceedings retained by the District Court, Superior Court or Supreme Judicial Court, and that public access to those records is as provided by rule or administrative order of the Supreme Judicial Court. § 2265 opens 'Notwithstanding Title 16, section 704' and does not mention section 708. Participant-facing copy must therefore say that sealing restricts what criminal justice agencies may disseminate and what appears on a State Bureau of Identification check, and must not say or imply that the court case disappears from a public docket search.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether CR-218 paragraph 3's broader wording is enforced as written or read against the narrower statutory window in § 2262(3). tracks.legalName: Motion to Seal Criminal Conviction for Engaging in Prostitution (15 M.R.S. § 2262-A)
tracks.publicName: Sealing a conviction for engaging in prostitution
tracks.mechanism: Section 2262-A permits sealing of criminal history record information relating to a conviction for the former Class E crime of engaging in prostitution under 17-A M.R.S. former § 853-A, repealed in 2023. The person must not have been convicted of a violation of 17-A M.R.S. §§ 852, 853, 853-B or 855, or of substantially similar conduct in another jurisdiction, and one year must have passed since the person fully satisfied each sentencing alternative for the conviction. Section 2262 opens 'Except as provided in sections 2262-A and 2262-B', so the general track's clean-record conditions in § 2262(3) and (4) and its pending-charge restriction in § 2262(5) do NOT apply here. Relief is mandatory: the information must be sealed if the conditions are met, and § 2264(5) requires the court to grant on a preponderance showing. Enacted by PL 2023, c. 409, § 2 and amended by PL 2025, c. 513, §§ 8 and 9, effective 29 July 2026, which repealed the eligible-criminal-conviction prerequisite formerly in § 2262-A(1). PL 2025, c. 513 also amended § 2264(7) so that the lifetime unsealing and self-reporting rule does not apply to a record sealed under this section.
exclusions: Any prostitution-adjacent offence other than 17-A M.R.S. former § 853-A. This is a named-offence route and it does not stretch.

A person convicted of a violation of 17-A M.R.S. § 852 (aggravated sex trafficking), § 853 (sex trafficking), § 853-B (engaging a person in prostitution) or § 855 (patronizing prostitution of a minor or a person with a mental disability), or of substantially similar conduct in another jurisdiction. The disqualifier is not time-limited on the face of the statute.

The general track's restrictions do NOT apply and must not be imposed here: there is no clean-record condition under § 2262(3) or (4) and no pending-charge restriction under § 2262(5), because § 2262 excepts this section in terms.

tracks.legalName: Confidential Criminal History Record Information for Non-Conviction Dispositions, and the § 709 Inspection and Correction Request (16 M.R.S. ch. 7)
tracks.publicName: Cases that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Maine does not seal or expunge non-convictions on motion. Under 16 M.R.S. § 703(2) the listed non-conviction dispositions are confidential criminal history record information BY OPERATION OF LAW, with no filing and no court involvement: a summons or arrest without disposition where more than one year has elapsed, no active prosecution is pending and the person is not a fugitive; a decision by law enforcement not to refer to a prosecutor; a decision by a prosecutor not to initiate or approve criminal proceedings; a grand jury finding of insufficient evidence; a charge dismissed with prejudice by the court or dismissed with finality by a prosecutor outside a plea agreement; an acquittal, which does not include a verdict or accepted plea of not criminally responsible by reason of insanity; a mistrial with prejudice; termination for lack of subject matter jurisdiction; termination for want of jurisdiction over the defendant; and the remaining paragraphs of § 703(2), which include a pardoned conviction. Confidential information may be disseminated only to the recipients listed in § 705, and a criminal justice agency may not confirm its existence or nonexistence to anyone not entitled to receive it. Separately, § 709 gives a person the right to inspect their own criminal history record information held by a Maine criminal justice agency and to request that it be amended or corrected: the agency has fifteen days to investigate and notify the requester with reasons for any refusal, the agency head must complete an administrative appeal within thirty days, a person denied on appeal may file a statement of disagreement that must accompany any future dissemination, final agency action is appealable to the Superior Court under 5 M.R.S. ch. 375 subch. 7, and on correction the agency must notify prior recipients within thirty days. Section 709(6) provides that the section does not apply to court records, access to which is governed by Supreme Judicial Court rules.
exclusions: A dismissal that WAS part of a plea agreement. § 703(2)(G) reaches a dismissal with finality by a prosecutor OUTSIDE a plea agreement, and this is the most commonly misunderstood point in Maine.

A dismissal without prejudice does not become confidential merely because it was a dismissal. It reaches confidentiality only through the summons-or-arrest-without-disposition category, and only where more than one year has elapsed, no active prosecution is pending and the person is not a fugitive.
A verdict or accepted plea of not criminally responsible by reason of insanity, which § 703(2) does not treat as an acquittal.

Court records. § 709(6) says the section does not apply to them and 16 M.R.S. § 708(3)(A) puts records of public judicial proceedings outside the Criminal History Record Information Act entirely, with public access governed by Supreme Judicial Court rule or administrative order. A publicly accessible docket entry is not cured by § 703(2) confidentiality.
Records held by a private background-check vendor, which chapter 7 does not bind. That is the business screening service track.
A charge dismissed after a completed deferred disposition, whose status under § 703(2) is not established. It routes through the deferred-disposition node and the packet promises nothing.

waitingPeriods.duration: More than one year from the summons or arrest, with no active prosecution pending and the person not a fugitive.

units.label: Confidentiality by operation of law — classification and verification, no filing
units.description: The base branch. Where the disposition falls inside the 16 M.R.S. § 703(2) list the record is already confidential criminal history record information and there is nothing to file: no court has any role, no motion exists, and generating CR-218 for a non-conviction would be affirmatively wrong because § 2262 reaches a specific criminal conviction only. The unit classifies the disposition against the § 703(2) list, explains that the confidentiality is automatic, walks the participant through obtaining their own State Bureau of Identification record to see what the State actually holds, and states plainly where the disposition falls outside the list that Maine offers no relief for it rather than routing them to a motion that will be denied. It also separates the three problems that participants conflate: the Bureau record, the court docket, and a private vendor's database.

units.label: 16 M.R.S. § 709 inspection and correction request to the criminal justice agency
units.description: The conditional branch, reached only where the agency record is demonstrably inaccurate — most often where the State Bureau of Identification is still carrying a disposition that § 703(2) makes confidential, or is carrying a disposition that is simply wrong. § 709(1) and (2) give the participant the right to inspect their own criminal history record information and to request that it be amended or corrected by contacting the agency, and the agency then has fifteen days to investigate and notify the requester with reasons for any refusal. No official Maine form exists for the request and none is prescribed by the statute, so this is a participant-signed written request that LegalEase drafts: it identifies the participant and the record, states the disposition and its § 703(2) category, states precisely what the agency record says and what it should say, attaches the disposition order, and asks for amendment or correction under § 709(2). The packet also carries the escalation path — administrative appeal to the agency head within thirty days, the statement of disagreement that must accompany any future dissemination, and Superior Court review of final agency action under 5 M.R.S. ch. 375 subch. 7 — as instructions rather than as generated documents. This unit is a separate legal act from unit 1: it has a participant submission, a named destination, its own statutory basis and its own legal output, where unit 1 has none of those.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether a charge dismissed after successful completion of a deferred disposition under 17-A M.R.S. ch. 67 subch. 4 is confidential criminal history record information under 16 M.R.S. § 703(2). This was checked against current official text and is NOT ESTABLISHED. Section 703(2) lists paragraphs A through L and none mentions a deferred disposition. The closest is paragraph G, which reaches a charge 'dismissed with prejudice by the court or dismissed with finality by a prosecutor outside a plea agreement'. Under 17-A M.R.S. § 1903 the State dismisses the charging instrument WITH PREJUDICE on compliance, which fits the first clause, but a deferred disposition arises from a written agreement between the defendant and the State, which arguably falls inside paragraph G's outside-a-plea-agreement carve-out. tracks.legalName: Deferred Disposition — Outcome Classification and Sealing-Eligibility Routing (17-A M.R.S. ch. 67, subch. 4; 15 M.R.S. § 2262(3))
tracks.publicName: Cases resolved through a deferred disposition
tracks.mechanism: A deferred disposition is not a record-clearing mechanism and produces no relief of its own. It is a disposition status with two possible outcomes and one sharp cross-track consequence, and it is modelled as a routing node for exactly that reason. Under 17-A M.R.S. § 1901 a deferred disposition arises from a written agreement between the defendant and the State; under § 1903, on compliance and the State's motion, the court permits withdrawal of the plea and the State dismisses the charging instrument with prejudice. Section 1903 says nothing about confidentiality or sealing. Where the case instead ends in conviction of a reduced offence, that conviction is evaluated on its own terms under chapter 310-A and qualifies only if it lands inside the § 2261(6) eligible set. The cross-track consequence is the one that matters most: under 15 M.R.S. § 2262(3) a criminal charge dismissed as the result of a deferred disposition, since the person fully satisfied the sentence for their most recent eligible criminal conviction, is an absolute disqualifier for the general sealing track. A deferred disposition is therefore good news for the case it resolves and bad news for a prior conviction the participant wanted sealed.
exclusions: This node produces no relief and no packet of its own. It is not a sealing remedy, it is not a paid-packet route, and no deferred-disposition sealing packet is generated.

tracks.legalName: Business Screening Service Dispute for Correction or Deletion of Criminal History Record Information (10 M.R.S. c. 239, § 1500-CC)
tracks.publicName: Getting a sealed record off a background check
tracks.mechanism: Chapter 239 regulates how a business screening service handles Maine criminal history record information. A business screening service under § 1500-AA is a person regularly engaged in the business of collecting, assembling, evaluating or disseminating criminal history record information about specific individuals for a fee, excluding a government entity and the news media. Under § 1500-CC, where the completeness or accuracy of a record is disputed by its subject, the service shall investigate WITHOUT CHARGE; must review and consider all relevant information the subject submits and determine whether its record accurately reflects the official record maintained by the State Bureau of Identification; must correct a record that does not accurately reflect the official record; and — the operative remedy here — if the disputed record is found to be sealed or the subject of a pardon, SHALL PROMPTLY DELETE the record. The service may terminate an investigation it reasonably determines is frivolous, but must then state the specific reasons and describe the information it needs. Within thirty days of receiving notice of the dispute the service must notify the subject of the results, including whether the investigation was completed or terminated and what records were corrected or deleted. Section 1500-DD requires a service disseminating records collected on or after 1 July 2010 to include the collection date and a notice that the information may include records that have been sealed or otherwise become inaccessible since. Section 1500-EE provides an FCRA safe harbour, deems foreign-corporation screening services to consent to Maine jurisdiction, and supplies a private right of action. Enacted by PL 2025, c. 513, § 1 and effective 29 July 2026.
exclusions: Records held by the State Bureau of Identification or any other criminal justice agency. Chapter 239 binds business screening services only; the agency record is corrected under 16 M.R.S. § 709.
Court records, which chapter 239 does not reach.
A government entity or the news media, both expressly excluded from the § 1500-AA definition of a business screening service.

The statutory remedy of $1,000 or actual damages, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees, under § 1500-EE(3). That is litigation and it is outside self-help. LegalEase does not plead it, demand it, threaten it, or calculate it.
A Fair Credit Reporting Act claim. § 1500-EE makes compliance with the relevant FCRA provisions a safe harbour and liability attaches only where conduct violates both, which is attorney analysis.

waitingPeriods.duration: None before sending. After the service receives notice of the dispute it has thirty days to notify the subject of the results of its investigation.

tracks.venue: Not applicable at the dispute stage. The letter goes to the screening service's own dispute address, wherever the service is located; § 1500-EE deems a foreign-corporation service that disseminates Maine criminal history record information, or obtains records from a Maine government entity or court, to consent to service and jurisdiction in Maine.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Seal Conviction for Victims of Sex Trafficking or Sexual Exploitation (15 M.R.S. § 2262-B)
tracks.publicName: Sealing a conviction connected to trafficking or exploitation
tracks.mechanism: Section 2262-B provides that criminal history record information relating to an eligible criminal conviction as described in § 2261(6)(C) must be sealed if the person filing the motion establishes, first, that the person has been a victim of sex trafficking or sexual exploitation, and second, that the commission of the crime for which the person was convicted was a substantial result of that sex trafficking or sexual exploitation. A motion under the section may be filed AT ANY TIME after the criminal conviction is entered. Section 2261(6)(C) defines an eligible criminal conviction for a § 2262-B motion as a criminal conviction for ANY current or former crime: there is no class limit, no chapter 11 exclusion and no offence list. Section 2261(8) defines sex trafficking and § 2261(9) defines sexual exploitation as engaging in the exchange of sex for money or resources because of a person's history of trauma, adverse childhood experiences, substance use disorder or other circumstances of victimization, exploitation or oppression. Section 2264(4-A) provides for remote participation by the person and any witnesses unless the court finds the person or a witness resides in Maine and the interests of justice require in-person participation; provides that official documentation of victim status is NOT required, and that if presented it creates a presumption that the person's participation in the offence was a substantial result of the trafficking or exploitation; and enumerates qualifying documentation, including an official record, certification or eligibility letter from a federal, state, tribal or local proceeding including a federal immigration approval notice, an affidavit or sworn testimony from clergy, a medical professional, victim services staff or another professional, and any other evidence the court finds of sufficient credibility or probative value. Section 2264(5) requires a hearing on a motion under the chapter EXCEPT that for a motion under § 2262-B the court may grant the motion without a hearing if the representative for the State consents. Section 2264(7), as amended, does not apply to records sealed under § 2262-A or § 2262-B, so a later conviction does not unseal and there is no self-reporting duty. Enacted by PL 2025, c. 513 and effective 29 July 2026.
exclusions: None on the face of the statute as to offence. § 2261(6)(C) reaches a conviction for any current or former crime, with no class limit, no Title 17-A chapter 11 exclusion and no offence list. This is by a wide margin the broadest sealing route in Maine.

No waiting period, no sentence-completion requirement, no pending-charge restriction and no case-count limit apply. The motion may be filed at any time after the conviction is entered, including while the person is still serving the sentence.

What the route does exclude is a case in which the two statutory elements cannot be established. That is a merits question for the participant and their advocate, not an eligibility filter LegalEase applies.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. The motion may be filed at any time after the criminal conviction is entered, and the person may file while still serving the sentence.

packetInstructions: Maine seals; it does not expunge. The Judicial Branch says in terms that Maine does not have expungement and the record is not completely erased. Never use 'expungement' in Maine participant copy.

Treat as no fee, confirm with the clerk, and do not promise a refund. Do not send the participant to CV-067 or CV-191: the $60 line applies to motions under the Maine Rules of Civil Procedure, and a sealing motion is filed in the underlying criminal proceeding.

Participant-facing copy must say that sealing restricts what criminal justice agencies may disseminate and what appears on a State Bureau of Identification background check, and must not say or imply that the court case disappears.

Official documentation is not required by § 2264(4-A)(B). If presented it creates a presumption that participation in the offence was a substantial result of the trafficking or exploitation. Frame the question so a no carries no implication, and never ask the participant to produce proof.

There is no waiting period, no sentence-completion requirement, no pending-charge restriction and no offence limit, and the motion may be filed while the person is still serving the sentence. This route is far broader than the prostitution route and participants on that route are screened into this one.

releaseBlockers.question: Form CR-308 page 2 carries a warning box stating that if at any time after the date of the order the defendant is convicted of a new crime in Maine or in any other jurisdiction, the new conviction extinguishes the order. That is inconsistent with 15 M.R.S. § 2264(7) as amended by PL 2025, c. 513, which now provides in terms that the subsection does not apply to records sealed pursuant to section 2262-A or 2262-B. Both the form and the amendment take effect 29 July 2026, so this is a live conflict on the face of two current official sources rather than a stale-form problem. LegalEase does not resolve it: the packet states the statutory rule, does not repeat the form's warning as advice, and carries the conflict as a release blocker.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether any clerk assesses a fee for a chapter 310-A motion in practice. Administrative Order JB-05-26 (A. 3-26) lists no fee for a criminal post-judgment motion; the $60 post-judgment figure is tied by its own terms to M.R. Civ. P. 55(b)(2), 59, 60(b), 62 and 66, which are civil rules, and the schedule separately provides 'Filing a Criminal Action, Traffic Infraction, or Civil Violation: No fee'. The packet therefore states that no fee is expected, tells the participant to confirm with the clerk, and promises no refund.

provenance.sourceStatement: Whether any clerk charges a fee for CR-218 in practice. Unresolved.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether a chapter 310-A sealing order removes the case from Maine's public court record search. 15 M.R.S. § 2265 makes the conviction confidential criminal history record information and restricts dissemination by a criminal justice agency, and § 2264(6) makes the State Bureau of Identification amend its records. But 16 M.R.S. § 708(3)(A) provides that the Criminal History Record Information Act does not apply to criminal history record information contained in the records of public judicial proceedings retained by the District Court, Superior Court or Supreme Judicial Court, and that public access to those records is as provided by rule or administrative order of the Supreme Judicial Court. § 2265 opens 'Notwithstanding Title 16, section 704' and does not mention section 708. Participant-facing copy must therefore say that sealing restricts what criminal justice agencies may disseminate and what appears on a State Bureau of Identification check, and must not say or imply that the court case disappears from a public docket search.

provenance.sourceHeading: A2. Sealing reaches the criminal history record; the court record is governed separately

tracks.legalName: Application to Set Aside Conviction(s) under MCL 780.621
tracks.publicName: Application to set aside a conviction
tracks.mechanism: The ordinary application route. Not more than 3 felonies total, not more than 2 assaultive-crime convictions in a lifetime, and not more than 1 felony for the same offence where that offence is punishable by more than 10 years; misdemeanours are otherwise unlimited. Deferred-and-dismissed cases count as misdemeanour convictions against those determinations. Relief is discretionary under MCL 780.621d(13) and (14). MC 227 is the SCAO-approved statewide form and MCL 780.621d(7) prescribes seven categories of required content without which the application is invalid.
exclusions: A felony, or attempt, punishable by life imprisonment.
Violations or attempted violations of MCL 750.136b(3), 750.136d(1)(b) or (c), 750.145c, 750.145d, 750.520c, 750.520d and 750.520g.
MCL 750.520e where the conviction occurred on or after January 12, 2015.

Traffic offences: operating while intoxicated by any person; any traffic offence by a commercial-endorsement holder committed while operating a commercial motor vehicle or otherwise a commercial motor vehicle violation; any traffic offence causing injury or death.
A felony domestic violence conviction where the person has a previous misdemeanour domestic violence conviction.
Human trafficking offences under MCL 750.462a to 750.462h and terrorism offences under MCL 750.543a to 750.543z.
Out-of-state and federal convictions, which are outside the act.

waitingPeriods.condition: More than one felony, from the last of sentence imposition, completion of felony probation, discharge from parole, or completion of imprisonment
waitingPeriods.duration: 7 years

waitingPeriods.condition: One felony, or one or more serious misdemeanours, or one first-violation operating-while-intoxicated offence
waitingPeriods.duration: 5 years

waitingPeriods.condition: One or more misdemeanours that are not serious misdemeanours, not a first-violation OWI and not assaultive
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years

tracks.venue: Statewide statute, filed court by court. File in the convicting court, district or circuit. A separate application is required for each court.

tracks.legalName: Application to Set Aside Misdemeanor Marihuana Conviction(s) under MCL 780.621e
tracks.publicName: Set aside a misdemeanor marijuana conviction
tracks.mechanism: Added by 2020 PA 192, effective April 11, 2021. Reaches a misdemeanour marihuana offence as defined at MCL 780.621e(7): a violation of MCL 333.7403(2)(d), MCL 333.7404(2)(d), or a marihuana paraphernalia violation of MCL 333.7453, or a substantially corresponding local ordinance. Filing raises a rebuttable presumption that the conviction was based on activity that would not have been a crime if committed on or after December 6, 2018, and the evidentiary burden rests solely on the objecting prosecuting agency. Absent a timely answer the court must enter the order.
exclusions: Anything broader than the MCL 780.621e(7) definition. Nothing outside MCL 333.7403(2)(d), MCL 333.7404(2)(d), MCL 333.7453 or a substantially corresponding local ordinance.

tracks.publicName: Set aside a first drunk-driving conviction
tracks.mechanism: 2021 PA 78, effective February 19, 2022, carved a first-violation operating-while-intoxicated offence back in against an otherwise categorical traffic exclusion. The offence is a violation of MCL 257.625(1), (2), (3), (6) or (8), or a corresponding tribal, other-state, federal or local provision, committed by an individual who at the time of the violation had no prior MCL 257.625 convictions. Once only, and excluded from automatic relief by MCL 780.621g(10).
exclusions: An operating-while-intoxicated conviction where the person had any prior MCL 257.625 conviction at the time of the violation.
A second application after a first-violation OWI conviction has already been set aside.
Automatic relief, which excludes OWI committed by any person under MCL 780.621g(10).

tracks.publicName: Set aside a conviction you got because you were trafficked
tracks.mechanism: Convictions under MCL 750.448, 750.449 or 750.450, or a substantially corresponding local ordinance, where the person committed the offence as a direct result of being a victim of a human trafficking violation. No waiting period; it may be filed at any time following conviction and more than one conviction may be set aside. The applicant must prove by a preponderance that the conviction was a direct result of being a victim, and the MCL 780.621d(13) public-welfare finding still applies. MCL 780.621d(7)(g) requires a statement of the facts supporting the trafficking contention.
exclusions: Convictions outside MCL 750.448, 750.449 and 750.450 or a substantially corresponding local ordinance.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. May be filed at any time following the date of conviction, and more than one conviction may be set aside.

tracks.publicName: Clearing a fourth-degree criminal sexual conduct conviction from before 2015
tracks.mechanism: A violation or attempted violation of MCL 750.520e committed before January 12, 2015 may be set aside, subject to a bespoke prior-record test: the individual must not have been convicted of another offence other than not more than two minor offences, where a minor offence is a misdemeanour or ordinance violation with a maximum term not exceeding 90 days and a maximum fine of not more than $1,000, committed by a person not more than 21 years old. Convictions on or after January 12, 2015 are categorically excluded by MCL 780.621c(c).
exclusions: Convictions on or after January 12, 2015, which MCL 780.621c(c) categorically excludes.
An individual convicted of any other offence beyond not more than two minor offences as defined.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Set-Aside of Felony Convictions under MCL 780.621g(2)
tracks.publicName: Felony convictions that clear on their own
tracks.mechanism: Effective April 11, 2023, up to two felony convictions are set aside by operation of law without any application, ten years after either imposition of sentence or completion of any term of imprisonment with the Michigan Department of Corrections, whichever occurs later. No court order is required; SCAO guidance states all eligible convictions are set aside by operation of law.
exclusions: Assaultive crimes, serious misdemeanours and crimes of dishonesty.
Any other offence punishable by 10 or more years.
Any offence listed in MCL 777.1 to 777.69 whose elements involve a minor, a vulnerable adult, injury or serious impairment, or death.
Any violation related to human trafficking.

tracks.mechanism: SCAO form MC 262, Order of Acquittal/Dismissal or Remand, carries the notice that the defendant's fingerprints and arrest card will be destroyed by Michigan State Police within 60 days of the order when permitted by MCL 28.243, and the clerk must advise the MSP Criminal Justice Information Center of the disposition under MCL 769.16a. Under MCL 28.243(8)(b), where the prosecutor agrees at any time after dismissal, or where neither the prosecutor nor the judge objects within 60 days of the dismissal order, the arrest record, all biometric data and fingerprints are destroyed and any LEIN entry is removed. MSP acts on receipt of an appropriate district or circuit court order.
exclusions: MCL 28.243(14): a person arraigned for enumerated offences, including the commission or attempted commission of a crime with or against a child under 16, and, materially for this population, a person who has a prior conviction other than a misdemeanour traffic offence.

waitingPeriods.condition: Entry of the order of acquittal or dismissal
waitingPeriods.duration: 60 days for MSP destruction; for a dismissal, where neither the prosecutor nor the judge objects within 60 days

tracks.legalName: Completed Deferrals and Their Record Consequences
tracks.publicName: What a completed deferral means for clearing your record
tracks.mechanism: Three things are simultaneously true for a participant with a completed deferral. The case record is already nonpublic by operation of the deferral statute, so there is usually nothing to set aside on the court side. The arrest record may still exist and is addressed by the biometric-destruction routes rather than the set-aside act. And under MCL 780.621(2) the deferred-and-dismissed disposition counts as a misdemeanour conviction for determining set-aside eligibility, with MCL 780.621d(7)(d) requiring every such action to be listed on any application.
exclusions: This is not relief. It alters no record and must not be counted as a paid packet mechanism or a substantive relief mechanism.

releaseBlockers.question: The operative date of Laws 2026, chapter 70, section 5 must be confirmed before participant-facing instructions state it. The session law was retrieved on 2026-08-02: section 5 adds a new paragraph (f) to § 609A.015, subd. 5, under which the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension unseals a record and notifies the judicial branch if it later determines the record did not qualify for automatic relief, making that determination only from a record stored in its criminal history system, and the following paragraphs are renumbered (g) through (j). It does not alter the BCA's identification duty, the court-sealing window or victim notice. Chapter 70 states an effective date only for section 4 (1 January 2027), so section 5 falls to the default in Minn. Stat. § 645.02. Packet identity is unaffected because this route has no packet; the participant-facing warning that a Clean Slate grant may later be unsealed is an instruction change.

tracks.legalName: Written Demand for Destruction of Arrest Identification Data under Minn. Stat. § 299C.11, subd. 1(b)
tracks.publicName: Arrest record destruction request (no court case)
tracks.mechanism: On written demand, law enforcement and the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension must destroy arrest identification data — fingerprints and thumbprints, photographs, distinctive physical mark identification data, known aliases and street names, and all copies and duplicates — where the person has no felony or gross-misdemeanour conviction anywhere in the ten years immediately preceding determination of all pending criminal actions in their favour, and either all charges were dismissed before a determination of probable cause, or the prosecuting authority declined to file and a grand jury did not indict. Relief is mandatory on demand where the conditions are met. The Minnesota Judicial Branch publishes six sample demand letters.
exclusions: Section 299C.11, subd. 3(1) provides that the following are not a determination in favour of the arrested person: sealing under § 152.18, subd. 1, § 242.31 or chapter 609A; successful completion of a diversion programme; an order of discharge under § 609.165; and a pardon under chapter 638.
Any felony or gross-misdemeanour conviction, in or outside Minnesota, in the ten years immediately preceding determination of all pending criminal actions in the person's favour.

tracks.legalName: Prosecutor-Agreed Sealing under Minn. Stat. § 609A.025
tracks.publicName: Prosecutor-agreed record sealing
tracks.mechanism: Where the prosecutor agrees, the court shall seal without any petition unless it determines that the interests of the public and public safety in keeping the record public outweigh the disadvantages to the subject. The prosecutor's agreement is discretionary and, before agreeing, the prosecutor must make a good-faith effort to notify identifiable victims of the intended agreement and of the opportunity to object. One statewide mechanism with county-specific intake.
exclusions: Dispositions outside the § 609A.02, subd. 3 grounds population.
Pending charges, as under § 609A.02, subd. 3.

waitingPeriods.condition: The § 609A.02, subd. 3 waiting periods apply by reference
waitingPeriods.duration: As under subd. 3. For a person described in subd. 3(a)(2), diversion or stay of adjudication, the prosecutor's agreement may occur before or after the charges are dismissed.

units.label: Request to the prosecuting authority
units.description: The participant asks the prosecuting authority to agree to sealing. LegalEase identifies the correct prosecuting authority from the county and offence location and prepares the participant's factual summary. Which sub-branch applies depends on whether the county runs a published programme.

units.label: County portal application
units.description: Hennepin, Ramsey and Washington Counties run published online applications. These are third-party intake systems with their own field requirements, so LegalEase prepares the participant's factual summary and routes them to the county portal. It does not complete or submit a county portal application.

units.label: Written request to the county or city attorney
units.description: Where the county runs no published programme, the participant contacts the county or city attorney directly. LegalEase generates a participant-signed written request setting out the case, the disposition, the applicable § 609A.02, subd. 3 ground and the participant's own account. The Attorney General page is the statewide entry point for identifying the correct authority.

units.label: Court sealing on prosecutor agreement
units.description: Once the prosecutor agrees, the court shall seal without any participant petition, unless the public-interest balance goes the other way. There is nothing for the participant to file at this stage.

tracks.legalName: Inherent-Authority Petition to Seal Judicial Branch Records
tracks.publicName: Petition to seal court records only
tracks.mechanism: A judicially recognised inherent authority to seal judicial branch records, outside chapter 609A. Ambaye sets two grounds: where the petitioner's constitutional rights may be seriously infringed by retention of the records, or, where constitutional rights are not involved, whether expungement yields a benefit to the petitioner commensurate with the disadvantages to the public and the burden on the court. Under Schultz, absent constitutional infringement the judicial branch cannot order non-judicial records sealed, so relief reaches court records only.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Arrest, Plea, Trial or Conviction (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.140)
tracks.publicName: Expunging a Missouri conviction
tracks.mechanism: Section 610.140 is Missouri's general expungement mechanism and the route most participants belong on. It was read in full from the Revisor's current text, effective 1 January 2025. Subsection 2(1) lets any person apply to any court in which the person was charged or found guilty for an order to expunge records of that arrest, plea, trial or conviction; subsection 1(1) defines "court" as any Missouri municipal, associate circuit or circuit court, and subsection 1(2) defines "crime" as any offense, violation or infraction of Missouri state, county, municipal or administrative law. Subsection 2(2) requires the petitioner to list every crime sought to be expunged in the one petition and bars any crime excluded under subsection 3. Subsection 6 sets the six criteria the court may consider: at the time the petition is filed at least three years for a felony or one year for a misdemeanor, municipal violation or infraction has run from the date the petitioner completed any authorized disposition imposed under § 557.011; during that same period the petitioner has not been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony, excluding traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307; all obligations relating to the disposition are satisfied including fines and restitution; no charges are pending; the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to public safety; and the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it. A pleading that the petitioner meets criteria (5) and (6) creates a rebuttable presumption so long as (1) to (4) are satisfied, and the burden then shifts to the prosecuting or circuit attorney; a victim has an opportunity to be heard and the court may find that the continuing impact on the victim rebuts the presumption. The clerk gives notice to the prosecuting attorney, whose written objection is due within thirty days after receipt of service, and the court holds a hearing within sixty days after a written objection unless the parties agree otherwise. Subsection 8 makes relief mandatory once the criteria are met and requires an order of expungement or of dismissal within six months of filing. Subsection 12 dismisses a petition where the criteria are not met or false information was knowingly provided, and bars a further petition until a year has passed since the date of filing the previous one. Subsection 13 caps a lifetime at not more than three misdemeanor offenses or ordinance violations carrying an authorized term of imprisonment and not more than two felony offenses, with no limit on infractions, and subsection 2(3) lets crimes committed as part of the same course of criminal conduct go in a single petition and count only at the highest level. Subsection 14 requires the court to make a form available for pro se petitioners carrying the declaration under penalty of perjury, which is what CR360 is. Expungement here is closure under § 610.120, never destruction.
exclusions: Class A felonies (§ 610.140.3(1)).
Dangerous felonies as defined in § 556.061 (§ 610.140.3(2)).
Any offense requiring registration as a sex offender (§ 610.140.3(3)).
Any felony offense where death is an element of the offense (§ 610.140.3(4)).
Felony assault offenses, misdemeanor or felony domestic assault offenses, and felony kidnapping (§ 610.140.3(5)).
The specifically enumerated chapter 566 sex offenses and the listed offenses in other chapters (§ 610.140.3(6)).
Offenses eligible under § 610.130, so the first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense occupies its own lane and never routes here (§ 610.140.3(7)).
Intoxication-related traffic offenses and intoxication-related boating offenses, and operating an aircraft with an excessive blood alcohol content or while intoxicated (§ 610.140.3(8)).
Any ordinance violation substantially equivalent to an excluded offense (§ 610.140.3(9)).
Any offense of a motor vehicle law or ordinance committed by a person holding, or required to hold, a commercial driver's license (§ 610.140.3(10)).
Most unlawful use of weapons offenses under § 571.030, subject to the specific statutory exceptions (§ 610.140.3(11)).

A crime prosecuted outside Missouri or outside the jurisdiction of a Missouri court. § 610.140.2(2) reaches only crimes that occurred within Missouri and were prosecuted under the jurisdiction of a Missouri court.

waitingPeriods.duration: Three years. Measured at the time the petition is filed, running back from the date the petitioner completed any authorized disposition imposed under § 557.011 — not from the arrest date and not from the conviction date.
One year, measured the same way: at the time the petition is filed, from the date the petitioner completed the authorized disposition.

The same three-year or one-year period, and the direction matters. The period runs backward from the filing of the petition, not forward from completion of the sentence. During it the petitioner must not have been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony, excluding traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307.

tracks.venue: Any Missouri municipal, associate circuit or circuit court in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty (§ 610.140.1(1) and 2(1)). Rule 155.01 commences the action by filing a petition in the circuit court of the county in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty. Where the participant's crimes were charged in more than one county the petition cannot reach them all: § 610.140.2(2) requires every crime in one petition but subsection 2(1) fixes venue by court of charge or finding of guilt, so a multi-county record is a self-help stop rather than a routing choice LegalEase makes.

destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of the municipal, associate circuit or circuit court where the crimes were charged or the finding of guilt entered. Missouri has forty-six judicial circuits covering 114 counties and the City of St. Louis, plus municipal divisions. The clerk assigns the case number, gives notice of the filing to the prosecuting attorney under § 610.140.6, and distributes the order under § 610.140.8. Local filing practice, copy counts and fees are confirmed with that clerk and are not optional.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name a Missouri case was filed under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.

List every Missouri case you want expunged: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county or municipality where it was charged, and a description of the charge. Every crime you want expunged has to be in this one petition.
Were all of the cases you listed charged, or the finding of guilt entered, in the same Missouri county? If they were in different counties, one petition cannot reach them all.
For each case, was the offense a felony, a misdemeanor, a municipal or ordinance violation, or an infraction?

For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date.
Have you paid every fine, court cost and restitution order in full on each of those cases?
Since the date you finished each case, have you been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any criminal charges pending right now, anywhere?

Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number, and say whether each was a felony, a misdemeanor or an ordinance violation with a possible jail term, or an infraction.

Were any of the cases you listed part of the same course of criminal conduct, or charged as counts in the same indictment or information? If so they can go in one petition and count only once, at the highest offense level.

Is any case on your list a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense that required sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an aircraft intoxication offense, an ordinance violation equivalent to any of those, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Work from your own paperwork: the circuit court division, any municipal division, the county sheriff's department, the municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county, the Missouri Department of Revenue, and anyone else. Add every agency whose name appears on any document you have.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Case.net printouts, your court paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?

The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Missouri Supreme Court Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and the number is not published through Case.net. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

Is any case on your list a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for unlawful use or possession of drug paraphernalia? From 1 January 2027 at the latest, Missouri will expunge some of those automatically and free of charge, and an automatic expungement uses up the same lifetime slots as this petition.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 5 — that the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to the public safety of the state
manualCompletionItems.why: It is a conclusion about the participant, sworn under penalty of perjury, and § 610.140.6(5) makes it one of the two criteria that create the rebuttable presumption. LegalEase prompts for the participant's own facts and never asserts the conclusion. The review lists it first among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 7 — that the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it
manualCompletionItems.why: The same reason. § 610.140.6(6) makes it the second presumption criterion, and it is a legal conclusion about the public interest rather than a fact about the participant.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection and the court and case number of any prior expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: Whether prior expungements have exhausted the § 610.140.13 caps is a legal judgment the review lists among the questions requiring individualized legal judgment. LegalEase asks for the participant's history, records their answer, and does not decide whether the caps remain available.

manualCompletionItems.item: Final verification of the defendant agency list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 1, defendant selections and the Other lines
manualCompletionItems.why: § 610.140.8 and the CR360 text both say the court's order of expungement shall not affect any person or entity not named as a defendant. A named agency closes its record; an unnamed agency keeps its copy, and the participant usually discovers that only when a later background check comes back. LegalEase builds the best list it can from the participant's own records because doing it badly is the most common way Missouri relief half-works, but the list is an assertion under oath about where records exist and the participant confirms it.

selfHelpBoundaries: Any case that may fall in one of the eleven § 610.140.3 exclusion categories, including any felony assault, domestic assault, kidnapping, sex, weapons, child or death-related offense.
Any sex-offender registration issue, current or historic.
Any intoxication-related traffic, boating or aircraft offense, which is excluded here and belongs on the § 610.130 route if anywhere.
Any commercial driver licence or commercial motor vehicle involvement.
Any § 571.030 unlawful use of weapons offense, including where a statutory exception may apply.
Any question whether the § 610.140.13 lifetime caps remain available, or whether an automatic § 610.141 expungement has already consumed one.
Any question whether separate cases were part of the same course of criminal conduct.
Cases charged in more than one Missouri county, which one petition cannot reach.
Any uncertainty about the exact date the authorized disposition was completed.
The prosecuting attorney files a written objection, or a victim appears or asks to be heard.
The court sets a contested hearing.
A previous petition was dismissed, which bars refiling until a year has passed since the date that petition was filed.
The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.
The participant asks about firearm rights, professional licensing, foster care or adoption, banking, insurance, gaming or federal employment.

The eleven § 610.140.3 exclusion categories are never auto-screened from participant self-report. Several turn on classification rather than on the offense name, and a wrong answer costs the participant a year's refiling bar.

A drink- or drug-driving matter must never be routed through § 610.140. § 610.140.3(7) and (8) exclude offenses eligible under § 610.130 and intoxication-related traffic and boating offenses generally, so the two routes do not overlap.

Self-help ends if the prosecuting attorney files a written objection within the thirty-day window, if a victim asks to be heard, or if the court sets a contested hearing. The initial packet is not retracted; the participant needs a lawyer for what happens next.

packetInstructions: Missouri expungement under § 610.140 is closure under § 610.120, not destruction. The record is closed to public access and specified entities keep access. Never say erased or destroyed on this track. Destruction language is accurate only under § 610.124 on the § 610.122 arrest track.

The order does not affect any entity not named as a defendant (§ 610.140.8). The packet builds the best agency list it can from the participant's own records, includes the current CR360 agency categories and free-text lines for others, and prints the warning that an omitted agency keeps its copy.

The refiling bar appears prominently above the signature block. Under § 610.140.12, if the court finds the petitioner has not met the criteria for any listed crime, or knowingly provided false information, it dismisses the petition and no further petition may be filed until a year has passed since the date the previous petition was filed — measured from the filing date, not from the dismissal.

Disclosure survives expungement in six situations and the participant must be told: an application for a licence, certificate or permit issued by Missouri to practise the participant's profession (§ 610.140.10(1)); any licence issued under chapter 313 or permit issued under chapter 571 (§ 610.140.10(2)); paid or unpaid employment with an entity licensed under chapter 313, any state-operated lottery, or any emergency services provider including any law enforcement agency (§ 610.140.10(3)); employment with a federally insured bank, savings institution or credit union or an affiliate, for 12 U.S.C. §§ 1829 and 1785 compliance (§ 610.140.10(4)); employment with an entity engaged in the business of insurance or any insurer, for 18 U.S.C. §§ 1033 and 1034 compliance (§ 610.140.10(5)); employment with any employer required by federal or state law to exclude applicants with certain criminal convictions (§ 610.140.10(6)). Outside those, § 610.140.11 lets the participant answer no to an employer's inquiry where no public record remains.

An expunged crime may still be considered a prior offense in determining a sentence for any later offense (§ 610.140.9), and the participant must disclose it to any court when asked or on being charged with a subsequent crime. Expungement is not erasure for sentencing purposes.
Do not quote the repealed $250 surcharge. § 488.650 was repealed effective 28 August 2023. Filing fees are ordinary circuit court fees, are county-variable, and are confirmed with the clerk.

FI-05 with case type code X5 is a required component of every § 610.140 packet, and the code is read from the Case Types List's circuit column rather than inferred from the track name. The review is right that a packet without the cover sheet and the right code gets bounced at the counter.

Where the participant reports a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for drug paraphernalia, the packet must explain the § 610.141 timing trade-off before they file: automatic expungement is free, is due no later than 1 January 2027, and consumes the same lifetime slots, so petitioning now may spend a slot on relief that was about to arrive at no cost. The packet must not promise that automatic relief will reach any particular record.

The certified docket and judgment, the payment history, the probation or parole discharge document and the Highway Patrol criminal record are obtained and attached by the participant before filing. None of them delays generation of the packet.
participantQuestions: The full Social Security number is required on FI-05 under Operating Rule 4.07 where the party is a person and it is reasonably available. It is asked once, placed only on the confidential sheet, and is not repeated on CR360, which does not request it.

The clean period runs backward from the filing of the petition, not forward from completion of the sentence, and the direction changes who is eligible. The intake asks the completion date and the conviction history separately for this reason.
scopeRestrictions: The lifetime caps are three misdemeanor offenses or imprisonable ordinance violations and two felony offenses, with no limit on infractions (§ 610.140.13). From the date § 610.141 becomes operative those caps are shared with automatic drug expungements under § 610.141.6, which counts expungements under both sections combined. The track is offered within those caps and never asserts that they remain available.

Offered only where every crime the participant wants expunged was charged, or the finding of guilt entered, in one Missouri county. A multi-county record cannot be reached by one petition and is routed to counsel.

releaseBlockers.question: The printed revision and current publication status of CR370, the Judgment and Order of Expungement under § 610.140. The form exists and is published by the Office of the State Courts Administrator — Missouri circuit clerks list it by number and title in their own form indexes — but courts.mo.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval from this environment, so no binary could be acquired and no revision stamp confirmed. Neither the repository corpus nor Master Library Edition 1.1 holds it; the repository's own artifact registry carries a CR370 row recorded as missing. The packet identity does not depend on it, but the proposed-order component cannot be field-mapped or rendered until the original is obtained.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Missouri expungement under § 610.140 is closure under § 610.120, not destruction. The record is closed to public access and specified entities keep access. Never say erased or destroyed on this track. Destruction language is accurate only under § 610.124 on the § 610.122 arrest track.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK 1 - General expungement of convictions, pleas, and trials
provenance.sourceStatement: Correct jurisdiction-specific terminology: "Expungement." In Missouri that means the record is closed from public access, not destroyed. § 610.120 governs what closure means and who retains access. Never say erased or destroyed on this track.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The order does not affect any entity not named as a defendant (§ 610.140.8). The packet builds the best agency list it can from the participant's own records, includes the current CR360 agency categories and free-text lines for others, and prints the warning that an omitted agency keeps its copy.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK 1 - General expungement of convictions, pleas, and trials
provenance.sourceStatement: The agency naming requirement is the single biggest packet-quality risk in Missouri. § 610.140 provides that the court's order does not affect an entity that was not named as a defendant.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The refiling bar appears prominently above the signature block. Under § 610.140.12, if the court finds the petitioner has not met the criteria for any listed crime, or knowingly provided false information, it dismisses the petition and no further petition may be filed until a year has passed since the date the previous petition was filed — measured from the filing date, not from the dismissal.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK 1 - General expungement of convictions, pleas, and trials
provenance.sourceStatement: The form does correctly warn that if the petitioner does not meet all criteria or knowingly provides false information the petition will be dismissed and no new petition may be filed for a year, which is a consequence the participant must understand before signing.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Disclosure survives expungement in six situations and the participant must be told: an application for a licence, certificate or permit issued by Missouri to practise the participant's profession (§ 610.140.10(1)); any licence issued under chapter 313 or permit issued under chapter 571 (§ 610.140.10(2)); paid or unpaid employment with an entity licensed under chapter 313, any state-operated lottery, or any emergency services provider including any law enforcement agency (§ 610.140.10(3)); employment with a federally insured bank, savings institution or credit union or an affiliate, for 12 U.S.C. §§ 1829 and 1785 compliance (§ 610.140.10(4)); employment with an entity engaged in the business of insurance or any insurer, for 18 U.S.C. §§ 1033 and 1034 compliance (§ 610.140.10(5)); employment with any employer required by federal or state law to exclude applicants with certain criminal convictions (§ 610.140.10(6)). Outside those, § 610.140.11 lets the participant answer no to an employer's inquiry where no public record remains.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK 1 - General expungement of convictions, pleas, and trials
provenance.sourceStatement: The mandatory disclosure list, which the participant must be told about: Missouri professional license applications; certain gaming and firearm-related licenses or permits; employment with law enforcement or emergency services; federally insured banks and credit unions; insurance businesses subject to federal law; and employers required by law to exclude applicants with certain convictions.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: An expunged crime may still be considered a prior offense in determining a sentence for any later offense (§ 610.140.9), and the participant must disclose it to any court when asked or on being charged with a subsequent crime. Expungement is not erasure for sentencing purposes.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Where the participant reports a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for drug paraphernalia, the packet must explain the § 610.141 timing trade-off before they file: automatic expungement is free, is due no later than 1 January 2027, and consumes the same lifetime slots, so petitioning now may spend a slot on relief that was about to arrive at no cost. The packet must not promise that automatic relief will reach any particular record.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge Records Related to an Arrest for an Eligible Crime (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.140.7)
tracks.publicName: An arrest that never became a charge
tracks.mechanism: Section 610.140.7 is a distinct petition inside the general expungement section and it was read verbatim from the Revisor's current text. It provides that a petition to expunge records related to an arrest for an eligible crime may be made in accordance with the provisions of the section to a court of competent jurisdiction in the county where the petitioner was arrested no earlier than eighteen months from the date of arrest, provided that during that time the petitioner has not been charged and has not been found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense. Two things follow and both were disputed in the retained review. The waiting period is eighteen months, not three years: the internal LegalEase reference was correct and the secondary source quoting three years was quoting a superseded version. And venue is the county of arrest, which differs from the court-of-charge rule that governs the conviction route. The eleven exclusion categories in § 610.140.3 apply unchanged, because the arrest must be for an eligible crime. Relief is mandatory under § 610.140.8 once the criteria are met, the clerk's notice, the thirty-day objection window, the sixty-day hearing rule and the six-month decision deadline all apply, and the effect is closure under § 610.120. This route is not § 610.122: that is a narrower false-information or qualifying-moving-violation mechanism with a different court, a different division, a fingerprint card, notarization and destruction rather than closure.
exclusions: Class A felonies (§ 610.140.3(1)).
Dangerous felonies as defined in § 556.061 (§ 610.140.3(2)).
Any offense requiring registration as a sex offender (§ 610.140.3(3)).
Any felony offense where death is an element of the offense (§ 610.140.3(4)).
Felony assault offenses, misdemeanor or felony domestic assault offenses, and felony kidnapping (§ 610.140.3(5)).
The specifically enumerated chapter 566 sex offenses and the listed offenses in other chapters (§ 610.140.3(6)).
Offenses eligible under § 610.130, so the first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense occupies its own lane and never routes here (§ 610.140.3(7)).
Intoxication-related traffic offenses and intoxication-related boating offenses, and operating an aircraft with an excessive blood alcohol content or while intoxicated (§ 610.140.3(8)).
Any ordinance violation substantially equivalent to an excluded offense (§ 610.140.3(9)).
Any offense of a motor vehicle law or ordinance committed by a person holding, or required to hold, a commercial driver's license (§ 610.140.3(10)).
Most unlawful use of weapons offenses under § 571.030, subject to the specific statutory exceptions (§ 610.140.3(11)).
Any arrest where the petitioner was charged during the eighteen months following the arrest. § 610.140.7 requires that the petitioner has not been charged during that time.
Any arrest where the petitioner was found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense during the eighteen months following the arrest.
An arrest that became a charge and then a conviction, plea or finding of guilt, which runs on mo-610-140-conviction instead.

An arrest based on false information, or an arrest for a chapter 303 misdemeanor or qualifying moving violation that was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, where the participant seeks destruction rather than closure. Those belong on mo-610-122-arrest-expungement, which is a different statute, court and division and a materially stronger remedy.

waitingPeriods.duration: Eighteen months from the date of arrest. Read verbatim from the current text: the petition may be made no earlier than eighteen months from the date of arrest. The three-year figure circulating in secondary sources is a superseded version and must not be used.
The same eighteen months. During that time the petitioner must not have been charged and must not have been found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense.

tracks.venue: A court of competent jurisdiction in the county where the petitioner was arrested (§ 610.140.7). This is the arrest county, and it is deliberately different from the conviction route's court-of-charge rule. Where the participant was arrested in one county and any charge would have been filed in another, the arrest county controls this petition.

destination.name: Clerk of the circuit court in the Missouri county where the arrest occurred
destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of a court of competent jurisdiction in the county of arrest. The clerk assigns the case number, notices the prosecuting attorney under § 610.140.6, and distributes the order under § 610.140.8. Local practice and fees are confirmed with that clerk.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based. Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record through MACHS. On an arrest that never became a charge this is usually the only document that proves the arrest date, the arresting agency and the offense of arrest, and it is the only search that shows records already closed. Confirm current fees with the Patrol; fingerprint capture carries a separate vendor service fee.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "On what date were you arrested? The eighteen-month waiting period runs from this date." against Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based, and correct the packet if they disagree.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name you may have been arrested under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.
On what date were you arrested? The eighteen-month waiting period runs from this date.
In which Missouri county were you arrested? If the arrest happened inside a municipality, name the municipality too. This petition is filed in the county of arrest.
Which agency arrested you?
What offense were you arrested for, as it appears on the arrest paperwork or on your Highway Patrol record?

Were you ever formally charged in court for this arrest — an information, an indictment, a complaint, a summons or a ticket that opened a court case? If a case was opened, this is not the right route.
Since the date of that arrest, have you been charged with any other criminal offense?
Since the date of that arrest, have you been found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense?

Was the offense you were arrested for a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense requiring sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an equivalent ordinance violation, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Was your arrest based on false information, or was it for a chapter 303 misdemeanor or a moving violation that was later dismissed, nolle prossed or ended in a not-guilty finding? If so there is a stronger Missouri route under § 610.122 that destroys the record rather than closing it, and you should look at that first.

Which agencies do you believe hold records of this arrest? Start with the arresting agency, the county sheriff's department, any municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for the county, the court, and the Missouri Department of Revenue.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Highway Patrol record and your arrest paperwork and confirmed this list is complete?
Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number and the offense level.
The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?
