tracks.legalName: Closure of Official Records on Nolle Prosequi, Dismissal, Acquittal or Suspended Imposition of Sentence (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.105)
tracks.publicName: Cases that already closed by law
tracks.mechanism: Section 610.105 was read in full from the Revisor's current text, effective 28 August 2006, and it is short. Subsection 1 provides that where the imposition of sentence is suspended in the court in which the case originated, or where a case is nolle prossed, dismissed, or the accused is found not guilty, official records pertaining to the case shall thereafter be closed records when the case is finally terminated, except as provided in subsection 2 and in § 610.120, save that the judgment or order of the court remains a public record. Where a not-guilty finding rests on mental disease or defect excluding responsibility under § 552.030, the records close upon that finding and access is limited to law enforcement, child-care agencies, facilities defined in § 198.006 and in-home services providers defined in § 192.2400. Subsection 2 supplies the section's only exception: where the charge is a chapter 566 offense or one of the enumerated offenses in §§ 568.045, 568.050, 568.060, 568.065, 568.175 or 573.200 and 573.205, and the imposition of sentence was suspended, the records shall be made available to the victim for use in the victim's own judicial proceeding, and a minor victim's parent or guardian may request them on the victim's behalf. Nothing in the section contemplates a petition, motion, application, request or filing of any kind by the person whose records close. Closure happens by operation of law on final termination, which for a suspended imposition of sentence means completion of probation. The review's enumeration of the statutory exceptions was left undone on its pass; there is exactly one, and it is a victim-access exception rather than a category of case that fails to close.
exclusions: Any case that has not been finally terminated. For a suspended imposition of sentence that means probation is still running; closure does not occur until it ends.
A conviction, a guilty plea followed by a suspended execution of sentence, or any disposition other than the four in § 610.105.1. Those close only through a § 610.140 petition, if at all.
The judgment or order of the court itself, which § 610.105.1 expressly keeps a public record even after the rest of the file closes.

Not an exception to closure but a limit on it: under § 610.105.2, where the charge was a chapter 566 offense or one of the enumerated offenses in §§ 568.045, 568.050, 568.060, 568.065, 568.175, 573.200 or 573.205 and imposition of sentence was suspended, the records are made available to the victim for use in the victim's own judicial proceeding.
The access § 610.120 preserves for law enforcement, courts, and the other entities that section names. Closure is not invisibility.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Closure operates on final termination of the case. For a nolle prosequi, dismissal or not-guilty finding that is the disposition itself; for a suspended imposition of sentence it is completion of the probation term.

tracks.venue: None. Closure operates by law in the court in which the case originated and at the central repository; there is no filing, so there is no venue. Where the participant needs to verify closure they deal with the clerk of the originating court and with the Missouri State Highway Patrol, neither of which is a filing destination.

destination.name: No participant filing destination — closure by operation of law
destination.detail: Nothing is filed and nothing is submitted. § 610.105 closes the records on final termination without any act by the person whose records they are. The participant's only dealings are informational: a Case.net search, a request to the clerk of the originating court for the docket, and a fingerprint-based criminal record request to the Missouri State Highway Patrol, which is the only search that shows records already closed.

components.conditionDescription: Included where the participant reports that a case appearing to qualify under § 610.105 is still showing publicly on Case.net, on a background check, or on their Highway Patrol record.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified docket sheet and the judgment or order of dismissal. Ask the clerk of the originating court for a certified copy of the docket and of the judgment or order. § 610.105.1 keeps the judgment or order a public record even after the rest of the file closes, so the clerk can supply it. This is the document that tells you which of the four dispositions you actually have.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court in which the case originated

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "How did the case end? Was it dismissed, was it nolle prossed by the prosecutor, were you found not guilty, or did the judge suspend the imposition of sentence and put you on probation?" against Certified docket sheet and the judgment or order of dismissal, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Obtain Case.net printout. Search Case.net for your name and name variants in the county where the case was filed, and print or screenshot what you find, including the date you looked.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Case.net, the Missouri Judiciary's public case management system

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "When you search Case.net for your name, does this case still come up?" against Case.net printout, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based. Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. A name-based search shows only open records, so it cannot tell you whether a case closed — it can only fail to show it. A fingerprint-based search returns closed and complete records for the requesting individual and is the only way to confirm that closure actually happened at the central repository. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Does this case appear on the criminal record you obtained from the Missouri State Highway Patrol?" against Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based, and correct the packet if they disagree.

packetInstructions: Closure is not expungement and the guidance must keep them apart. A closed § 610.105 record leaves the judgment or order a public record, preserves the access § 610.120 grants, and may be reached by a victim under § 610.105.2. A § 610.140 order does more. Telling a participant their case is closed is not telling them it is gone.

Only a fingerprint-based Highway Patrol search shows records that are already closed. A name-based search cannot confirm closure; it can only fail to show the record, which is not the same answer. The guidance must say so or the participant will draw the wrong conclusion from a clean name-based result.
participantQuestions: A suspended imposition of sentence and a suspended execution of sentence are asked apart before anything else. The first closes automatically on completion of probation; the second is a conviction and does not close at all. Participants conflate them constantly and the consequence of getting it wrong is a wasted filing or a missed remedy.

Whether the case still appears on Case.net, on the Highway Patrol record and on any third-party background check are asked separately, because the three are different systems with different remedies and a participant reporting the record is still out there usually means only one of them.
scopeRestrictions: The track covers only the four § 610.105.1 dispositions — nolle prosequi, dismissal, not guilty, and suspended imposition of sentence — plus the § 552.030 mental-disease acquittal. Anything else is routed elsewhere and no closure is asserted for it.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether closure under § 610.105 reaches arresting-agency records and central-repository entries, or only the records of the court in which the case originated. The section speaks of official records pertaining to the case becoming closed records, which is broad, and § 610.120 governs who may still see a closed record; but the section does not enumerate custodians and does not direct any agency to act. It determines what the participant should expect to see on a Highway Patrol record and on a background check, and the review left it open.

openLegalQuestions.question: Whether a participant whose case closed under § 610.105 obtains any material benefit from also petitioning under § 610.140. The two have different effects — closure leaves the judgment a public record and preserves § 610.120 access, while a § 610.140 order restores civil rights, is a complete removal of all effects for 18 U.S.C. § 921(a)(33)(B)(ii) purposes, and directs named entities to close their own records — but § 610.140 consumes a lifetime cap slot and costs a filing fee. The trade-off is real and the guidance presents it as a question rather than a recommendation.

tracks.legalName: Verified Petition for Expungement of Arrest Records (Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 610.122, 610.123 and 610.124)
tracks.publicName: An arrest based on false information
tracks.mechanism: Sections 610.122, 610.123 and 610.124 were read in full from the Revisor's current text and together they are the strongest record-clearing remedy Missouri has. § 610.122, effective 28 August 2021, allows any record of arrest recorded under § 43.503 to be expunged on either of two alternative grounds. The first is that the court determines the arrest was based on false information and that there is no probable cause at the time of the action to expunge to believe the individual committed the offense, no charges will be pursued as a result of the arrest, and the subject did not receive a suspended imposition of sentence for the offense of arrest or any related offense. The second is that the court determines the person was arrested for, or subsequently charged with, a misdemeanor offense of chapter 303 or any moving violation as defined in § 302.010 other than an intoxication-related traffic offense as defined in § 577.023, that each offense or violation related to the arrest was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, and that the person is not a commercial driver's licence holder and was not operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the arrest. § 610.122.2 adds that a record is eligible only if no civil action is pending relating to the arrest or the records sought to be expunged. § 610.123 supplies the procedure and it is unusually specific: a verified petition filed in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest, which shall be dismissed if it does not contain the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, Social Security number and address at the time of arrest, the offense charged, the date of arrest, the county and any municipality of arrest, the arresting agency, the case number and court, and the petitioner's fingerprints on a standard fingerprint card at the time of filing, forwarded to the central repository for the sole purpose of positively identifying the petitioner. The petition names as defendants all law enforcement agencies, courts, prosecuting attorneys, central state depositories and others the petitioner has reason to believe may possess the records, and the court's order does not affect any person or entity not named. The court sets a hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing and gives reasonable notice to each named entity. § 610.123.4 makes relief mandatory on the findings — if the court finds the petitioner is entitled to expungement of any record that is the subject of the petition, it shall enter an order directing expungement — which closes an open question the review could not answer. § 610.124 then requires that all records ordered expunged be destroyed, or blacked out where destruction is not feasible because of the permanent nature of the record books, removed from all electronic files maintained with the State of Missouri, and that the central repository request the Federal Bureau of Investigation to expunge the records from its files. § 610.124.2 gives any petitioner, or agency protesting the expungement, the ordinary civil right of appeal. This is the one Missouri track where the word destroyed is accurate.
exclusions: Any arrest where the subject received a suspended imposition of sentence for the offense of arrest or for any offense related to the arrest (§ 610.122.1(1)(c)). This bars the false-information ground outright.

Any record where a civil action is pending relating to the arrest or to the records sought to be expunged (§ 610.122.2). This is a bar on both grounds and it reaches civil actions the participant may not think of as related.

On the moving-violation ground, any intoxication-related traffic offense or intoxication-related boating offense as defined under § 577.001. Those are excluded expressly and belong on the § 610.130 route if anywhere.
On the moving-violation ground, any person who is a commercial driver's licence holder or who was operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the arrest (§ 610.122.1(2)(b)).
On the moving-violation ground, any offense or violation related to the arrest that was not nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted. Every related offense must have ended that way.
An offense that is neither a chapter 303 misdemeanor nor a moving violation as defined in § 302.010, where the participant is relying on the moving-violation ground rather than on false information.
An arrest that resulted in a conviction, which is not reachable under § 610.122 on either ground and runs on § 610.140 instead.

waitingPeriods.duration: none. Neither § 610.122 nor § 610.123 states a waiting period, and none is implied. What the false-information ground requires instead is a present-tense finding — that there is no probable cause at the time of the action to expunge — so the question is the state of the evidence now rather than the passage of time.

tracks.venue: The civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest (§ 610.123.1). Both the court and the division differ from the § 610.140 routes: this is a civil action, not a criminal-side petition, and it is fixed to the arrest county rather than to the court of charge. Where the arrest occurred in a municipality the municipality is named in the petition but the filing is still in the circuit court's civil division for that county.

destination.name: Civil division of the Missouri circuit court in the county of arrest
destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of the circuit court, civil division, for the county where the arrest occurred. The clerk then does three things the printed instructions on CR145 set out: issues a copy of the petition to the prosecuting attorney; sends a copy of the petition and the fingerprint card to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository at the Highway Patrol; and gives notice of the hearing to the prosecuting attorney and to each official, agency or other entity named in the petition. The court sets the hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing.

components.conditionDescription: Generated where the participant's circuit expects the petitioner to tender a proposed judgment rather than the court preparing it.
Generated only where the participant answers that they cannot pay the filing fee and court costs.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Three standard fingerprint cards. Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: A local law enforcement agency — a municipal police department or county sheriff's department that takes applicant prints

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have you arranged to get three standard fingerprint cards from a local law enforcement agency? You need them before you file." against Three standard fingerprint cards, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Arrest report or booking record. Make an open-records request to the arresting agency for the arrest or booking record. It supplies the date of arrest, the citation number, the offense charged and the agency name, all of which § 610.123 makes mandatory contents of the petition.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The arresting law enforcement agency

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "On what date were you arrested?" against Arrest report or booking record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Certified record of the dismissal, nolle prosequi or not-guilty finding. Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the entry disposing of each offense related to the arrest. The ground requires that every related offense or violation was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, so the participant needs the disposition for each one, not just the lead charge.

If even one is outstanding or resulted in a conviction, this ground does not apply." against Certified record of the dismissal, nolle prosequi or not-guilty finding, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where a charge was filed and the participant is relying on the chapter 303 or moving-violation ground.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based. Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. It is how the participant builds the agency list and confirms the prior-and-subsequent-conviction condition. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

Obtain Missouri Department of Revenue driver record. Order your Missouri driver record. It shows the offense classification and whether a commercial driver licence was ever issued, and commercial licence status at the time of arrest is an outright bar on the moving-violation ground.

Answer for the time of the arrest, not for now." against Missouri Department of Revenue driver record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

participantActionRequired.description: The selection between the two sworn grounds — CR145 page 1, the two checkbox paragraphs.
Any assertion that the arrest was based on false information — CR145 page 1, first ground — recited only from the participant's own words.
Any assertion that there is no probable cause to believe the petitioner committed the offense — CR145 page 1, first ground.
Any assertion that the participant is not a commercial driver licence holder — CR145 page 1, second ground.
The notarial block — the date, the notary's commission expiry and the signature of the notary, judge or clerk — CR145 page 2, subscribed-and-sworn block.

The false-information ground is an unconditional referral. LegalEase records the participant's own account and does not assert that an arrest was based on false information or that probable cause is absent.

A hearing is required on this route and is not by itself a reason to withhold the packet. Self-help ends if the prosecuting attorney or a named agency protests, or if an appeal is taken under § 610.124.2.
postGenerationHandoffs: A hearing is required on this route and is not by itself a reason to withhold the packet. Self-help ends if the prosecuting attorney or a named agency protests, or if an appeal is taken under § 610.124.2.
packetInstructions: This is the one Missouri track where destroyed is accurate. § 610.124 requires records ordered expunged to be destroyed, or blacked out where destruction is not feasible because of the permanent nature of the record books, removed from all Missouri electronic files, with the central repository requesting the Federal Bureau of Investigation to expunge its files. Destruction language must never migrate to a § 610.140 closure.

Filing is in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of arrest — a different court and a different division from the § 610.140 routes. The packet says so plainly, because a participant who files this on the criminal side will be sent away.

The full Social Security number goes on the face of CR145, not only on the confidential cover sheet, because § 610.123.1(1)(f) makes it a mandatory content of the petition and directs dismissal where the information is not given. This is the single exception to Missouri's ordinary rule of confining the number to FI-05, and it exists because the controlling statute and the controlling form both require it.

The clerk's printed distribution steps are reproduced in the participant packet so the participant can check they happened: a copy of the petition to the prosecuting attorney, a copy of the petition and the fingerprint card to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository, and notice of the hearing to the prosecuting attorney and to each entity named.
The order does not affect any person or entity not named as a defendant (§ 610.123.2). The same agency-completeness warning as the § 610.140 routes applies, and the participant verifies the list.

The standard fingerprint card is required before filing and is a mandatory content of the petition under § 610.123.1(7). It is obtained from a local law enforcement agency, three cards are wanted, and it never delays generation of the packet. It is sequenced at the front of the participant's task list.
participantQuestions: Whether any civil action is pending relating to the arrest or the records is asked early and broadly, because § 610.122.2 makes it an outright bar and participants do not think of an insurance dispute or an employment claim as related.
scopeRestrictions: Commercial driver licence holders and anyone operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of arrest are outside the moving-violation ground, and intoxication-related traffic and boating offenses are outside it entirely.

Open question blocks release (packet_components): The printed revision and current publication status of CR143, the Judgment and Order of Expungement of Arrest Record. The form exists and is published by the Office of the State Courts Administrator — Missouri circuit clerks list it by number and title — but courts.mo.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval from this environment, so no binary could be acquired and no revision confirmed. The review did not identify the form at all. Packet identity does not depend on it; field mapping and rendering do.

Open question blocks release (participant_instructions): The current cost of a standard fingerprint card and whether every Missouri local law enforcement agency will produce one. A secondary Missouri pro se guide published in June 2024 records three dollars per card at one metropolitan police department, payable in cash, with a warning that some agencies cannot complete three cards in a visit. That is one agency in one region in one year and is not a statewide figure. The procedure is now known well enough to instruct a participant — a local law enforcement agency, three cards, ring ahead, bring identification — which is what the review's build blocker actually needed; the price is not.

Open question blocks release (correct_form): Whether the current SJRC (04-24) CR145 remains the published revision as of the current date. Master Library Edition 1.1 retains it as a packet-form candidate and it supersedes the OSCA (10-16) copy the review examined. Byte-level confirmation against the publisher could not be made because courts.mo.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval.

Open question blocks release (legal_effect_or_warning): How the § 610.124 blacking-out alternative is presented to a participant. The section requires destruction, and where destruction is not feasible because of the permanent nature of the record books the entries are blacked out instead. The packet cannot say which will happen to any particular record, and a participant told their record will be destroyed and then shown a redacted page will reasonably feel misled. The instructions state both outcomes; whether counsel wants a stronger caveat is open.
One or more official sources have no recorded SHA-256, so staleness cannot be detected.

tracks.legalName: Application for Expungement of a First Intoxication-Related Traffic or Boating Offense (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.130)
tracks.publicName: A first drink-driving or boating offense
tracks.mechanism: Section 610.130 was read in full from the Revisor's current text. It was transferred from former § 577.054 in 2014 and has been effective in its present form since 1 January 2017. Subsection 1 allows an individual who has pleaded guilty to or been convicted of a first intoxication-related traffic offense or intoxication-related boating offense which is a misdemeanor or a county or city ordinance violation, and which is not a conviction for driving a commercial motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol, and who since that date has not been convicted of any intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, to apply after a period of not less than ten years to the court in which he or she pled guilty or was sentenced for an order expunging from all official records all recordations of the arrest, plea, trial or conviction. Subsection 2 makes relief mandatory: if the court determines, after hearing, that the person has not been convicted of any subsequent intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, has no other subsequent alcohol-related enforcement contacts as defined in § 302.525, and has no other such offense or alcohol-related enforcement action pending at the time of the hearing, the court shall enter an order of expungement. Subsection 3 makes the records confidential and available only to the parties or by order of the court for good cause shown, restores the person to the status occupied before the arrest, plea or conviction as if the event had never taken place, supplies a perjury shield, and limits a person to one expungement under the section, while allowing the director to keep records sufficient to enforce that limit. Subsection 4 excludes anyone who has been issued or is required to possess a commercial driver's licence in Missouri or any other state. The section stands entirely apart from § 610.140, which excludes offenses eligible under § 610.130 at subsection 3(7) and intoxication-related traffic and boating offenses generally at subsection 3(8), so the two never overlap and a drink-driving matter must never be routed through the general track. Two points the review left open are now answered. Alcohol-related enforcement contacts is not an open-textured phrase: § 302.525.3 defines it as any suspension or revocation under §§ 302.500 to 302.540, any suspension or revocation entered in Missouri or any other state for a refusal to submit to chemical testing under an implied consent law, and any conviction in Missouri or any other state for a violation involving driving while intoxicated, driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol, or driving a vehicle while having an unlawful alcohol concentration. And relief under this section reaches the administrative side: S.S. v. Mitchell holds that the section authorises a court to expunge the records of a driver's administrative alcohol suspension and to make those records confidential.
authority: S.S. v. Mitchell, 289 S.W.3d 797 (Mo. App. E.D. 2009)
exclusions: Any person who has been issued a commercial driver's licence, or who is required to possess one, in Missouri or any other state (§ 610.130.4). This is a status bar, not an offense bar, and it is asked about current status as well as status at the time of the offense.
A conviction for driving a commercial motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol (§ 610.130.1).
Any felony intoxication-related traffic or boating offense. The section reaches a misdemeanor or a county or city ordinance violation only.
Any person convicted of a subsequent intoxication-related traffic offense or intoxication-related boating offense since the first plea or conviction (§§ 610.130.1 and 2).

Any person with a subsequent alcohol-related enforcement contact as defined in § 302.525.3 — a suspension or revocation under §§ 302.500 to 302.540, a suspension or revocation in any state for refusing chemical testing under an implied consent law, or a conviction in any state for driving while intoxicated, driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol, or driving with an unlawful alcohol concentration.
Any person with an intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, or an alcohol-related enforcement action, pending at the time of the hearing (§ 610.130.2).
Any person who has already had one expungement under this section (§ 610.130.3). It is once in a lifetime and there is no second chance.
An offense that occurred outside Missouri. The application is made to the Missouri court in which the person pled guilty or was sentenced.

waitingPeriods.condition: First intoxication-related traffic or boating offense (§ 610.130.1)
waitingPeriods.duration: Not less than ten years. The section says after a period of not less than ten years an individual who has pleaded guilty or been convicted may apply, so the clock runs from the plea or conviction. During the whole of that period the person must not have been convicted of any intoxication-related traffic or boating offense.

Assessed as at the date of the hearing rather than the date of application: no subsequent intoxication-related traffic or boating conviction, no other subsequent alcohol-related enforcement contact as defined in § 302.525, and no such offense or enforcement action pending at the time of the hearing.

tracks.venue: The court in which the person pled guilty or was sentenced (§ 610.130.1). This is the court of plea or sentence, which for an ordinance violation will often be a municipal division and for a state misdemeanor an associate circuit division. It is not the county of arrest and it is not a freely chosen circuit court.

The court holds a hearing before entering the order; the clerk supplies the local filing rules, the fee and the copy count.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case may be under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What was the offense? Was it a drink- or drug-driving offense, or a boating offense?
Was it charged as a state misdemeanor, or as a county or city ordinance violation? A felony is not eligible under this section.
On what date did you plead guilty or were you sentenced? The ten-year period runs from then.
Which court took your plea or sentenced you — the municipal division, the associate circuit division, or the circuit court — and in which county? That is where this application is filed.
What was the case number?
Was this your first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, anywhere? The section reaches a first offense only.
Since that plea or conviction, have you been convicted of any other drink- or drug-driving offense or intoxication-related boating offense, in Missouri or any other state?

Since then, has your driving licence been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it is the question people most often answer wrongly.
Do you have any drink- or drug-driving charge, boating offense, or licence suspension or revocation proceeding pending right now?

Have you ever been issued a commercial driver's licence, in Missouri or in any other state, or are you required to hold one for your work? This bars the whole section, whether or not it had anything to do with the offense.
Were you driving a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the offense?
Have you ever had an expungement under this section before? You are entitled to only one, ever, and it cannot be undone.

Which agencies do you believe hold records of this matter? Include the court, the arresting agency, the prosecuting or city attorney, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division and the Missouri Department of Revenue.
Have you checked your driver record and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

selfHelpBoundaries: Every intoxication-related matter. The review refers all of them, and the ten-year clean-record showing plus the once-in-a-lifetime consequence make this unsuitable for unassisted self-help; the packet is generated with an attorney-review recommendation on its face.
The driver record shows any suspension, revocation or refusal entry the participant cannot explain.
Any out-of-state licence, conviction, suspension or revocation.
Any commercial driver licence has ever been issued in any state, or the participant's work requires one.
Whether an entry is an alcohol-related enforcement contact under § 302.525.3 is arguable.
The participant is unsure whether the offense was truly their first.
Any intoxication-related matter or enforcement action is pending.
The prosecutor or a named agency opposes, or the court sets a contested hearing.
The participant is weighing whether to spend the one lifetime expungement now or wait.
The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.
The participant asks about the effect on insurance, employment as a driver, or licensing.

Every intoxication-related matter carries an attorney-review recommendation and a contested-hearing handoff on the face of the packet. The ten-year showing turns on a driver record most participants have never read, and getting it wrong spends the one lifetime application.
Self-help ends if the prosecutor or a named agency opposes, or the court sets a contested hearing on any of the three statutory conditions.
postGenerationHandoffs: Self-help ends if the prosecutor or a named agency opposes, or the court sets a contested hearing on any of the three statutory conditions.
packetInstructions: Once in a lifetime, and the warning goes above the signature block. § 610.130.3 entitles a person to only one expungement under the section and lets the director keep records sufficient to enforce the limit. There is no second application.

This section and § 610.140 do not overlap and a drink-driving matter must never be routed through the general track. § 610.140.3(7) excludes offenses eligible under § 610.130 and § 610.140.3(8) excludes intoxication-related traffic and boating offenses generally.

Relief is mandatory on the findings. § 610.130.2 says the court shall enter an order of expungement where the three conditions are met after hearing. The packet must not describe the outcome as discretionary, and a required hearing is not a reason to withhold the packet.

The definition of alcohol-related enforcement contact is reproduced verbatim from § 302.525.3 in the participant materials, because a participant asked whether they have had one will otherwise answer from memory of convictions and miss an administrative suspension entirely.

The Department of Revenue driver record, any out-of-state driver records, the certified docket and the Highway Patrol criminal record are obtained by the participant before filing. None of them delays generation.
participantQuestions: Commercial driver licence status is asked as an ever-held question across every state, not as a question about the offense. § 610.130.4 disapplies the whole section to anyone issued or required to possess a commercial driver's licence in Missouri or any other state.
scopeRestrictions: Offered only for a first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense that was a Missouri misdemeanor or a county or city ordinance violation, where ten years have passed and no commercial driver licence has ever been issued.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether any Missouri circuit or municipal division publishes a local form for a § 610.130 expungement, notwithstanding that the Office of the State Courts Administrator publishes none. Two independent Missouri sources confirm no statewide form exists — the 16th Judicial Circuit's informational sheet says there are no forms provided and the applicant or their attorney must draft and file all pleadings, and a June 2024 pro se guide lists § 610.130 among the statutes with no Missouri court forms prepared. tracks.legalName: Marijuana Expungement, Vacatur and Release from Supervision (Mo. Const. art. XIV, § 2)
tracks.publicName: Clearing a marijuana record
tracks.mechanism: Article XIV, section 2 of the Missouri Constitution is constitutional rather than statutory, which matters because ordinary legislation cannot narrow it. Its expungement provisions were read from the Revisor's current constitutional text and they create three legally different situations rather than one. A person currently incarcerated in a prison, jail or halfway house for a marijuana-related offense that would not have been an offense, or would have been a lesser offense, under sections 1 and 2, or who is serving a sentence for a qualifying marijuana misdemeanor or a class E or class D felony involving three pounds or less, may petition the sentencing court to vacate the sentence, order immediate release or a change in supervision status, and expunge all government records of the case. A person on probation or parole for such an offense has the sentence automatically vacated and supervision terminated without any petition. A person who has completed the sentence is entitled to court-ordered expungement, and the courts were directed to process those cases on a schedule — ninety days for misdemeanor marijuana offenses, one hundred and eighty days for class E felonies and the remaining misdemeanors, and two hundred and seventy days for class D felonies involving three pounds or less and lesser offenses — with class A, B and C felonies expunged on completion of incarceration including any supervised probation or parole. Excluded throughout are offenses involving distribution or delivery to a minor, offenses involving violence, and offenses of operating a motor vehicle while under the influence of marijuana. The effect is the strongest in Missouri: the order is legally effective immediately, the conviction and sentence are vacated as legally invalid, the person is treated in all respects as if he or she had never been arrested, convicted or sentenced, and the court must issue a certificate stating that the offense has been expunged. The state public defender was directed to provide accessible pro se forms and circuit courts to make them readily available; the Office of the State Courts Administrator now publishes SJRC (10-24) CR375 for the purpose, which supersedes the unofficial modified public-defender form in the corpus.
exclusions: Any offense involving distribution or delivery of marijuana to a minor.
Any offense involving violence.
Any offense of operating a motor vehicle while under the influence of marijuana.
A class D felony involving more than three pounds of marijuana.

Class A, B and C marijuana felonies, which are not excluded outright but are expunged only upon completion of incarceration including any period of supervised probation or parole, so a participant still serving is not yet within the completed-sentence branch.

Any offense that would still be an offense of the same grade under Article XIV sections 1 and 2. The eligibility test is what the conduct would be under current law, not what it was called at the time.

waitingPeriods.duration: none. There is no waiting period for a person who has completed the sentence; the courts were directed to process those cases on the ninety, one hundred and eighty and two hundred and seventy day schedules.
none. The petition to the sentencing court may be made while the person is incarcerated, and asks for vacatur, immediate release or a change in supervision status, and expungement.

waitingPeriods.duration: Expungement is ordered upon completion of the person's incarceration, including any period of supervised probation or parole. The trigger is completion of supervision rather than a period of years.

units.label: Court-ordered and automatic Article XIV relief — verification, no participant filing
units.description: The first branch, and it is a legally distinct mechanism rather than a preliminary check. Article XIV, section 2 directs the courts themselves to order expungement for people who have completed their sentences, on constitutional deadlines the courts were given, and automatically vacates the sentence and terminates supervision for a person on probation or parole without any petition at all. For both of those populations there is no participant filing, no application, no request and no form: the constitution puts the act on the court. CR375 confirms the design from the other direction — its two selectable postures are currently incarcerated and not currently incarcerated or on probation, so a participant presently on probation or parole for a marijuana offense fits neither box, because the constitution does not ask them to petition. The unit's output is therefore verification and explanation: identify the marijuana case and the sentencing county, check Case.net and the Highway Patrol record to see whether expungement was already ordered, and, where it was, help the participant ask the court for the certificate of expungement the constitution requires it to issue. Where relief was not entered the participant is routed to the second unit. What the unit must not do is promise that relief occurred: the constitution directed the courts to process these cases, and a direction is not a receipt.

units.label: CR375 petition to the sentencing court under Article XIV, section 2
units.description: The second branch: the participant's own petition on the current statewide form, SJRC (10-24) CR375, filed in the county where the conviction was charged or the finding of guilt entered. It is the required route for a person currently incarcerated for a qualifying marijuana offense, who the constitution says may petition the sentencing court to vacate the sentence, order immediate release or a change in supervision status, and expunge all government records. And it is the fallback for a person who has completed their sentence and for whom the court-directed relief in unit 1 did not happen, which is why the two units are alternatives rather than stages. LegalEase completes the caption, the defendant agency selections, the identity block and the case table, and recites the participant's selection of posture. The relief the form requests — vacatur of the sentence, immediate release from incarceration or other supervision, and expungement of the record of arrest, plea, trial and conviction — is the constitution's own language and is not softened. Where the participant is currently incarcerated or under supervision the packet is generated with a mandatory attorney handoff on its face, because a petition seeking immediate release is a liberty application and not a self-help filing.

tracks.venue: For the petition branch, the county where the conviction was charged or the finding of guilt entered, which is what CR375 states on its face — the marijuana-related convictions listed below occurred and were prosecuted within the state of Missouri and I am filing this petition in the county where the conviction(s) was/were charged or I was found guilty. The review recorded venue as the county of the original sentencing court, taken from the unofficial public-defender form; the official form says court of charge or finding of guilt and the official form controls. For the incarcerated posture the constitution speaks of petitioning the sentencing court, and where the sentencing court and the court of charge differ the participant confirms with the clerk. For the verification branch there is no venue, because there is no filing.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Case.net printout for each marijuana case. Search Case.net for your name and name variants in the county where each case was charged, and print what you find with the date you looked. A case that has been expunged will usually have disappeared from public view, so an absence is evidence — but not proof, because Case.net does not cover every municipal division.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have you checked Case.net and your Highway Patrol record to see whether this case has already been expunged? Missouri courts were directed by the constitution to clear many of these cases without anyone asking, and filing for something you already have wastes your money." against Case.net printout for each marijuana case, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based. Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. It is the only search that shows records already closed, so it is the one that can tell you whether Article XIV relief was already entered. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

generationRequirements.question: Right now, are you in prison, jail or a halfway house for this marijuana case; on probation or parole for it; or have you finished the sentence completely? Missouri treats those three situations differently under the constitution.
What is your full legal name, and any other name the case may be under?
What year were you born? CR375 asks only for the year, not the full date.
CR375 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.
What is your current mailing address, or the address of the facility where you are held?
List each marijuana case: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county where it was charged, and the number and description of the charge.
In which Missouri county was each case charged, or the finding of guilt entered? That is where the petition is filed.
For each case, was the offense a misdemeanor, a class E felony, a class D felony, a class A, B or C felony, or a city or county ordinance violation?
For each case, how much marijuana was involved? Three pounds is the line for a class D felony.
Did any of these cases involve giving or selling marijuana to someone under 21, any violence, or driving while under the influence of marijuana? Any of those is outside this route.

Have you checked Case.net and your Highway Patrol record to see whether this case has already been expunged? Missouri courts were directed by the constitution to clear many of these cases without anyone asking, and filing for something you already have wastes your money.

If the case was already expunged, would you like help asking the court for the certificate of expungement? The constitution requires the court to issue one and it is the document you can show an employer.
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where verification indicates expungement has already been ordered.

generationRequirements.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Include the circuit court division, the county sheriff's department, any municipal police department, the Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division and the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county.
Have you checked your paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?
The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and is not published through Case.net. What is it?

Would what you did still be a crime today under Missouri's marijuana amendment, and if so would it be a lesser offense than what you were convicted of? This is the eligibility test and it is about current law, not about what the charge was called at the time.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Case.net printout for each marijuana case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Case.net, the Missouri Judiciary's public case management system
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Search Case.net for your name and name variants in the county where each case was charged, and print what you find with the date you looked. A case that has been expunged will usually have disappeared from public view, so an absence is evidence — but not proof, because Case.net does not cover every municipal division.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. It is the only search that shows records already closed, so it is the one that can tell you whether Article XIV relief was already entered. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified docket sheet and judgment for each case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the case was charged or the finding of guilt entered
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the docket and the judgment. It supplies the case number, the court, the offense grade and the charge description, and on a marijuana case it is often the only place the quantity appears.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certificate of expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered the expungement order
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where expungement has already been ordered, or after an order is entered on the participant's own petition.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that entered the order for the certificate of expungement. Article XIV, section 2 requires the court to issue a certificate stating that the offense has been expunged. Ask what the fee is and how long it takes. This is the document to keep.

releaseBlockers.question: How a participant currently on probation or parole for a qualifying marijuana offense obtains the automatic vacatur and termination of supervision Article XIV gives them. The constitution says the sentence is vacated and supervision terminated without a petition, and CR375 offers no posture that fits them — its two boxes are currently incarcerated and not currently incarcerated or on probation. If supervision is in fact still running, the participant has a constitutional right nobody has enforced and no form to enforce it with. The unit 1 guidance describes the right and refers to counsel; it does not manufacture a motion.

tracks.legalName: Expungement of Records on Stolen or Mistaken Identity (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.145)
tracks.publicName: You were named for someone else's case
tracks.mechanism: Section 610.145 was read verbatim from the Revisor's current text, effective 28 August 2017, and it contains two mechanisms rather than one. Subsection 1(1) is the petition: where a person is named in a charge for an infraction or offense, whether a misdemeanor or a felony, as a result of another person using the identifying information of the named person or as a result of mistaken identity, and the charges were dismissed or the person was found not guilty, the named person may apply by petition or written motion to the court where the charge was last pending, on a form approved by the office of state courts administrator and supplied by the clerk of the court, for an order expunging from all official records any entries relating to the person's apprehension, charge or trial. The court, after providing notice to the prosecuting attorney, shall hold a hearing and, upon finding that the person's identity was used without permission and the charges were dismissed or the person was found not guilty, shall order the expungement. Subsection 1(2) is the second mechanism and it needs no petition at all: where a person is named in a charge as a result of another person using their identifying information or of mistaken identity and the charge against the named person is dismissed, the prosecutor or other judicial officer who ordered the dismissal shall provide notice to the court of the dismissal, and the court shall order the expungement. Subsection 3 confirms the character of that second route by calling the beneficiary the person eligible for automatic expungement under subdivision (2) of subsection 1. Subsection 3 also directs the court to expunge its own entries and to direct all law enforcement agencies, the department of corrections, the department of revenue or any other state or local government agency identified by the petitioner — or by the person eligible for automatic expungement — to expunge their records, with the clerk notifying state and local agencies, and provides that the costs of expunging the records shall not be taxed against the person eligible for expungement under the section. Subsections 4, 5 and 6 supply substantial ancillary relief that the review did not carry: the department of revenue must expunge its entries, reverse administrative actions including licence points, suspensions and revocations, supply a certified corrected driver history at no cost and reinstate any licence at no cost; the department of corrections and any other agency must do the same and any reinstatement fee is waived; and any insurance company that charged an additional premium on insurance points from the expunged matter must refund those premiums for the three years before the expungement. Subsection 7 defines mistaken identity as erroneous arrest resulting from misidentification by a witness or law enforcement, confusion as to the identity of the person who committed the offense, misinformation provided to law enforcement as to that identity, or some other mistake on the part of a witness or law enforcement. The section is materially different from the § 575.120.4 identity-theft correction route on the CR300 form, which runs on a different statute, in a different court and division, and produces correction of the record to identify the actual defendant rather than expungement of entries relating to the participant.
exclusions: Any case in which the charges against the named person were not dismissed and did not end in a finding of not guilty. Both subdivisions require that outcome; a conviction is outside the section entirely.

Any case in which the participant was correctly identified as the person who committed the offense. The section reaches only a person named as a result of another using their identifying information or of mistaken identity as defined in § 610.145.7.

Where the participant seeks correction of a record so that it identifies the person actually arrested or convicted, rather than expungement of entries relating to themselves. That is § 575.120.4 relief on the CR300 form and is a separate track: it runs in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of arrest, requires a fingerprint card, and is available even where a conviction was entered against the impersonator.
The automatic route in § 610.145.1(2) is limited to a charge that is dismissed. It does not reach a not-guilty finding, which is within the petition route only.

waitingPeriods.duration: none. The section states no waiting period; the trigger is the dismissal or the not-guilty finding.
none. The prosecutor's or judicial officer's duty to notify arises on the dismissal itself.

units.label: Automatic expungement on prosecutor or judicial-officer notice — no participant filing
units.description: The first branch, and the statute itself calls it automatic. Under § 610.145.1(2), where the participant was named in a charge because another person used their identifying information or because of mistaken identity and that charge is dismissed, the prosecutor or other judicial officer who ordered the dismissal shall notify the court and the court shall order the expungement. There is no petition, no motion, no application and no form: the duty is on the prosecutor or the judicial officer, and § 610.145.3 confirms it by describing the beneficiary as the person eligible for automatic expungement under subdivision (2) of subsection 1. That has a direct product consequence, which is why this is a unit rather than a footnote: generating CR301 for a participant whose charge was dismissed on exactly this ground asks a court for relief the law has already told it to enter, and may cost them a filing fee for nothing. The unit's output is verification and explanation — check Case.net and the Highway Patrol record, ask the clerk whether an expungement order was entered on the dismissal, and understand that the participant may still identify agencies for the order to reach, because § 610.145.3 extends that right to the automatic beneficiary as well as to a petitioner. Where the order was not entered, the participant moves to the second unit.

units.label: CR301 petition to the court where the charge was last pending
units.description: The second branch: the participant's own petition or written motion under § 610.145.1(1), on OSCA CR301, filed in the court where the charge was last pending. It is the route where the participant was found not guilty rather than having the charge dismissed, since the automatic route reaches dismissals only; and it is the fallback where the charge was dismissed but the § 610.145.1(2) order was never entered. The form choice is not a preference: § 610.145.1(1) requires the application to be made on a form approved by the office of state courts administrator and supplied by the clerk of the court, so a custom pleading is not available here and official_pdf_fill is the only lawful strategy. CR301 is a single page with a short, factual allegation structure — the review calls it the cleanest form fill in Missouri and that is right. What it does not make easy is the proof: whether the participant's identity was used without permission, or whether a witness or law-enforcement officer made one of the four mistakes § 610.145.7 defines, is the finding the court must make, and the packet recites the participant's own account rather than characterising it.

tracks.venue: The court where the charge was last pending (§ 610.145.1(1)). Where a case moved — from a municipal division to an associate circuit division, or between counties on a change of venue — it is the last court, not the first, and the participant confirms it from the docket. The automatic route has no venue because there is no filing; the court that took the dismissal is the court that orders the expungement.

generationRequirements.question: How did the charge against you end — was it dismissed, or were you found not guilty at trial? If it was dismissed because of the identity problem, Missouri law says the prosecutor or judge should have told the court and the court should have expunged it without you filing anything.

Which happened? Did somebody else use your name, date of birth, Social Security number or other identifying information? Or was it a mistake — a witness or an officer misidentified you, was confused about who committed the offense, or was given wrong information about who it was?
In your own words, what happened? How did your name come to be on this case, and how did you find out?
What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
CR301 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?
What is your full Social Security number? CR301 asks for it on the face of the petition.
What is your driver licence number?
What was your address at the time of the arrest or apprehension?
What offense were you named in?
What was the date of the arrest or apprehension?
Which court was the charge last pending in, and in which county? If the case moved courts, it is the last one that matters.
What was the case number, and was it in the circuit, associate or municipal division?
Have you asked the clerk of that court whether an expungement order was already entered when the charge was dismissed?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant reports the charge was dismissed rather than tried.

generationRequirements.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records naming you on this case? § 610.145 lets you identify them and the order reaches every one you name — law enforcement agencies, the Department of Corrections, the Department of Revenue and any other state or local government agency.

Did this matter affect your driving licence — points, a suspension or a revocation? If so the order requires the Department of Revenue to reverse it and to give you a corrected driving history and a reinstatement at no cost.

Did your insurance premium go up because of insurance points from this matter? If so, the insurer has to refund the extra premium for the three years before the expungement once you notify and verify it.

What proof do you have that this was not you — a police report naming someone else, an identity-theft report, a letter from the prosecutor, a court entry, an alibi record? You do not need it to prepare the petition, but the court will want to see it.

selfHelpBoundaries: The identity theft or mistaken identity requires proof, which the review notes is most cases. LegalEase never holds, inspects or assesses that proof.
The charges were not fully dismissed, or some counts remain.
The participant was convicted of anything arising from the case.
The prosecuting attorney disputes the identity account, or the court sets a contested hearing.

The participant wants the record corrected to name the person who actually committed the offense, rather than expunged as to themselves. That is the § 575.120.4 route on CR300, in a different court and division.
The participant is pursuing a civil claim against anyone arising from the identity theft.
The impersonator is a family member, which changes both the evidence and the advice.
The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.
The participant asks whether they can recover losses from the identity theft.

Disputed identity evidence goes to counsel. The review refers where the identity theft or mistaken identity requires proof, which is most cases, and that position is preserved: LegalEase never holds, inspects or assesses the proof and never asserts the finding.

A hearing is mandatory on this route — § 610.145.1(1) says the court shall hold one — and that is not a reason to withhold the packet. Self-help ends if the prosecuting attorney disputes the account or the court sets a contested hearing.
postGenerationHandoffs: A hearing is mandatory on this route — § 610.145.1(1) says the court shall hold one — and that is not a reason to withhold the packet. Self-help ends if the prosecuting attorney disputes the account or the court sets a contested hearing.
packetInstructions: Automatic relief runs first. Where the charge was dismissed on identity grounds the packet checks whether the § 610.145.1(2) order was already entered before offering a petition, because a participant who files for relief the court was already obliged to enter pays for nothing.

The costs of expunging the records are not taxed against the person eligible for expungement (§ 610.145.3), and any licence or privilege reinstatement fee is waived (§ 610.145.5). The packet tells the participant so, and tells them to raise it with the clerk if a fee is demanded.

The ancillary relief in §§ 610.145.4 to 6 is set out in full, because it is unusually broad and participants do not know to ask for it: Department of Revenue expungement, reversal of administrative actions including licence points, suspensions and revocations, a certified corrected driver history at no cost, licence reinstatement at no cost, Department of Corrections and other-agency expungement and reversal, and an insurer's obligation to refund three years of additional premium charged on insurance points from the matter.
Venue is the court where the charge was last pending, which on a case that moved is not the court it started in. The packet says so and directs the participant to the docket.
The certified docket, the proof of the identity problem and the driver record are obtained by the participant before filing. LegalEase never holds or assesses any of them, and none delays generation.
participantQuestions: Whether the charge was dismissed or ended in a not-guilty finding is asked before anything is generated, because the automatic route reaches dismissals only and the answer decides which unit applies.
scopeRestrictions: Offered only where the charges were dismissed or the participant was found not guilty. A conviction, even one obtained against an impersonator, is outside this section and belongs on the § 575.120.4 correction route.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Correction of Arrest/Court Records on False Impersonation (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 575.120.4, procedure under § 610.123)
tracks.publicName: Correcting a record created by identity theft
tracks.mechanism: The review recorded the statutory basis and scope of CR300 as not established and made it the track's build blocker. It is now established, from the official form's own face and from the statute it cites. CR300 states: Pursuant to sections 575.120.4 and 610.123, RSMo, I hereby request that the court issue an order to expunge the following arrest and court records that falsely identify me and to correct the arrest and court records to accurately reflect the identity of the defendant. Its footer carries the same two citations. § 575.120 is the false impersonation offense, and subsection 4 supplies the victim's civil remedy: any person who is the victim of a false impersonation and whose identity has been falsely reported in arrest or conviction records may move for expungement and correction of those records under the procedures set forth in § 610.123, and upon a showing that a substantial number of identifying factors of the victim was falsely ascribed to the person actually arrested or convicted, the court shall order the false identifying factors contained in the arrest and court records amended to correctly and accurately identify the defendant and shall expunge the incorrect and inaccurate factors from the arrest and court records. That single provision answers every question the review left open. The relief is correction plus targeted expungement of the false identifying factors, not expungement of the case. The proof is a substantial number of identifying factors falsely ascribed, which is a different and in some ways lower showing than § 610.145's identity-used-without-permission finding. Relief is mandatory on that showing: the court shall order. The procedure is § 610.123's, which means a verified petition in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest, the eleven mandatory contents whose absence requires dismissal, the standard fingerprint card filed with the petition and forwarded to the central repository, defendants named with the order reaching only those named, and a hearing set no sooner than thirty days from filing with reasonable notice to each named entity. And critically the section reaches arrest or conviction records: unlike § 610.145 it does not require that the charge against the participant was dismissed or that they were acquitted, because the point is that somebody else was arrested or convicted under the participant's identity. The adopted Batch 2 memorandum's direction to keep this route separate from CR301 is therefore not merely preserved but strengthened: they are different statutes, different courts, different divisions, different proof and different remedies. The memorandum's primary-authority line cites § 610.145 for both forms; the form's own citation controls and is recorded as a correction.
exclusions: A person who was not the victim of a false impersonation. § 575.120.4 opens the remedy to the victim of a false impersonation whose identity has been falsely reported in arrest or conviction records, so the predicate is that someone else used the participant's identity.
A record in which the participant's own identifying factors were correctly ascribed to the participant. The remedy corrects false identifying factors, so there must be something false to correct.
A showing that does not reach a substantial number of identifying factors falsely ascribed to the person actually arrested or convicted. A single coincident name is unlikely to meet it.

A case where the participant was themselves named in a charge because of misidentification by a witness or officer and the charge was dismissed or they were acquitted. That is § 610.145 relief on CR301, in the court where the charge was last pending, and it expunges entries relating to the participant rather than correcting the record to name someone else.

Federal records, which no Missouri court order reaches directly, although § 610.124 requires the central repository to ask the Federal Bureau of Investigation to expunge records expunged under § 610.123.

generationRequirements.question: In your own words, what happened? Somebody else appears to have been arrested or convicted using your name or your identifying information. How did you find out, and what do you know about who it was?

Which of your identifying details appear on the record that is not yours — your name, date of birth, Social Security number, driver's licence number, address, or others? List every one, because the court has to find that a substantial number of your identifying factors were falsely ascribed to the person actually arrested or convicted.
What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
CR300 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?
What is your full Social Security number? On this route the law requires it on the face of the petition — § 610.123 says the petition shall be dismissed if it is not given.
What is your driver licence number?
What was your address at the time of the arrest recorded against your name? If you do not know, give the address you were living at then.
What offense is recorded against your name?
What is the date of the arrest recorded against your name?
In which Missouri county did that arrest occur, and if it was in a municipality, which one? This petition is filed in the circuit court for that county.
Which agency made the arrest?
What is the arrest citation number, if you know it?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant has obtained the arrest record.

generationRequirements.question: Was there a conviction on that record, and if so on what date? Unlike the mistaken-identity route, this one is available even where a conviction was entered — because it was entered against someone else.
What was the case number, which court and which division — circuit, associate or municipal?

If you know who used your identity, what are their full name, sex, race, date of birth, Social Security number and driver's licence number? Give only what you actually know. CR300 has a block for this and the court's order is meant to correct the record to name them.
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant reports knowing or believing they know who used their identity.

generationRequirements.question: Do you know the person who used your identity — is it a family member, a former partner, or someone else you know? This changes both what evidence exists and what you should do next.

Which agencies hold the record that falsely identifies you? Include the court division, the arresting agency, the county sheriff's department, any municipal police department, the Highway Patrol troop, the Missouri Criminal Records Repository and the prosecutor's office.
The court's order will not reach any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?
Have you arranged to get three standard fingerprint cards from a local law enforcement agency? You need them before you file, and on this route they are the strongest evidence you have.
Have you reported the identity theft to the police, or filed a Federal Trade Commission identity-theft report?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

selfHelpBoundaries: The impersonator is a family member, a former partner or someone else known to the participant, which changes both the available evidence and what the participant should do next.
A conviction was entered under the participant's identity, particularly where a sentence was served or supervision imposed.
The participant has been arrested, detained or denied employment, housing or a licence because of the false record.
The prosecuting attorney or a named agency disputes the account, or the court sets a contested hearing.
The participant is unsure whether their situation is false impersonation under § 575.120 or mistaken identity under § 610.145, because the two run in different courts on different forms.
The record appears on a private background check after the court order, which a Missouri court order does not reach.
The participant is contemplating a civil claim against the impersonator or against an agency.
There are false records in more than one Missouri county, or in another state.
The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.
The participant cannot obtain fingerprint cards from any local agency.

Whether a substantial number of the participant's identifying factors was falsely ascribed is the court's finding and LegalEase never asserts it. Where the impersonator is known to the participant, or where a conviction and sentence were entered, the packet refers out before it is generated.
A hearing is required and is not a reason to withhold the packet. Self-help ends if the prosecuting attorney or a named agency disputes the account, or the court sets a contested hearing.
postGenerationHandoffs: A hearing is required and is not a reason to withhold the packet. Self-help ends if the prosecuting attorney or a named agency disputes the account, or the court sets a contested hearing.
packetInstructions: This route corrects a record so that it identifies the person actually arrested or convicted, and expunges the incorrect and inaccurate identifying factors. It does not make the case disappear. The packet says so plainly, because a participant told their record will be expunged and then shown the case still existing under someone else's name will reasonably feel misled.

This track is kept separate from the § 610.145 mistaken-identity route and the two are never substituted for one another. Different statute, different court, different division, different proof, different remedy — and only this one is available where a conviction was entered under the participant's identity.

Filing is in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of arrest, which CR300 recites on its face. A participant who takes this to the court where the case was heard, as they would for a mistaken-identity petition, will be in the wrong place.

A Missouri court order does not reach a private background-check database or a credit file. The packet routes the participant to the ordinary consumer identity-theft remedies alongside the court filing and says plainly that they are different problems with different fixes.

The full Social Security number goes on the face of CR300 because § 610.123.1(1)(f) makes it a mandatory content whose absence requires dismissal, and the impersonator's identifying details may appear too where the participant knows them. The confidentiality of the filing therefore matters more on this route than anywhere else in the Missouri set, and the packet says so.

The standard fingerprint card is a mandatory content of the petition under § 610.123.1(7) and is obtained before filing from a local law enforcement agency. On this route it is also the participant's best evidence, because a fingerprint is the one identifier an impersonator cannot borrow. It never delays generation.
scopeRestrictions: Offered only where the participant reports that another person's arrest or conviction was recorded under their identity. Where the participant was themselves named because a witness or officer misidentified them and the charge was dismissed or they were acquitted, the route is § 610.145 on CR301.
