tracks.legalName: Application for Expungement of a First Minor-in-Possession Violation (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 311.326)
tracks.publicName: An underage drinking charge
tracks.mechanism: Section 311.326 was read in full from the Revisor's current text, effective 28 August 2009, and it is a single unnumbered paragraph that does a great deal of work. After a period of not less than one year after reaching the age of twenty-one, a person who has pleaded guilty to or been found guilty of violating § 311.325 for the first time, and who since that conviction has not been convicted of any other alcohol-related offense, may apply to the court in which he or she was sentenced for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, plea, trial and conviction. No records shall be expunged if the person is licensed as a commercial motor vehicle driver or was operating a commercial motor vehicle as defined in § 302.700 at the time of the violation. If the court determines, upon review, that the person has not been convicted of any other alcohol-related offense at the time of the application and has had no other alcohol-related enforcement contacts as defined in § 302.525, the court shall enter an order of expungement. The effect is to restore the person to the status occupied before the arrest, plea or conviction as if the event had never happened, with a perjury shield. A person is entitled to only one expungement under the section, and courts and other state officials may keep records necessary to enforce that limit. Three points are worth drawing out because the review left them open or unstated. Relief is mandatory: the court shall enter the order. The section says upon review rather than after hearing, which distinguishes it from § 610.130 and suggests no hearing is required, although it does not forbid one. And the alcohol-related enforcement contact condition borrows the same § 302.525.3 definition as § 610.130 — any suspension or revocation under §§ 302.500 to 302.540, any suspension or revocation in any state for refusing chemical testing under an implied consent law, and any conviction in any state involving driving while intoxicated, driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol, or driving with an unlawful alcohol concentration — so a participant with an administrative licence suspension that never became a conviction is ineligible even though nothing in the phrase alcohol-related offense would tell them so.
exclusions: Any violation other than a first violation of § 311.325. The section reaches a person who pleaded guilty to or was found guilty of violating that section for the first time.
Any person convicted of any other alcohol-related offense since the § 311.325 conviction.

Any person who has had any other alcohol-related enforcement contact as defined in § 302.525 — a suspension or revocation under §§ 302.500 to 302.540, a suspension or revocation in any state for refusing chemical testing under an implied consent law, or a conviction in any state involving driving while intoxicated, driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol, or driving with an unlawful alcohol concentration.
Any person licensed as a commercial motor vehicle driver, or who was operating a commercial motor vehicle as defined in § 302.700 at the time of the violation.
Any person who has already had one expungement under this section (§ 311.326). It is once in a lifetime.
Any person who has not yet reached the age of twenty-two, since the application may be made only after a period of not less than one year after reaching the age of twenty-one.
A municipal or county ordinance violation for underage possession that was not a violation of § 311.325 itself. The section names the state statute.

waitingPeriods.duration: Not less than one year after reaching the age of twenty-one. The trigger is the participant's age, not the date of the offense or the conviction, so the earliest possible application is at twenty-two regardless of when the violation occurred.

tracks.venue: The court in which the person was sentenced (§ 311.326). For a § 311.325 violation that will usually be an associate circuit division, and it may be a municipal division where the case was heard there. It is the sentencing court, which on a case transferred or certified elsewhere may not be the court where the charge was first filed.

destination.name: Clerk of the Missouri court in which the participant was sentenced
destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of the court that imposed the sentence. § 311.326 prescribes no notice recipients, no objection period and no hearing — it says the court determines the conditions upon review — so the local clerk's practice governs whether an application opens a new case, whether a cover sheet is required and whether the prosecuting or city attorney is noticed.

components.conditionDescription: Generated where the application opens a new case rather than proceeding under the original case number, and where the sentencing court requires the sheet.
Generated only where the participant answers that they cannot pay the filing fee and court costs, and the sentencing court accepts the statewide form.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified docket sheet and judgment from the sentencing court. Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the docket and the judgment. It establishes the statute of conviction — which must be § 311.325 rather than a local ordinance — the sentencing date and the case number.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that imposed the sentence

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Was the charge a violation of Missouri's minor-in-possession law, § 311.325? If you were charged under a city or county ordinance instead of the state statute, this route may not apply." against Certified docket sheet and judgment from the sentencing court, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Missouri Department of Revenue driver record. Order your Missouri driver record. It is where an administrative alcohol-related suspension or revocation appears, and § 302.525.3 makes any such action an enforcement contact that disqualifies you under § 311.326 even though it was never a criminal conviction. A participant answering this question from memory of court cases will very often be wrong.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Has your driving licence ever been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it disqualifies you from this expungement." against Missouri Department of Revenue driver record, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Obtain Out-of-state driver records. Request your driver record from each state where you have been licensed. § 302.525.3 counts a suspension, revocation or conviction in any other state.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The licensing authority of each other state where the participant has held a licence
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where the participant has held a driving licence outside Missouri.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Has your driving licence ever been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it disqualifies you from this expungement." against Out-of-state driver records, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where the participant has held a driving licence outside Missouri.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record. Order your own criminal record. It supports the agency list and the no-other-alcohol-related-offense condition. Confirm current fees with the Patrol.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Since that conviction, have you been convicted of any other alcohol-related offense, anywhere?" against Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, and correct the packet if they disagree.
The FI-05 case type code, where a cover sheet is required — FI-05, case type code and description.
The case number in the caption — Application, proposed order and cover-sheet captions.
The applicant's signature and date — Application, below the declaration under penalty of perjury.
The judge's determination, granting language, date and signature — Proposed Order of Expungement.
Any assertion that a particular licence action was or was not an alcohol-related enforcement contact — Not present in the packet at all.
Any assertion that the violation was the participant's first — Recited on the application only as the participant's own sworn allegation.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case may be under?
What is your date of birth? The application cannot be made until at least a year after you turned twenty-one.
What is your current mailing address?
Was the charge a violation of Missouri's minor-in-possession law, § 311.325? If you were charged under a city or county ordinance instead of the state statute, this route may not apply.
Was this the first time you pleaded guilty to or were found guilty of that offense?
Which court sentenced you, and in which county? That is where this application is filed.
On what date were you sentenced, and what was the case number?
Since that conviction, have you been convicted of any other alcohol-related offense, anywhere?

Has your driving licence ever been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it disqualifies you from this expungement.
Are you licensed as a commercial motor vehicle driver, or were you driving a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the violation? Either one bars this route.
Have you ever had an expungement under this section before? You are entitled to only one, ever.

Which agencies do you believe hold records of this matter? Include the sentencing court, the agency that arrested or cited you, the prosecuting or city attorney and the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division.
Have you checked your Highway Patrol record and your court paperwork and confirmed this list is complete?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

tracks.legalName: State-Initiated Automatic Expungement of Eligible Drug Offenses (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.141, enacted by CCS SS SB 1421, 2026)
tracks.publicName: Drug records that clear themselves
tracks.mechanism: The review's headline finding was that Missouri had passed Clean Slate provisions ten weeks earlier and that it could not confirm whether the Governor had signed the bill. That is now resolved from the enrolled text and the Governor's own record. Conference Committee Substitute for Senate Substitute for Senate Bill No. 1421, 103rd General Assembly, Second Regular Session, truly agreed to and finally passed as file 5940S.07T, was approved by Governor Mike Kehoe on 9 July 2026. It repeals fifty-four sections and enacts sixty-eight in lieu thereof, three of which are new chapter 610 sections: 610.141, 610.143 and 610.144. § 610.140 is not among the repealed sections and was not amended. § 610.141 is the mechanism. It defines an eligible offense as one that is a qualifying offense, is a final conviction, is the only charge of conviction in a case or part of a case containing only qualifying convictions, is one year past final disposition for a misdemeanor or three years for a felony, belongs to an offender with no misdemeanor or felony conviction within that same period excluding traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307, belongs to an offender with no outstanding arrest or pending charges at the time of analysis, and is not a class A felony. A qualifying offense is a conviction for possession of a controlled substance under § 195.202 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, unlawful use of drug paraphernalia under § 195.233 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, possession or control of a controlled substance under § 579.015, or unlawful possession of drug paraphernalia under § 579.074 — four offenses, nothing wider. Expungement is defined as closure of the record pursuant to § 610.120, so the legal effect is closure and not destruction. Final disposition means completion of all court-imposed terms and conditions and unconditional release from custody. Subsection 2 provides that all eligible offenses shall automatically be expunged as a matter of law upon eligibility and applies the section retroactively to any arrest, charge, trial or conviction for which there is an electronic record regardless of date. Subsection 3 puts the work on the central repository — the Missouri State Highway Patrol — which must screen the statewide criminal history database on a rolling basis not less than once per week, expunge eligible offenses, reflect the expungement through the Missouri uniform law enforcement system, rerun the analysis if further information is learned, and send the Supreme Court of Missouri a weekly list of changes. Subsection 4 requires the repository to notify the Office of the State Courts Administrator of its designations, makes the corresponding case records in the statewide court automation system confidential, and directs the Office of the State Courts Administrator to expunge those case records based only on the information in that system and the repository's designations. No participant submits anything at any point. Subsection 6 is the coordination answer the review flagged as a build blocker: an offender is limited to three misdemeanor and two felony expungements under this section and § 610.140 combined, and where a case contains more than one expungable offense only the highest-level offense counts. Subsection 7 preserves the right to file an expungement petition under any other law, and subsection 8 provides that notwithstanding any other provision of law the sole remedy for failure to expunge under the section is the filing of a § 610.140 petition. Subsection 10 is the timing provision: the provisions of the section shall be effective when technically feasible for both the Office of the State Courts Administrator and the central repository, but no later than 1 January 2027. Subsection 11 requires the Patrol to give consumer reporting agencies information sufficient to identify and delete records of expunged offenses, under an agreement restricting use and requiring destruction. Subsection 12 directs the Office of the State Courts Administrator, the Department of Corrections and the Patrol jointly to develop an explanatory document to be given at sentencing and on release from supervision. Subsection 9 requires annual statistical reporting to legislative committees beginning 1 January 2028. § 610.143 bars continued reporting of arrests, indictments and convictions once a pardon or expungement is known, gives the Attorney General enforcement powers and consumers injunctive relief, immunises employers, volunteer organisations and landlords who engage a person whose record was expunged absent a failure of reasonable care, and preserves mandatory disclosure for banking, insurance and § 610.120 contexts. § 610.144 creates the Missouri Expungement Fund to pay for the technology.

Trafficking, distribution, delivery, manufacture and every other drug offense are outside the section.

generationRequirements.question: Is the conviction for possessing a controlled substance, or for drug paraphernalia? Missouri's automatic expungement law reaches only those four offenses — it does not reach trafficking, distribution, delivery or manufacture.
Was it a misdemeanor or a felony? And if a felony, was it a class A felony? A class A felony is excluded.
On what date did you finish everything the court ordered and were released from any custody or supervision? The law calls that final disposition, and the one-year or three-year clock runs from it.
Was this the only conviction in that case? If the same case included a conviction for something that is not one of the four covered offenses, the automatic law does not reach any of it.
Since that date, have you been convicted of any misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any outstanding arrest, warrant or pending criminal charge right now?

Have you had any Missouri expungement before, under any law? From the date the automatic law starts operating, automatic expungements and petition expungements share the same lifetime limits — three misdemeanors and two felonies between them.

Do you need this record cleared by a particular date — for a job, a licence, housing or an immigration matter? The automatic mechanism has no published start date beyond a 1 January 2027 outer limit and cannot be relied on for a deadline.

Knowing that a petition under § 610.140 is available now but costs a filing fee and uses one of your lifetime slots, and that automatic relief is free but not yet shown to be running and uses the same slot, would you like to talk through which makes sense for you?

packetInstructions: The scope is four offenses, not a category. § 610.141 reaches possession of a controlled substance under § 195.202 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, unlawful use of drug paraphernalia under § 195.233 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, possession or control of a controlled substance under § 579.015, and unlawful possession of drug paraphernalia under § 579.074. Trafficking, distribution, delivery and manufacture are outside it, and Missouri must never be described as a general clean-slate state.

Automatic expungement consumes a lifetime slot. § 610.141.6 limits an offender to three misdemeanor and two felony expungements under §§ 610.140 and 610.141 combined, counting only the highest-level offense where a case contains more than one. This closes the review's cap-coordination build blocker and belongs on the § 610.140 packet as well as this one.

The relief is closure of the record under § 610.120, which § 610.141.1(4) says in terms. It is the same legal effect as a § 610.140 order, not destruction, and the packet must not describe it as erasure.

The participant must be told the uncertainty and the alternative together. The section operates when technically feasible and no later than 1 January 2027, no implementation notice has been published, and a § 610.140 petition is available now. Telling a participant to wait for future relief without explaining both is not acceptable.

The sole remedy for a failure to expunge is a § 610.140 petition, which § 610.141.8 provides notwithstanding any other provision of law. There is no appeal to the Highway Patrol and no correction application, and the guidance routes a participant whose record was missed to the petition track rather than to an agency.

Secondary summaries of Missouri clean slate must not be used. The enacted § 610.141 is narrower than the press coverage and differs materially from SB 1494, the broader vehicle that did not become law but whose text is widely conflated with it — including a bulk-processing deadline that appears nowhere in the enacted section. Only the enrolled CCS SS SB 1421 text governs.
participantQuestions: Urgency is asked directly, because a participant who needs a record cleared by a fixed date cannot rely on a mechanism with no published start date, and that answer alone may settle the timing decision.
scopeRestrictions: The route is runtime-disabled as legislative and implementation monitoring rather than as participant-facing relief, until the Office of the State Courts Administrator or the Missouri State Highway Patrol publishes an implementation notice showing the mechanism is operating. That is an operational release gate, not an unanswered question about whether the law exists.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether § 610.141 is yet operating. Subsection 10 makes the section effective when technically feasible for both the Office of the State Courts Administrator and the central repository, but no later than 1 January 2027. Neither body has published an implementation notice, eligibility instructions, a form, a portal, a schedule or verification guidance that could be located, and the Highway Patrol's Criminal Records and Identification Division pages say nothing about automatic expungement, clean slate or § 610.141. The mechanism is enacted; it is not shown to be operating. The adopted memorandum makes an administering-agency implementation notice a condition of releasing this route, and that condition is not met.

provenance.sourceStatement: Do not release a track based on a passed bill, sponsor statement, or implementation projection. Require an official signed-act/chapter citation, current codified text, effective date, and administering-agency implementation notice. Until those are in the source bundle, keep the node disabled as legislative monitoring, not participant-facing relief.

releaseBlockers.question: The precise general effective date of § 610.141 as an enactment, as distinct from the operational trigger in subsection 10. CCS SS SB 1421 carries an emergency clause at Section B, but it applies only to the enactment of §§ 589.900 and 589.902 and the repeal and reenactment of § 577.800, and there is no general effective-date section. The remaining sections therefore take effect on the ordinary Missouri constitutional date for an act of a session that adjourned on 15 May 2026, which is 28 August 2026. The distinction matters because subsection 10 then conditions the section's provisions on technical feasibility with a 1 January 2027 outer limit, so enactment, effectiveness and operation are three different dates and the participant-facing statement must use the right one.

provenance.sourceStatement: Implementation date: By January 1, 2027, or as soon as feasible for MSHP and the Office of the State Courts Administrator.

releaseBlockers.question: How a participant learns that an automatic expungement has occurred. The section provides no notice to the person whose record is expunged: the repository notifies the Supreme Court and the Office of the State Courts Administrator, and § 610.141.12's explanatory document is given at sentencing or on release from supervision rather than when relief arrives. The only practical check is a fingerprint-based Highway Patrol record the participant pays for. That is a real gap in a scheme whose whole premise is that people should not have to act.

provenance.sourceStatement: Monitor the implementation date.
provenance.counselQuestion: Does any Missouri body notify a person that their record has been expunged under § 610.141, or is a paid fingerprint-based criminal record check the only way to find out? If the latter, what should the packet tell participants about how often to check?

releaseBlockers.question: How the § 610.141.6 shared cap operates in time. The subsection limits an offender to three misdemeanor and two felony expungements under § 610.141 and § 610.140 combined, and § 610.140.13 as it stands counts only expungements granted under § 610.140. Whether a § 610.140 petition granted before § 610.141 becomes operative counts against the combined limit, and whether the repository can see prior § 610.140 expungements when it runs its analysis, are not addressed. It matters directly: a participant with two prior § 610.140 felony expungements may or may not be within the combined felony cap.

provenance.sourceStatement: Whether automatic expungements count against the § 610.140 lifetime caps.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether the § 610.143 consumer-reporting and employer-immunity provisions apply to expungements granted under § 610.140 as well as under § 610.141. § 610.143 speaks generally of records for which a full pardon or expungement has been granted, and sits between the two, but is enacted in the same act as the automatic mechanism. If it reaches § 610.140 orders it is a substantial and previously unavailable participant-facing benefit that belongs in the § 610.140 packet instructions as well, and the packet does not currently assert it there.

provenance.sourceStatement: Whether the relief is closure under § 610.120 or something stronger.

openLegalQuestions.question: Whether a participant may opt out of, accelerate or request an automatic expungement. Nothing in § 610.141 provides for any of the three, and subsection 8 forecloses the obvious alternative by making a § 610.140 petition the sole remedy for a failure to expunge. The narrow reading is that there is no opt-out and no acceleration, and the packet applies it; the review's open question is answered on that basis rather than left open, but the absence of any provision is not the same as an express prohibition.

Open question blocks release (governing_mechanism): Whether § 610.141 is yet operating. Subsection 10 makes the section effective when technically feasible for both the Office of the State Courts Administrator and the central repository, but no later than 1 January 2027. Neither body has published an implementation notice, eligibility instructions, a form, a portal, a schedule or verification guidance that could be located, and the Highway Patrol's Criminal Records and Identification Division pages say nothing about automatic expungement, clean slate or § 610.141. The mechanism is enacted; it is not shown to be operating. The adopted memorandum makes an administering-agency implementation notice a condition of releasing this route, and that condition is not met.

Open question blocks release (legal_effect_or_warning): The precise general effective date of § 610.141 as an enactment, as distinct from the operational trigger in subsection 10. CCS SS SB 1421 carries an emergency clause at Section B, but it applies only to the enactment of §§ 589.900 and 589.902 and the repeal and reenactment of § 577.800, and there is no general effective-date section. The remaining sections therefore take effect on the ordinary Missouri constitutional date for an act of a session that adjourned on 15 May 2026, which is 28 August 2026. The distinction matters because subsection 10 then conditions the section's provisions on technical feasibility with a 1 January 2027 outer limit, so enactment, effectiveness and operation are three different dates and the participant-facing statement must use the right one.

Open question blocks release (participant_instructions): How a participant learns that an automatic expungement has occurred. The section provides no notice to the person whose record is expunged: the repository notifies the Supreme Court and the Office of the State Courts Administrator, and § 610.141.12's explanatory document is given at sentencing or on release from supervision rather than when relief arrives. The only practical check is a fingerprint-based Highway Patrol record the participant pays for. That is a real gap in a scheme whose whole premise is that people should not have to act.

Open question blocks release (eligibility_branch): How the § 610.141.6 shared cap operates in time. The subsection limits an offender to three misdemeanor and two felony expungements under § 610.141 and § 610.140 combined, and § 610.140.13 as it stands counts only expungements granted under § 610.140. Whether a § 610.140 petition granted before § 610.141 becomes operative counts against the combined limit, and whether the repository can see prior § 610.140 expungements when it runs its analysis, are not addressed. It matters directly: a participant with two prior § 610.140 felony expungements may or may not be within the combined felony cap.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge the Record of a Case That Did Not End in Conviction (Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-71(4))
tracks.publicName: Clearing a case that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Section 99-19-71(4), read from the enrolled text of 2026 HB 1546 which reenacts the whole section effective 1 July 2026, provides: 'Upon petition therefor, a justice, county, circuit or municipal court shall expunge the record of any case in which an arrest was made, the person arrested was released and the case was dismissed or the charges were dropped or there was no disposition of such case, or the person was found not guilty at trial.' Relief is MANDATORY on the statutory language — the court 'shall expunge' — which makes this one of very few mandatory record-clearing provisions in the country and the headline of the Mississippi product. There is no offence list, no waiting period, no completion requirement, no pending-charge restriction and no first-offender requirement in subsection (4). It is the broadest relief in Mississippi. Crucially, the one-felony-per-lifetime cap sits in subsection (2)(a) and applies to felony CONVICTION expungement only, so a participant who uses this track has not spent their one felony expunction. Section 99-19-71(3) governs the effect: a nonpublic record is retained by the Mississippi Criminal Information Center solely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings, a district attorney's office may retain a nonpublic record for law enforcement purposes, an employer may still ask whether an order of expunction has been entered, the person is restored in contemplation of law to the status occupied before arrest or indictment, and the person is not guilty of perjury for failing to recite the arrest except when first-offender status is being determined.
exclusions: None stated in subsection (4). There is no offence list, no waiting period and no first-offender requirement on this track.
A conviction. A case that ended in a conviction belongs on the first-offender misdemeanour track, the felony track, or one of the special-route tracks.
A nonadjudication dismissal, whose routing between § 99-15-26 and § 99-19-71(4) is unresolved and which is handled on its own track rather than pleaded here.
A pretrial-intervention or intervention-court completion, which produces its own disposition and is handled on the diversion node.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Subsection (4) imposes no waiting period, no completion requirement and no clean-record condition.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current address, phone number and email?
Which Mississippi county and city do you live in?

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?

How did the case end? Choose the one that matches: you were arrested and released and the case was dismissed; the charges were dropped; there was never any disposition; or you were found not guilty at trial.
On what date did that happen?
Was the case ever presented to a grand jury and indicted? Many cases are not, and the petition only pleads an indictment where one exists.
What exactly does your paperwork say about how the case ended? Copy the wording. Phrases like 'passed to the file' or 'retired to the file' need a closer look before we go further.
Was this a nonadjudication, a pretrial intervention programme, or an intervention or drug court? Those end differently and route differently.
Was anyone charged with you whose case is still open?

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

The order directs every person and agency keeping official records to expunge them EXCEPT fingerprint records, and the Mississippi Criminal Information Center retains a nonpublic record solely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings. Participant-facing copy must not say the record is erased everywhere.

Section 99-19-71(3) expressly provides that the existence of an order of expunction does not preclude an employer from asking a prospective employee whether an order of expunction has been entered on their behalf. This is a real and unusual limitation and participants must be told about it. A person called as a prospective juror must also, on request, advise the court in camera of the previous conviction and expunction.

A participant who uses this track has not spent their one felony expungement. The one-felony-per-lifetime cap sits in § 99-19-71(2)(a) and applies to conviction expungement, not to subsection (4). That is an important thing to tell people and to encode.
Relief is mandatory. The statute says the court "shall expunge", which is one of very few mandatory record-clearing provisions in the country and should be the headline of the Mississippi product.
The disposition order is obtained by the participant from the clerk and attached as an exhibit. It never delays generation of the petition.
participantQuestions: Plead the indictment allegation only where the case was actually indicted. The Fourth District model makes it mandatory and that is wrong for most cases.
scopeRestrictions: Do not inherit the Fourth District models' defects. Do not reuse the conviction petition's certificate of service, which is captioned for the dismissal petition. Do not plead a grand jury indictment as a mandatory allegation, because most misdemeanours are never indicted and many dismissed cases are dismissed before indictment. Do not cite § 99-15-26 and § 99-19-71 together unless both genuinely apply. Do not carry the hardcoded five-year recital, the hardcoded 2020 dates, the three-county field, or the Greenville address. Do not inherit the race field, and treat the full Social Security number as a deliberate decision rather than an inheritance.

Mississippi has no automatic record clearance. HB 1344 of the 2026 session, which would have created Department of Public Safety automatic expungement at seven years for misdemeanours and ten for felonies, died in committee on 3 February 2026, and substantially identical bills failed in 2024 and 2025. Nothing in the product may suggest automatic clearance exists or is coming.

Screen gently for trafficking-survivor relief under § 97-3-54.6(6) on every Mississippi intake, because it reaches any misdemeanour or non-violent felony at any time with no waiting period and no first-offender limit, and is therefore broader and faster than this track. Use trauma-sensitive screening, require a legal-aid, attorney or qualified survivor-services handoff, do not elicit unnecessary graphic detail, and never write the survivor narrative or the causal legal argument.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. legalDesignLimitations.statement: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

provenance.sourceStatement: The four archived Mississippi forms are local forms from one judicial district, and they are being treated as if they were statewide. legalDesignLimitations.statement: Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Do not inherit the Fourth District models' defects. Do not reuse the conviction petition's certificate of service, which is captioned for the dismissal petition. tracks.legalName: First-Offender Misdemeanor Conviction Expungement (Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-71(1))
tracks.publicName: Clearing a first misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: Section 99-19-71(1), read from the enrolled text of 2026 HB 1546, provides: 'Any person who has been convicted of a misdemeanor that is not a traffic violation, and who is a first offender, may petition the justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the conviction was had for an order to expunge any such conviction from all public records.' Subsection (1) contains NO waiting period, no completion requirement and no pending-charge restriction — the payment condition sits in subsection (2)(a) and is written for the felony track. Relief is permissive as to petitioning ('may petition') and the statute does not say the court shall grant, so it is treated as discretionary. Two elements carry the whole eligibility test: the offence must not be a traffic violation, and the person must be a first offender. Section 99-19-71(3) resolves what 'first offender' has to survive: a nonpublic record of every expunction is retained by the Mississippi Criminal Information Center 'solely for the purpose of determining whether, in subsequent proceedings, the person is a first offender', and the section's own perjury protection is expressly disapplied 'for the purpose of determining, in any subsequent proceedings under this section, whether the person is a first offender'. A previously expunged conviction therefore remains available to defeat first-offender status on a later petition, and the participant may not deny it for that purpose.
exclusions: A traffic violation. The statute reaches 'a misdemeanor that is not a traffic violation', and many Mississippi misdemeanours sit near that line.

A person who is not a first offender. A previously expunged conviction remains available to the Criminal Information Center under § 99-19-71(3) precisely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings, so an earlier expunction does not restore first-offender status.
DUI, which has its own route and must never be handled here.
A felony, which is subsection (2).

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Subsection (1) states no waiting period. This is counterintuitive and is a genuine advantage for the participant, and no waiting period is invented for this track.

tracks.venue: The justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the conviction was had, per subsection (1).

destination.name: Clerk of the court of conviction
destination.detail: File with the clerk of the court that entered the conviction. In municipal court the prosecuting authority is the city prosecutor, not the district attorney.

Obtain Mississippi criminal history record. Obtain your own Mississippi criminal history so you can see every case on your record before you file. It is the only reliable way to check first-offender status or good conduct across all courts, and self-report is not enough.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Advisable on every track and effectively necessary wherever first-offender status or a multi-court good-conduct period is in issue.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Advisable everywhere; required in practice in many courts even though subsection (1) does not say so.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

The order directs every person and agency keeping official records to expunge them EXCEPT fingerprint records, and the Mississippi Criminal Information Center retains a nonpublic record solely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings. Participant-facing copy must not say the record is erased everywhere.

Section 99-19-71(3) expressly provides that the existence of an order of expunction does not preclude an employer from asking a prospective employee whether an order of expunction has been entered on their behalf. This is a real and unusual limitation and participants must be told about it. A person called as a prospective juror must also, on request, advise the court in camera of the previous conviction and expunction.
Subsection (1) states no waiting period. Do not invent one.
participantQuestions: Do not assert first-offender status from participant self-report alone, and do not auto-classify traffic status.
scopeRestrictions: Do not inherit the Fourth District models' defects. Do not reuse the conviction petition's certificate of service, which is captioned for the dismissal petition. Do not plead a grand jury indictment as a mandatory allegation, because most misdemeanours are never indicted and many dismissed cases are dismissed before indictment. Do not cite § 99-15-26 and § 99-19-71 together unless both genuinely apply. Do not carry the hardcoded five-year recital, the hardcoded 2020 dates, the three-county field, or the Greenville address. Do not inherit the race field, and treat the full Social Security number as a deliberate decision rather than an inheritance.

Mississippi has no automatic record clearance. HB 1344 of the 2026 session, which would have created Department of Public Safety automatic expungement at seven years for misdemeanours and ten for felonies, died in committee on 3 February 2026, and substantially identical bills failed in 2024 and 2025. Nothing in the product may suggest automatic clearance exists or is coming.

Screen gently for trafficking-survivor relief under § 97-3-54.6(6) on every Mississippi intake, because it reaches any misdemeanour or non-violent felony at any time with no waiting period and no first-offender limit, and is therefore broader and faster than this track. Use trauma-sensitive screening, require a legal-aid, attorney or qualified survivor-services handoff, do not elicit unnecessary graphic detail, and never write the survivor narrative or the causal legal argument.

A previously expunged conviction remains available under § 99-19-71(3) to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings, so an earlier expungement does not restore first-offender status. Encode that rule precisely and tell the participant.
The driving record maintained under Title 63 is expressly unaffected by the parallel lower-court provision, which is a strong signal that traffic-adjacent expectations must be managed carefully.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

releaseBlockers.question: Trafficking-survivor relief under Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6, as amended by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, is recorded here as a separately-listed matter and NOT as a tenth normalized source node, because neither the adopted Batch 2 memorandum nor the authoritative source crosswalk lists it among Mississippi's nine core adult slots. The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.

provenance.sourceStatement: this relief is easier to obtain than ordinary misdemeanor conviction expungement under § 99-19-71, which is limited to first offenders and carries waiting periods and court-debt payment requirements. For a survivor, the trafficking route is both broader and faster. Wilma should be screening for it, gently, on every intake, not treating it as an edge case.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Mississippi has no automatic record clearance. HB 1344 of the 2026 session, which would have created Department of Public Safety automatic expungement at seven years for misdemeanours and ten for felonies, died in committee on 3 February 2026, and substantially identical bills failed in 2024 and 2025. Nothing in the product may suggest automatic clearance exists or is coming.

provenance.sourceStatement: Automatic record clearing. None exists in Mississippi. It died in committee on February 3, 2026. Nothing in the product should suggest automatic clearance is coming.

Open question blocks release (filing_process): Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

Open question blocks release (filing_process): Local practice in the twenty-one circuit court districts other than the Fourth, and in every municipal and justice court, was not surveyed. Both the review and the Fourth District materials establish that districts maintain their own petition and order preferences and that some expect the district attorney to sign the order as approved as to form before the judge will sign. This is a scaling constraint rather than a legal one: the statutory mechanism is the same statewide, but the accepted document and the practical gate vary. Every Mississippi track therefore carries localFormOverride and a mandatory clerk-contact instruction.

Open question blocks release (governing_mechanism): Trafficking-survivor relief under Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6, as amended by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, is recorded here as a separately-listed matter and NOT as a tenth normalized source node, because neither the adopted Batch 2 memorandum nor the authoritative source crosswalk lists it among Mississippi's nine core adult slots. The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.

Open question blocks release (eligibility_branch): Whether 'first offender' in § 99-19-71(1) is measured statewide, by court, or by offence type. The statute does not define it in the subsection. Section 99-19-71(3)'s retention of a nonpublic record by the Mississippi Criminal Information Center 'solely for the purpose of determining whether, in subsequent proceedings, the person is a first offender' points strongly to a statewide, record-based test rather than a court-specific one, and the packet is built on that reading, but the point is not settled by express text. The packet fails closed by asking the participant to obtain their Mississippi criminal history and by routing any prior conviction or prior expungement to advice.

Open question blocks release (packet_components): Whether Mississippi courts require proof of payment of fines and costs on a subsection (1) petition where the subsection does not impose it. The payment condition appears in subsection (2)(a), which governs the felony track. Practice reportedly requires a zero balance anyway. The packet asks for the balance sheet as an advisable attachment rather than pleading payment as a statutory element.

Open question blocks release (eligibility_branch): How a traffic violation is distinguished from an ordinary misdemeanour for § 99-19-71(1) purposes. The statute excludes 'a traffic violation' without defining it, and many Mississippi misdemeanours sit near the line. LegalEase does not auto-classify; the participant states the offence and an uncertain classification routes to advice.
One or more official sources have no recorded SHA-256, so staleness cannot be detected.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge One Felony Conviction (Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-71(2), as amended by 2026 HB 1546)
tracks.publicName: Clearing one felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: Read from the ENROLLED text of 2026 HB 1546, which amends § 99-19-71 and took effect 1 July 2026. Subsection (2)(a): except as otherwise provided in the subsection, a person convicted of a felony who has paid all criminal fines and costs of court imposed in the sentence of conviction may petition the court in which the conviction was had for an order to expunge ONE conviction from all public records THREE (3) YEARS after the successful completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence, upon a hearing as determined in the discretion of the court. HB 1546 struck 'five (5)' and inserted 'three (3)'. Twelve categories are ineligible: a crime of violence under § 97-3-2; arson, first degree under §§ 97-17-1 and 97-17-3; trafficking in controlled substances under § 41-29-139; a third, fourth or subsequent offence DUI under § 63-11-30(2)(c) and (2)(d); felon in possession of a firearm under § 97-37-5; failure to register as a sex offender under § 45-33-33; voyeurism under § 97-29-61; witness intimidation under § 97-9-113; abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable person under § 43-47-19; embezzlement under §§ 97-11-25 and 97-23-19; and, NEWLY ADDED BY HB 1546, felony procuring prostitution under § 97-29-51 and promoting prostitution under § 97-29-51. A person is eligible for only one felony expunction under paragraph (a), and the enrolled text now defines the terms: 'one (1) conviction' and 'one (1) felony expunction' mean and include all convictions that arose from a COMMON NUCLEUS OF OPERATIVE FACTS as determined in the discretion of the court. Subsection (2)(b): the petitioner shall give ten (10) days' written notice to the district attorney before any hearing; the court may grant if it determines, on the record or in writing, that the applicant is rehabilitated from the offence; and where the court denies, its findings must be identified specifically and not generally. Subsection (5): no public official is eligible for expunction under the section for any conviction related to his official duties. HB 1546 carries no applicability clause limiting it to convictions or petitions after a given date; SECTION 4 provides only that the act takes effect from and after 1 July 2026.
exclusions: A crime of violence as provided in Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-2. This is a defined list and it is long.
Arson, first degree, as provided in §§ 97-17-1 and 97-17-3.
Trafficking in controlled substances as provided in § 41-29-139.
A third, fourth or subsequent offence DUI as provided in § 63-11-30(2)(c) and (2)(d).
Felon in possession of a firearm as provided in § 97-37-5.
Failure to register as a sex offender as provided in § 45-33-33.
Voyeurism as provided in § 97-29-61.
Witness intimidation as provided in § 97-9-113.
Abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable person as provided in § 43-47-19.
Embezzlement as provided in §§ 97-11-25 and 97-23-19.
Felony procuring prostitution as provided in § 97-29-51 — ADDED by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026.
Promoting prostitution as provided in § 97-29-51 — ADDED by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026.
A public official, for any conviction related to his official duties (§ 99-19-71(5)).
A person who has already had one felony expunction under paragraph (a). The allowance is once per lifetime.

waitingPeriods.condition: Felony conviction under § 99-19-71(2)(a), for a petition governed by the law in force from 1 July 2026
waitingPeriods.duration: THREE (3) years after the successful completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence for the conviction. 2026 HB 1546 struck 'five (5)' and inserted 'three (3)' and took effect 1 July 2026 with no applicability clause. The clock runs from successful completion of ALL terms and conditions — incarceration, probation, supervised release, and payment of all fines, costs and restitution — not from the conviction date and not from the release date. All criminal fines and costs of court imposed in the sentence must additionally have been paid, which is a separate statutory condition in subsection (2)(a).

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current address, phone number and email?
Which Mississippi county and city do you live in?

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?
On what date were you convicted of the felony?
What felony were you convicted of, and under which Mississippi Code section?
What did your sentence include — incarceration, probation, supervised release, fines, costs, restitution, treatment, or a combination?
On what date did you successfully complete the LAST of all those terms and conditions? Not the conviction date and not your release date.
Are all criminal fines and costs of court imposed in the sentence paid in full? This is a separate statutory condition.

Is your conviction any of these: a crime of violence under § 97-3-2; first-degree arson; trafficking in controlled substances; a third or subsequent DUI; felon in possession of a firearm; failure to register as a sex offender; voyeurism; witness intimidation; abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable person; embezzlement; felony procuring prostitution; or promoting prostitution?
Have you ever had a felony conviction expunged in Mississippi before? You are eligible for only one felony expunction in your lifetime.

Were you convicted of more than one felony out of the same set of events? Mississippi counts all convictions arising from a common nucleus of operative facts as ONE conviction and ONE expunction, and the court decides that in its discretion.
Were you a public official, and was the conviction related to your official duties?
In your own words, what have you done since the offence? The court has to decide whether you are rehabilitated, and this is your statement, not ours. A lawyer should review it before you file.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. releaseBlockers.question: Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. tracks.legalName: Discretionary Expungement of Additional Justice Court or Municipal Court Misdemeanors (Miss. Code Ann. §§ 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6))
tracks.publicName: Clearing additional misdemeanors in city or justice court
tracks.mechanism: Two parallel provisions give the lower courts a discretionary power to expunge their own misdemeanour convictions: § 9-11-15(3) for justice court and § 21-23-7(6) for municipal court. They share one mechanism, one filing vehicle and one legal effect and differ only in which court is petitioned and which prosecutor is noticed, so they are modelled as ONE node with two venue branches rather than split. The complete text of both was obtained and compared word for word: every operative element is identical and the only differences are the court petitioned, the prosecutor noticed, clause order and pronoun style. Section 9-11-15(3) was added by Laws 2016 ch. 406 § 1 as a copy of the then-existing municipal provision; § 21-23-7(6) was last amended by Laws 2021 ch. 356. The court may, in its discretion, expunge the record of conviction of any or all misdemeanours in THAT court, on a showing made in open court of (i) rehabilitation, (ii) good conduct for two years since the last conviction in ANY court, and (iii) that the best interest of society would be served. The two-year clock runs from the last conviction in any court, not merely in the petitioned court, so a criminal-history check rather than self-report is required. Each court expunges only its own misdemeanours, so a participant with convictions in two municipal courts needs two petitions. The order does not apply to the confidential records of law-enforcement agencies and has NO effect on the driving record maintained under Title 63. Relief is expressly discretionary. Section 99-19-72's fee applies by its terms to petitions under § 99-19-71 and does not reach these sections.

Do not plead a grand jury indictment as a mandatory allegation, because most misdemeanours are never indicted and many dismissed cases are dismissed before indictment. Do not cite § 99-15-26 and § 99-19-71 together unless both genuinely apply. Do not carry the hardcoded five-year recital, the hardcoded 2020 dates, the three-county field, or the Greenville address. Mississippi has no automatic record clearance. HB 1344 of the 2026 session, which would have created Department of Public Safety automatic expungement at seven years for misdemeanours and ten for felonies, died in committee on 3 February 2026, and substantially identical bills failed in 2024 and 2025. Nothing in the product may suggest automatic clearance exists or is coming.

Use trauma-sensitive screening, require a legal-aid, attorney or qualified survivor-services handoff, do not elicit unnecessary graphic detail, and never write the survivor narrative or the causal legal argument.

Both the review and the Fourth District materials establish that districts maintain their own petition and order preferences and that some expect the district attorney to sign the order as approved as to form before the judge will sign. releaseBlockers.question: Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

releaseBlockers.question: Trafficking-survivor relief under Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6, as amended by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, is recorded here as a separately-listed matter and NOT as a tenth normalized source node, because neither the adopted Batch 2 memorandum nor the authoritative source crosswalk lists it among Mississippi's nine core adult slots. The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.

Open question blocks release (filing_process): Local practice in the twenty-one circuit court districts other than the Fourth, and in every municipal and justice court, was not surveyed. Both the review and the Fourth District materials establish that districts maintain their own petition and order preferences and that some expect the district attorney to sign the order as approved as to form before the judge will sign. This is a scaling constraint rather than a legal one: the statutory mechanism is the same statewide, but the accepted document and the practical gate vary. Every Mississippi track therefore carries localFormOverride and a mandatory clerk-contact instruction.

Open question blocks release (filing_process): Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

Open question blocks release (governing_mechanism): Trafficking-survivor relief under Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6, as amended by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, is recorded here as a separately-listed matter and NOT as a tenth normalized source node, because neither the adopted Batch 2 memorandum nor the authoritative source crosswalk lists it among Mississippi's nine core adult slots. The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.

tracks.mechanism: Under § 99-15-26 the court withholds acceptance of a guilty plea and sentence, imposes conditions, and on successful completion directs that the cause be dismissed and the case closed. Expungement of the resulting record is available on petition under the section's expungement subsection, which the retained review identifies as § 99-15-26(5). The complete text was obtained on this pass. Subsection (1)(a) excludes crimes against the person, a crime of violence as defined in § 97-3-2, a violation of § 97-11-31, and crimes in which a person unlawfully takes, obtains or misappropriates funds received by or entrusted to them by virtue of public office or employment; subsection (1)(d) additionally excludes trafficking under § 41-29-139(f) and every offence under the Implied Consent Law, which can only be nonadjudicated under § 63-11-30, and makes the benefit ONCE-ONLY. Subsection (4) makes the dismissal automatic on successful completion, and the expungement subsection is (5), which requires a petition. The routing question is live and unresolved: whether a successful nonadjudication dismissal requires its own § 99-15-26 petition, qualifies independently under § 99-19-71(4) as a case that was dismissed, or permits either route. The two statutes are NOT merged without authority, and the archived Fourth District conviction petition's practice of citing § 99-15-26 and § 99-19-71 together is exactly the conflation to avoid: they are separate tracks with different eligibility, different completion requirements and different proof, and a petition pleading both invites denial on whichever does not fit.

The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. releaseBlockers.question: The complete current text of Miss. Code Ann. § 99-15-26 was obtained on this pass and resolves most of what the review left open. The section is the integration of two 2019 acts under § 1-1-109 — Laws 2019 ch. 362 § 4 and Laws 2019 ch. 466 § 41, the Criminal Justice Reform Act — with no enacted amendment since. Subsection (1)(a) covers felony and misdemeanour cases in circuit or county court on a guilty plea entered on or after 1 July 2014, OTHER THAN crimes against the person, a crime of violence as defined in § 97-3-2, a violation of § 97-11-31, or crimes in which a person unlawfully takes, obtains or misappropriates funds received by or entrusted to the person by virtue of public office or employment; (1)(b) covers misdemeanours in justice or municipal court; (1)(c) covers misdemeanour domestic violence in any of the four courts. Subsection (1)(d) makes the benefit ONCE-ONLY — 'No person having previously qualified under the provisions of this section shall be eligible to qualify for release in accordance with this section for a repeat offense' — and excludes trafficking under § 41-29-139(f) and any offence under the Implied Consent Law, which can only be nonadjudicated under § 63-11-30. Subsection (2) sets the conditions the court may impose, with good behaviour up to five years in circuit or county court and two years in justice or municipal court. Subsection (4) makes the DISMISSAL automatic: on successful completion the court 'shall direct that the cause be dismissed and the case be closed'. The expungement subsection is (5) as the review recorded, and it requires a petition. One textual gap survives and is preserved rather than resolved: § 99-15-26(5) and § 99-19-71(4) are near-verbatim twins, and BOTH are keyed to 'a case in which an arrest was made, the person arrested was released and the case was dismissed', which describes a pre-adjudication arrest-and-release posture rather than a post-guilty-plea nonadjudication dismissal under (4). Neither section says in terms that a subsection (4) dismissal is expungeable on petition.

The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.
