unresolvedQuestions.question: The complete current text of Miss. Code Ann. § 99-15-26 was obtained on this pass and resolves most of what the review left open. The section is the integration of two 2019 acts under § 1-1-109 — Laws 2019 ch. 362 § 4 and Laws 2019 ch. 466 § 41, the Criminal Justice Reform Act — with no enacted amendment since. Subsection (1)(a) covers felony and misdemeanour cases in circuit or county court on a guilty plea entered on or after 1 July 2014, OTHER THAN crimes against the person, a crime of violence as defined in § 97-3-2, a violation of § 97-11-31, or crimes in which a person unlawfully takes, obtains or misappropriates funds received by or entrusted to the person by virtue of public office or employment; (1)(b) covers misdemeanours in justice or municipal court; (1)(c) covers misdemeanour domestic violence in any of the four courts. Subsection (1)(d) makes the benefit ONCE-ONLY — 'No person having previously qualified under the provisions of this section shall be eligible to qualify for release in accordance with this section for a repeat offense' — and excludes trafficking under § 41-29-139(f) and any offence under the Implied Consent Law, which can only be nonadjudicated under § 63-11-30. Subsection (2) sets the conditions the court may impose, with good behaviour up to five years in circuit or county court and two years in justice or municipal court. Subsection (4) makes the DISMISSAL automatic: on successful completion the court 'shall direct that the cause be dismissed and the case be closed'. The expungement subsection is (5) as the review recorded, and it requires a petition. One textual gap survives and is preserved rather than resolved: § 99-15-26(5) and § 99-19-71(4) are near-verbatim twins, and BOTH are keyed to 'a case in which an arrest was made, the person arrested was released and the case was dismissed', which describes a pre-adjudication arrest-and-release posture rather than a post-guilty-plea nonadjudication dismissal under (4). Neither section says in terms that a subsection (4) dismissal is expungeable on petition.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Do not inherit the Fourth District models' defects. Do not reuse the conviction petition's certificate of service, which is captioned for the dismissal petition. Do not plead a grand jury indictment as a mandatory allegation, because most misdemeanours are never indicted and many dismissed cases are dismissed before indictment. Do not cite § 99-15-26 and § 99-19-71 together unless both genuinely apply. Do not carry the hardcoded five-year recital, the hardcoded 2020 dates, the three-county field, or the Greenville address. Do not inherit the race field, and treat the full Social Security number as a deliberate decision rather than an inheritance.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Mississippi has no automatic record clearance. HB 1344 of the 2026 session, which would have created Department of Public Safety automatic expungement at seven years for misdemeanours and ten for felonies, died in committee on 3 February 2026, and substantially identical bills failed in 2024 and 2025. Nothing in the product may suggest automatic clearance exists or is coming.

provenance.sourceStatement: Automatic record clearing. None exists in Mississippi. HB 1344 of the 2026 session would have created Department of Public Safety automatic expungement at 7 years for misdemeanors and 10 years for felonies, capped at two felonies, with a computer program to be built by July 1, 2027. It died in committee on February 3, 2026. Nothing in the product should suggest automatic clearance is coming.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Screen gently for trafficking-survivor relief under § 97-3-54.6(6) on every Mississippi intake, because it reaches any misdemeanour or non-violent felony at any time with no waiting period and no first-offender limit, and is therefore broader and faster than this track. Use trauma-sensitive screening, require a legal-aid, attorney or qualified survivor-services handoff, do not elicit unnecessary graphic detail, and never write the survivor narrative or the causal legal argument.

tracks.legalName: First-Offense DUI Expungement (Miss. Code Ann. § 63-11-30)
tracks.publicName: Clearing a first DUI
tracks.mechanism: Section 63-11-30 carries its own first-offence DUI expungement provision, entirely separate from the ordinary misdemeanour route, and a DUI must never be routed through § 99-19-71(1). Every condition must be met: at least five years after successful completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence; the person did not hold a commercial driver's licence or a commercial learner's permit at the time of the offence; the person did not refuse the blood or breath test; blood alcohol concentration below .16 where test results are available; no other DUI conviction and no pending DUI; the person has not previously had a DUI nonadjudication or a DUI expungement; and the person must justify the expungement to the court. Relief is discretionary. Venue is the CIRCUIT COURT of the county of conviction: the Attorney General has opined that a municipal court judge is not authorized to expunge a DUI conviction, although municipal and justice courts may handle expungement of nonadjudicated first-offence DUI charges in certain circumstances. That is the most likely way a Mississippi DUI petition gets filed in the wrong court. A third, fourth or subsequent DUI under § 63-11-30(2)(c) and (2)(d) is separately excluded from felony expungement under § 99-19-71(2)(a)(iv). The complete current text was obtained on this pass from enrolled SB 2095 (Laws 2022 ch. 303), the last enacted amendment: the expungement provision is subsection (13), captioned 'Expunction'. It is frequently cited in practice as § 63-11-30(14); per the 2022 enrolled act (13) is Expunction and (14) is Nonadjudication. Subsection (13)(b) additionally makes a person eligible for only ONE expunction under the subsection and directs the Department of Public Safety to maintain a permanent confidential registry of all such expunctions solely to determine eligibility for expunction, for nonadjudication, or as a first offender. Subsection (13)(c) requires the court to state in writing the justification for which the expunction was granted and to forward the order to the Department of Public Safety within five days.
exclusions: A person who held a commercial driver's licence or a commercial learner's permit at the time of the offence.
A person who refused the blood or breath test.
A blood alcohol concentration of .16 or above where test results are available.
Any other DUI conviction, and any pending DUI.
A person who has previously had a DUI nonadjudication or a DUI expungement.
A second, third, fourth or subsequent DUI. Third and subsequent DUI under § 63-11-30(2)(c) and (2)(d) is also excluded from felony expungement under § 99-19-71(2)(a)(iv).
Filing anywhere other than the circuit court of the county of conviction. A municipal court judge is not authorized to expunge a DUI conviction.

waitingPeriods.duration: At least FIVE years after successful completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence imposed for the conviction, per Miss. Code Ann. § 63-11-30(13)(a). This period was not affected by 2026 HB 1546, which reduced only the general felony period in § 99-19-71(2)(a) to three years, and § 63-11-30 has had no enacted amendment since Laws 2022 ch. 303.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current address, phone number and email?
Which Mississippi county and city do you live in?

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?
On what date were you convicted of the DUI?
Which court entered the DUI conviction? Note that the expungement petition itself goes to the circuit court of that county, not back to the convicting court.
On what date did you successfully complete all terms and conditions of the sentence?
Did you hold a commercial driver's licence or a commercial learner's permit at the time of the offence?
Did you refuse the blood or breath test?
If a test was taken, what was the blood alcohol concentration result?
Do you have any other DUI conviction, or any DUI charge pending now?
Have you ever had a DUI nonadjudication or a DUI expungement before?
In your own words, why should the court grant this expungement? The statute requires you to justify it, and this is your statement.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the DUI judgment of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that entered the DUI conviction for a certified copy of the judgment.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Blood or breath test result, or documentation that no test was refused
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The arresting agency, the court file, or the Mississippi Crime Laboratory
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the test result. The statute conditions relief on not having refused the test and, where results are available, on a concentration below .16, so this document is central rather than optional.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified driving record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Mississippi Department of Public Safety
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain your certified driving record. It establishes whether any other DUI appears and whether you held a commercial licence.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Account balance sheet from the clerk showing a zero balance
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the case was heard
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for an account balance sheet showing that all fines, costs and restitution are paid in full. Mississippi courts commonly require a zero balance in practice even where the subsection does not say so, and on the felony track payment of all criminal fines and costs of court is a statutory condition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Mississippi criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Mississippi Criminal Information Center
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Advisable on every track and effectively necessary wherever first-offender status or a multi-court good-conduct period is in issue.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain your own Mississippi criminal history so you can see every case on your record before you file. It is the only reliable way to check first-offender status or good conduct across all courts, and self-report is not enough.

manualCompletionItems.item: The finding that the petitioner meets the criteria for expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: That is the court's finding. LegalEase drafts it as a proposal for the judge to make, never as an assertion of fact.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature, the date, and the order's entry
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is the court's.

manualCompletionItems.item: The APPROVED AS TO FORM signature for the prosecuting authority
manualCompletionItems.why: Both archived Fourth District orders carry this block, which is the clearest evidence that Mississippi practice runs through prosecutor sign-off. The block is retained because it costs nothing where it is not expected, and it is never pre-signed or pre-filled.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's signature and the date of signing
manualCompletionItems.why: LegalEase never signs for the participant. The archived models' phrase 'by and through his attorney' is removed, because this is a self-help product.

manualCompletionItems.item: The cause number where the court assigns a new one
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Petition, proposed order and certificate of service captions
manualCompletionItems.why: Supplied by the clerk where a new number is assigned.

manualCompletionItems.item: The participant's justification for the expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: The statute requires the person to justify the expungement to the court. LegalEase prompts for the participant's own words and formats them; it never composes the justification.

manualCompletionItems.item: The determination that every statutory condition is met
manualCompletionItems.why: All seven conditions are hard gates and each is a legal determination. The participant states the facts and every DUI packet goes to attorney review before filing.

manualCompletionItems.item: LegalEase must not generate: that the petitioner meets the criteria for expungement, which is the court's finding; that the offence is an 'Expungeable Offense', which appears in the Fourth District caption block as though it were a data field but is a legal conclusion; that the petitioner is a first offender; that the petitioner is rehabilitated; that a dismissal was 'with prejudice' unless the order says so; any statement about immigration, firearms, federal records or professional licensing consequences; or any assertion that the record will be erased everywhere.
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.
scopeRestrictions: Do not inherit the Fourth District models' defects. Do not reuse the conviction petition's certificate of service, which is captioned for the dismissal petition. Do not plead a grand jury indictment as a mandatory allegation, because most misdemeanours are never indicted and many dismissed cases are dismissed before indictment. Do not cite § 99-15-26 and § 99-19-71 together unless both genuinely apply. Do not carry the hardcoded five-year recital, the hardcoded 2020 dates, the three-county field, or the Greenville address. Do not inherit the race field, and treat the full Social Security number as a deliberate decision rather than an inheritance.

Mississippi has no automatic record clearance. HB 1344 of the 2026 session, which would have created Department of Public Safety automatic expungement at seven years for misdemeanours and ten for felonies, died in committee on 3 February 2026, and substantially identical bills failed in 2024 and 2025. Nothing in the product may suggest automatic clearance exists or is coming.

Screen gently for trafficking-survivor relief under § 97-3-54.6(6) on every Mississippi intake, because it reaches any misdemeanour or non-violent felony at any time with no waiting period and no first-offender limit, and is therefore broader and faster than this track. Use trauma-sensitive screening, require a legal-aid, attorney or qualified survivor-services handoff, do not elicit unnecessary graphic detail, and never write the survivor narrative or the causal legal argument.
Do not route DUI through the ordinary misdemeanour track. The internal reference's rule that DUI must never be routed through ordinary misdemeanour expungement is correct and is a hard gate.

Venue is the circuit court of the county of conviction. A municipal court judge is not authorized to expunge a DUI conviction. This is a venue trap and the most likely way a Mississippi DUI petition gets filed in the wrong court.

releaseBlockers.question: The complete current text was obtained on this pass and resolves the review's open questions on this track. The expungement provision is Miss. Code Ann. § 63-11-30(13), from enrolled SB 2095 (Laws 2022 ch. 303), which is the last enacted amendment — no 2023 to 2026 amendment touched it, and 2026 HB 1546 changed only § 99-19-71(2). The waiting period is confirmed as at least FIVE years after successful completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence, and it was NOT affected by HB 1546's reduction of the general felony period to three years. Venue is confirmed as the circuit court of the county in which the conviction was had. One practical caution survives: the provision is widely cited as § 63-11-30(14), and per the enrolled act (13) is Expunction while (14) is Nonadjudication, so the subsection letter should be confirmed against the current print before filing.

releaseBlockers.question: Local practice in the twenty-one circuit court districts other than the Fourth, and in every municipal and justice court, was not surveyed. Both the review and the Fourth District materials establish that districts maintain their own petition and order preferences and that some expect the district attorney to sign the order as approved as to form before the judge will sign. This is a scaling constraint rather than a legal one: the statutory mechanism is the same statewide, but the accepted document and the practical gate vary. Every Mississippi track therefore carries localFormOverride and a mandatory clerk-contact instruction.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

releaseBlockers.question: Trafficking-survivor relief under Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6, as amended by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, is recorded here as a separately-listed matter and NOT as a tenth normalized source node, because neither the adopted Batch 2 memorandum nor the authoritative source crosswalk lists it among Mississippi's nine core adult slots. The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.

provenance.sourceStatement: this relief is easier to obtain than ordinary misdemeanor conviction expungement under § 99-19-71, which is limited to first offenders and carries waiting periods and court-debt payment requirements. For a survivor, the trafficking route is both broader and faster. Wilma should be screening for it, gently, on every intake, not treating it as an edge case.

tracks.legalName: Expungement After Pretrial Intervention or Intervention Court Completion (Miss. Code Ann. §§ 99-15-123, 9-23-23)
tracks.publicName: Cases you resolved through a program
tracks.mechanism: The complete text of both provisions was obtained on this pass, and it splits this slot into two legally distinct branches rather than one. PRETRIAL INTERVENTION, § 99-15-123 (last amended Laws 2008 ch. 444 § 1): subsection (1) makes the DISPOSITION automatic — on successful completion 'the court shall make a noncriminal disposition of the charge or charges', which § 99-15-103 defines as dismissal of the charge without prejudice to reinstatement on the district attorney's motion — but subsection (3) makes the EXPUNGEMENT petition-based: 'Upon petition therefor, the court shall expunge the record of any case in which an arrest was made, the person arrested was released and the case was dismissed or the charges were dropped or there was no disposition of such case.' The court's duty is mandatory once petitioned, but no order enters without the petition. Note subsection (3) omits the 'found not guilty at trial' limb that § 99-19-71(4) contains. INTERVENTION COURT, § 9-23-23 (last amended by 2019 HB 1352 § 13, which substituted 'intervention' for 'drug' and inserted 'and not waived by the court'): 'If the participant completes all requirements imposed upon him by the intervention court, including the payment of fines and fees assessed and not waived by the court, the charge and prosecution shall be dismissed. If the defendant or participant was sentenced at the time of entry of plea of guilty, the successful completion of the intervention court order and other requirements of probation or suspension of sentence will result in the record of the criminal conviction or adjudication being expunged. However, no expunction of any implied consent violation shall be allowed.' That section contains NO petition language, no application requirement, no fee, no hearing, no notice and no waiting period — unlike §§ 99-19-71, 99-15-26(5), 99-15-123(3), 41-29-150(d)(2) and 63-11-30(13), every one of which expressly requires a petition or application. Its expungement language is the most self-executing in the Mississippi scheme.
exclusions: A programme that was terminated rather than successfully completed. Under § 99-15-123(2) the district attorney may terminate participation, the § 99-15-115 waiver becomes void on removal, and prosecution of the pending charges resumes.
A programme still in progress.
An implied consent violation, which § 9-23-23 expressly bars from expunction in intervention court and which routes to the DUI track under § 63-11-30 instead.
The programme itself is not record-clearance relief. It produces a disposition; only the § 99-15-123(3) petition, or the § 9-23-23 result, clears a record.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Section 99-15-123 imposes no waiting period before petitioning; the trigger is the noncriminal disposition that follows successful completion.

units.label: Pretrial intervention — § 99-15-123(3) petition to expunge
units.description: The petition branch. Successful completion of pretrial intervention produces a noncriminal disposition automatically under § 99-15-123(1) — the court 'shall make' it, and no participant filing is involved — but the expungement of the resulting record does NOT follow automatically. Section 99-15-123(3) provides expungement 'Upon petition therefor', and the court's duty is mandatory only once the petition is filed. That is a distinct participant request for relief with its own statutory basis, its own destination and its own legal output, which is why this slot carries a genuine relief branch rather than verification alone. LegalEase drafts the petition, the proposed order and the certificate of service to § 99-15-123(3), pleading the pretrial intervention, its successful completion, the noncriminal disposition and its date. The pleaded category is taken from subsection (3)'s own terms, which reach a case in which an arrest was made and the person was released and the case was dismissed, or the charges were dropped, or there was no disposition — and which, unlike § 99-19-71(4), do NOT include a finding of not guilty at trial.

units.label: Intervention court — verification of the self-executing result, and routing
units.description: The verification branch. Section 9-23-23 states a result rather than a procedure: on completion of all requirements the charge and prosecution 'shall be dismissed', and where the person was sentenced at the time of the guilty plea completion 'will result in the record of the criminal conviction or adjudication being expunged'. There is no petition language, no application, no fee, no hearing, no notice and no waiting period anywhere in the section — which is unique in the Mississippi scheme and is why no petition is generated on this branch. The section does not, however, direct any officer to enter or transmit an order, so whether an expungement order in fact issues without the participant asking is a matter of local practice and is preserved as an open question. The correct product output is therefore verification: establish from the clerk what was actually entered and when, obtain a certified copy of any dismissal or expungement order that already exists, and route onward only where the record shows relief did not issue. Implied consent violations are expressly barred from expunction here and route to the DUI track.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current address, phone number and email?
Which Mississippi county and city do you live in?

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?

Which was it — a pretrial intervention programme, or an intervention court such as a drug court, mental health court or veterans court? They are governed by different statutes and they end differently.
Did you complete the programme successfully, including paying any fines and fees that were not waived, or was it terminated?
On what date did you complete it?
What did the court enter when you finished — a noncriminal disposition, a dismissal, or something else? And on what date?
Were you sentenced at the time of your guilty plea, or was sentencing withheld? On an intervention court this decides whether completion produces a dismissal or an expungement of the conviction.
Do you know whether the court has already entered an order dismissing or expunging the case? Many people have relief already entered and simply do not hold a copy.
Did the case involve a DUI or any other implied consent violation? Those cannot be expunged in intervention court and go to the DUI route instead.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

On the intervention court branch, where relief has already been entered by operation of the statute, the correct product output is a verification and a certified copy, not a filing. Participants frequently have an order they do not hold a copy of.

A noncriminal disposition under § 99-15-103 is a dismissal WITHOUT PREJUDICE to the state reinstating criminal proceedings on the district attorney's motion. Participant-facing copy must not describe it as a final bar to prosecution.
participantQuestions: Establish whether the resulting record is a noncriminal disposition, a dismissal, or an expunged conviction, because those route differently. On an intervention court case, whether the person was sentenced at the time of the guilty plea decides which of the two § 9-23-23 outcomes applies.
scopeRestrictions: Mississippi has no automatic record clearance. HB 1344 of the 2026 session, which would have created Department of Public Safety automatic expungement at seven years for misdemeanours and ten for felonies, died in committee on 3 February 2026, and substantially identical bills failed in 2024 and 2025. Nothing in the product may suggest automatic clearance exists or is coming.

Screen gently for trafficking-survivor relief under § 97-3-54.6(6) on every Mississippi intake, because it reaches any misdemeanour or non-violent felony at any time with no waiting period and no first-offender limit, and is therefore broader and faster than this track. Use trauma-sensitive screening, require a legal-aid, attorney or qualified survivor-services handoff, do not elicit unnecessary graphic detail, and never write the survivor narrative or the causal legal argument.

Do not count the programme itself as paid record-clearance relief merely because it affects the final disposition. Diversion produces a disposition; the § 99-15-123(3) petition or the § 9-23-23 result is what clears a record.
No expunction of any implied consent violation is allowed in intervention court under § 9-23-23. Those route to the DUI track under § 63-11-30.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether the § 9-23-23 expungement of a conviction, where the person was sentenced at the time of the guilty plea, issues without the participant asking. The section's operative language is automatic in FORM — completion 'will result in the record of the criminal conviction or adjudication being expunged' — and it is the only expungement provision in the Mississippi scheme with no petition, application, fee, hearing, notice or waiting period. But it also does not direct any officer to enter or transmit an order, and does not say the record shall be expunged without further action. Whether an order in fact issues sua sponte is therefore local practice and is NOT ESTABLISHED. The packet fails closed by verifying with the clerk what was actually entered before concluding anything, and in practice a movant should expect to submit a proposed order.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether a pretrial intervention noncriminal disposition satisfies the predicate in § 99-15-123(3), which reaches 'any case in which an arrest was made, the person arrested was released and the case was dismissed or the charges were dropped or there was no disposition of such case'. A § 99-15-103 noncriminal disposition IS a dismissal, but the subsection's arrest-and-release phrasing describes a pre-intervention posture and neither section says in terms that a noncriminal disposition under subsection (1) is expungeable under subsection (3). The same textual gap affects the near-identical § 99-15-26(5) and § 99-19-71(4). The packet pleads the statutory category that matches the participant's actual record and routes an ambiguous docket to advice.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

releaseBlockers.question: Local practice in the twenty-one circuit court districts other than the Fourth, and in every municipal and justice court, was not surveyed. Both the review and the Fourth District materials establish that districts maintain their own petition and order preferences and that some expect the district attorney to sign the order as approved as to form before the judge will sign. This is a scaling constraint rather than a legal one: the statutory mechanism is the same statewide, but the accepted document and the practical gate vary. Every Mississippi track therefore carries localFormOverride and a mandatory clerk-contact instruction.

releaseBlockers.question: Trafficking-survivor relief under Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6, as amended by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, is recorded here as a separately-listed matter and NOT as a tenth normalized source node, because neither the adopted Batch 2 memorandum nor the authoritative source crosswalk lists it among Mississippi's nine core adult slots. The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.

The same textual gap affects the near-identical § 99-15-26(5) and § 99-19-71(4). The packet pleads the statutory category that matches the participant's actual record and routes an ambiguous docket to advice.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Trafficking-survivor relief under Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6, as amended by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, is recorded here as a separately-listed matter and NOT as a tenth normalized source node, because neither the adopted Batch 2 memorandum nor the authoritative source crosswalk lists it among Mississippi's nine core adult slots. The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.

provenance.sourceStatement: this relief is easier to obtain than ordinary misdemeanor conviction expungement under § 99-19-71, which is limited to first offenders and carries waiting periods and court-debt payment requirements. tracks.legalName: Controlled-Substance Conditional Discharge and Expungement (Miss. Code Ann. § 41-29-150)
tracks.publicName: First-time drug possession cases
tracks.mechanism: Section 41-29-150 carries Mississippi's controlled-substance conditional discharge and its associated expungement. A first-time eligible drug possession or paraphernalia case may be handled WITHOUT entering a judgment of guilt: the court defers proceedings, places the person on probation, and on successful completion discharges the person and dismisses the proceedings without an adjudication of guilt. Expungement of the record is then available on application to the court. The benefit is once-only, and a nonpublic record is retained for future eligibility checks, which is the same design as the § 99-19-71(3) first-offender retention. Trafficking under § 41-29-139 is a separate offence and is outside this route entirely; it is also independently excluded from felony expungement under § 99-19-71(2)(a)(iii). The complete current text was obtained on this pass, from the last enacted amendment, Laws 2010 ch. 460 § 2. The conditional discharge is § 41-29-150(d)(1) and the expungement remedy is § 41-29-150(d)(2). Eligibility reaches a person NOT previously convicted of violating § 41-29-139, or the laws of the United States or another state relating to narcotic drugs, stimulant or depressant substances, other controlled substances or marihuana, who is found guilty of a violation of § 41-29-139(c) or (d) — simple possession and paraphernalia — after trial or on a plea. The court may, without entering a judgment of guilt and with the person's consent, defer further proceedings and place them on probation for not more than three years; if no condition is violated, on expiry the court SHALL discharge the person and dismiss the proceedings, without adjudication of guilt. Discharge and dismissal may occur ONLY ONCE with respect to any person, and a nonpublic record is retained by the Bureau of Narcotics solely for the courts to determine whether the person qualifies again. Under (d)(2) the person may then APPLY to the court for an expungement order; the court determines the matter AFTER HEARING and, on the requisite findings, SHALL enter the order. Section 41-29-150 specifies no fee.
exclusions: Trafficking, sale, distribution and manufacture under § 41-29-139(a) and § 41-29-139(f). This route reaches only violations of § 41-29-139(c), simple possession, and § 41-29-139(d), paraphernalia.
Distribution and sale offences.
A person with a prior drug disposition, since the conditional discharge is a once-only benefit and a nonpublic record is retained for future eligibility checks.

A case in which the court accepted the plea and adjudicated guilt. The conditional discharge operates WITHOUT entering a judgment of guilt, and where guilt was adjudicated and sentence imposed § 41-29-150(d)(2) never opens.

A person previously convicted of violating § 41-29-139, or the laws of the United States or another state relating to narcotic drugs, stimulant or depressant substances, other controlled substances or marihuana.
A conditional discharge whose probation was not successfully completed.

tracks.legalName: Underage Alcohol Possession Expungement (Miss. Code Ann. § 67-3-70)
tracks.publicName: Underage drinking charges
tracks.mechanism: Section 67-3-70 governs underage alcohol offences and carries its own expungement provision at subsection (6). The complete current text was obtained on this pass from enrolled HB 917 § 34 (Laws 2020 ch. 314), the last enacted amendment, so the one-year period is now supported by PRIMARY authority rather than by the secondary clearinghouse source the review relied on. Subsection (6) reads: 'Any person who has been charged with a violation of subsections (1) or (2) of this section may, not sooner than one (1) year after the dismissal and discharge or completion of any sentence and/or payment of any fine, apply to the court for an order to expunge from all official records all recordation relating to his arrest, trial, finding or plea of guilty, and dismissal and discharge. If the court determines that such person was dismissed and the proceedings against him discharged or that such person had satisfactorily served his sentence and/or paid his fine, it shall enter such order.' Four consequences follow. The route reaches subsections (1) and (2) only — underage purchase or possession of light wine, light spirit product or beer, and an underage false-age statement or false document — and does not reach subsection (3), furnishing to a minor. It reaches anyone 'CHARGED WITH' such a violation, so dismissed and discharged cases qualify as well as convictions. The one-year clock runs from the LATER of dismissal and discharge, or completion of any sentence and payment of any fine, not from the offence or the charge. And relief is MANDATORY on the findings — 'it shall enter such order' — unlike the discretionary lower-court misdemeanour route. The section prescribes no petition contents, no prosecutor notice, no open-court showing, no rehabilitation finding, no hearing and no fee, and it contains no restoration-of-status clause, no perjury-protection clause and no Title 63 carve-out.
exclusions: Offences outside § 67-3-70(1) and (2). The route reaches underage purchase or possession of light wine, light spirit product or beer, and an underage false-age statement or presentation of a false document for that purpose. It does NOT reach § 67-3-70(3), furnishing or purchasing for a minor, which is an adult offence.
DUI, which has its own route and is never handled here.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

The one-year waiting period is retained ONLY because § 67-3-70(6) was read from primary authority on this pass — enrolled HB 917 § 34, Laws 2020 ch. 314 — and not because a secondary clearinghouse source reported it. The clock runs from the later of dismissal and discharge or completion of any sentence and payment of any fine.

Relief is mandatory on the statutory findings — 'it shall enter such order' — unlike the discretionary lower-court misdemeanour route. Section 67-3-70 contains no restoration-of-status clause, no perjury-protection clause and no Title 63 carve-out, so participant-facing copy must not import those effects from § 99-19-71.
Instruct the participant to confirm the current waiting period, the correct court and any fee with the clerk before filing.
scopeRestrictions: Do not inherit the Fourth District models' defects. Do not reuse the conviction petition's certificate of service, which is captioned for the dismissal petition. Do not plead a grand jury indictment as a mandatory allegation, because most misdemeanours are never indicted and many dismissed cases are dismissed before indictment. Do not cite § 99-15-26 and § 99-19-71 together unless both genuinely apply. Do not carry the hardcoded five-year recital, the hardcoded 2020 dates, the three-county field, or the Greenville address. Do not inherit the race field, and treat the full Social Security number as a deliberate decision rather than an inheritance.

Mississippi has no automatic record clearance. HB 1344 of the 2026 session, which would have created Department of Public Safety automatic expungement at seven years for misdemeanours and ten for felonies, died in committee on 3 February 2026, and substantially identical bills failed in 2024 and 2025. Nothing in the product may suggest automatic clearance exists or is coming.

Screen gently for trafficking-survivor relief under § 97-3-54.6(6) on every Mississippi intake, because it reaches any misdemeanour or non-violent felony at any time with no waiting period and no first-offender limit, and is therefore broader and faster than this track. Use trauma-sensitive screening, require a legal-aid, attorney or qualified survivor-services handoff, do not elicit unnecessary graphic detail, and never write the survivor narrative or the causal legal argument.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

releaseBlockers.question: Trafficking-survivor relief under Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6, as amended by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, is recorded here as a separately-listed matter and NOT as a tenth normalized source node, because neither the adopted Batch 2 memorandum nor the authoritative source crosswalk lists it among Mississippi's nine core adult slots. The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Misdemeanor Records (Mont. Code Ann. tit. 46, ch. 18, pt. 11)
tracks.publicName: Misdemeanor expungement
tracks.mechanism: Title 46, chapter 18, part 11 lets a person petition a district court to expunge the records of one or more misdemeanour convictions entered in Montana state courts, whether in one court or several and whether in one case or several (§ 46-18-1104(1)). The petition is once in a lifetime: a person who has already had records expunged under the part, or who has already petitioned, may not petition again (§ 46-18-1104(1) and (2)). Venue is a district court in a judicial district where at least one of the convictions occurred (§ 46-18-1105), so a participant with convictions in several districts chooses among them. Section 46-18-1106(1) requires notice to every prosecution office that prosecuted an offence for which expungement is requested, and § 46-18-1106(2) gives that office fourteen days from receiving the petition to attempt to notify any victim. Section 46-18-1107 creates a presumption in favour of expungement where the person is not detained, charged or subject to pending charges as verified by the prosecution office, and either five years have passed since completion of the sentencing terms with no conviction of any offence in Montana, another state or federal court, or the person meets the military condition in § 46-18-1107(1)(b). Section 46-18-1108(1) removes the presumption entirely for convictions for assault, partner or family member assault, stalking, sexual assault, violation of a protective order, DUI however named, or any offence carrying a statutorily enhanced penalty for driving under the influence, and § 46-18-1108(2) then directs the court to weigh age at the offence, elapsed time, rehabilitation, likelihood of reoffending and any other relevant factor. Section 46-18-1109(2) lets the presumption be overcome on a determination that the interests of public safety demand dismissal, and the standard throughout is a preponderance of the evidence. The court may expunge all, some or none of the offences (§ 46-18-1110(1)). Section 46-18-1103(1) defines expungement as permanently destroying, deleting or erasing a record from the DOJ criminal history record information system, and § 46-18-1110(2)(a) directs the arresting agency, the prosecutor's office and the clerk of the convicting court to permanently seal their own records. Crucially, § 46-18-1110(2)(b) puts the second stage on the participant: the person whose records are being expunged sends the order, fingerprints and the DOJ form to those agencies and to the Department of Justice. No amendment since Ch. 384, L. 2019; § 46-18-1101 is repealed.

units.label: District-court petition for expungement of misdemeanor records
units.description: The court stage. A Petition for Expungement of Misdemeanor Records, a certificate of service and a proposed order, filed in a district court in a judicial district where at least one conviction occurred. Title 46, chapter 18, part 11 prescribes no form; § 46-18-1111 grants rulemaking authority but no statewide expungement form has been adopted under it, and the only published petition and order — ER-100 and ER-200 — are a Montana Legal Services Association and Access to Justice Commission work product licensed for non-commercial use only and are neither mandatory nor usable in a paid packet. LegalEase therefore drafts its own, which is both lawful and cleaner. The petition pleads the participant's identity and contact details; that at least one conviction occurred in the district, establishing venue; each conviction with crime, case number, conviction date and court; completion of all sentencing terms including financial obligations and court-ordered treatment; that the petitioner is not detained, charged or subject to pending charges; that the petitioner has not previously petitioned for or received expungement under the part; the years since the last conviction or the military basis; and that the petitioner will be fingerprinted to validate identity under § 46-18-1104(3). The prayer asks that the listed misdemeanours be expunged from the DOJ criminal history record information system, that the arresting agencies, prosecutors' offices and clerks permanently seal their records under § 46-18-1110(2)(a), and that the clerk seal the record of the expungement matter itself. The certificate of service covers every county attorney and city attorney office that prosecuted a case in the petition. The proposed order leaves the date and signature blank for the judge.

units.label: DOJ CRISS expungement submission after the court order
units.description: The Department of Justice stage, and a genuinely separate legal unit: a different destination, a different actor's form, and a participant submission the statute places on the participant rather than on the court or the clerk. Section 46-18-1110(2)(b) requires the person whose records are being expunged to send the order, fingerprints and a form prepared by the Department of Justice to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk of the convicting court and the Department. LegalEase completes the participant-owned fields of the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form with the misdemeanour expungement request type selected, and supplies the mailing checklist, the § 46-18-1110(2)(b) distribution list and the verification steps. The FD-258 blue applicant fingerprint card is a physical prerequisite of this stage — cards are free from DOJ CRISS but there is a fee to have prints taken — and it is sequenced at the FRONT of the participant's task list rather than surfaced at the end. It is required before the CRISS submission, never before LegalEase generates the court packet. Without this stage a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

tracks.venue: A Montana district court in a judicial district where at least one of the convictions occurred (§ 46-18-1105). packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.
LegalEase drafts its own petition, certificate of service, and proposed order. It must not reproduce ER-100, ER-200, or the MLSA fee-waiver forms.
Do not promise that the court order alone completes expungement. The participant must complete the DOJ CRISS stage under § 46-18-1110(2)(b).

The FD-258 fingerprint step must appear at the front of the participant's task list, not at the end. It is a physical dependency of the CRISS submission and is never a condition of generating the court packet.
participantQuestions: The once-in-a-lifetime rule requires a hard confirmation gate before generation, showing the participant the full list of convictions being included and warning that omitted convictions cannot be added later.
Venue is a participant choice with strategic consequences and must be presented as a choice, not auto-selected, where convictions span more than one judicial district.
scopeRestrictions: Montana has no general felony expungement and no automatic conviction sealing. Part 11 reaches misdemeanours only. The only felony relief is marijuana-specific under § 16-12-113 and trafficking-survivor vacatur under § 46-18-608. There is no Clean Slate analogue, and eligibility copy must say this plainly rather than implying a felony pathway exists.

The Misdemeanor Expungement in Montana packet (ER-100, ER-200 and the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees) and the Dismissal After Completing a Deferred Sentence packet (DS-100 and DS-200) are stamped '© 2025 Montana Legal Services Association and Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission. This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed. legalDesignLimitations.statement: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

provenance.sourceStatement: Correct jurisdiction-specific terminology: "Expungement." Montana defines the word narrowly at § 46-18-1103(1): to permanently destroy, delete, or erase a record of an offense from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law enforcement agencies, and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Do not use the two words interchangeably in participant copy.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Montana has no general felony expungement and no automatic conviction sealing. Part 11 reaches misdemeanours only. The only felony relief is marijuana-specific under § 16-12-113 and trafficking-survivor vacatur under § 46-18-608. There is no Clean Slate analogue, and eligibility copy must say this plainly rather than implying a felony pathway exists.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The court order is not the end in Montana. tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement or Redesignation of a Marijuana Conviction, Sentence Completed (Mont. Code Ann. § 16-12-113(5)-(10), (12))
tracks.publicName: Marijuana conviction expungement or redesignation
tracks.mechanism: Under § 16-12-113(5)(a) a person who has COMPLETED a sentence for an act that is now permitted under Title 16, chapter 12, or that is now punishable by a lesser sentence under that chapter than the person was awarded, may petition for expungement of the conviction or for redesignation of the conviction as a misdemeanour or as a civil infraction. Section 16-12-113(5)(b) requires service on the county attorney for the county in which the petition is filed — the statute keys service to the county of FILING, not the county of prosecution. Section 16-12-113(6) directs the court to presume the petitioner satisfies the criteria unless the county attorney provides the court with a reasonable basis on which the petitioner does not; the 2021 amendment lowered that prosecutorial burden from clear and convincing evidence to providing a reasonable basis. Once the criteria are satisfied the court shall redesignate or expunge. Section 16-12-113(7) provides that unless requested by the applicant, no hearing is necessary. Section 16-12-113(8) provides that a felony conviction designated as a misdemeanour or civil infraction must be considered a misdemeanour or civil infraction for all purposes, and a misdemeanour designated as a civil infraction must be considered a civil infraction for all purposes. Section 16-12-113(9) waives no other right or remedy, § 16-12-113(10) preserves the finality of judgments in cases outside the chapter, § 16-12-113(11) applies the relief equally to juvenile cases, and § 16-12-113(12) expressly preserves the right to petition separately for misdemeanour expungement under Title 46, chapter 18, part 11. Procedure is governed by the Temporary Rules adopted by Montana Supreme Court order AF 22-0129, filed 15 March 2022, and the Office of the Court Administrator publishes Form B with a Certificate of Service and a Proposed Order. Enacted as Sec. 36, I.M. No. 190, effective 1 January 2021, amended by Sec. 48, Ch. 576, L. 2021.
exclusions: Acts that remain criminal at the same level under Title 16, chapter 12. The whole test is whether the conduct is now permitted or is now punishable by a lesser sentence.
Non-marijuana controlled substance convictions.
Convictions from out-of-state, federal or Tribal courts.
A participant who is still serving the sentence, who belongs on the currently-serving track under § 16-12-113(1) rather than this one.
Anything outside Title 16, chapter 12: § 16-12-113(10) preserves the finality of judgments in those cases.

waitingPeriods.condition: Marijuana conviction with the sentence completed
waitingPeriods.duration: None. There is no waiting period; the gating event is completion of the sentence. If the sentence is not complete the participant belongs on the currently-serving track.

units.label: MMRTA Form B petition in the sentencing court, with certificate of service and proposed order
units.description: The court stage. One complete set per conviction — MMRTA Form B, the OCA Certificate of Service and the OCA Proposed Order — filed in the court that sentenced the participant, with a copy of the participant's Montana Department of Justice criminal record attached, which Form B marks required. The Office of the Court Administrator publishes the whole set under Montana Supreme Court authority in AF 22-0129, the forms carry no use restriction, and they encode the statutory offence list, the required attachments, the § 16-12-113(7) hearing election and the § 16-12-113(5)(b) service requirement. LegalEase completes the caption for the correct court level, the participant's identity and case facts, the offence selection the participant makes from the enumerated list, and the conviction date. It does not complete the narrative explaining why the conviction is eligible, and it does not choose among expungement, misdemeanour redesignation and civil-infraction redesignation. The Certificate of Service names the county attorney for the county in which the petition is filed. The Proposed Order leaves every judicial finding and the signature blank.

units.label: DOJ CRISS submission after an expungement order
units.description: The Department of Justice stage, and a separate legal unit with its own destination and its own participant submission: the court order does not itself clear the DOJ criminal history record. LegalEase completes the participant-owned fields of the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form and supplies the mailing checklist and verification steps; the participant encloses the original or certified court judgment and the court order of expungement and mails them to CRISS. This unit applies where the outcome is EXPUNGEMENT. Where the participant instead obtains redesignation as a misdemeanour or as a civil infraction, the conviction is not expunged and there is no DOJ deletion stage to complete, so the unit does not apply and the packet says so rather than sending a request that will be refused. No FD-258 fingerprint card is required for the marijuana request type, unlike the misdemeanour expungement track.

The offence-mapping question is a self-help boundary: whether the historical conduct is now permitted, or is now punishable by a lesser sentence, under Title 16, chapter 12 requires mapping decades-old charging language and quantities against the current chapter, and it is the central legal question of the track. LegalEase presents the enumerated statutory list and the participant selects; the free-text specify-offence path is an attorney handoff.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.

One complete form set per conviction, never a consolidated petition. The OCA instructions require a separate form for each conviction even where the convictions occurred at the same time. This is the opposite of the misdemeanour expungement track, where one petition covers the whole record, and the rules engine must not generalise across the two.

Fee lookup must branch on court level and must not default to the District Court figure. The $120 civil commencement fee is the District Court schedule; Justice, Municipal and City Court fees are different and were not resolved. The OCA instructions confirm the participant is responsible for filing fees and other costs.

The OCA instructions state expressly that the participant must follow all applicable filing rules including local filing rules, and route the participant to the Court Locator for local rules and contact information. This is an acknowledged local-practice dependency and is built as a required lookup step.

§ 16-12-113(12) is express: petitioning under that section does not make a person ineligible to petition for misdemeanour expungement under Title 46, chapter 18, part 11. A participant can use both, and the eligibility engine must present them as complementary rather than alternative.
Note that § 16-12-113(5)(b) keys service to the county in which the petition is filed, not the county of prosecution.
participantQuestions: LegalEase does not choose among expungement, redesignation as a misdemeanour, and redesignation as a civil infraction. These are materially different outcomes with different consequences, the form requires the participant to choose, and the election is the participant's alone. Any analysis of which outcome is better is legal advice and triggers handoff.
scopeRestrictions: The Misdemeanor Expungement in Montana packet (ER-100, ER-200 and the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees) and the Dismissal After Completing a Deferred Sentence packet (DS-100 and DS-200) are stamped '© 2025 Montana Legal Services Association and Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission. This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

No participant-facing statement that the participant may deny the conviction after expungement, after a deferred dismissal, or after a non-conviction removal. No Montana perjury shield or restoration-to-prior-status provision was located in any of the three statutes, and whether a cleared record may lawfully be denied is a hard self-help stop.

releaseBlockers.question: Which CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form version the Department of Justice enforces in practice, and what the current required attachment set is. The 2023 PDF and the 29 April 2024 DOCX disagree: the 2023 version requires valid photo identification for the Non-Conviction Removal and Deferred Imposition request types and requires the 'Original Court Order' for misdemeanour expungement, while the 2024 version drops the photo-ID requirement, requires the 'Original Court Judgement' instead, and adds 'Deferred Prosecution' to the fourth request type. Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the 2024 version as the supporting-process asset and does not retain the 2023 PDF. The 2024 version is used for legal design and the 2023 version is preserved as history only; the packet includes photo identification by default, which is the fail-closed reading, and asks for a certified copy of the judgment.

provenance.sourceStatement: The 2023 and 2024 CRISS form versions disagree on required attachments. Unresolved which set CRISS enforces in practice.

releaseBlockers.question: Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form as a SUPPORTING_PROCESS asset with document role SUPPORTING_FORM, not as a packet form. The authority gate treats a supporting-process asset as one that cannot back an official_pdf_fill component, so every Montana component that maps to it is recorded as an authority role mismatch. The classification is the issue, not the mechanism: the form is a genuine Department of Justice agency form, it carries no use restriction, § 46-18-1110(2)(b) and § 46-18-204(2) both refer to a form prepared by the department of justice, and it is the required and only vehicle for the DOJ stage of four Montana tracks and for the whole of the non-conviction removal track. The mapping is retained rather than dropped, because pointing at the retained asset is truthful and preserves traceability, and the asset-class question is carried here as an explicit release blocker and a proposed Edition 1.2 reclassification. Edition 1.1 is not modified.

releaseBlockers.question: Master Library Edition 1.1 gives the OCA MMRTA Proposed Order and the OCA MMRTA Certificate of Service the SAME document ID, MT-OCA-MMRTA, distinguished only by document role, ORDER against SERVICE. They are two different binaries with two different SHA-256 values, so a component that names MT-OCA-MMRTA matches two retained assets carrying conflicting hashes and the authority gate records an authority hash conflict. This is an Edition 1.1 source-identity problem rather than a defect in the Montana legal design: both forms exist, both are published by the Office of the Court Administrator, both are retained, and both are correctly placed in the packet. Each needs its own document ID in a successor edition before either component can be resolver-selectable. The mappings are retained and the tracks stay authority-gated.
