legalDesignLimitations.statement: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

provenance.sourceStatement: Correct jurisdiction-specific terminology: "Expungement." Montana defines the word narrowly at § 46-18-1103(1): to permanently destroy, delete, or erase a record of an offense from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law enforcement agencies, and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Do not use the two words interchangeably in participant copy.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The Misdemeanor Expungement in Montana packet (ER-100, ER-200 and the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees) and the Dismissal After Completing a Deferred Sentence packet (DS-100 and DS-200) are stamped '© 2025 Montana Legal Services Association and Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission. This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement or Resentencing of a Marijuana Conviction While Currently Serving (Mont. Code Ann. § 16-12-113(1)-(4), (8)-(12))
tracks.publicName: Marijuana conviction expungement or resentencing while serving a sentence
tracks.mechanism: Under § 16-12-113(1) a person CURRENTLY SERVING a sentence for an act that is permitted under Title 16, chapter 12, or that is punishable by a lesser sentence under that chapter than the person was awarded, may petition for expungement or resentencing. Section 16-12-113(2) directs the court to presume the petitioner satisfies the criteria unless the county attorney provides a reasonable basis otherwise, and, where the criteria are satisfied, to grant the petition UNLESS the court determines that granting it would pose an unreasonable risk of danger to public safety. That public-safety override does not appear in the subsection (6) pathway used by the completed-sentence track, and it is the principal reason the two are separate mechanisms rather than branches. Section 16-12-113(3) requires credit for time already served and prohibits supervision after resentencing; § 16-12-113(4) prohibits a term longer than the original sentence and prohibits reinstatement of charges dismissed under a negotiated plea agreement. Sections 16-12-114 through 16-12-116 define an expungement or resentencing of marijuana conviction court and authorise appointment of a decriminalized marijuana conviction expungement judge with the authority and power of an elected district court judge. Procedure is governed by the AF 22-0129 Temporary Rules and the Office of the Court Administrator publishes Form A specifically for the currently-serving posture, with the same Certificate of Service and Proposed Order.
exclusions: Acts that remain criminal at the same level under Title 16, chapter 12.
Non-marijuana controlled substance convictions.
Convictions from out-of-state, federal or Tribal courts.
A participant who has completed the sentence, who belongs on the completed-sentence track under § 16-12-113(5).
Relief may still be refused where the court determines that granting the petition would pose an unreasonable risk of danger to public safety (§ 16-12-113(2)). That override is unique to this track.

waitingPeriods.condition: Marijuana conviction, sentence still being served
waitingPeriods.duration: None. The gating condition is the inverse of the completed-sentence track: the participant must still be serving.

units.label: MMRTA Form A petition in the sentencing court, with certificate of service and proposed order
units.description: The court stage, and the substantive heart of the track. MMRTA Form A is published by the Office of the Court Administrator specifically for the currently-serving posture: the caption, the 'I am currently serving my sentence for this conviction' recital and the resentencing election are all built into it. The adopted Batch 2 resolution memorandum controls here and is explicit that Form A is a packet product and that the currently-serving posture is a scope restriction and a substantive-choice warning rather than a reason to downgrade the mechanism to guidance. LegalEase completes the caption for the correct court level, the participant's identity and case facts, the offence selection the participant makes from the enumerated list, and the conviction date, and assembles the OCA Certificate of Service and the OCA Proposed Order. It does not choose between expungement and resentencing, does not calculate a resentencing result, and does not author any public-safety argument. Required attachments are the participant's DOJ criminal record and the supporting court documents.

units.label: Conditional DOJ CRISS submission, only where the court grants expungement
units.description: The conditional Department of Justice stage. Where the court grants EXPUNGEMENT the participant must separately submit the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form with the court judgment and the expungement order, because the court order does not itself clear the DOJ criminal history record. Where the outcome is RESENTENCING rather than expungement the conviction stands with a modified sentence, there is nothing for DOJ to delete, and this unit does not apply — the packet says so plainly rather than sending a request that will be refused. That conditionality is why the unit exists as a distinct unit rather than as a step inside unit 1.

tracks.venue: Whichever court sentenced the participant, on the same three caption options as the completed-sentence track. Sections 16-12-114 and 16-12-115 additionally define an expungement or resentencing of marijuana conviction court and permit appointment of a designated decriminalized marijuana conviction expungement judge; whether any such judge has been appointed, and whether that changes the practical filing destination in any county, is unresolved.

packetInstructions: YES — STAGED OFFICIAL-FORM PACKET. OCA MMRTA Form A is expressly designed for the currently-serving posture. That posture is a scope restriction and a substantive-choice warning, not a reason to downgrade the mechanism to guidance. LegalEase must not choose between expungement, misdemeanor resentencing, and civil-infraction resentencing or author a public-safety argument. After an expungement outcome, the participant must complete the separate DOJ CRISS stage.

Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

One complete form set per conviction, never a consolidated petition. The OCA instructions require a separate form for each conviction even where the convictions occurred at the same time. This is the opposite of the misdemeanour expungement track, where one petition covers the whole record, and the rules engine must not generalise across the two.

The OCA instructions state expressly that the participant must follow all applicable filing rules including local filing rules, and route the participant to the Court Locator for local rules and contact information. This is an acknowledged local-practice dependency and is built as a required lookup step.
participantQuestions: LegalEase does not choose among expungement, redesignation as a misdemeanour, and redesignation as a civil infraction. These are materially different outcomes with different consequences, the form requires the participant to choose, and the election is the participant's alone. Any analysis of which outcome is better is legal advice and triggers handoff.

The public-safety override in § 16-12-113(2) is unique to this track and does not appear in the completed-sentence pathway. Any case where it is plausibly in play is a handoff.

This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

releaseBlockers.question: Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form as a SUPPORTING_PROCESS asset with document role SUPPORTING_FORM, not as a packet form. The authority gate treats a supporting-process asset as one that cannot back an official_pdf_fill component, so every Montana component that maps to it is recorded as an authority role mismatch. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Strike Plea or Verdict, Dismiss Charge, and Seal Case After a Completed Deferred Imposition (Mont. Code Ann. § 46-18-204)
tracks.publicName: Dismissal and sealing after a completed deferred sentence
tracks.mechanism: Section 46-18-204 has two limbs sharing one process, one destination, one document set and one legal effect, differing only on whether relief is mandatory. Under § 46-18-204(1)(a), on a FELONY deferred imposition, after termination of the deferral period or upon termination of the time remaining under § 46-18-208, the court SHALL strike the plea of guilty or nolo contendere or the verdict of guilty and order the charge dismissed, PROVIDED THAT a petition for revocation under § 46-18-203 has not been filed. Under § 46-18-204(1)(b), on a MISDEMEANOUR deferred imposition, upon motion of the court, the defendant or the defendant's attorney, the court MAY allow withdrawal of the plea or strike the verdict and order dismissal — discretionary, with no statutory factors. After dismissal, all records and data relating to the charge are confidential criminal justice information as defined in § 44-5-103, and public access may be obtained only by district court order upon good cause shown. This is sealing, not expungement: the record is not destroyed, and per DOJ the agencies listed in § 44-5-103 retain access to the sealed record in its entirety, DOJ specifically naming law enforcement including the military and Border Patrol. Section 46-18-204(2) puts the second stage on the participant: a copy of the order of dismissal must be sent to the prosecutor and to the Department of Justice with the DOJ form. Amended by Sec. 25, Ch. 321, L. 2017; no amendment since.
exclusions: A felony case in which a petition for revocation under § 46-18-203 was filed. That is the operative bar on the mandatory limb and it defeats § 46-18-204(1)(a) outright.

A SUSPENDED sentence. The published guidance states expressly that it does not apply to suspended sentences, and a participant who received a suspended rather than a deferred sentence is outside this route entirely.
A participant seeking early termination under § 46-18-208 rather than post-completion dismissal.
A deferral period that has not terminated and where no early termination under § 46-18-208 has occurred.
A case the court has already dismissed and sealed on its own, which the published guidance warns may have happened. The clerk-contact step is designed to catch this before anything is filed.

waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond expiry of the deferral period, or termination of the time remaining under § 46-18-208. There is no additional waiting period and, unlike the misdemeanour expungement track, this is not once in a lifetime.

units.label: Motion in the sentencing court to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge and seal the case
units.description: The court stage. A motion to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge and seal the case, with a certificate of service and a proposed order, filed in the court that issued the deferred sentence, under the SAME case number as the original criminal case. This is a motion in the existing criminal case rather than a new civil action, which is why no new filing fee is ordinarily expected. Section 46-18-204 prescribes no form, and the only published forms — DS-100 and DS-200 — carry the same non-commercial-use restriction as the misdemeanour expungement packet and cannot be shipped in a paid packet, so LegalEase drafts its own. The motion pleads the crime of conviction and whether it is a misdemeanour or a felony; whether the defendant pleaded guilty or nolo contendere or was found guilty by verdict; the date of sentencing and the fact of a deferred sentence; that the period of deferral has expired; that the defendant complied with all conditions; and that the prosecuting agency did not file a petition to revoke during the deferral period. The felony limb recites the mandatory shall and the no-revocation-petition proviso expressly; the misdemeanour limb is pleaded as discretionary. The prayer asks the court to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge, seal the case, classify all records and data as confidential criminal justice information accessible to the public only by district court order upon good cause shown, and send a copy of the order to the prosecuting agency, and recites that the defendant will be responsible for providing a copy to the Department of Justice. localFormOverride is set because the published guidance acknowledges that individual courts may have their own procedures or different forms, and a court's current local form takes precedence over the drafted motion.

units.label: DOJ CRISS submission after the dismissal order
units.description: The Department of Justice stage, a separate participant submission to a different destination that § 46-18-204(2) places on the participant. LegalEase completes the participant-owned fields of the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form with the deferred-imposition request type selected, and supplies the mailing checklist and the verification steps; the participant encloses the deferred sentence order and the dismissal order and mails them to CRISS. Without this stage the DOJ criminal history record continues to show the charge.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.

A DOJ removal or expungement does not reach public county court records. Montana has no centralised court records system, so each county court must be searched separately, and a participant who successfully clears the DOJ record may still find the case on a county court portal. Participant-facing copy must say so.

Stage 1, the call to the clerk, is a required packet step with a script. The published guidance says courts may have their own procedures or forms and that the case may already have been dismissed and sealed.
LegalEase drafts its own motion, certificate of service, and proposed order. It must not reproduce DS-100 or DS-200.

Participant-facing copy must say "sealed and treated as confidential criminal justice information," never "destroyed" or "erased." Agencies listed in § 44-5-103 retain access to the sealed record in its entirety, and DOJ specifically names law enforcement including the military and Border Patrol.
participantQuestions: Whether a petition to revoke was ever filed is dispositive for the felony limb and must be confirmed with the clerk rather than asserted from the participant's recollection.
scopeRestrictions: The Misdemeanor Expungement in Montana packet (ER-100, ER-200 and the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees) and the Dismissal After Completing a Deferred Sentence packet (DS-100 and DS-200) are stamped '© 2025 Montana Legal Services Association and Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission. This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

No participant-facing statement that the participant may deny the conviction after expungement, after a deferred dismissal, or after a non-conviction removal. No Montana perjury shield or restoration-to-prior-status provision was located in any of the three statutes, and whether a cleared record may lawfully be denied is a hard self-help stop.
Immigration warning before generation. A dismissal after deferred imposition may still be a conviction for federal immigration purposes, and a noncitizen participant is a hard stop.

The qualifying felony deferred-imposition limb is mandatory where no revocation petition was filed; the misdemeanour limb remains discretionary with no statutory factors. The distinction must be preserved in the pleading and in participant expectations.
Local court procedures and forms remain release gates. localFormOverride is set and a court's current local form takes precedence over the drafted motion.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

provenance.sourceStatement: Correct jurisdiction-specific terminology: "Expungement." Montana defines the word narrowly at § 46-18-1103(1): to permanently destroy, delete, or erase a record of an offense from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law enforcement agencies, and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Do not use the two words interchangeably in participant copy.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The Misdemeanor Expungement in Montana packet (ER-100, ER-200 and the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees) and the Dismissal After Completing a Deferred Sentence packet (DS-100 and DS-200) are stamped '© 2025 Montana Legal Services Association and Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission. This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

tracks.legalName: Non-Conviction Record Removal Request to DOJ CRISS (Mont. Code Ann. § 44-5-202(8))
tracks.publicName: Non-conviction record removal
tracks.mechanism: Montana distinguishes removal, where the record is deleted from the database and hard copy destroyed, from sealing under § 46-18-204, where the record persists but is confidential. Section 44-5-202(8), read with § 44-5-213(2), compels the disposition to be reported to the state repository within fourteen business days, requires photographs and fingerprints to be returned to the originating agency which shall expunge all copies, and provides that a criminal justice agency may not maintain any copies. DOJ publishes a single agency form, the Expungement/Removal Request Form, with a dedicated Non-Conviction Removal request type, and its published list of eligible dispositions is charges dismissed, deferred prosecution dismissed, acquitted, charges dropped and charges not filed; in statute the categories are released without the filing of charges, charges that did not result in a conviction, and a conviction later invalidated. Two gaps must be recorded rather than papered over. First, § 44-5-202 is titled Photographs and fingerprints and subsection (8) by its terms compels expungement of PHOTOGRAPHS AND FINGERPRINTS; it does not on its face compel deletion of the criminal history record entry itself, and § 44-5-212 separately limits expunging, purging or destroying criminal justice information. DOJ nonetheless treats § 44-5-202(8) as the authority for removing non-conviction arrest data and instructs participants to quote it, so LegalEase follows the published practice but does not represent the outcome as legally guaranteed beyond the photographs and fingerprints. Second, § 44-5-202(8) reaches the state repository and originating agencies and does NOT reach court records; Montana has no comparable authority to seal non-conviction court records and no centralised court records system, so a participant who succeeds here may still find the case on a county court portal.
exclusions: Convictions. This route reaches non-conviction records only.
A deferred imposition that has not yet been dismissed. DOJ routes those back to the court, which means the deferred-dismissal track comes first.
A deferred sentence that was revoked, which the DOJ flowchart treats as a conviction.
Court records. § 44-5-202(8) reaches the state repository and originating agencies only, and the case may remain publicly searchable on a county court portal.
Records in other states, federal records and Tribal records.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

A DOJ removal or expungement does not reach public county court records. Montana has no centralised court records system, so each county court must be searched separately, and a participant who successfully clears the DOJ record may still find the case on a county court portal. Participant-facing copy must say so.
Participant-facing copy must state clearly that this track does not reach court records and that the case may still appear on a county court portal.
Do not describe the outcome as legally guaranteed beyond photographs and fingerprints; the cited statute is narrower than the published DOJ practice.
The CHOPRS check is a required prerequisite step, per DOJ, and must be run before the request is submitted.
Include photo ID by default pending resolution of the 2023 versus 2024 form discrepancy.
scopeRestrictions: No participant-facing statement that the participant may deny the conviction after expungement, after a deferred dismissal, or after a non-conviction removal. No Montana perjury shield or restoration-to-prior-status provision was located in any of the three statutes, and whether a cleared record may lawfully be denied is a hard self-help stop.
A deferred imposition not yet dismissed routes to the deferred-dismissal track first, and a revoked deferred sentence is treated by DOJ as a conviction and is outside this route.

releaseBlockers.question: Which CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form version the Department of Justice enforces in practice, and what the current required attachment set is. The 2023 PDF and the 29 April 2024 DOCX disagree: the 2023 version requires valid photo identification for the Non-Conviction Removal and Deferred Imposition request types and requires the 'Original Court Order' for misdemeanour expungement, while the 2024 version drops the photo-ID requirement, requires the 'Original Court Judgement' instead, and adds 'Deferred Prosecution' to the fourth request type. Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the 2024 version as the supporting-process asset and does not retain the 2023 PDF. The 2024 version is used for legal design and the 2023 version is preserved as history only; the packet includes photo identification by default, which is the fail-closed reading, and asks for a certified copy of the judgment.

openLegalQuestions.question: The DOJ Records Removal Flowchart states that convictions are 'not eligible for Expungement or sealing unless by order of the MT Supreme Court'. That does not match Part 11, which vests misdemeanour expungement in the DISTRICT courts, or § 16-12-113, which vests marijuana relief in the sentencing court. It reads as a drafting error for 'district court'. It matters because the flowchart is the first document many participants will see, and the packet must correct the impression rather than repeat it.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Non-Conviction Removal for Post-July-2017 Dispositions (Mont. Code Ann. § 44-5-202(8))
tracks.publicName: Automatic non-conviction removal
tracks.mechanism: Section 44-5-202(8), as amended by Ch. 321, L. 2017 effective 1 July 2017 and read with § 44-5-213(2), underpins a DOJ practice of removing non-conviction arrest data without any participant request. The Montana Department of Justice states on its Non-Conviction Removal and Sealing page that after 1 July 2017 CRISS will automatically remove all non-conviction arrest data per § 44-5-202 and that NO Record Removal Form is required. The trigger is the court's report of the disposition to the state repository, which the statute requires within fourteen business days. Relief is mandatory and automatic, there is no waiting period and no case-count limit, and there is no petition, application, motion or form for a participant to submit. The only practical question on this route is whether a record that has not been removed is ineligible or is simply the product of a court that failed to report the disposition, which is a records problem rather than a legal one.
exclusions: Dispositions occurring before 1 July 2017, which are not reached by the automatic practice and go to the non-conviction removal request route instead.
Convictions.
A revoked deferred sentence, which the DOJ flowchart treats as a conviction.
Court records, which the automatic removal does not reach and which remain publicly searchable on the county court portal.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

provenance.sourceStatement: Correct jurisdiction-specific terminology: "Expungement." Montana defines the word narrowly at § 46-18-1103(1): to permanently destroy, delete, or erase a record of an offense from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law enforcement agencies, and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Do not use the two words interchangeably in participant copy.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: A DOJ removal or expungement does not reach public county court records. Montana has no centralised court records system, so each county court must be searched separately, and a participant who successfully clears the DOJ record may still find the case on a county court portal. Participant-facing copy must say so.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK 5 - NON-CONVICTION REMOVAL ON WRITTEN REQUEST
provenance.sourceStatement: A second gap with real participant impact. § 44-5-202(8) reaches the state repository and originating agencies. It does not reach court records. Montana has no comparable authority to seal non-conviction court records, and the state has no centralized court records system, so each county court must be searched separately.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: No participant-facing statement that the participant may deny the conviction after expungement, after a deferred dismissal, or after a non-conviction removal. No Montana perjury shield or restoration-to-prior-status provision was located in any of the three statutes, and whether a cleared record may lawfully be denied is a hard self-help stop.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Expunction of Dismissals and Findings of Not Guilty or Not Responsible under G.S. 15A-146(a4)
tracks.publicName: Your dismissed North Carolina case may have cleared itself
tracks.mechanism: Where a person is charged with a misdemeanor, a felony or an infraction and all charges in the case are disposed on or after December 1, 2021 by dismissal, a finding of not guilty, or a finding of not responsible, the charges are expunged by operation of law not less than 180 and not more than 210 days after the date of final disposition, if the statutory conditions are met. The General Assembly postponed the automatic process until July 1, 2024; it is now underway.
exclusions: Dispositions before December 1, 2021.
Cases in which not every charge was disposed favorably.
Dismissals through deferred prosecution or conditional discharge, which are treated differently and route to the petition track.
Under G.S. 15A-146(a), no case with a felony charge dismissed pursuant to a plea agreement is expunged under that subsection.

Effective for dismissals on or after December 1, 2025, a dismissal by the court of a charge against a defendant found incapable to proceed is not eligible for expunction under G.S. 15A-146 and should not be included in an automatic expunction.

tracks.legalName: Written Request to a Non-Court Record Holder to Conform Its Records to an Automatic Expunction under G.S. 15A-146(a4)
tracks.publicName: Ask an agency to clear a record that already cleared in court
tracks.mechanism: Where charges were expunged by operation of law under G.S. 15A-146(a4), the clerk is not required to transmit an expunction order to other entities. An agency that still holds and disseminates the charge may therefore be unaware the expunction occurred. G.S. 15A-153 restores the person to the status they occupied before the arrest, charge or conviction, and G.S. 15A-150 states the notification scheme for expunctions generally. This supporting action produces the participant's own written request asking the record holder to conform its records to the expunction that has already happened. It seeks no new relief and asks no court for anything.
exclusions: Any case where the automatic expunction under G.S. 15A-146(a4) has not in fact occurred. This action presupposes the expunction; where it did not run, the petition tracks apply instead.
Any case still inside the 180-to-210-day statutory window, which has not yet matured.
Federal record holders and out-of-state agencies, which North Carolina expunction does not reach.
The court record itself, which is the clerk's and the AOC's to maintain under G.S. 15A-151(a1).

The letter states the case, the disposition, the disposition date, the statutory basis for the automatic expunction and the date the 210-day window closed, and asks the holder to conform its records. LegalEase writes the participant's request; it does not certify that the agency failed to act and does not assert that the expunction occurred as a matter of fact.

packetInstructions: The letter asks a record holder to conform its records to an expunction that has already happened. It must not assert that the agency has broken any duty, and it must not certify that the expunction occurred; it states the participant's account and the statutory basis and asks the holder to check its own records.

The participant obtains a right-to-review copy of their own SBI criminal history before the request goes out, because that is what identifies which holders still show the charge. LegalEase never sees it.

tracks.legalName: Petition and Order of Expunction of Dismissed Charges under G.S. 15A-146(a) and (a1)
tracks.publicName: Clear a North Carolina charge that was dismissed
tracks.mechanism: On petition, the court expunges the records of a charge dismissed by the State or by the court, for a single dismissal under subsection (a) and for multiple dismissals under subsection (a1). There is no prior-conviction bar and no prior-expunction bar; the 2017 legislation eliminated the prior-expunction bar. A judge may grant the petition without a hearing under subsection (a6). Any petition under this section must be on a form approved by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
exclusions: No case with a felony charge dismissed pursuant to a plea agreement is expunged under subsection (a).

Effective for dismissals on or after December 1, 2025, a court dismissal of a charge against a defendant found incapable to proceed is not eligible. AOC-CR-287 (Dec. 2025) reflects this and does not limit the exclusion by date, which leaves earlier dismissals unresolved.
Out-of-state and federal convictions and charges are outside this relief; it reaches North Carolina records only.

rules.filing: File the AOC-approved form with the clerk of superior court in the county where the charge was brought. G.S. 15A-146(c) requires any petition under this section to be on a form approved by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
rules.fees: none for a true dismissal. $175 applies where the charge was dismissed pursuant to a deferred prosecution or conditional discharge agreement. Separately, the costs of expunging the records required under G.S. 15A-150 are not taxed against the petitioner.
rules.feeWaiver: Where the $175 fee under G.S. 15A-146(d) applies and the petitioner cannot pay it, the operative expunction indigency filing is AOC-G-106, Petition to Proceed as an Indigent (printed revision 11/24, two pages), which the Judicial Branch's expunction fee answer links directly; its fourth principal election is 'Petition To File Expunction Petition', with an affidavit, a legal-services certification and court-order blocks. AOC-CV-226, Civil Affidavit of Indigency (Rev. 4/23), is supplemental financial information that many counties use when the court asks for more; it is not the expunction fee-waiver filing, and its side-two oath concerns arbitration fees and is never rewritten or presented as an expunction assertion. Benefit receipt (SNAP, TANF, SSI) and legal-services representation are selections on G-106 that require actual participant support; absence of benefit receipt does not by itself foreclose the separate inability-to-pay selection. Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research; not counsel approval. (Before 2026-09-06 this rule read: 'Indigency waiver available where a fee applies, on AOC-CV-226, including for petitioners receiving SNAP, TANF or SSI or represented by a legal services organization.')

rules.service: none required by the AOC form for dismissals. A DNA expunction application under G.S. 15A-146(b1) is a separate matter and must be served on the district attorney not less than 20 days before the hearing.

researchParticipantText.text: Filing fee and inability to pay. An ordinary dismissal petition under this route has no filing fee. The $175 fee applies when the dismissal resulted from the specified deferred-prosecution or conditional-discharge process. If that fee applies and you cannot afford it, submit the Petition to Proceed as an Indigent with your expunction petition. Complete only truthful answers and sign its affidavit before an official authorized to administer the oath. The court decides your request. Provide additional financial information if the court requests it.

tracks.legalName: Petition and Order of Expunction of a Finding of Not Guilty or Not Responsible under G.S. 15A-146(a2)
tracks.publicName: Clear a North Carolina charge you were found not guilty of
tracks.mechanism: On petition, the court expunges the records of a finding of not guilty on a misdemeanor or felony charge, or a finding of not responsible for certain infractions. The bars, effect, venue, fee, hearing and packet are identical to the dismissal petition: no prior-conviction bar, no prior-expunction bar and free filing for a true acquittal. This is a separate track because it is a different subsection with a different official form, and using AOC-CR-287 for an acquittal is a rejection risk.
exclusions: Out-of-state and federal charges are outside this relief; it reaches North Carolina records only.

tracks.legalName: Petition and Order of Expunction of Nonviolent Misdemeanor Convictions under G.S. 15A-145.5
tracks.publicName: Expunge a nonviolent North Carolina misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: On petition, the court may expunge nonviolent misdemeanor convictions. Nonviolent is defined by exclusion in G.S. 15A-145.5(a). The waiting period is three years for one nonviolent misdemeanor conviction, for petitions filed on or after July 9, 2025, and seven years for more than one, each measured from the conviction and completion of any active, probationary or post-release sentence, whichever is later. The petitioner consents to two record checks: the AOC checks for prior expunctions and the DPS State Bureau of Investigation checks for prior convictions. The district attorney is given notice and may be heard.
exclusions: Any Class A through G felony, so only Class H and I felonies can qualify as nonviolent.
Any Class A1 misdemeanor.
Impaired driving under G.S. 20-138.1 and related offenses. DWI is the classic trap.
Sex offenses and any offense requiring sex offender registration.
Offenses with assault as an essential element, certain offenses against minors, stalking and other enumerated crimes.
Methamphetamine offenses, certain controlled substance trafficking, and hate crimes, as enumerated.
Any non-traffic conviction at any time other than the offense or offenses being expunged bars relief on this track.
A new conviction during the waiting period.
Generally, more than one expunction under G.S. 15A-145.5 in a lifetime.
Outstanding restitution on the conviction to be expunged, until satisfied.
Pending charges at the time of the petition.
Out-of-state and federal convictions are not expungeable here, but they count toward eligibility.

waitingPeriods.condition: One nonviolent misdemeanor conviction, for petitions filed on or after July 9, 2025
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the conviction and completion of any active, probationary or post-release sentence, whichever is later

waitingPeriods.condition: More than one nonviolent misdemeanor conviction
waitingPeriods.duration: 7 years from the last conviction and completion of sentence

On a grant the order directs the SBI, DPS, DMV, the AOC, the clerk and the arresting agency to expunge the records, and the clerk notifies State and local agencies under G.S. 15A-150.

packetInstructions: The AOC-CR-297 and AOC-CR-298 identities are pinned as follows, read off the official publication on 2026-08-06: AOC-CR-297 is "Petition And Order Of Expunction Under G.S. 15A-145.5 (Nonviolent Felony(ies))" at Rev. 6/25, and AOC-CR-298 is "Petition And Order Of Expunction Under G.S. 15A-145.5 (Nonviolent Misdemeanor(s))" at Rev. 7/25. Both sit on the same statute and differ only by offence class, so a transposed number is a live rejection risk. This track uses AOC-CR-298. Any archive metadata that crosses the two is corrected against this record.

The route was previously staged as a composed track: record gathering, then AOC-CR-298, then filing and follow-through. It is one petition. The petitioner is the only filer, the clerk of superior court is the only destination, AOC-CR-298 is the only submission, and the expunction order is the only legal effect. The record-gathering step is preparation before filing and the follow-through step is ordinary post-filing handoff, so neither is a legally distinct unit. Both survive as required components and packet instructions on a single official_pdf_fill route, which is what the review's own "official form status: AOC-approved and required" finding describes.
Good-character affidavits are participant-supplied third-party documents. Build the request, do not draft the content.
scopeRestrictions: The any-non-traffic-conviction bar on this track is absolute and must be screened against the SBI record, not participant recall.
DWI and Class A1 misdemeanors are categorically out.
Any non-traffic conviction anywhere bars the misdemeanor track.

tracks.legalName: Petition and Order of Expunction of Nonviolent Felony Convictions under G.S. 15A-145.5
tracks.publicName: Expunge a nonviolent North Carolina felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: On petition, the court may expunge nonviolent felony convictions. Only Class H and I felonies can be nonviolent; Class A through G felonies are categorically out. The waiting period is ten years from completion of the sentence for one nonviolent felony conviction and twenty years for two or three. All nonviolent felonies disposed in the same session of court count as one nonviolent felony conviction for both the count and the waiting tier.
exclusions: Any Class A through G felony. Only Class H and I felonies can be nonviolent.
Sex offenses and any offense requiring sex offender registration.
Offenses with assault as an essential element, certain offenses against minors, stalking and other enumerated crimes.
Methamphetamine offenses, certain controlled substance trafficking, and hate crimes, as enumerated.
More than three nonviolent felony convictions.
Disqualifying convictions, and any new conviction during the waiting period.
Outstanding restitution on the conviction to be expunged, until satisfied.
Generally, more than one expunction under G.S. 15A-145.5 in a lifetime.
Pending charges at the time of the petition.
Out-of-state and federal convictions are not expungeable here, but they count toward eligibility.

waitingPeriods.duration: 10 years from completion of the sentence

waitingPeriods.condition: Two or three nonviolent felony convictions
waitingPeriods.duration: 20 years from completion of the sentence

waitingPeriods.condition: Nonviolent felonies disposed in the same session of court
waitingPeriods.duration: Counted as one nonviolent felony conviction for both the count and the waiting tier, which can move a petitioner from the twenty-year tier to the ten-year tier or from ineligible to eligible

destination.detail: As in the misdemeanor track, with AOC-CR-297 in place of AOC-CR-298. On a grant the order directs the SBI, DPS, DMV, the AOC, the clerk and the arresting agency to expunge the records.

The record-gathering step is preparation before filing and the follow-through step is ordinary post-filing handoff, so neither is a legally distinct unit. Both survive as required components and packet instructions on a single official_pdf_fill route, which is what the review's own "official form status: AOC-approved and required" finding describes.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Close Nonconviction Court Records Entered Before 1 August 2025 (N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-05(2))
tracks.publicName: Close the court record of a North Dakota case that ended without a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Where an order of nonconviction was entered before 1 August 2025, the defendant may petition to close the court record, and the court shall enter the closing order within ten days of filing. A closed record may be examined only by the clerk, a judge, the juvenile commission, a criminal justice agency, the defendant, defence counsel, the state's attorney, or any person on the written order of a judge. Closing reaches the court record only: it does not close prosecutor or law enforcement records and does not reach BCI criminal history record information.
exclusions: A dismissal resulting from a plea agreement involving conviction on another offence.
A dismissal on a fitness-to-proceed finding under N.D.C.C. Chapter 12.1-04.
A verdict of not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility under N.D.C.C. Chapter 12.1-04.1.
Any case that was appealed.
Partial dispositions. Section 12-60.1-01(5) requires that all charges were dismissed or all acquitted.
Orders of nonconviction entered on or after 1 August 2025, which close automatically and need no petition.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Closing of Nonconviction Court Records Entered On or After 1 August 2025 (N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-05(1))
tracks.publicName: Check that your North Dakota nonconviction record closed on its own
tracks.mechanism: Where an order of nonconviction is entered on or after 1 August 2025, the court shall close the court record upon the expiration of sixty-one days. Nothing is filed and nothing is requested. The access limits and the reach limits are the same as on the petition route.
exclusions: A dismissal resulting from a plea agreement involving conviction on another offence.
A dismissal on a fitness-to-proceed finding under Chapter 12.1-04.
A verdict of not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility under Chapter 12.1-04.1.

Any case that was appealed. The statute says 'The case was appealed', not only 'an appeal is pending': any appeal history, including a concluded appeal, is flagged for legal review under this workflow and is never automatically admitted (research correction of 2026-09-06).
Partial dispositions.

waitingPeriods.duration: Sixty-one days from the date the court entered the order, computed under N.D.R.Crim.P. 45: the entry date is excluded, calendar days are counted, and a last day falling on a weekend or legal holiday extends to the next day that is not; no mail-service days are added to an entry-date clock. The product's first administrative check falls on the next business day after the adjusted period expires; that check-day delay is a product choice, not a statutory waiting period. Calendar examples from the research, assuming no legal holiday: entered August 1, 2025 → day 61 October 1 (Wednesday) → first check October 2; entered August 4, 2025 → day 61 October 4 (Saturday) → adjusted October 6 → first check October 7. Implementation supplies the applicable holiday calendar rather than inferring it.

rules.researchProductMechanismVersusLaw: The nonfiled clerk-correction request is a proposed administrative step; the five-business-day interval after confirmed receipt is an optional LegalEase cure interval, not a statutory prerequisite, and an express refusal or an instruction to seek a judicial order may allow the product to advance earlier. The statute prescribes no letter, interval or specially named enforcement motion; counsel or design adoption is still required for the custom escalation strategy. The proposed escalation is a motion in the original case requesting performance of the statutory closing duty, not a discretionary conviction-sealing petition or an appellate challenge; relief is restricted to court-controlled records and never promises removal of prosecutor, police, federal or private database records.
rules.researchEnforcementPacket: An approved enforcement design includes the original caption, the motion, a notice of motion and short supporting brief (N.D.R.Ct. 3.2 requires notice and a brief; its note allows a liberal understanding of what constitutes a brief; a concise legal-grounds section suffices), a factual declaration and exhibits where needed, a proposed order, and proof of service. N.D.R.Crim.P. 47(c) generally requires a written motion and hearing notice at least 21 days before a hearing unless another rule or court order sets a different time; no automatic 21-day delay is hardcoded for a motion submitted on briefs and the five-day administrative interval never satisfies hearing notice. Rule 3.2 supplies a 14-day answer-brief period and a seven-day reply period and allows a hearing request. Rule 49 requires service on the other parties, ordinarily through the prosecuting attorney, by permitted methods with proof filed. The official six-page packet (Rev. April 2026) is principally the petition and order package for pre-August-2025 nonconvictions; its earlier-case petition is never populated as the post-period letter and its note about a judge possibly requiring a prosecutor copy is not imported into the Rule 49 motion.

researchClerkRequestDraft.use: Administrative correspondence only, for legal and design adoption: not an official form, not a filed motion, not a sworn declaration; no case-specific fact is generated automatically; the actual sent and received dates are recorded separately; the original letter and response are kept as evidence; no certificate of service is prefilled for an act that has not occurred.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal a Misdemeanor Conviction (N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-02(1)(a))
tracks.publicName: Ask a North Dakota court to seal a misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person who pled guilty to or was found guilty of a misdemeanor may petition to seal the record if they have not been convicted of a new crime for at least three years before filing the petition. Sealing prohibits disclosure of the existence or contents of court and prosecution records except by court order. The three years are a look-back from filing, not a wait measured from sentence completion; completion of imprisonment and probation and payment of restitution are separate findings the court must make under § 12-60.1-04(1)(c) and (d).
exclusions: Any offence for which the offender has been ordered to register under N.D.C.C. § 12.1-32-15.

packetInstructions: Sealing under Chapter 12-60.1 does not reach BCI criminal history record information or the criminal justice data system, and it does not reach federal, tribal, military, out-of-state or private-database records. The order also states that the petitioner remains subject to N.D.C.C. § 12.1-33-02.1 and that the information is released where an entity has a statutory obligation to run a background check.
The proposed order is filed with the petition, not after it. N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-03(3) makes it mandatory and a petition without one is incomplete.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal a Felony Conviction (N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-02(1)(b))
tracks.publicName: Ask a North Dakota court to seal a felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person who pled guilty to or was found guilty of a felony may petition to seal the record if they have not been convicted of a new crime for at least five years before filing. The chapter bars a felony offence involving violence or intimidation during the period in which the offender is ineligible to possess a firearm under N.D.C.C. § 62.1-02-01(1)(a), which is ten years from the latest of conviction, release from incarceration, release from parole or release from probation, for offences in chapters 12.1-16 through 12.1-25.
exclusions: A felony offence involving violence or intimidation, during the firearm-disability period under N.D.C.C. § 62.1-02-01(1)(a). The offence set is N.D.C.C. chapters 12.1-16 through 12.1-25 or an equivalent out-of-state or federal offence, and the disability runs ten years from the latest of conviction, release from incarceration, release from parole or release from probation.
Any offence for which the offender has been ordered to register under N.D.C.C. § 12.1-32-15.
Impaired-driving offences, which route to N.D.C.C. § 39-08-01.6.

tracks.publicName: Ask a North Dakota court to seal a conviction the Governor has pardoned
tracks.mechanism: A person granted an unconditional pardon for a North Dakota conviction may petition to seal the record. This ground carries no look-back period of its own. A pardon does not remove the fact of the conviction unless the certificate of pardon says so, which is why sealing is a separate step.
exclusions: A conditional pardon. N.D.C.C. § 12-55.1-01(2) defines a conditional pardon as one subject to terms and conditions established by the governor.
The chapter-level bars in N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-02(2) still apply and are not lifted by a pardon.
Impaired-driving offences, which route to N.D.C.C. § 39-08-01.6.

waitingPeriods.duration: none. This ground carries no look-back period

tracks.venue: The existing criminal case for the offence, under N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-03(1). There is no separate civil action. District court or municipal court, whichever holds the case.

The petitioner serves the prosecuting attorney under N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-03(4), which routes through N.D.R.Crim.P. 49 to N.D.R.Civ.P. 5(b).

awaitingCounselClassification.question: Whether the six findings in N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-04(1), including reformation, must still be pleaded where a pardon is the ground. The structure of the chapter says they do: § 12-60.1-02 supplies grounds to file and § 12-60.1-04(1) governs whether the court may grant, with no pardon carve-out, and the official research guide lists the same six findings without exception. That is an inference from structure rather than an express provision, and it changes what the petition must argue.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal a Driving Under the Influence Record (N.D.C.C. § 39-08-01.6)
tracks.publicName: Ask a North Dakota court to seal a DUI record
tracks.mechanism: The court shall seal a criminal record relating to a conviction under N.D.C.C. § 39-08-01, in accordance with §§ 12.1-32-07.1 and 12.1-32-07.2, where the individual has not committed a further violation of § 39-08-01 or an equivalent ordinance, or any other criminal offence, within seven years of the first violation. The seal is the § 12.1-32-07.2(2) restricted-access regime: the records may be examined by the clerk, a judge, the juvenile commissioner, probation officers, the defendant or defence counsel and the state's attorney, and by others only on the written order of a judge. A prosecutor retains access to a prior offence for enhancement under § 39-08-01(3).
exclusions: An individual licensed as a commercial driver under N.D.C.C. § 39-06.2-10.
Any further violation of § 39-08-01 or an equivalent ordinance within the seven-year clean period.
Any other criminal offence within the seven-year clean period. The clean period is not limited to impaired driving.
Out-of-state impaired-driving convictions, which a North Dakota court cannot reach.

waitingPeriods.condition: No further § 39-08-01 or equivalent-ordinance violation and no other criminal offence
waitingPeriods.duration: seven years measured from the date of the first violation, not from conviction or sentence completion

tracks.legalName: Motion to Seal a First Marijuana or THC Possession Conviction (N.D.C.C. § 19-03.1-23(9))
tracks.publicName: Ask a North Dakota court to seal a first marijuana possession conviction
tracks.mechanism: Where a person pleads guilty or is found guilty of a first offence of possessing one ounce or less of marijuana or two grams or less of tetrahydrocannabinol and a judgment of guilt is entered, the court shall, upon motion, seal the court record of that conviction if the person is not subsequently convicted within two years of a further violation of the chapter. Relief is mandatory on the elements, and once sealed the record may not be opened even by order of the court, which makes this seal stronger than Chapter 12-60.1 sealing.
exclusions: Anything other than a first offence.
Quantities above one ounce of marijuana or two grams of tetrahydrocannabinol.
A subsequent conviction of a further violation of Chapter 19-03.1 within two years.
Any non-marijuana charge in the same case. The subsection seals the court record of that conviction.

tracks.legalName: Deferred Imposition of Sentence: Automatic Withdrawal, Dismissal and Sealing, and the Fallback Motion (N.D.R.Crim.P. 32.1; N.D.C.C. §§ 12.1-32-07.1, 12.1-32-07.2)
tracks.publicName: Clear a North Dakota case where the court deferred your sentence
tracks.mechanism: N.D.R.Crim.P. 32.1 makes it a mandatory term of every order deferring imposition of sentence that, sixty-one days after probation expires or terminates, the guilty plea is withdrawn or the verdict set aside, the case is dismissed and the file is sealed. Since the amendment effective 1 March 2019 the rule applies in all cases, not only misdemeanors and infractions. Where the term did not operate, the defendant may move under N.D.C.C. § 12.1-32-07.1, which also permits the court, on application by the defendant, to reduce a felony to a misdemeanor before dismissing. A deferred disposition remains pleadable in a later prosecution under § 12.1-32-02(4) and counts as a conviction for firearm purposes under § 62.1-02-01(2).
exclusions: A petition for revocation filed within sixty days of expiration or termination of probation.
An outstanding bench warrant in the deferred matter.
Registration consequences under N.D.C.C. § 12.1-32-15 and firearm consequences under § 62.1-02-01, both of which survive dismissal.
Deferral orders entered before 1 March 2019, which may carry the narrower misdemeanor and infraction term, and orders before 1 March 1999, which predate the rule.

waitingPeriods.duration: sixty-one days, after which the automatic term operates. The modification window closes at sixty days

units.label: Verify the automatic withdrawal, dismissal and sealing at sixty-one days
units.description: Confirms the deferral order was entered, that probation expired or terminated, that no revocation petition was filed within sixty days and no bench warrant is outstanding, and that at day sixty-one the plea was withdrawn or the verdict set aside, the case dismissed and the file sealed. The participant obtains the final dismissal order from the clerk. Nothing is filed, because the rule makes this a term of the court's own order.

units.description: Filed in the existing criminal case where the deferral order predates the Rule 32.1 regime, or where the clerk's file shows the sixty-one-day term was not carried out. Asks the court to withdraw the plea or set aside the verdict, dismiss the information or indictment, and where applicable reduce a felony to a misdemeanor on the defendant's application. No official form exists.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Prohibit Remote Public Access to a Criminal Case Record After Dismissal or Acquittal (N.D.Sup.Ct.Admin.R. 41 § 4(a)(7))
tracks.publicName: Ask a North Dakota court to take your dismissed case off the internet
tracks.mechanism: Where the charges against a defendant are dismissed or the defendant is acquitted, the court may, after conducting the balancing analysis and making the findings required by section 4(a)(3), prohibit remote access to the individual defendant's electronic case record if the interest of justice will be served. The search result then displays the words Internet Access Prohibited under N.D.Sup.Ct.Admin.R. 41, and the record remains available by in-person request at a court facility. This does not expunge, does not seal, and does not touch law enforcement, prosecution or BCI records.
exclusions: Municipal court cases. The official packet is district court only.

tracks.legalName: Application to Pardon Eligible Marijuana Offences (N.D.C.C. ch. 12-55.1; SFN 61663)
tracks.publicName: Apply for North Dakota's summary marijuana pardon
tracks.mechanism: An application for clemency must be made with the pardon clerk on a form prescribed by the clerk. The summary marijuana process uses SFN 61663 and covers misdemeanor convictions for possession of marijuana, ingestion of marijuana and possession of marijuana paraphernalia. A pardon removes punishment but does not remove the fact of the conviction unless the certificate of pardon says so, and the form warns in terms that a pardon request will not expunge a criminal history record.
exclusions: Any felony conviction, which must use the regular application SFN 14859 instead.
Any other criminal conviction in any court, North Dakota, tribal, another state or federal, within the last five years.
Prosecution for intent to deliver, delivery or manufacture, or any offence other than the three listed.
Federal, traffic and tribal offences, which are outside the Board's jurisdiction.

tracks.legalName: North Dakota Pardon Advisory Board Application (N.D.C.C. ch. 12-55.1; SFN 14859)
tracks.publicName: Apply to the North Dakota Pardon Advisory Board
tracks.mechanism: The regular clemency application, SFN 14859, covers a pardon, a commutation of sentence, a reprieve of sentence and a remission of fine. It is the required route for any felony and for any applicant excluded from the summary marijuana process. An unconditional pardon obtained through it is the eligibility ground for a petition to seal a pardoned conviction under N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-02(1)(c).
exclusions: Federal, traffic and tribal offences, which are outside the Board's jurisdiction.

Applicants who do not fall within the Board's eligibility policy, which reaches those in Department custody, on parole or on probation, those with no remedy through the Parole Board, and those not under supervision who have encountered a significant problem with the consequences of the conviction or sentence.

tracks.legalName: Routing of Juvenile Court Records (N.D.C.C. § 27-20.2-25)
tracks.publicName: Where to go about a North Dakota juvenile record
tracks.mechanism: Juvenile court records are retained and disposed of under rules and policies established by the Supreme Court, and on final destruction the proceeding must be treated as if it never occurred, with the juvenile court notifying each agency named and index references deleted. Retention runs ten years after the final order or age eighteen, whichever is later, for delinquency, and one year after age eighteen or expiry of the final order, whichever is later, for a child in need of services. A participant-facing motion packet for early destruction is published by the ND Legal Self Help Center.
exclusions: Adult records, which route to the adult tracks.
Any case with juvenile or criminal charges pending in another court.

tracks.legalName: Routing of DNA Profile Removal (N.D.C.C. § 31-13-07)
tracks.publicName: Where to go about a North Dakota DNA profile
tracks.mechanism: An individual whose DNA profile is in the state database may petition the district court to seal the court record on enumerated grounds. On receipt of a certified order the laboratory expunges all identifiable information and destroys all samples, and the sealed record may not be opened even by order of the court. A detention, arrest or conviction based on database information is not invalidated even if the samples should have been expunged.
exclusions: Any case with a felony charge or felony conviction that keeps the profile in the database.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Set Aside a Conviction Sentenced to Probation, Fine or Community Service (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-2264(2))
tracks.publicName: Set aside a Nebraska conviction where you were not sent to jail
tracks.mechanism: Where an offender was sentenced to probation, a fine or community service and has satisfactorily completed it, the sentencing court may set aside the conviction. The order nullifies the conviction and removes all civil disabilities and disqualifications imposed as a result of it, and must notify the offender to consult an attorney about firearm effects. Offence reaches any violation of state law or of a political subdivision, including felonies, misdemeanors, infractions, traffic infractions and ordinance violations. Section 29-2264(9) makes the 2018 and 2020 changes apply without regard to the date of the conviction.
exclusions: None stated in subsection (2). The four mandatory-denial grounds in § 29-2264(3)(b) are textually confined to subsection (3) petitions and must not be applied here.

waitingPeriods.condition: Satisfactory fulfilment of probation for the whole period, or discharge from probation before termination, plus payment of any fine and completion of any community service
waitingPeriods.duration: none independent of completion. There is no date gate: § 29-2264(9) applies the changes without regard to the date of conviction

tracks.venue: The sentencing court: the Nebraska county court or district court that imposed the sentence.

In district court the participant obtains a hearing date from the judge's bailiff and then files DC 1:15 and gives a copy to the prosecutor; in county court the clerk schedules and mails notice.

packetInstructions: Say set aside, never expunge, clear or erase. Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-2264(5) nullifies the conviction and removes civil disabilities and disqualifications; it does not seal, erase or remove the record, and § 29-2264(6) lists the many purposes for which the conviction still counts.

A set-aside does not restore firearm rights. Section 29-2264(6) preserves the conviction for the firearm statute, and § 29-2264(5)(c) requires the order itself to tell the participant to consult an attorney about firearm effects. A pardon is the only route.
One petition per conviction. A participant with several convictions needs a separate packet for each, and the fee position for each is a clerk-level question.
scopeRestrictions: The four mandatory-denial grounds in § 29-2264(3)(b) belong to the custodial branch and must not be screened against a subsection (2) petitioner.

releaseBlockers.question: The fee-waiver branch has no fitting official form. DC 6:7.1's case-type box offers only Civil, Name change and Emancipation, and its official title is scoped to civil, appeals and emancipation matters, while a set-aside petition or sealing motion is filed in the existing criminal case. There is no county-court in forma pauperis application form at all: CC 8:1 is the order only. Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-2301.01 nonetheless permits proceeding in forma pauperis in a civil or criminal case in any county or state court, so the mechanism exists and the form does not fit it. A custom affidavit and application under §§ 25-2301 to 25-2310 is the resolution rather than mis-scoping DC 6:7.1.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Set Aside a Conviction Sentenced to One Year or Less (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-2264(3))
tracks.publicName: Set aside a Nebraska conviction after a short jail sentence
tracks.mechanism: Where an offender was sentenced other than as described in subsection (2), but not to a term of imprisonment of more than one year, the sentencing court may set aside the conviction after completion of the sentence. Subsection (3)(b) imposes four mandatory denial grounds that do not exist on the non-custodial branch, so the eligibility screen must branch and a wrong branch costs the participant two years.
exclusions: Any criminal charge pending in any court in the United States or in any other country.
Any period in which the person is required to register under the Sex Offender Registration Act.
Any misdemeanor or felony motor vehicle offence under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 28-306 or the Nebraska Rules of the Road.
Any petition filed within two years after a denial of a petition to set aside under this same subsection.
Any sentence of imprisonment of more than one year.

A set-aside does not restore firearm rights. Section 29-2264(6) preserves the conviction for the firearm statute, and § 29-2264(5)(c) requires the order itself to tell the participant to consult an attorney about firearm effects. A pardon is the only route.
One petition per conviction. A participant with several convictions needs a separate packet for each, and the fee position for each is a clerk-level question.
participantQuestions: Imprisonment for this branch excludes pretrial jail and jail served as a condition of probation. The judiciary states both exclusions in its own eligibility questionnaire, and the questions must reflect that or eligible participants will be turned away.
scopeRestrictions: The four mandatory denial grounds are absolute. The screen denies on any uncertainty rather than proceeding, because a wrong filing costs the participant two years.

releaseBlockers.question: The fee-waiver branch has no fitting official form. DC 6:7.1's case-type box offers only Civil, Name change and Emancipation, and its official title is scoped to civil, appeals and emancipation matters, while a set-aside petition or sealing motion is filed in the existing criminal case. There is no county-court in forma pauperis application form at all: CC 8:1 is the order only. Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-2301.01 nonetheless permits proceeding in forma pauperis in a civil or criminal case in any county or state court, so the mechanism exists and the form does not fit it. A custom affidavit and application under §§ 25-2301 to 25-2310 is the resolution rather than mis-scoping DC 6:7.1.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Removal of Non-Conviction Records from the Public Record (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-3523(3))

tracks.mechanism: Criminal history record information about an arrest, citation in lieu of arrest or referral for prosecution becomes confidential by operation of law on the timetables in § 29-3523(3), and a criminal justice agency must then respond to a public inquiry as if there were no such information. Under § 29-3523(8) the person cannot be questioned about the offence in any application for employment, bonding, licence, education or other right or privilege, in any appearance as a witness or in any other public inquiry, and may answer as if the offence never occurred.

Any period in which the person is an announced candidate for or holder of public office.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Seal a Pre-2017 Dismissal or Acquittal (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-3523(6))
tracks.publicName: Ask a Nebraska court to seal a case that was dismissed before 2017
tracks.mechanism: Where a case was dismissed before 1 January 2017 for one of the qualifying reasons, the court shall grant a motion to seal. This is the only conviction-adjacent Nebraska route with no judicial discretion. The resulting order places the records outside the public record, bars dissemination other than to criminal justice agencies, orders the notified agencies to seal, and reaches the transferring court. Section 29-3523(10) makes the provision retroactive regardless of the arrest, citation or referral date.
exclusions: Convictions, which this subsection does not reach.
Cases dismissed on or after 1 January 2017, which are sealed automatically and free of charge.
Any dismissal reason outside the five qualifying categories in § 29-3523(3)(c).

tracks.legalName: Motion to Seal a Pardoned Conviction (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-3523(5))
tracks.publicName: Ask a Nebraska court to seal a conviction that has been pardoned
tracks.mechanism: Where the Nebraska Board of Pardons has pardoned a conviction, the sentencing court shall grant a motion to seal the criminal history record information and any cases related to those charges or that conviction. Relief is mandatory. The finding is the fact of the pardon rather than a dismissal reason.
exclusions: Any case with no Nebraska Board of Pardons pardon.
Federal and out-of-state convictions, which Nebraska cannot pardon.
A warrant of discharge, a set-aside or a firearm-rights restoration, none of which is a pardon for this purpose.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge Criminal History Record Information After an Arrest Made in Error (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-3523(9))
tracks.publicName: Ask a Nebraska court to erase an arrest the police made by mistake
tracks.mechanism: A person arrested due to the error of a law enforcement agency may file a petition with the district court. The court may order the criminal history record information related to the arrest expunged on clear and convincing evidence that the arrest was due to agency error. This is the only Nebraska adult mechanism that uses the word expunge, and product copy may use it here and nowhere else.
exclusions: Anything that is not agency error. A lawful arrest that simply did not lead to charges belongs to the automatic non-conviction route.
Federal, out-of-state and tribal arrests.

tracks.publicName: Make an agency clear a Nebraska record that should already be sealed
tracks.mechanism: Where any officer or employee of the state, its agencies or its political subdivisions, or any state agency or political subdivision, fails to comply with the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act, any person aggrieved may bring an action, including but not limited to an action for mandamus, to compel compliance. Venue is statutory: the district court of any district in which the records involved are located, or the district court of Lancaster County. This is the route State v. Coble identifies as correct, in contrast to a motion in the criminal case.

tracks.legalName: Set Aside and Seal a Conviction or Adjudication Resulting From Sex Trafficking Victimisation (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 29-3005, 29-3523(4))
tracks.publicName: Clear a Nebraska conviction that came from being trafficked
tracks.mechanism: A movant convicted or adjudicated of a prostitution-related offence, or of any other offence committed as a direct result of or proximately caused by being a victim of sex trafficking, may move to set the conviction aside; the court shall grant the motion on the requisite finding, and the order has the same effect as a set-aside under § 29-2264(5) and (6). Separately, § 29-3523(4) permits a motion in the sentencing court to seal a conviction that was set aside under § 29-3005, which produces the § 29-3523(7) sealing order and the § 29-3523(8) right to answer as if the offence never occurred. The two are different reliefs obtained by different filings, and the second is legally unavailable until the first is granted.
exclusions: None stated by either section.

Relief is mandatory: the court shall grant the motion. No official form exists. The movant may request that the hearing be held in camera, and the rules of evidence do not apply.

researchStructure.firstStage: A custom motion under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-3005, not CC 6:12, filed after completion of the sentence or juvenile disposition in the county, district or separate juvenile court of the county of conviction or adjudication. The statute distinguishes two branches that must not be collapsed: (a) a prostitution-related offense as defined in § 29-3005(1) committed while the movant was a victim of sex trafficking OR proximately caused by that status; (b) any other offense committed as a direct result of OR proximately caused by that status. No further multi-year waiting period in that section. Only the selected, fact-supported branch is pleaded; both alternatives are never printed as already true; the court makes the findings.
researchStructure.evidence: The rebuttable presumption of victim status may rest on government documentation OR on affidavits or sworn testimony from an attorney, clergy member, medical professional, trained victim-services professional, or other professional from whom the movant sought relevant assistance; official documentation is not a prerequisite; other sufficiently credible and probative evidence may be considered. The presumption concerns victim status, not every other element. On the movant's request a hearing on this motion must be held in camera and the rules of evidence do not apply to it; this authorises no promise that all filings are confidential or that the later sealing hearing follows the same rule. No unnecessarily graphic evidence is solicited and no testimony invented.
