Open question blocks release (eligibility_branch): Whether a conviction arising from the same criminal episode as the offence being set aside counts as a disqualifying other conviction. The controlling review states that it does not, calls the same-episode rule the clearest treatment of any single doctrine in the series and directs that it be preserved in the engine. The enacted text of Oregon Laws 2025 chapter 349, read at the Oregon Legislature's own channel on 2026-08-06, reads the other way on its face: ORS 137.225(7)(a)(B) disqualifies a person convicted of any other offence within the applicable period "whether or not the other conviction is for conduct associated with the same criminal episode". The enacted text does carve out motor vehicle violations, unlawful possession of a controlled substance constituting a drug enforcement misdemeanour, and under ORS 137.225(7)(b) a single non-motor-vehicle violation; the Oregon Judicial Department's own packet describes the carve-out the same way, as "except traffic violations or a single violation offense", and does not mention same-episode convictions. Neither reading is adopted here and no eligibility statement is made where a second conviction from the same episode is in play.

Open question blocks release (participant_instructions): The current Oregon State Police record-check fee. ORS 137.225(2)(d) as enacted leaves the figure to the department, capped at actual cost, so the review's reported figure of about $33 per conviction cannot be confirmed from the statute and the department's current schedule was not obtained. The statute does settle one thing the review did not have: where the department performs only one record check it may charge only one fee regardless of how many counties the person files in.

Open question blocks release (eligibility_branch): How far the 2025 monetary-obligations relief actually reaches. The controlling review describes Oregon Laws 2025 chapter 395 section 1 as a general rule that expired judgment remedies for monetary obligations in any judgment of conviction count as sentence completion. The enacted text read at the Oregon Legislature's own channel on 2026-08-06 is narrower in its operative first subsection: it expires the judgment remedies for a judgment entered in a municipal court or justice court for a pre-July 1, 2015 marijuana-possession offence under one ounce. Subsection (2) then applies the sentence-completion consequence to obligations that have expired "under subsection (1) of this section". Whether the consequence in subsection (2) reaches obligations that expire under ORS 18.194 generally, or only those expired by subsection (1), is the difference between a broad unlock and a marijuana-specific one.

Open question blocks release (eligibility_branch): Whether the categorical exclusion lists in ORS 137.225(5), (6) and (7)(a)(A) as enacted have been amended again since Oregon Laws 2025 chapter 349, and how the person-felony and person Class A misdemeanor definitions in the rules of the Oregon Criminal Justice Commission map to particular offences. The exclusion screen depends on a classification the participant cannot supply.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Set Aside a Contempt of Court Finding (ORS 137.225(1)(a), (1)(b)(B) and (1)(b)(D))
tracks.publicName: Set aside an Oregon contempt of court finding
tracks.mechanism: A person found in contempt of court who has fully complied with and performed the sentence for the contempt finding may move to set the finding aside. The enacted text splits contempt across two tiers. A finding of a person in contempt of court for violating an order related to abuse or a person crime sits in the five-year tier alongside Class C felonies. A finding of contempt not so described sits in the one-year tier alongside Class B and C misdemeanors and violations. Each runs from the date of the finding or the release from imprisonment for the finding sought to be set aside, whichever is later. ORS 137.225(13)(b) defines "order related to abuse or a person crime" as a court order issued under ORS 107.095(1)(c) or (d), 107.700 to 107.735, 124.005 to 124.040, 133.035, 135.247 or 163.760 to 163.777, or a court order arising from a criminal case involving a sex crime, stalking under ORS 163.732, or a person felony or person Class A misdemeanor committed against the person's family or household member as defined in ORS 135.230. Oregon calls it a set-aside and there are no separate sealing and expungement tracks: the court sets aside and seals, and under ORS 137.225(4) the conviction, arrest, citation, charge or other proceeding is deemed not to have occurred and the person may answer accordingly any questions relating to its occurrence. The order reaches Oregon court and law enforcement records including the Oregon State Police LEDS system. It does not reach federal or other states' records. Under 2024 Oregon State Police policy a set-aside does not restore firearm rights; a separate restoration process is required. Two statutory carve-outs survive: under ORS 137.225(10) the deemed-not-to-have-occurred rule does not apply in a civil action where truth is an element of a claim or defence, and a party may apply for disclosure; and under ORS 137.225(11) a court may order records reopened on a prosecutor's or defendant's motion supported by affidavit showing good cause, and a prosecuting attorney may unseal a set-aside arrest, citation or charge to initiate a proceeding within the statute of limitations, on written notice to the person.
exclusions: A person under charge of any crime, or of contempt of court for violating an order related to abuse or a person crime, at the time the motion is pending. ORS 137.225(7)(a)(C).

A person convicted of any other offence, or found in contempt of court for violating an order related to abuse or a person crime, within the applicable look-back period, subject to the motor vehicle, single-violation and drug enforcement misdemeanour carve-outs. ORS 137.225(7)(a)(B) and (7)(b).
Federal and other states' records.

The controlling review states that it does not, calls the same-episode rule the clearest treatment of any single doctrine in the series and directs that it be preserved in the engine. The enacted text of Oregon Laws 2025 chapter 349, read at the Oregon Legislature's own channel on 2026-08-06, reads the other way on its face: ORS 137.225(7)(a)(B) disqualifies a person convicted of any other offence within the applicable period "whether or not the other conviction is for conduct associated with the same criminal episode". The enacted text does carve out motor vehicle violations, unlawful possession of a controlled substance constituting a drug enforcement misdemeanour, and under ORS 137.225(7)(b) a single non-motor-vehicle violation; the Oregon Judicial Department's own packet describes the carve-out the same way, as "except traffic violations or a single violation offense", and does not mention same-episode convictions. Neither reading is adopted here and no eligibility statement is made where a second conviction from the same episode is in play.

Open question blocks release (participant_instructions): The current Oregon State Police record-check fee. ORS 137.225(2)(d) as enacted leaves the figure to the department, capped at actual cost, so the review's reported figure of about $33 per conviction cannot be confirmed from the statute and the department's current schedule was not obtained. The statute does settle one thing the review did not have: where the department performs only one record check it may charge only one fee regardless of how many counties the person files in.
One or more official sources have no recorded SHA-256, so staleness cannot be detected.

It is CPCMS 2046 (two pages, financial questions, an unsworn-falsification verification under 18 Pa.C.S. § 4904 rather than a notary block; no new printed revision date asserted), held in custody as PA-IFP-CCP (sha256 b1255ef0503f…). rules.service: Service on the attorney for the Commonwealth concurrently with filing, per Pa.R.Crim.P. 790. Rule 790's Comment directs filing and service to Rule 576 and treats the petition as a motion for Rules 575–577, so the paper-service method is supplied by rule, not an unanswerable local-law question: Rule 576 methods include mailing a copy to the party's attorney; a copy is also served on the court administrator by the methods Rule 576 lists; a signed certificate of service records the date and manner of service and each recipient's name, address and telephone number; electronic filing follows Rule 576.1 rather than assuming an emailed document accomplishes service. Current recipient addresses and any e-filing choice remain local inputs, and service facts are completed after service, never pre-certified. (Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research; previously stated only the Rule 790 recipient and timing.)

rules.proposedOrder: The blank expungement order (PA-RCRIM-P-790-ORDER) is optional, not a filing prerequisite: the AOPC public-forms page expressly says the proposed order is not mandatory (PA3). researchCertificateSpecimen.use: Proposed completion content for the existing composed certificate of service, not a newly accepted official form: original caption and docket number; a body certifying service on an actual date of an identified document on the listed recipients by the method recorded for each; a recipient table (attorney for the Commonwealth, court administrator, other party if applicable) with verified address, telephone number and the method actually used; signature of the unrepresented petitioner. Service is never pre-certified; no fictional recipients or numbers.

researchParticipantText.text:
Filing and service. File the Rule 790 petition with the clerk of courts in the judicial district where the charges were disposed. Serve the attorney for the Commonwealth at the same time. Follow Rule 576 for the method, service on the court administrator, and the certificate documenting actual service. Mailing to the proper attorney's office is an available paper-service method. Confirm the recipients' current addresses; follow the applicable electronic-filing rule when filing electronically.

Order and costs. The blank proposed order is optional, not a filing prerequisite. Confirm the filing charge with the filing office. When requesting permission to proceed without paying because you cannot afford the fee, complete and submit the Common Pleas Motion to Proceed In Forma Pauperis. Use your actual financial information. The judge decides the request; submitting it is not an approval.

tracks.publicName: Expunge an old Pennsylvania summary conviction

tracks.legalName: Expungement of the Arrest Record on Successful Completion of Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition
tracks.publicName: Check that finishing ARD cleared your arrest record
tracks.mechanism: When the judge orders dismissal of the charges after successful completion of Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition, Rule 320 provides that the judge also shall order expungement of the defendant's arrest record, subject to a Commonwealth objection filed within 30 days after service of the motion for dismissal, on which the Commonwealth must show compelling reasons to retain the record. Section 9122(b.1) removes the court's authority to expunge the arrest record where ARD was granted for enumerated sexual offences and the victim was under 18.
exclusions: ARD granted for an offence under 18 Pa.C.S. §§ 3121 through 3127, § 5902(b) or § 5903 where the victim was under 18 years of age. Section 9122(b.1) removes the court's authority to expunge the arrest record in those cases.

tracks.legalName: Expungement Following an Unconditional Pardon
tracks.publicName: Clear a record after you receive a pardon
tracks.mechanism: A pardon is executive clemency and does not by itself erase the record. Where an unconditional pardon has been granted, § 9122 provides for expungement: the Board of Pardons transmits eligible records to the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts quarterly, the AOPC sends the record to the court of common pleas, and the court orders expungement after confirming the criteria. A conditional pardon may instead trigger Clean Slate limited access under § 9122.2(a)(4).
exclusions: Records for which no pardon has been granted. The pardon application itself is out of scope.
Conditional pardons, which are routed to Clean Slate limited access under § 9122.2(a)(4) rather than to expungement.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Order for Limited Access Under 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122.1
tracks.publicName: Petition to seal a Pennsylvania conviction from public view
tracks.mechanism: Section 9122.1(a) permits a petition for limited access to a qualifying misdemeanour or ungraded offence carrying a maximum penalty of no more than five years where the person has been free from conviction for a period of seven years, has completed all court-ordered restitution, and has paid the authorized fee. Section 9122.1(a.1), added by Act 36 of 2023, extends the petition to qualifying felonies other than felonies of the first and second degree where the person has been free from conviction for a period of ten years on the same conditions. Rule 791 prescribes the petition, the attached Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing, service on the attorney for the Commonwealth, and the order.
exclusions: Offences punishable by more than two years in the following categories, per § 9122.1(b): offences involving danger to the person under Article B of Part II; offences against the family under Article D; firearms and other dangerous articles under Chapter 61; offences requiring registration under 42 Pa.C.S. § 9799.14 or § 9799.55; and corruption of minors.

Prior-record bars under § 9122.1(b)(2): a conviction for murder or a felony of the first degree; certain serious offences within the preceding 15 years; and two or more offences punishable by more than two years within the preceding 10 years.
Felonies of the first and second degree, which are outside the § 9122.1(a.1) qualifying-felony route.
A drug felony on which a minimum sentence of 30 months or more, or a maximum sentence of 60 months or more, was imposed, which falls outside the § 9102 definition of qualifying offence.

tracks.legalName: Clean Slate Automatic Limited Access Under 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122.2
tracks.publicName: Check whether Clean Slate has sealed your record automatically
tracks.mechanism: Section 9122.2 provides automatic limited access without any petition. Subsection (a)(1) reaches a conviction of a misdemeanour of the second degree or a misdemeanour punishable by no more than two years where the person has been free for seven years from conviction for any offence punishable by imprisonment of one or more years. Subsection (a)(1.1) reaches a qualifying offence on the same terms after ten years. Subsection (a)(2) reaches charges resulting in a final disposition other than a conviction. Subsection (a)(3) reaches a summary conviction when five years have elapsed since entry of the judgment of conviction. Subsection (a)(4) reaches a conviction for which a conditional pardon was granted. Under subsection (b) the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts transmits eligible records to the Pennsylvania State Police central repository and removes records for which a notification of ineligibility is received.
exclusions: The exclusions in § 9122.3 are keyed by subsection rather than expressed as one generic ineligible-offence list. Section 9122.3(a) states that limited access under § 9122.2(a)(1) shall not be granted for the enumerated categories, and § 9122.3(a)(2) carries its own separate structure; § 9122.3(c) provides that an offence eligible for clean slate limited access is also eligible for a petition for limited access under § 9122.1. The subsection-specific structure is preserved and is not collapsed.
Offences requiring registration under 42 Pa.C.S. § 9799.14 or § 9799.55, and failure to comply with registration requirements under 18 Pa.C.S. § 4915.1, per § 9122.3(a)(1)(iv) and (a)(2)(iv)(C).
An otherwise qualifying conviction where a conviction punishable by five or more years, or another excluded offence, arose out of the same case, except for a qualifying offence.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge a Single Misdemeanor Conviction as a First Offender (R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-2)
tracks.publicName: Clear a single misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: A first offender — a person convicted of a felony or misdemeanor who has not previously been convicted of or placed on probation for a felony or misdemeanor, and who has no pending criminal proceeding — may move to expunge a misdemeanor conviction five years after completion of sentence, where the person has not been convicted of a crime of violence, has no pending criminal proceeding, has had no felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the lookback period, and has paid or obtained waiver or reduction of all court-imposed or court-related financial obligations. Relief is discretionary on findings of good moral character, rehabilitation to the court's satisfaction, and consistency with the public interest.
exclusions: Any conviction for a crime of violence as statutorily defined: murder, manslaughter, first-degree arson, kidnapping with intent to extort, robbery, larceny from the person, first- and second-degree sexual assault, first- and second-degree child molestation, assault with intent to murder, assault with intent to rob, assault with intent to commit first-degree sexual assault, burglary, and entering a dwelling with intent to commit murder, robbery, sexual assault or larceny.
Any person previously convicted of, or placed on probation for, a felony or misdemeanor; prior probation alone defeats first-offender status.
Any felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the five-year lookback. An arrest alone, without conviction, defeats eligibility.
Any pending criminal proceeding.
Court-imposed or court-related financial obligations that are unpaid and not waived or reduced by court order.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records.

waitingPeriods.duration: 5 years from completion of sentence, including completion of probation

waitingPeriods.condition: Lookback free of any felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction
waitingPeriods.duration: 5 years

units.label: BCI record, docket and eligibility classification
units.description: The judgment stage. Pull the BCI criminal history and the court docket, obtain the BCI number the forms require, and classify the case: first-offender status including prior probation, the crime-of-violence bar, whether the sentence and any probation are complete, whether any arrest or conviction fell inside the lookback, whether financial obligations are paid, waived or reduced, and whether the offence has been reclassified by the General Assembly so the reclassification overlay applies. Nothing is filed at this stage and LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates any record.

units.label: Court-specific Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order
units.description: The document stage. The correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit is completed — District Court form DC-33, the Superior Court misdemeanor version, or the Family Court misdemeanor form, according to where the conviction occurred. The form requires the defendant's name, case number, BCI number, counts, charges, dispositions and the charging police department, and requires the filer to elect seal or expunge — a legal choice with different consequences, never a checkbox preference. The proposed order is prepared to be brought to the hearing for the judge's signature. A custom pleading is not advisable: the Judiciary publishes the forms and the affidavit must be sworn.

units.label: Notice to the Attorney General and charging police department, the hearing, and delivery of certified orders
units.description: The procedural stage, which runs after the packet exists and continues after the judge signs. File with the clerk, who fills in the hearing date; the hearing must be at least ten days after filing because notice must reach the Attorney General and the charging police department. Sign the affidavit before a notary or clerk. Attend the hearing with the proposed order. On a grant the clerk prepares three certified copies after all conditions are satisfied, and the petitioner delivers one to the Attorney General's BCI unit and one to the charging police department — if that delivery does not happen, nothing changes on the record. Verify afterwards with a fresh BCI record.

rules.filing: File the correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order, with the clerk of the court where the conviction occurred. The clerk fills in the hearing date.
rules.fees: No expungement filing fee in the Superior Court. The Rhode Island Superior Court's own expungement FAQ, 'Is there a fee associated with my expungement?' (https://www.courts.ri.gov/Courts/superiorcourt/Pages/FAQs.aspx), expressly says the process requires no fee; R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-3 (https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE12/12-1.3/12-1.3-3.htm) is the statutory branch for the route's own conditions. Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research handoff. This is court-specific, not a national fee rule: fines, costs, restitution and other obligations already ordered in the underlying case remain the participant's and remain the separate statutory eligibility condition; a no-fee filing cancels no unpaid court obligation, and no filing-fee-waiver application is required solely to waive a $0 filing fee. No dollar amount is attributed to Superior-55 or any form without locating it in that form's own text.
rules.feeWaiver: Not stated for the motion itself. Court-imposed financial obligations on the underlying case may be waived or reduced by court order, and that waiver or reduction satisfies the eligibility condition.
rules.notice: Notice must be given to the Rhode Island Department of Attorney General and to the police department that brought the charge, at least ten days before the hearing. A hearing is required. The court may grant if it finds no felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the lookback, no pending criminal proceeding, financial obligations satisfied or waived or reduced, good moral character, rehabilitation to the court's satisfaction, and that expungement is consistent with the public interest.
rules.service: Serve the Attorney General and the charging police department at least ten days before the hearing. After a grant, the petitioner delivers certified copies of the order to the Attorney General's BCI unit and the charging police department.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the affidavit before a notary or a clerk. This is a sworn document and the signature must be witnessed in person.
rules.notarization: Required. The affidavit must be signed before a notary or a clerk.

researchParticipantText.fee: The Rhode Island Superior Court does not charge an expungement filing fee. This is separate from fines, costs, restitution, or other obligations already ordered in your case. Follow the requirements for your particular expungement route concerning any remaining obligations. A no-fee filing does not cancel an unpaid court obligation.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge a Single Felony Conviction as a First Offender (R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-2)
tracks.publicName: Clear a single felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: A first offender may move to expunge a single felony conviction ten years after completion of sentence, with a ten-year lookback free of any felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction. All other conditions are as for the misdemeanor route: no crime of violence, no pending criminal proceeding, financial obligations paid or waived or reduced, and the court's findings of good moral character, rehabilitation and consistency with the public interest. The Superior Court felony form is Superior-55.
exclusions: Any conviction for a crime of violence as statutorily defined: murder, manslaughter, first-degree arson, kidnapping with intent to extort, robbery, larceny from the person, first- and second-degree sexual assault, first- and second-degree child molestation, assault with intent to murder, assault with intent to rob, assault with intent to commit first-degree sexual assault, burglary, and entering a dwelling with intent to commit murder, robbery, sexual assault or larceny.
Any person previously convicted of, or placed on probation for, a felony or misdemeanor; prior probation alone defeats first-offender status.
Any felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the five-year lookback. An arrest alone, without conviction, defeats eligibility.
Any pending criminal proceeding.
Court-imposed or court-related financial obligations that are unpaid and not waived or reduced by court order.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records.

waitingPeriods.duration: 10 years from completion of sentence, including completion of probation

waitingPeriods.condition: Lookback free of any felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction
waitingPeriods.duration: 10 years

units.label: BCI record, docket and eligibility classification
units.description: The judgment stage. Pull the BCI criminal history and the court docket, obtain the BCI number the forms require, and classify the case: first-offender status including prior probation, the crime-of-violence bar, whether the sentence and any probation are complete, whether any arrest or conviction fell inside the lookback, whether financial obligations are paid, waived or reduced, and whether the offence has been reclassified by the General Assembly so the reclassification overlay applies. Nothing is filed at this stage and LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates any record.

units.label: Court-specific Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order
units.description: The document stage. The Superior Court felony Motion to Expunge or Seal Record, Superior-55, is completed. The form requires the defendant's name, case number, BCI number, counts, charges, dispositions and the charging police department, and requires the filer to elect seal or expunge — a legal choice with different consequences, never a checkbox preference. The proposed order is prepared to be brought to the hearing for the judge's signature. A custom pleading is not advisable: the Judiciary publishes the forms and the affidavit must be sworn.

units.label: Notice to the Attorney General and charging police department, the hearing, and delivery of certified orders
units.description: The procedural stage, which runs after the packet exists and continues after the judge signs. File with the clerk, who fills in the hearing date; the hearing must be at least ten days after filing because notice must reach the Attorney General and the charging police department. Sign the affidavit before a notary or clerk. Attend the hearing with the proposed order. On a grant the clerk prepares three certified copies after all conditions are satisfied, and the petitioner delivers one to the Attorney General's BCI unit and one to the charging police department — if that delivery does not happen, nothing changes on the record. Verify afterwards with a fresh BCI record.

rules.filing: File the correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order, with the clerk of the court where the conviction occurred. The clerk fills in the hearing date.
rules.fees: No expungement filing fee in the Superior Court. The Rhode Island Superior Court's own expungement FAQ, 'Is there a fee associated with my expungement?' (https://www.courts.ri.gov/Courts/superiorcourt/Pages/FAQs.aspx), expressly says the process requires no fee; R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-3 (https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE12/12-1.3/12-1.3-3.htm) is the statutory branch for the route's own conditions. Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research handoff. This is court-specific, not a national fee rule: fines, costs, restitution and other obligations already ordered in the underlying case remain the participant's and remain the separate statutory eligibility condition; a no-fee filing cancels no unpaid court obligation, and no filing-fee-waiver application is required solely to waive a $0 filing fee. No dollar amount is attributed to Superior-55 or any form without locating it in that form's own text.
rules.feeWaiver: Not stated for the motion itself. Court-imposed financial obligations on the underlying case may be waived or reduced by court order, and that waiver or reduction satisfies the eligibility condition.
rules.notice: Notice must be given to the Rhode Island Department of Attorney General and to the police department that brought the charge, at least ten days before the hearing. A hearing is required. The court may grant if it finds no felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the lookback, no pending criminal proceeding, financial obligations satisfied or waived or reduced, good moral character, rehabilitation to the court's satisfaction, and that expungement is consistent with the public interest.
rules.service: Serve the Attorney General and the charging police department at least ten days before the hearing. After a grant, the petitioner delivers certified copies of the order to the Attorney General's BCI unit and the charging police department.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the affidavit before a notary or a clerk. This is a sworn document and the signature must be witnessed in person.
rules.notarization: Required. The affidavit must be signed before a notary or a clerk.

researchParticipantText.fee: The Rhode Island Superior Court does not charge an expungement filing fee. This is separate from fines, costs, restitution, or other obligations already ordered in your case. Follow the requirements for your particular expungement route concerning any remaining obligations. A no-fee filing does not cancel an unpaid court obligation.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge Multiple Misdemeanor Convictions (R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-2)
tracks.publicName: Clear more than one misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person with more than one but fewer than six misdemeanor convictions and no felony conviction may move to expunge any or all of them, ten years after completion of the last sentence, with no felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction in the ten years before filing, no pending criminal proceedings, and good moral character. Domestic violence offences under chapter 12-29, driving under the influence under § 31-27-2, and chemical test refusal under § 31-27-2.1 are excluded from this route specifically.
exclusions: Domestic violence offences under chapter 12-29, the Domestic Violence Prevention Act.
Driving under the influence under R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-27-2.
Chemical test refusal under R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-27-2.1.
Any felony conviction, which disqualifies a person from this route entirely.
Six or more misdemeanor convictions.
Any conviction for a crime of violence.
Any felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the ten-year lookback.
Any pending criminal proceeding.
Unpaid court financial obligations not waived or reduced by court order.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records.

units.label: BCI record, docket and eligibility classification
units.description: The judgment stage. Pull the BCI criminal history and the court docket, obtain the BCI number the forms require, and classify the case: first-offender status including prior probation, the crime-of-violence bar, whether the sentence and any probation are complete, whether any arrest or conviction fell inside the lookback, whether financial obligations are paid, waived or reduced, and whether the offence has been reclassified by the General Assembly so the reclassification overlay applies. Nothing is filed at this stage and LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates any record.

units.label: Court-specific Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order
units.description: The document stage. The correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit is completed for each conviction being cleared. The form requires the defendant's name, case number, BCI number, counts, charges, dispositions and the charging police department, and requires the filer to elect seal or expunge — a legal choice with different consequences, never a checkbox preference. The proposed order is prepared to be brought to the hearing for the judge's signature. A custom pleading is not advisable: the Judiciary publishes the forms and the affidavit must be sworn.

units.label: Notice to the Attorney General and charging police department, the hearing, and delivery of certified orders
units.description: The procedural stage, which runs after the packet exists and continues after the judge signs. File with the clerk, who fills in the hearing date; the hearing must be at least ten days after filing because notice must reach the Attorney General and the charging police department. Sign the affidavit before a notary or clerk. Attend the hearing with the proposed order. On a grant the clerk prepares three certified copies after all conditions are satisfied, and the petitioner delivers one to the Attorney General's BCI unit and one to the charging police department — if that delivery does not happen, nothing changes on the record. Verify afterwards with a fresh BCI record.

rules.filing: File the correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order, with the clerk of the court where the conviction occurred. The clerk fills in the hearing date.
rules.fees: No expungement filing fee in the Superior Court. The Rhode Island Superior Court's own expungement FAQ, 'Is there a fee associated with my expungement?' (https://www.courts.ri.gov/Courts/superiorcourt/Pages/FAQs.aspx), expressly says the process requires no fee; R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-3 (https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE12/12-1.3/12-1.3-3.htm) is the statutory branch for the route's own conditions. Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research handoff. This is court-specific, not a national fee rule: fines, costs, restitution and other obligations already ordered in the underlying case remain the participant's and remain the separate statutory eligibility condition; a no-fee filing cancels no unpaid court obligation, and no filing-fee-waiver application is required solely to waive a $0 filing fee. No dollar amount is attributed to Superior-55 or any form without locating it in that form's own text.
rules.feeWaiver: Not stated for the motion itself. Court-imposed financial obligations on the underlying case may be waived or reduced by court order, and that waiver or reduction satisfies the eligibility condition.
rules.notice: Notice must be given to the Rhode Island Department of Attorney General and to the police department that brought the charge, at least ten days before the hearing. A hearing is required. The court may grant if it finds no felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the lookback, no pending criminal proceeding, financial obligations satisfied or waived or reduced, good moral character, rehabilitation to the court's satisfaction, and that expungement is consistent with the public interest.
rules.service: Serve the Attorney General and the charging police department at least ten days before the hearing. After a grant, the petitioner delivers certified copies of the order to the Attorney General's BCI unit and the charging police department.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the affidavit before a notary or a clerk. This is a sworn document and the signature must be witnessed in person.
rules.notarization: Required. The affidavit must be signed before a notary or a clerk.

researchParticipantText.fee: The Rhode Island Superior Court does not charge an expungement filing fee. This is separate from fines, costs, restitution, or other obligations already ordered in your case. Follow the requirements for your particular expungement route concerning any remaining obligations. A no-fee filing does not cancel an unpaid court obligation.

selfHelpStopConditions: Any crime of violence, which bars conviction expungement outright.
Any prior conviction or prior probation, which defeats first-offender status.
Any arrest during the lookback period, even without a conviction.
Unpaid or unclear court financial obligations.
Any pending criminal proceeding.
The good moral character and rehabilitation showing, which is the court's finding and not a fact LegalEase can supply.
Immigration exposure. Rhode Island expungement does not resolve immigration consequences.

Any goal involving law enforcement employment, bar admission or bar character and fitness, a teaching certificate, a coaching certificate, or early childhood education work, where disclosure survives expungement.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records, which Rhode Island relief does not reach.
Any count near the five-conviction ceiling, because whether 'fewer than six' means up to five and whether the count includes convictions not being expunged are both unresolved.

Every domestic violence, DUI and chemical test refusal conviction. These exclusions are specific to this subsection and must be escalated for exact statutory review rather than treated as a bar on every route.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge Records of a Completed Deferred Sentence (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 12-19-19, 12-1.3-2(e))
tracks.publicName: Clear a record after completing a deferred sentence
tracks.mechanism: A person who received a deferred sentence may move for expungement after completion of the deferred sentence. If the court finds after a hearing that the person complied with all terms of the deferral agreement, including payment of fines, fees, costs, assessments and restitution, the person becomes immediately eligible for consideration for expungement. There is no waiting period beyond completion. The court must also find no pending criminal proceedings and good moral character, and no person convicted of a crime of violence may have deferred-sentence records expunged. A deferred sentence is not an automatic expungement: the court process and the hearing are still required.
exclusions: Any person convicted of a crime of violence, who may not have deferred-sentence records expunged.
Any deferral where the terms are not complete, including unpaid fines, fees, costs, assessments or restitution.
Any pending criminal proceeding.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records.

waitingPeriods.condition: Completion of the deferred sentence and compliance with all terms of the deferral agreement
waitingPeriods.duration: none beyond completion; eligibility for consideration is immediate on the court's compliance finding

units.label: BCI record, docket and eligibility classification
units.description: The judgment stage. Pull the BCI criminal history and the court docket, obtain the BCI number the forms require, and classify the case: first-offender status including prior probation, the crime-of-violence bar, whether the sentence and any probation are complete, whether any arrest or conviction fell inside the lookback, whether financial obligations are paid, waived or reduced, and whether the offence has been reclassified by the General Assembly so the reclassification overlay applies. Nothing is filed at this stage and LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates any record.

units.label: Court-specific Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order
units.description: The document stage. The correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit is completed, on the same form set as the general conviction tracks. The form requires the defendant's name, case number, BCI number, counts, charges, dispositions and the charging police department, and requires the filer to elect seal or expunge — a legal choice with different consequences, never a checkbox preference. The proposed order is prepared to be brought to the hearing for the judge's signature. A custom pleading is not advisable: the Judiciary publishes the forms and the affidavit must be sworn.

units.label: Notice to the Attorney General and charging police department, the hearing, and delivery of certified orders
units.description: The procedural stage, which runs after the packet exists and continues after the judge signs. File with the clerk, who fills in the hearing date; the hearing must be at least ten days after filing because notice must reach the Attorney General and the charging police department. Sign the affidavit before a notary or clerk. Attend the hearing with the proposed order. On a grant the clerk prepares three certified copies after all conditions are satisfied, and the petitioner delivers one to the Attorney General's BCI unit and one to the charging police department — if that delivery does not happen, nothing changes on the record. Verify afterwards with a fresh BCI record.

tracks.venue: The court where the conviction occurred. Rhode Island has no county layer for this purpose; the forms are court-specific rather than local, which makes venue simpler than most states.

rules.filing: File the correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record and Affidavit, with the proposed order, with the clerk of the court where the conviction occurred. The clerk fills in the hearing date.
rules.fees: No expungement filing fee in the Superior Court. The Rhode Island Superior Court's own expungement FAQ, 'Is there a fee associated with my expungement?' (https://www.courts.ri.gov/Courts/superiorcourt/Pages/FAQs.aspx), expressly says the process requires no fee; R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-3 (https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE12/12-1.3/12-1.3-3.htm) is the statutory branch for the route's own conditions. Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research handoff. This is court-specific, not a national fee rule: fines, costs, restitution and other obligations already ordered in the underlying case remain the participant's and remain the separate statutory eligibility condition; a no-fee filing cancels no unpaid court obligation, and no filing-fee-waiver application is required solely to waive a $0 filing fee. No dollar amount is attributed to Superior-55 or any form without locating it in that form's own text.
rules.feeWaiver: Not stated for the motion itself. Court-imposed financial obligations on the underlying case may be waived or reduced by court order, and that waiver or reduction satisfies the eligibility condition.
rules.notice: Notice must be given to the Rhode Island Department of Attorney General and to the police department that brought the charge, at least ten days before the hearing. A hearing is required. The court may grant if it finds no felony or misdemeanor arrest or conviction during the lookback, no pending criminal proceeding, financial obligations satisfied or waived or reduced, good moral character, rehabilitation to the court's satisfaction, and that expungement is consistent with the public interest.
rules.service: Serve the Attorney General and the charging police department at least ten days before the hearing. After a grant, the petitioner delivers certified copies of the order to the Attorney General's BCI unit and the charging police department.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the affidavit before a notary or a clerk. This is a sworn document and the signature must be witnessed in person.
rules.notarization: Required. The affidavit must be signed before a notary or a clerk.

researchParticipantText.fee: The Rhode Island Superior Court does not charge an expungement filing fee. This is separate from fines, costs, restitution, or other obligations already ordered in your case. Follow the requirements for your particular expungement route concerning any remaining obligations. A no-fee filing does not cancel an unpaid court obligation.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other names you have used?
What is your date of birth?

What is the case number?
What were the charges, and how did each one end?
Which police department brought the charge?
On what date did you finish your sentence, including any probation?
Before this case, had you ever been convicted of, or placed on probation for, any felony or misdemeanor?
Have you been arrested for, or convicted of, any felony or misdemeanor since you finished your sentence?
Do you have any criminal case pending right now?
Have all court fines, fees, costs, assessments and restitution been paid, or waived or reduced by court order?

Was the offence any of: murder, manslaughter, first-degree arson, kidnapping with intent to extort, robbery, larceny from the person, first- or second-degree sexual assault, first- or second-degree child molestation, assault with intent to murder or rob or commit first-degree sexual assault, burglary, or entering a dwelling with intent to commit murder, robbery, sexual assault or larceny?
Has the Rhode Island General Assembly changed this offence from a felony to a misdemeanor since you were sentenced?
Do you want the record sealed or expunged? These are different remedies with different consequences.
Did you receive a deferred sentence under an agreement with the Attorney General?
Did you complete every term of the deferral agreement, including all fines, fees, costs, assessments and restitution?
Have you checked the final order in your case to see what actually happened at the end of the deferral?

tracks.legalName: Non-Conviction Sealing and Destruction of Identification Records (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 12-1-12, 12-1-12.1)
tracks.publicName: Seal a case that did not end in conviction
tracks.mechanism: For acquittals, dismissals, no true bills, no informations and other exonerations, identification records such as fingerprints, photographs, physical measurements and other arrest identification records must generally be destroyed within 60 days, and court records are sealed consistent with § 12-1-12.1. District Court Rule 48(a) dismissals on or after 1 January 2023 are sealed automatically by the court not less than 10 and not more than 20 days after dismissal; Rule 48(a) dismissals before that date are sealed administratively by the clerk at the defendant's request, with the order sent electronically to BCI and carried out within 90 days of receipt. All other non-conviction outcomes may be reached by a motion to seal, with notice to the Attorney General and the police department at least ten days before the hearing.

units.label: Verify whether the record has already sealed
units.description: The default branch, and the one that must run first. Establish which sealing route applies: a Rule 48(a) dismissal on or after 1 January 2023 seals automatically; one before that date seals administratively on the defendant's request; and the Judiciary reportedly began a broader automatic programme in 2024 covering acquittals, dismissals and no-file decisions. Pull a BCI record to see whether the record has in fact cleared, and check that identification records were destroyed. Where relief has already happened there is nothing to file and no motion should be generated or sold.

units.label: Motion to seal where automatic or administrative sealing does not apply
units.description: The fallback branch, selected only where the verification branch establishes that no automatic or administrative route reaches the record. The court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record is completed with the SEAL election rather than the expunge election, with notice to the Attorney General and the police department at least ten days before the hearing. Selection between the two branches is on the participant's disposition facts and the sealing route that applies, never on array order.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Expungement of Marijuana Possession Records (R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-1.3-5)
tracks.publicName: Check that an old marijuana possession record has been cleared
tracks.mechanism: A person with a prior civil violation, misdemeanor conviction or felony conviction for possession only of a marijuana offence since decriminalized is entitled to automatic expungement, notwithstanding the general Chapter 12-1.3 rules. Records were to be expunged before 1 July 2024 on a timeline set by the chief justice, with an expedited procedure available on written request. Where the amount is not stated in the record the court presumes two ounces or less. Pending cases, prior convictions and violent convictions do not block the relief; outstanding fines, fees and costs do not block it and eligible marijuana-related amounts are waived; other counts in the same case do not prevent expungement of the eligible marijuana count; and a marijuana expungement under this section is not treated as a prior conviction or civil adjudication for sentencing a later crime. Under subsection (e) anyone incarcerated for misdemeanor or felony marijuana possession has all court costs waived with respect to expungement. Under subsection (f) the court, not the participant, sends a copy of the order to the Attorney General, the arresting agency and any other agency known to hold records. Under subsection (m) custodians may not disclose the existence of the records on inquiry from any source, except from the individual, a bar admission or character and fitness or disciplinary body, the commissioner of elementary and secondary education, or a law enforcement agency where the nature of a new charge would be affected.
exclusions: Anything other than possession only. Possession with intent to distribute and distribution charges are not covered.
Marijuana offences that were not decriminalized under R.I. Gen. Laws § 21-28.11-22 thresholds.
Non-marijuana counts in the same case, which this section does not clear even though they do not block expungement of the eligible marijuana count.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records.

units.label: Verify the automatic § 12-1.3-5 expungement
units.description: The default stage, and the one that must run first. Section 12-1.3-5 entitles a person with a prior civil violation, misdemeanor conviction or felony conviction for possession only of a since-decriminalized marijuana offence to automatic expungement, and Rhode Island completed the initial statewide effort in June 2023 — more than 23,000 records, being 3,015 in Superior Court, 9,952 in the Traffic Tribunal and 10,650 in District Court — over a year ahead of the 1 July 2024 deadline. The participant pulls a BCI criminal history and checks whether the record has already cleared. Nothing is filed at this stage and no participant submission exists: the relief is automatic and, under § 12-1.3-5(f), the court rather than the participant distributes the order to the Attorney General, the arresting agency and any other agency known to hold records. Where the record has cleared, the route ends here and no motion is generated or sold.

units.label: Participant-signed expedited written request where the record has not cleared
units.description: The conditional stage, reached only where the participant confirms from their BCI record that the eligible marijuana possession record has not been expunged. Section 12-1.3-5 makes an expedited procedure available on written request, so the participant signs and submits a request to the court in which the marijuana case was heard. It seeks the same statutory legal effect as the automatic route — expungement of the same eligible marijuana count — so this is one mechanism with two stages, not two remedies. Rhode Island publishes no official form for the request, so it is drafted from controlled participant facts. The unit is unavailable until the verification stage establishes that the automatic action did not reach the record; it is never offered at the outset.

Where the automatic action did not reach the record, the participant's signed expedited written request goes to the court in which the marijuana case was heard.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge an Offence Decriminalized After Conviction (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 12-1.3-2(g), 12-1.3-3(e))
tracks.publicName: Clear a conviction for something that is no longer a crime
tracks.mechanism: Separate from the marijuana route, a person may file for expungement of an offence that was decriminalized after the date of conviction. The court holds a hearing and may require the petitioner to demonstrate that the prior conviction would qualify as a decriminalized offence under current Rhode Island law, which may be done by the petitioner's own affidavit. Where the conditions of the original sentence are complete and required fines, fees and costs are paid in full, the court orders the expungement without cost to the petitioner. There is no waiting period.
exclusions: Any offence that has not been decriminalized under current Rhode Island law.
Any case where the conditions of the original sentence are not complete.
Any case where required fines, fees and costs have not been paid in full.
Federal, out-of-state, military and tribal records.

tracks.legalName: Summary Court Expungement of a Non-Conviction, S.C. Code § 17-22-950
tracks.publicName: Clear a South Carolina magistrate or municipal court charge that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17-22-950 splits on a single fact: whether the accused person was fingerprinted. Under subsection (A), where charges were brought in a summary court, the person was found not guilty or the charges were dismissed or nolle prossed, and the person WAS fingerprinted, the summary court shall immediately issue an expungement order at no cost, obtain and verify all necessary signatures and distribute copies to the arresting agency, the detention facility, the solicitor's office, the clerk of court where applicable, the summary courts involved and SLED. Nothing is submitted by the participant on that branch. Under subsection (B), where the person was NOT fingerprinted, the accused person may apply to the summary court, at no cost, for an order to expunge, and on application and verification the court shall issue the order and distribute copies to the arresting agency and the summary courts involved but not to SLED. That application is SCCA 223E, a participant-signed form. Both branches are barred where the dismissal occurred at a preliminary hearing or where the person has charges pending in summary court and General Sessions arising out of the same course of events. Subsection (C) fixes the timing at no sooner than the appeal expiration date and no later than thirty days after it. Subsection (E) requires removal from all internet-based public records no later than thirty days from the disposition date regardless of whether an application is made. Subsection (F) allows a prosecution or law enforcement agency to object, on the sole grounds of other pending charges or ineligibility, with written notice to the accused person no later than thirty days after the disposition, in which case a General Sessions judge decides; the objection is transmitted on SCCA 223D1, which is completed by the summary court judge and not by the participant.
exclusions: A dismissal that occurred at a preliminary hearing.
Any case where the person has charges pending in summary court and in a court of general sessions arising out of the same course of events.
Convictions of any kind. This route reaches non-convictions only.

Charges dismissed or nolle prossed because of successful completion of pretrial intervention, the traffic education programme, the alcohol education programme, a conditional discharge or any other statutorily authorised diversion programme operated by a solicitor's office. SCCA 223E says in terms that those must be applied for at the solicitor's office, and they route to their own tracks.
General Sessions charges, which route to sc_17_1_40_general_sessions.

waitingPeriods.duration: The expungement must occur no sooner than the appeal expiration date and no later than thirty days after the appeal expiration date, § 17-22-950(C).

A prosecution or law enforcement agency must give written notice of objection no later than thirty days after the person is found not guilty or the charges are dismissed or nolle prossed, § 17-22-950(F).

units.label: Fingerprinted: the summary court must issue the order itself, § 17-22-950(A)
units.description: Where the person was fingerprinted for the charge, the summary court shall immediately issue the expungement order at no cost to the accused person, obtain and verify all necessary signatures, and distribute copies to the arresting law enforcement agency, the detention facility or jail, the solicitor's office, the clerk of court in appealed or remanded cases, the summary courts involved and SLED. There is no participant submission on this branch and no fee, so the deliverable is guidance: confirm the disposition date and the appeal expiration date, expect the order within thirty days of the appeal expiration date, obtain the certified or raised-seal copy the court must provide under subsection (D), confirm the charge has come off internet-based public records within thirty days of disposition under subsection (E), and escalate to the summary court clerk where the order did not issue. units.label: Not fingerprinted: the participant applies on SCCA 223E, § 17-22-950(B)
units.description: Where the person was not fingerprinted for the charge, subsection (B) gives the accused person an application to make, at no cost, to the summary court. SCCA 223E, read at source on 2026-08-06, is that application: it is captioned 'Application for Expungement Pursuant to § 17-22-950(B)', it is signed by the defendant, and it asks for the identity block, current address, alias, full name at time of arrest, phone number, date of offence, warrant or ticket number, charge, arresting agency, whether the person was fingerprinted, disposition and disposition date. Every one of those is a participant-supplied fact, so the form generates from the intake answers. This branch is selected by the fingerprinting answer alone and is not a step toward or after unit A; exactly one of the two applies. Filing and the resulting order remain free.

tracks.legalName: Solicitor Application to Destroy Arrest Records of a General Sessions Non-Conviction, S.C. Code § 17-1-40
tracks.publicName: Clear a South Carolina General Sessions charge that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17-1-40(B)(1) provides that where a person's record is expunged under Article 9 of Chapter 22 because the person was charged with a criminal offence, or issued a courtesy summons, and the charge was discharged, proceedings were dismissed, or the person was found not guilty, the arrest and booking record, associated bench warrants, mug shots and fingerprints must be destroyed and no evidence of the record may be retained by any municipal, county or state agency. Two provisos qualify that destruction and must be disclosed: law enforcement and prosecution agencies retain the arrest and booking record, bench warrants, mug shots and fingerprints under seal for three years and one hundred twenty days, and may retain them indefinitely under seal for ongoing or future investigation and prosecution of the offence, administrative hearings and litigation defence; and detention and correctional facilities retain booking records and institutional files under seal for the same period. The route runs through the Solicitor's Office. Section 17-22-940(A)(1) exempts a § 17-1-40 applicant from the $250 administrative fee unless the charge was dismissed, discharged or nolle prossed as part of the plea arrangement under which the defendant pled guilty and was sentenced to other charges; § 17-22-940(E)(1) exempts the route from the $25 SLED verification fee and § 17-22-940(E) from SLED verification itself; and § 17-22-940(H) bars the clerk from charging a filing fee where the charge was discharged, dismissed, nolle prossed or the applicant was acquitted. Section 17-22-940(G) permits multiple charges from a single incident on one application.
exclusions: Convictions of any kind.
Summary court non-convictions, which are free and route to sc_17_22_950_summary.
Charges dismissed on completion of a diversion programme, which route to their own solicitor tracks.

The sealed retentions the section preserves: law enforcement, prosecution, detention and correctional agencies keep the record under seal for three years and one hundred twenty days, and law enforcement and prosecution may keep it indefinitely under seal for the statutory purposes.
Unredacted incident and supplemental reports, investigative files and gathered evidence, which § 17-1-40(C)(1) preserves under seal.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Section 17-1-40 imposes no waiting period; the application may be made once the charge is discharged, dismissed, nolle prossed or the person is acquitted.

releaseBlockers.question: The single-incident fee. Section 17-22-940(G) as amended by 2018 Act No. 254 was read at source on 2026-08-06 and provides that where multiple charges from a single incident are combined under § 17-1-40 or § 17-22-150(a), 'only one two hundred fifty-dollar fee, one twenty-five dollar SLED verification fee, and one thirty-five dollar clerk of court filing fee may be charged'. The controlling review reports the single-incident solicitor fee as one hundred fifty dollars, drawn from Supreme Court expungement guidance. The current statutory figure is two hundred fifty dollars. The packet quotes the statutory figure and does not promise the lower one.

provenance.sourceStatement: There is a second, lower solicitor fee the reference does not mention. The standard administrative fee is $250, but the Supreme Court's expungement guidance provides that where expungement is sought for **multiple charges arising out of a single incident** under §§ 17-1-40 or 17-22-150(a), those charges may go on **one application** and only **one fee of $150** is charged, plus one $25 SLED verification fee and one $35 clerk fee where applicable.

tracks.legalName: Solicitor Application to Destroy Arrest Records After Successful Pretrial Intervention, S.C. Code § 17-22-150(a)
tracks.publicName: Clear a South Carolina charge after you completed Pretrial Intervention
tracks.mechanism: After successful completion of a pretrial intervention programme the solicitor effects a noncriminal disposition of the charge and the person may apply to have the official record of arrest destroyed. Violation of the programme resumes prosecution. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17-22-940(D) requires the circuit pretrial intervention director to attest by signature on the application to the eligibility of the charge for expungement before either the solicitor or his designee and then the circuit court judge signs; § 17-22-940(E) exempts the route from SLED verification and § 17-22-940(E)(1) from the $25 SLED verification fee; and § 17-22-940(G) permits multiple charges from a single incident to be combined on one application, this being one of only two routes for which that is allowed. The pretrial intervention application and participation fees under § 17-22-110 are programme costs, not expungement costs.
exclusions: Any participant who did not successfully complete the programme; violation resumes prosecution.
Convictions of any kind.
Charges never accepted into pretrial intervention, which route by their own disposition.
The sealed retentions preserved by § 17-1-40.

waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond successful completion of the programme and the solicitor's noncriminal disposition.

tracks.legalName: Solicitor Application to Destroy Arrest Records After Successful Alcohol Education Program Completion, S.C. Code § 17-22-530(A)
tracks.publicName: Clear a South Carolina underage-alcohol charge after you completed the Alcohol Education Program
tracks.mechanism: The controlling citation is settled at source. Article 5 of Chapter 22, Title 17 is the Alcohol Education Program: § 17-22-510 gives each circuit solicitor prosecutorial discretion to establish the programme, § 17-22-520 sets eligibility, and § 17-22-530 governs disposition on completion. Under § 17-22-530(A), when a person successfully completes an alcohol education programme the circuit solicitor shall effect a noncriminal disposition of the alcohol-related offence and no record may be maintained except by the Commission on Prosecution Coordination to prevent a second use; under § 17-22-530(B) the person may then apply to the court for an order to destroy all official records relating to the arrest. Section 17-22-520 confines eligibility to a person at least seventeen but under twenty-one at the time of arrest, with no prior alcohol-related offence and no significant history of prior delinquency or criminal activity, charged with one of eleven enumerated offences or another offence similar in nature and severity as determined by the circuit solicitor, expressly excluding the offences enumerated in §§ 56-5-2930 and 56-5-2933. Participation is once only. Section 17-22-940(D) names the alcohol education program director as an attestor and § 17-22-940(E)(1) exempts § 17-22-530(A) from the SLED verification fee.
exclusions: Any person under seventeen or twenty-one or older at the time of arrest.
Any person with a prior alcohol-related offence, or a significant history of prior delinquency or criminal activity.
Any second participation; § 17-22-520(B) allows the programme only once.
Driving under the influence offences under §§ 56-5-2930 and 56-5-2933, which § 17-22-520(C)(11) expressly excludes.
Any offence outside the eleven enumerated in § 17-22-520(C) unless the circuit solicitor determines it similar in nature and severity.
Any participant who violated the conditions and was terminated, in which case the offence is reinstated.

waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond successful completion and the solicitor's noncriminal disposition under § 17-22-530(A).

The § 17-22-550 programme enrolment fee of $250, and any provider fees, are programme costs; participation may not be denied for inability to pay and those fees may be waived or reduced at the solicitor's discretion.

Each solicitor's office also maintains a private donation account which may defray up to fifty per cent of the administrative fee on a first-come first-served basis, § 17-22-940(A)(2).

releaseBlockers.question: The single-incident fee. Section 17-22-940(G) as amended by 2018 Act No. 254 was read at source on 2026-08-06 and provides that where multiple charges from a single incident are combined under § 17-1-40 or § 17-22-150(a), 'only one two hundred fifty-dollar fee, one twenty-five dollar SLED verification fee, and one thirty-five dollar clerk of court filing fee may be charged'. The controlling review reports the single-incident solicitor fee as one hundred fifty dollars, drawn from Supreme Court expungement guidance. The current statutory figure is two hundred fifty dollars. The packet quotes the statutory figure and does not promise the lower one.

provenance.sourceStatement: There is a second, lower solicitor fee the reference does not mention. The standard administrative fee is $250, but the Supreme Court's expungement guidance provides that where expungement is sought for **multiple charges arising out of a single incident** under §§ 17-1-40 or 17-22-150(a), those charges may go on **one application** and only **one fee of $150** is charged, plus one $25 SLED verification fee and one $35 clerk fee where applicable.
provenance.counselQuestion: Does the $150 single-incident fee in the Supreme Court guidance survive the 2018 amendment to § 17-22-940(G), which says only one $250 fee may be charged in that circumstance? Which figure does the packet quote?

openLegalQuestions.question: Status of H.3730 and H.428 of the 2025-2026 session. H.3730 would add § 17-22-915 creating a first-nonviolent-offence route and a drug treatment court route; H.428 would add § 34-11-90(f) for multiple fraudulent check convictions after ten years and add § 17-1-43 requiring destruction of arrest records made as a result of mistaken identity within 180 days. Neither appears in the enacted text of Chapter 22 or Chapter 11 read at source on 2026-08-06, so neither is available and neither is offered. Both remain worth a standing monitor.

Neither was enacted as of March 2026.

tracks.legalName: Solicitor Application to Destroy Arrest Records After Successful Traffic Education Program Completion, S.C. Code § 17-22-330(A)
tracks.publicName: Clear a South Carolina traffic charge after you completed the Traffic Education Program
tracks.mechanism: The controlling citation is settled at source. Article 3 of Chapter 22, Title 17 is the Traffic Education Program Act: § 17-22-310 gives each circuit solicitor prosecutorial discretion to establish a programme for persons who commit traffic-related offences punishable only by a fine and loss of four points or less, and bars participation where the offence resulted in death or serious bodily injury; § 17-22-320 confines eligibility to a person with no significant history of traffic violations and allows participation only once; and § 17-22-330(A) provides that on successful completion the administering governmental agency shall effect a noncriminal disposition of the offence, with no record maintained except by the programme to prevent a second use. Subsections (C) and (D) allow termination and reinstatement for violating the conditions, and require termination where the person receives a subsequent traffic violation in the six months following the ticket. Section 17-22-940(D) names the traffic education program director as an attestor and § 17-22-940(E)(1) exempts § 17-22-330(A) from the SLED verification fee.
exclusions: Any traffic-related offence not punishable only by a fine and loss of four points or less.
Any offence that resulted in death or serious bodily injury to another person.
Any person with a significant history of traffic violations.
Any second participation; § 17-22-320(A) allows the programme only once.
Any participant terminated for violating the conditions, or terminated because of a subsequent traffic violation within six months of the ticket.
Criminal convictions of any kind.

waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond successful completion and the noncriminal disposition under § 17-22-330(A). Note that a subsequent traffic violation within six months of the ticket terminates the programme and reinstates the offence.

releaseBlockers.question: The single-incident fee. Section 17-22-940(G) as amended by 2018 Act No. 254 was read at source on 2026-08-06 and provides that where multiple charges from a single incident are combined under § 17-1-40 or § 17-22-150(a), 'only one two hundred fifty-dollar fee, one twenty-five dollar SLED verification fee, and one thirty-five dollar clerk of court filing fee may be charged'. The controlling review reports the single-incident solicitor fee as one hundred fifty dollars, drawn from Supreme Court expungement guidance. The current statutory figure is two hundred fifty dollars. The packet quotes the statutory figure and does not promise the lower one.

provenance.sourceStatement: There is a second, lower solicitor fee the reference does not mention. The standard administrative fee is $250, but the Supreme Court's expungement guidance provides that where expungement is sought for **multiple charges arising out of a single incident** under §§ 17-1-40 or 17-22-150(a), those charges may go on **one application** and only **one fee of $150** is charged, plus one $25 SLED verification fee and one $35 clerk fee where applicable.
provenance.counselQuestion: Does the $150 single-incident fee in the Supreme Court guidance survive the 2018 amendment to § 17-22-940(G), which says only one $250 fee may be charged in that circumstance? Which figure does the packet quote?

Neither appears in the enacted text of Chapter 22 or Chapter 11 read at source on 2026-08-06, so neither is available and neither is offered. Both remain worth a standing monitor.

tracks.legalName: Solicitor Application to Expunge Records After a First-Offence Drug Conditional Discharge, S.C. Code § 44-53-450(b)
tracks.publicName: Clear a first South Carolina drug possession case that ended in a conditional discharge
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 44-53-450(A) allows a person not previously convicted of any offence under Article 3 of Chapter 53, Title 44, or under any state or federal marijuana, stimulant, depressant or hallucinogenic drug statute, who pleads guilty to or is found guilty of possession of a controlled substance under § 44-53-370(c) or (d) or § 44-53-375(A), to be placed on probation without entry of a judgment of guilt, with the court discharging the person and dismissing the proceedings on fulfilment of the terms. The discharge is not a conviction for purposes of any disqualification or disability, a nonpublic record is retained by the Department of Narcotic and Dangerous Drugs under SLED solely to determine whether a later offence is a subsequent one, and the discharge and dismissal may occur only once with respect to any person. Subsection (B) is the expungement: on dismissal and discharge the person may apply to the court for an order expunging from all official records, other than the retained nonpublic record, all recordation relating to the arrest, indictment or information, trial, finding of guilt, and the dismissal and discharge, and if the court determines after hearing that the person was dismissed and discharged it shall enter the order, restoring the person in the contemplation of law to the status occupied before arrest. Subsection (C) requires payment before discharge of a fee of $350 in general sessions court or $150 in summary court, waivable, reducible or suspendable only for indigency. Section 17-22-940(D) requires the summary court judge to attest where the matter was in summary court, and § 17-22-940(E) exempts the route from SLED verification and its fee.
exclusions: Any person previously convicted of an offence under Article 3 of Chapter 53, Title 44, or under any state or federal statute relating to marijuana, or stimulant, depressant or hallucinogenic drugs.
Any person who has already had one discharge and dismissal under § 44-53-450; it may occur only once.
Any person whose terms and conditions were violated and against whom the court entered an adjudication of guilt.
Offences other than possession of a controlled substance under § 44-53-370(c) or (d) or § 44-53-375(A).
The nonpublic record retained by the Department of Narcotic and Dangerous Drugs under SLED, which the expungement order expressly does not reach.
Any case where the § 44-53-450(C) fee remains unpaid, since payment precedes discharge and dismissal.

waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond fulfilment of the terms and conditions, the court's discharge and dismissal, and payment of the § 44-53-450(C) fee. Unlike several other states' conditional-discharge routes, § 44-53-450(B) imposes no post-discharge waiting period.

Section 17-22-940(G) as amended by 2018 Act No. 254 was read at source on 2026-08-06 and provides that where multiple charges from a single incident are combined under § 17-1-40 or § 17-22-150(a), 'only one two hundred fifty-dollar fee, one twenty-five dollar SLED verification fee, and one thirty-five dollar clerk of court filing fee may be charged'. The controlling review reports the single-incident solicitor fee as one hundred fifty dollars, drawn from Supreme Court expungement guidance. The current statutory figure is two hundred fifty dollars. The packet quotes the statutory figure and does not promise the lower one.

tracks.legalName: Solicitor Application to Expunge a First-Offence Fraudulent Check Conviction, S.C. Code § 34-11-90(e)
tracks.publicName: Clear a first South Carolina bad-check conviction after one year
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 34-11-90(e) provides that after a conviction under the chapter on a first offence the defendant may, after one year from the date of the conviction, apply or cause someone acting on his behalf to apply to the court for an order expunging the records of the arrest and conviction. The provision does not apply to any crime classified as a felony, and a conviction is classified as a felony where the instrument drawn or uttered exceeds five thousand dollars. If the defendant has had no other conviction during the one-year period following the conviction, the court shall issue the order. No person has any rights under the section more than one time. After expungement SLED keeps a nonpublic record of the offence and the date of expungement to prevent a second use, which is not releasable under § 34-11-95 or the Freedom of Information Act except to authorised officials. 'Conviction' includes a guilty plea, a plea of nolo contendere, or the forfeiting of bail, and each instrument drawn or uttered constitutes a separate offence. Section 17-22-940(E) requires SLED verification on this route and provides that a conviction for any minor traffic-related offence unrelated to driving under the influence is not a bar.
exclusions: Any fraudulent check offence classified as a felony, which the section reaches where the instrument exceeds five thousand dollars.
Any person who has had any other conviction during the one-year period following the conviction sought to be expunged.
Any person who has already used the section once; the right is available one time only.
The SLED nonpublic record of the offence and the date of expungement, which is retained to prevent a second use.
Each instrument drawn or uttered is a separate offence, so a participant with several bad cheques has several convictions and § 17-22-940(G)'s one-charge-per-order rule applies.

waitingPeriods.duration: One year from the date of the conviction, with no other conviction during that year. This is the shortest waiting period of any South Carolina conviction route.
