packetInstructions: Where the eligibility requirements are satisfied there is a rebuttable presumption that the petition should be granted, which shifts the practical burden to the district attorney general to object. Public Chapter 719, effective 2026-04-14, rewrote T.C.A. § 40-32-108(d)(2) and preserved that presumption for petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E), while providing that the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety. The packet may describe the presumption; it may not state that the petition will be granted.

Confirm the statutory citation with the county clerk or district attorney general before every filing. Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025, effective 2025-04-24, and codified by Public Chapter 608, the 2026 Code Bill, effective 2026-03-25. Clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering: the Tennessee AOC's own expunction page is titled to say updated information is coming to reflect changes to T.C.A. § 40-32-101 and still reasons from that section, which since 2025-04-24 has been nothing but a definitions section. A generated petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet is built to carry the current citation with the superseded one noted, and instructs the participant to confirm before filing.

Routing added by the integrated Tennessee 2026 route inventory decision, without any change to this route's own eligibility rules. A participant refused here because the conviction is outside the § 40-32-107(a)(1) lists but who holds a gubernatorial pardon is evaluated under tn_post_pardon. A participant refused here only by the § 40-32-107(a)(3)(A) predating condition because of a DUI conviction, who completed a certified recovery court programme with a ten-year interval, is evaluated under tn_recovery_court. The exclusion list is unchanged in both cases.
participantQuestions: Public Chapter 930, effective 2026-07-01, applies only to offences committed on or after 2026-07-01 and is not applied retroactively. Its enrolled application clause reads: this act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it, and applies to offenses committed on or after that date. Its effect on this route is to relocate burglary under T.C.A. § 39-13-1002 within the § 40-32-107(a)(1) eligibility lists, deleting it from the Class E felony list at (a)(1)(C)(xxi) and substituting it in the Class D felony list at (a)(1)(B)(xviii) as burglary other than habitation, tracking the reclassification of burglary to a Class D felony. Because the waiting period is five years for a misdemeanour or Class E felony and ten years for a Class C or D felony, that doubles the wait for the affected offence — but only for offences committed on or after 2026-07-01. No reach to federal records; a diversion guilty plea may remain visible on clearance checks.

releaseBlockers.question: Current authority reveals statutory record-clearing routes that are outside the adopted nine-slot mechanism inventory and are therefore not built here. Public Chapter 268 created T.C.A. § 40-32-107(c), expunction after a conviction for illegal registration or voting under § 2-19-107 on a fifteen-year wait, and § 40-32-109, expunction of an arrest record where the court with jurisdiction has no record of the arrest, with a clerk search and certification. Public Chapter 719 rewrote the § 40-32-107(d) post-pardon route, replacing an open-textured judicial nonviolent-crime finding with a closed seven-item felony exclusion list, which substantially broadens it. Public Chapter 1061 added § 40-32-107(e), the recovery-court route, effective 2026-07-01 with no offence-date limitation. Each petitions under § 40-32-108. Adding any of them would change the adopted denominator, which a normalization worker may not do, so they are recorded for a captain-authorized inventory amendment instead.

releaseBlockers.question: The prior-expunction bars across the T.C.A. § 40-32-107 subsections are asymmetric on the enacted text and the asymmetry cannot be resolved from it. Subsections (a), (b) and (c) each bar a petitioner previously granted expunction under (a), (b) or (c), and name neither (d) nor (e). Subsection (e)(1)(D) bars a petitioner previously granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e). Subsection (d) states no prior-expunction bar at all and is named by none of the others. AFFECTED TRACKS: tn_eligible_conviction, tn_two_offense, tn_post_pardon, tn_recovery_court and tn_illegal_voting. SCREENING IMPACT: the intake asks whether the participant has previously been granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e) and records the answer, but no screen infers a bar that the subsection under which the participant is applying does not state, and in particular no bar is inferred against or from subsection (d). CURRENT PACKET TREATMENT: the packet reports the participant's own answer and states which bars the governing subsection actually contains; it asserts no conclusion about a subsection that is silent, and it does not tell a participant that a route is closed on the strength of a bar the statute does not impose. REQUIRED FUTURE CLARIFICATION: a statutory amendment naming the subsections reciprocally, or a counsel determination on whether a prior (e) grant closes (a), (b) and (c) and on whether any prior grant closes (d). RUNTIME EFFECT: none. Every Tennessee route is runtime-disabled and none can be served to a participant, so the open question governs release readiness and screening copy rather than anything a participant can reach today.

provenance.sourceStatement: The prior-expunction bars across the § 40-32-107 subsections are asymmetric on the enacted text, and the asymmetry is reported rather than resolved because it cannot be resolved from the text. On the face of the text a prior (e) grant bars a later (e) petition and, by (e)(1)(D), is itself barred by a prior (a), (b) or (c) grant — but (a), (b) and (c) do not name (e), so whether a prior (e) grant closes them is unresolved. Subsection (d) is outside every bar in both directions. This is carried as a release blocker on Routes 2 and 3 and on the two existing conviction tracks, and no screening question asserts a conclusion about it.

Open question blocks release (legal_effect_or_warning): Three ancillary current-text exports remain pending and are recorded as source-completeness follow-ups only, exactly as the captain-owned authority receipt directs. T.C.A. § 40-32-104 is the chapter's penalty provision, confirmed by the official cross-reference at new § 40-32-102(e)(2), which makes unlawful release of confidential expunged records a Class A misdemeanour punishable as described in § 40-32-104. T.C.A. § 40-6-204 could not be confirmed from any official Tennessee source and is not asserted; no official act retrieved cites, quotes or amends it. Open question blocks release (governing_mechanism): Current authority reveals statutory record-clearing routes that are outside the adopted nine-slot mechanism inventory and are therefore not built here. Public Chapter 268 created T.C.A. § 40-32-107(c), expunction after a conviction for illegal registration or voting under § 2-19-107 on a fifteen-year wait, and § 40-32-109, expunction of an arrest record where the court with jurisdiction has no record of the arrest, with a clerk search and certification. Public Chapter 719 rewrote the § 40-32-107(d) post-pardon route, replacing an open-textured judicial nonviolent-crime finding with a closed seven-item felony exclusion list, which substantially broadens it. Public Chapter 1061 added § 40-32-107(e), the recovery-court route, effective 2026-07-01 with no offence-date limitation. Each petitions under § 40-32-108. Adding any of them would change the adopted denominator, which a normalization worker may not do, so they are recorded for a captain-authorized inventory amendment instead.

Open question blocks release (eligibility_branch): The prior-expunction bars across the T.C.A. § 40-32-107 subsections are asymmetric on the enacted text and the asymmetry cannot be resolved from it. Subsections (a), (b) and (c) each bar a petitioner previously granted expunction under (a), (b) or (c), and name neither (d) nor (e). Subsection (e)(1)(D) bars a petitioner previously granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e). Subsection (d) states no prior-expunction bar at all and is named by none of the others. AFFECTED TRACKS: tn_eligible_conviction, tn_two_offense, tn_post_pardon, tn_recovery_court and tn_illegal_voting. SCREENING IMPACT: the intake asks whether the participant has previously been granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e) and records the answer, but no screen infers a bar that the subsection under which the participant is applying does not state, and in particular no bar is inferred against or from subsection (d). CURRENT PACKET TREATMENT: the packet reports the participant's own answer and states which bars the governing subsection actually contains; it asserts no conclusion about a subsection that is silent, and it does not tell a participant that a route is closed on the strength of a bar the statute does not impose. REQUIRED FUTURE CLARIFICATION: a statutory amendment naming the subsections reciprocally, or a counsel determination on whether a prior (e) grant closes (a), (b) and (c) and on whether any prior grant closes (d). RUNTIME EFFECT: none. Every Tennessee route is runtime-disabled and none can be served to a participant, so the open question governs release readiness and screening copy rather than anything a participant can reach today.

tracks.publicName: Expunge up to two offences, once in your life
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Section 40-32-107(b) defines an eligible petitioner as a person seeking expunction of no more than two offences. Each offence must be eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1) and must have occurred prior to any conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence, including ineligible federal and other-state convictions. The permitted combinations are exhaustive: two misdemeanours, or one felony and one misdemeanour. Two felonies are not available on this route. At filing there must be five years since completion of sentence for any misdemeanour or Class E felony being expunged and ten years for any Class C or Class D felony being expunged, every sentence requirement must be fulfilled for each offence, and the person must not previously have been granted expunction under subsection (a), this subsection (b) or subsection (c). Subsection (b)(2) provides a single-episode merger mirroring (a)(1)(F): contemporaneous same-location single-intent convictions count as a single offence for the purposes of the two-offence limit, so one episode does not consume both slots. Subsection (b)(3) directs the petitioner to § 40-32-108, so the same DA-prepared petition procedure applies. The reciprocal bars across (a), (b) and (c) are lifetime, which is why using this pathway forecloses a later second use and makes the timing decision consequential.
exclusions: Any conviction that is not on the enumerated eligible lists at T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a)(1), which are section-specific Class C, Class D and Class E felony lists and a misdemeanour category subject to a long exclusion list.

Sexual offences and any offence requiring sex offender registration.
Class A and Class B felonies, violent offences and crimes against the person enumerated in the statute.
Vehicular assault and vehicular homicide.
Domestic assault under T.C.A. § 39-13-111, stalking under § 39-17-315, protective-order violations, and certain offences against children, all of which appear in the misdemeanour exclusion list.
Offences committed by a public official in an official capacity.
A conviction that did not occur on or after 1 November 1989, unless it satisfies the separate pre-1989 route at § 40-32-107(a)(1)(E) and its nine substantive tests.
A person who has previously been granted expunction under § 40-32-107(a), (b) or (c). The bars are reciprocal and lifetime.

A person holding a commercial driver licence convicted of a controlled-substance offence occurring in a motor vehicle, or holding any licence where the offence occurred in a commercial motor vehicle, under § 40-32-107(a)(2).
More than two offences. The limit at § 40-32-107(b)(1) is absolute.
Two felonies. The permitted combinations are two misdemeanours, or one felony and one misdemeanour.
A person who has previously been granted expunction under § 40-32-107(a), (b) or (c). The bars are reciprocal and lifetime, so a single earlier grant closes this route.

generationRequirements.question: Which court handled the case, and in which county? A separate filing is needed in each county where you have a case.
What is the docket or case number?
What was the charge, and exactly how did the case end?
On what date did the case end?
What is the state control number on your TBI criminal history? The expunction order cannot be completed without it.
List every other conviction you have anywhere, including federal and out-of-state.
Are you asking about this because of immigration, federal employment or a security clearance? Tennessee expunction does not reach federal records.
What is the exact T.C.A. section you were convicted under? The offence name and class are not enough — Tennessee's eligible lists are section by section.
On what date was the offence committed? This matters independently of the conviction date, because a 2026 change applies only to offences committed on or after 1 July 2026.
Did the conviction occur on or after 1 November 1989?
On what date did you finish the entire sentence — including any imprisonment or probation, all release conditions, and every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment?
Is every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment paid in full? Anything outstanding means the sentence is not complete and the clock has not started.

Have you ever had a conviction expunged in Tennessee before under T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a), (b), (c) or (e)? This route is available once in a lifetime and a previous grant under (a), (b) or (c) closes it. A grant under (e) is recorded because the statute is asymmetric on the point, and no bar is applied against you that the subsection does not state.
Did you hold a commercial driver licence at the time, and did the offence involve a controlled substance or a commercial motor vehicle?
Did your sentence require a period free from dependency on or abuse of alcohol or a controlled substance? If so, have you met at least one year of it?
How many offences are you asking to clear? The limit is two.
Are the two offences both misdemeanours, or one felony and one misdemeanour? Two felonies cannot be done on this route.
Did the offences happen at the same time and place as part of one continuous incident with a single intent? If so they may count as one, leaving your second slot open.
This pathway can be used once in your life. Do you have any other conviction that might become eligible later? Using it now closes the door on that.
Have you received a pardon from the Governor for this conviction? If you have, a different route may reach it even where this one cannot.

If a DUI conviction is what is standing in the way: have you successfully completed a certified recovery court programme, and did the offence you want cleared happen at least ten years after that DUI conviction?

The eligible lists at T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a)(1) are enumerated section by section — Class C, Class D and Class E felony lists and a misdemeanour category with a long exclusion list — and the legislature has expanded them repeatedly, most recently by Public Chapter 930. packetInstructions: Where the eligibility requirements are satisfied there is a rebuttable presumption that the petition should be granted, which shifts the practical burden to the district attorney general to object. Public Chapter 719, effective 2026-04-14, rewrote T.C.A. § 40-32-108(d)(2) and preserved that presumption for petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E), while providing that the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety. The packet may describe the presumption; it may not state that the petition will be granted.

Confirm the statutory citation with the county clerk or district attorney general before every filing. Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025, effective 2025-04-24, and codified by Public Chapter 608, the 2026 Code Bill, effective 2026-03-25. Clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering: the Tennessee AOC's own expunction page is titled to say updated information is coming to reflect changes to T.C.A. § 40-32-101 and still reasons from that section, which since 2025-04-24 has been nothing but a definitions section. A generated petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet is built to carry the current citation with the superseded one noted, and instructs the participant to confirm before filing.

A participant refused here because the conviction is outside the § 40-32-107(a)(1) lists but who holds a gubernatorial pardon is evaluated under tn_post_pardon. releaseBlockers.question: The prior-expunction bars across the T.C.A. § 40-32-107 subsections are asymmetric on the enacted text and the asymmetry cannot be resolved from it. Subsections (a), (b) and (c) each bar a petitioner previously granted expunction under (a), (b) or (c), and name neither (d) nor (e). Subsection (e)(1)(D) bars a petitioner previously granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e). Subsection (d) states no prior-expunction bar at all and is named by none of the others. AFFECTED TRACKS: tn_eligible_conviction, tn_two_offense, tn_post_pardon, tn_recovery_court and tn_illegal_voting. SCREENING IMPACT: the intake asks whether the participant has previously been granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e) and records the answer, but no screen infers a bar that the subsection under which the participant is applying does not state, and in particular no bar is inferred against or from subsection (d). CURRENT PACKET TREATMENT: the packet reports the participant's own answer and states which bars the governing subsection actually contains; it asserts no conclusion about a subsection that is silent, and it does not tell a participant that a route is closed on the strength of a bar the statute does not impose. REQUIRED FUTURE CLARIFICATION: a statutory amendment naming the subsections reciprocally, or a counsel determination on whether a prior (e) grant closes (a), (b) and (c) and on whether any prior grant closes (d). RUNTIME EFFECT: none. Every Tennessee route is runtime-disabled and none can be served to a participant, so the open question governs release readiness and screening copy rather than anything a participant can reach today.

A previous expunction was granted under § 40-32-107(a), (b) or (c), which closes the route for life.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Under T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e) the petition and proposed order must be prepared by the office of the district attorney general and given to the petitioner to be filed with the clerk of the court. The petition is therefore a prosecutor instrument, and LegalEase does not generate it. What LegalEase generates is the participant's own written request to the district attorney general's office for the conviction-expunction packet, with the supporting eligibility record. Both the Tennessee AOC and the TBI direct participants to request a conviction expungement packet from the district attorney's office, which is the practical face of that provision.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Where the eligibility requirements are satisfied there is a rebuttable presumption that the petition should be granted, which shifts the practical burden to the district attorney general to object. Public Chapter 719, effective 2026-04-14, rewrote T.C.A. § 40-32-108(d)(2) and preserved that presumption for petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E), while providing that the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety. The packet may describe the presumption; it may not state that the petition will be granted.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Mapping the offence to its exact T.C.A. section and checking it against the current eligible list is not something an offence label or class can settle. The packet checks the current list rather than assuming, and any borderline offence goes to review.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Confirm the statutory citation with the county clerk or district attorney general before every filing. Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025, effective 2025-04-24, and codified by Public Chapter 608, the 2026 Code Bill, effective 2026-03-25. Clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering: the Tennessee AOC's own expunction page is titled to say updated information is coming to reflect changes to T.C.A. § 40-32-101 and still reasons from that section, which since 2025-04-24 has been nothing but a definitions section. A generated petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet is built to carry the current citation with the superseded one noted, and instructs the participant to confirm before filing.

tracks.legalName: Expunction of a conviction for illegal registration or voting, T.C.A. § 40-32-107(c) with procedure at § 40-32-108
tracks.publicName: Clear a conviction for illegal registration or voting
tracks.mechanism: Expunction of the conviction record. Under T.C.A. § 40-32-110 the petitioner is entitled to have all public records of the expunged conviction destroyed in the manner set out in the chapter, restoring the person in contemplation of law to the status occupied before arrest, indictment, information, trial and conviction. A person convicted of illegal registration or voting under T.C.A. § 2-19-107, where fifteen years have elapsed since completion of the sentence, every sentence requirement has been fulfilled, the offence occurred prior to any conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence, and the person has not previously been granted expunction under § 40-32-107(a), (b) or (c). The fifteen-year wait is the longest in the chapter — three times the misdemeanour and Class E felony period and half again the Class C and D felony period — and it attaches to a single named offence rather than to an offence class. Codified through Public Chapter 608 and untouched by Public Chapters 719, 930 and 1061. Subsection (c) is not reached by the § 40-32-108(d)(2) rebuttable presumption, which is keyed only to petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E), so no presumption applies and the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety.
exclusions: Any conviction other than a violation of T.C.A. § 2-19-107. The subsection reaches that one named offence and no other elections or fraud provision.
Any case where fewer than fifteen years have elapsed since completion of the sentence, measured at the time the petition is filed.

Any case where a sentence requirement remains unfulfilled, including any unpaid fine, restitution amount, court cost or other assessment, any uncompleted term of imprisonment or probation, or any unmet condition of supervised or unsupervised release.

Any case where the offence did not occur prior to a conviction for a criminal offence that is ineligible for expunction, including federal convictions and convictions in other states that would be ineligible in Tennessee.
A person previously granted expunction under T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a), (b) or (c) for another criminal offence. Subsection (c)(1)(D) names exactly those three and does not name subsection (d).
Restoration of voting rights. That is a separate remedy under separate machinery and is not what expunction under this subsection does.

waitingPeriods.duration: Fifteen years from completion of the sentence imposed for the offence being expunged, measured at the time of filing the petition. This is the longest waiting period in the chapter.

On completion of the sentence, which means every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment paid, any term of imprisonment or probation completed, and all conditions of supervised or unsupervised release met. Anything outstanding means the sentence is not complete and the clock has not started.
The court may not order sooner than 61 days after the petition is served on the district attorney general, who has 60 days to submit recommendations.
No further petition for at least two years from the date of the denial, under § 40-32-108(d)(3).

tracks.legalName: Expunction of a pardoned conviction, T.C.A. § 40-32-107(d) as amended by Public Chapter 719, with procedure at § 40-32-108
tracks.publicName: Clear a conviction you have been pardoned for
tracks.mechanism: Expunction of the pardoned conviction record, with the § 40-32-110 effect. The pardon by itself does not clear the record; it opens this route. A person who received a pardon from the Governor following a positive vote of the Board of Parole recommending it, who petitions the convicting court, and whose conviction the judge finds was not for one of seven enumerated felonies, or an attempt, conspiracy, facilitation or solicitation to commit one of them: first degree murder under § 39-13-202; second degree murder under § 39-13-210; especially aggravated kidnapping under § 39-13-305; aggravated child abuse under § 39-15-402; especially aggravated robbery under § 39-13-403; commission of an act of terrorism under § 39-13-805; or a sexual offence for which the offender must register as a sexual offender or violent sexual offender under chapter 39, part 2 of title 40, or any sexual offence involving a minor. Codified through Public Chapter 608 and then amended by Public Chapter 719, effective 2026-04-14. Public Chapter 719 Section 1 deleted from § 40-32-107(d)(1) the language 'was convicted of a nonviolent crime if the person', and Section 2 deleted and substituted § 40-32-107(d)(1)(A), replacing an open-textured judicial finding that the offence was a nonviolent crime with a closed list of excluded felonies. Public Chapter 719 Section 3 rewrote § 40-32-108(d)(2). Confirmed from the enacted text and material to the design: subsection (d) contains no waiting period, no sentence-completion checklist, no no-prior-expunction bar and no requirement that the offence predate a conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence. Those conditions appear in subsections (b) and (c) but not in (d). Its three requirements at (d)(1)(A), (B) and (C) are cumulative and exhaustive: the judicial finding against the seven-item exclusion list, a positive vote from the board of parole to receive a pardon, and receipt of a pardon by the governor. The eligibility screen for this route must therefore not import the (a) or (c) conditions, which would wrongly refuse petitioners the statute admits. Public Chapter 719 Section 3 rewrote § 40-32-108(d)(2) so that the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety; the rebuttable presumption that the petition should be granted is preserved only for petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E). A subsection (d) petitioner therefore gets no presumption, and the court instead considers whether the offence sought to be expunged was violent and any other relevant factors presented by the petitioner and the district attorney general. Violence moved from a jurisdictional bar to a merits consideration.

Confirmed from the enacted text and material to the design: subsection (d) contains no waiting period, no sentence-completion checklist, no no-prior-expunction bar and no requirement that the offence predate a conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence. releaseBlockers.question: The prior-expunction bars across the T.C.A. § 40-32-107 subsections are asymmetric on the enacted text and the asymmetry cannot be resolved from it. Subsections (a), (b) and (c) each bar a petitioner previously granted expunction under (a), (b) or (c), and name neither (d) nor (e). Subsection (e)(1)(D) bars a petitioner previously granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e). Subsection (d) states no prior-expunction bar at all and is named by none of the others. AFFECTED TRACKS: tn_post_pardon, tn_recovery_court, tn_illegal_voting, tn_eligible_conviction and tn_two_offense. SCREENING IMPACT: the intake asks whether the participant has previously been granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e) and records the answer, but no screen infers a bar that the subsection under which the participant is applying does not state, and in particular no bar is inferred against or from subsection (d). CURRENT PACKET TREATMENT: the packet reports the participant's own answer and states which bars the governing subsection actually contains; it asserts no conclusion about a subsection that is silent, and it does not tell a participant that a route is closed on the strength of a bar the statute does not impose. REQUIRED FUTURE CLARIFICATION: a statutory amendment naming the subsections reciprocally, or a counsel determination on whether a prior (e) grant closes (a), (b) and (c) and on whether any prior grant closes (d). RUNTIME EFFECT: none. Every Tennessee route is runtime-disabled and none can be served to a participant, so the open question governs release readiness and screening copy rather than anything a participant can reach today.

provenance.sourceStatement: The prior-expunction bars across the § 40-32-107 subsections are asymmetric on the enacted text, and the asymmetry is reported rather than resolved because it cannot be resolved from the text. selfHelpStopConditions: The office of the district attorney general declines to prepare the petition, or indicates it will oppose. Self-help stops and the participant is handed off to an attorney; the participant keeps the generated request, the controlled factual record and the instructions.

Eligibility is disputed by the district attorney general's office. That is a contested determination for that office and, on filing, for the court; it is handed off to an attorney rather than argued in the packet.
Any other conviction anywhere on the record, including federal and out-of-state convictions that would be ineligible in Tennessee. Handed off to an attorney before anything is sent.

Any unpaid court costs, fines, restitution or other assessments, which mean the sentence is not complete. The participant is directed to the convicting court's clerk to resolve the balance before the route reopens.
Any borderline offence whose exact section cannot be matched against the current eligible list. Handed off to an attorney.
Federal, military, tribal or out-of-state records, immigration consequences and any security-clearance question, each of which is referred out because Tennessee expunction does not reach them.

Any case where the conviction may fall within one of the seven excluded felony categories, or within an attempt, conspiracy, facilitation or solicitation form of one. Handed off to an attorney rather than tested in the packet.

Any case where the violence question is genuinely contested. After Public Chapter 719 it is a merits factor the court weighs, and arguing it is individualized advocacy; the participant is handed off to an attorney.
Any participant who does not yet hold a pardon. The clemency application is a separate proceeding before the board of parole and the Governor and is referred out.

tracks.legalName: Expunction after completion of a certified recovery court programme following a prior DUI conviction, T.C.A. § 40-32-107(e) added by Public Chapter 1061, with procedure at § 40-32-108
tracks.publicName: Clear an eligible offence after finishing recovery court, where an old DUI is in the way
tracks.mechanism: Expunction of one otherwise-eligible offence, with the § 40-32-110 effect. It does not expunge the DUI. A person seeking expunction of an offence that is eligible for expunction under § 40-32-107(a)(1) and that occurred at least ten years after the person's conviction for an offence under T.C.A. § 55-10-401; who has fulfilled all requirements of the sentence for the offence being expunged, including payment of all fines, restitution, court costs and other assessments, completion of any term of imprisonment or probation, and meeting all conditions of supervised or unsupervised release; who has successfully completed a certified recovery court programme established under title 16; who has not previously been granted expunction under subsection (a), (b), (c) or (e); and who has not been convicted under § 55-10-401 more than one time. This is a relief-from-the-DUI-bar route, not a DUI-expunction route, and reading it the other way would be the single most damaging error available on it. A DUI under § 55-10-401 is itself expunction-ineligible and appears in the § 40-32-107(a)(1)(D) misdemeanour exclusion list, and § 40-32-107(e)(3) provides that a court shall not grant an expunction under the subsection if the offence sought to be expunged involves a motor vehicle and the use of alcohol or a controlled substance, including but not limited to a violation of § 55-10-401. What subsection (e) does is let a person who carries one DUI conviction expunge a different, otherwise-eligible offence committed at least ten years after it — relief that § 40-32-107(a)(3)(A) would otherwise deny, because that provision requires the offence to have occurred prior to any conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence. Added in its entirety by Public Chapter 1061, the Recovery Court Renewal Act, SB1232 / HB1346, effective 2026-07-01. Public Chapter 1061 Section 3 provides that the act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it, and — unlike Public Chapter 930 — imposes no offence-date limitation, so it applies on its effective date to qualifying petitioners regardless of when the offence was committed. Subsection (e) is not named in the § 40-32-108(d)(2) rebuttable presumption, which reaches only petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E), and it is not reached by the violence-weighing sentence Public Chapter 719 added for subsection (d) petitioners. An (e) petitioner therefore falls into the bare default: the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety.
exclusions: The DUI itself. Subsection (e)(3) provides that a court shall not grant an expunction under the subsection if the offence sought to be expunged involves a motor vehicle and the use of alcohol or a controlled substance, including but not limited to a violation of T.C.A. § 55-10-401. This route does not expunge a DUI and must never be described as doing so.
Any offence sought to be expunged that involves a motor vehicle and the use of alcohol or a controlled substance, which is an absolute bar under (e)(3) even where every other condition is met.
Any offence that is not itself eligible for expunction under T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a)(1), which subsection (e)(1)(A)(i) independently requires.
Any offence that did not occur at least ten years after the person's conviction for an offence under T.C.A. § 55-10-401.
A person convicted under T.C.A. § 55-10-401 more than one time, under (e)(1)(E).
A person who has not successfully completed a certified recovery court programme established under title 16.

Any case where a sentence requirement for the offence being expunged remains unfulfilled, including any unpaid fine, restitution amount, court cost or other assessment, any uncompleted term of imprisonment or probation, or any unmet condition of supervised or unsupervised release.
A person previously granted expunction under T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a), (b), (c) or (e), under (e)(1)(D).

waitingPeriods.duration: The offence being expunged must have occurred at least ten years after the person's conviction for an offence under T.C.A. § 55-10-401. This is an interval between two events rather than a wait from sentence completion.

All requirements of the sentence for the offence being expunged must be fulfilled: every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment paid, any term of imprisonment or probation completed, and all conditions of supervised or unsupervised release met.
Successful completion of a certified recovery court programme established under title 16.
The court may not order sooner than 61 days after the petition is served on the district attorney general, who has 60 days to submit recommendations.
No further petition for at least two years from the date of the denial, under § 40-32-108(d)(3).

tracks.venue: The convicting court, under § 40-32-108(a). The request goes to the district attorney general for that judicial district. A person with convictions in more than one judicial district deals with each separately.

destination.name: The office of the district attorney general for the judicial district of the convicting court, then the clerk of that court
destination.detail: Once the district attorney general's office prepares the petition and proposed order, the petitioner files them with the clerk of the convicting court under § 40-32-108(a) and pays the clerk's fee under T.C.A. § 8-21-401. The generated artifact on this route is the participant's own controlled written request to the office of the district attorney general, together with the participant's controlled eligibility record. It is not the statutory petition and it is not the proposed order: T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e) requires both of those to be prepared by the office of the district attorney general and given to the petitioner to be filed with the clerk. LegalEase does not draft, complete, sign or hold out either instrument as its own, and does not make the district attorney general's legal determination.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain TBI criminal history. Order the TBI criminal history first. It supplies the state control number referenced in T.C.A. § 8-4-115, without which the order cannot be completed, and it establishes the no-other-conviction position. LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates it.

What document evidences it and which body issues it was not established from the adopted authority chain, so the participant should ask the recovery court what it issues.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The recovery court that certified the programme

Obtain The judgment for the T.C.A. § 55-10-401 conviction. Ask that clerk for the judgment. It fixes the date the ten-year interval runs from and shows whether there is more than one such conviction.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that entered the DUI conviction

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "What is the date of that DUI conviction? The ten-year interval runs from it." against The judgment for the T.C.A. § 55-10-401 conviction, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Obtain Proof that every sentence requirement for the offence being expunged is fulfilled. Ask the clerk for a current balance and for confirmation that probation or supervision was completed.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the convicting court, and any agency holding restitution or costs

The state control number referenced in T.C.A. § 8-4-115 — Participant request and eligibility record, the identifying block.

Subsection (e) is not named in the § 40-32-108(d)(2) rebuttable presumption, which reaches only petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E), and it is not reached by the violence-weighing sentence Public Chapter 719 added for subsection (d) petitioners. An (e) petitioner therefore falls into the bare default: the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety.

scopeRestrictions: LegalEase does not obtain the district attorney general's agreement, does not negotiate with that office, does not prepare or sign its petition or proposed order, does not create the TBI certificate or the TBI expungement order, does not create a clerk certification, makes no judicial finding, certifies no eligibility and promises neither filing nor relief. Refusal, opposition or disputed eligibility routes to an attorney handoff, and the participant still receives the generated request, the controlled factual record and the instructions before that handoff.

This is a relief-from-the-DUI-bar route, not a DUI-expunction route, and reading it the other way would be the single most damaging error available on it. A DUI under § 55-10-401 is itself expunction-ineligible and appears in the § 40-32-107(a)(1)(D) misdemeanour exclusion list, and § 40-32-107(e)(3) provides that a court shall not grant an expunction under the subsection if the offence sought to be expunged involves a motor vehicle and the use of alcohol or a controlled substance, including but not limited to a violation of § 55-10-401. What subsection (e) does is let a person who carries one DUI conviction expunge a different, otherwise-eligible offence committed at least ten years after it — relief that § 40-32-107(a)(3)(A) would otherwise deny, because that provision requires the offence to have occurred prior to any conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence.

releaseBlockers.question: The prior-expunction bars across the T.C.A. § 40-32-107 subsections are asymmetric on the enacted text and the asymmetry cannot be resolved from it. Subsections (a), (b) and (c) each bar a petitioner previously granted expunction under (a), (b) or (c), and name neither (d) nor (e). Subsection (e)(1)(D) bars a petitioner previously granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e). Subsection (d) states no prior-expunction bar at all and is named by none of the others. AFFECTED TRACKS: tn_recovery_court, tn_post_pardon, tn_illegal_voting, tn_eligible_conviction and tn_two_offense. SCREENING IMPACT: the intake asks whether the participant has previously been granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e) and records the answer, but no screen infers a bar that the subsection under which the participant is applying does not state, and in particular no bar is inferred against or from subsection (d). CURRENT PACKET TREATMENT: the packet reports the participant's own answer and states which bars the governing subsection actually contains; it asserts no conclusion about a subsection that is silent, and it does not tell a participant that a route is closed on the strength of a bar the statute does not impose. REQUIRED FUTURE CLARIFICATION: a statutory amendment naming the subsections reciprocally, or a counsel determination on whether a prior (e) grant closes (a), (b) and (c) and on whether any prior grant closes (d). RUNTIME EFFECT: none. Every Tennessee route is runtime-disabled and none can be served to a participant, so the open question governs release readiness and screening copy rather than anything a participant can reach today.

Subsection (d) is outside every bar in both directions. This is carried as a release blocker on Routes 2 and 3 and on the two existing conviction tracks, and no screening question asserts a conclusion about it.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: This is a relief-from-the-DUI-bar route, not a DUI-expunction route, and reading it the other way would be the single most damaging error available on it. A DUI under § 55-10-401 is itself expunction-ineligible and appears in the § 40-32-107(a)(1)(D) misdemeanour exclusion list, and § 40-32-107(e)(3) provides that a court shall not grant an expunction under the subsection if the offence sought to be expunged involves a motor vehicle and the use of alcohol or a controlled substance, including but not limited to a violation of § 55-10-401. What subsection (e) does is let a person who carries one DUI conviction expunge a different, otherwise-eligible offence committed at least ten years after it — relief that § 40-32-107(a)(3)(A) would otherwise deny, because that provision requires the offence to have occurred prior to any conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence.

Open question blocks release (eligibility_branch): The prior-expunction bars across the T.C.A. § 40-32-107 subsections are asymmetric on the enacted text and the asymmetry cannot be resolved from it. SCREENING IMPACT: the intake asks whether the participant has previously been granted expunction under (a), (b), (c) or (e) and records the answer, but no screen infers a bar that the subsection under which the participant is applying does not state, and in particular no bar is inferred against or from subsection (d). tracks.legalName: Expunction where no charge was filed, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. arts. 55A.051 and 55A.052
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest where charges were never filed
tracks.mechanism: Texas says expunction, not expungement, and the filing is an ex parte petition by a petitioner. Chapter 55A was enacted by H.B. 4504 of the 88th Legislature as a nonsubstantive revision effective 2025-01-01, replacing repealed Chapter 55, and was amended by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01. Under art. 55A.052 a person arrested for a felony or misdemeanour is entitled to expunction where no indictment or information was ever presented, once the applicable period has run — 180 days for a Class C misdemeanour arrest with no felony from the same transaction, one year for a Class A or B misdemeanour arrest on the same condition, three years for a felony arrest or where a felony charge arose from the same transaction — or where the attorney representing the state certifies the records are not needed for any criminal investigation or prosecution. Entitlement exists regardless of whether a limitations period exists or has expired, under art. 55A.052(b). The art. 55A.051 threshold applies throughout: released, no final conviction, no charge pending, and no Chapter 42A community supervision other than for a Class C misdemeanour. Relief is mandatory: if the court finds entitlement it shall enter the order.
exclusions: A final conviction for the offence.
Court-ordered community supervision under Chapter 42A other than for a Class C misdemeanour.
A charge still pending.
An arrest made on a community-supervision violation warrant issued under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
A person who intentionally or knowingly absconded from the jurisdiction after release under Chapter 17, who is ineligible under art. 55A.154.
Driver's licence suspension or revocation records, which under art. 55A.152 may be expunged only through Transportation Code 524.015 or 724.048.

tracks.venue: Statewide in scope with county-level filing. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

destination.detail: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

participantActionRequired.description: The clerk sends the petition and notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested, or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax. A state or local agency with a listed e-mail address must accept electronic service. The participant does not serve in the ordinary case; a certificate of service is included only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly.

An ex parte petition, verified, filed with the district clerk of the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, through eFileTexas, in person, or by mail where the clerk allows. The matter is a new civil action and receives a new cause number. Justice court or municipal court of record is available under art. 55A.252 only where the arrest was for a fine-only offence.

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

Where entitlement rests on the expiry of an art. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) period without prosecutor certification, art. 55A.302(c) requires the court to allow the law enforcement agency and the prosecutor to retain the records. tracks.legalName: Expunction where the charge was dismissed or quashed, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. arts. 55A.051 and 55A.053
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest where the charge was dismissed
tracks.mechanism: Where an indictment or information was presented and then dismissed or quashed, expunction is available if the court finds the dismissal or quashal was because the person completed a veterans treatment court programme under Government Code Chapter 124, completed a mental health court programme under Chapter 125, completed a pretrial intervention programme authorised under Government Code 76.011, the presentment was made because of mistake, false information or another similar reason indicating absence of probable cause at the time of dismissal, or the charging instrument was void. Entitlement does not depend on any limitations period, under art. 55A.053(d). A person may receive only one expunction on the veterans court ground and only one on the mental health court ground, and must file an affidavit attesting to that fact. Relief is mandatory on the findings, but the court must make the finding about why the case was dismissed, which is a real evidentiary burden: a dismissal order that simply says dismissed establishes no statutory ground.
exclusions: A dismissal whose stated reason is not one of the five art. 55A.053(a)(2) grounds. Dismissed alone is not enough and the packet hard-stops where the reason is not documented.
A deferred adjudication that ended in discharge and dismissal, which is not a dismissal for these purposes except for certain Class C matters and is the most common misrouting in Texas.
An informal county diversion programme that was not authorised under Government Code 76.011.
A second expunction on the veterans treatment court ground, or a second on the mental health court ground.
The art. 55A.051 threshold conditions, and the art. 55A.153 probation-violation-warrant bar.

waitingPeriods.duration: None stated in art. 55A.053, and entitlement does not depend on any limitations period under art. 55A.053(d).

Where entitlement would otherwise rest on the expiry of an art. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) period without prosecutor certification, art. 55A.302(c) requires records retention, so waiting for limitations to run can change what the participant actually gets.
Set not earlier than the 30th day following the date the petition is filed.

Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

participantFilingRequirements.name: Texas DPS criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

tracks.legalName: Expunction where the limitations period has expired, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. arts. 55A.051 and 55A.054
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest the State can no longer prosecute
tracks.mechanism: Where prosecution is no longer possible because the limitations period has expired, expunction is mandatory on the art. 55A.051 threshold conditions. The applicable criminal limitations period varies by offence and is set outside Chapter 55A. Article 55A.154 expressly makes a person who intentionally or knowingly absconded from the jurisdiction after release under Chapter 17 ineligible under art. 55A.054.
exclusions: Any offence for which the limitations period has not expired, or has been tolled.
A person who intentionally or knowingly absconded from the jurisdiction after release under Chapter 17, expressly ineligible under art. 55A.154.

waitingPeriods.duration: The applicable criminal limitations period for the offence, which varies by offence and is set outside Chapter 55A. Tolling can extend it.

tracks.venue: Statewide in scope with county-level filing. An ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred (art. 55A.251) — not the county of residence. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

destination.name: A district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, filed through the district clerk
destination.detail: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

participantFilingRequirements.name: Texas DPS criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.
participantQuestions: District clerk publishes the agency and e-mail list under 55A.253(c).
scopeRestrictions: TexasLawHelp forms carry non-commercial site terms and may not be filled and delivered inside a paid product. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 that texaslawhelp.org is operated by the Texas Legal Services Center as a legal-aid self-help site and that its expunction forms are neither promulgated nor mandatory nor statewide court forms. The Texas Justice Court Training Center forms are training aids for justice and municipal courts published by Texas State University, likewise not statewide court forms. County and district clerk packets are local only. LegalEase drafts its own petition and order to arts. 55A.253 and 55A.301 and uses none of these as a form.

provenance.sourceHeading: 2.1 Chapter 55A expunction: no mandatory statewide form
provenance.sourceStatement: Finding: Texas has no mandatory or statewide-approved expunction petition form. The Texas State Law Library states that Texas has very few official legal forms and that official forms, where they exist, appear on the court or clerk website. Article 55A.253 prescribes the contents of the petition instead. Consequence: expunction is a custom_pleading jurisdiction. Do not classify it as official_pdf_fill merely because unofficial fillable PDFs circulate.

tracks.legalName: Expunction after trial court acquittal, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. arts. 55A.002 and 55A.201
tracks.publicName: Clear a record after being found not guilty
tracks.mechanism: A person tried and acquitted by the trial court is entitled to expunction. Under art. 55A.201 the order shall be entered not later than the 30th day after the date of acquittal, on request of the acquitted person after notice to the state, or on request of the attorney representing the state with the person's consent. On acquittal the trial court shall advise the person of the right to expunction. The requesting party must provide the information required in an art. 55A.253 petition. The order is prepared by the acquitted person's attorney if the person was represented, otherwise by the attorney representing the state. Where the 30-day window has closed or the court did not act, the person falls back to an ordinary ex parte petition under art. 55A.251, which lists art. 55A.002 among the qualifying entitlements. Article 55A.151 bars relief where the acquitted offence arose out of a criminal episode as defined by Penal Code 3.01 and the person was convicted of, or remains subject to prosecution for, at least one other offence in that episode. Under art. 102.0061(c), read at source on 2026-08-06, the filing fee must be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal.
exclusions: An acquittal arising out of a criminal episode as defined by Penal Code 3.01 where the person was convicted of, or remains subject to prosecution for, at least one other offence in that episode. Article 55A.151 bars relief outright.
An acquittal by the Court of Criminal Appeals or a court of appeals, which is the discretionary art. 55A.101 route and is modelled separately.
A mixed-verdict multi-count case, which requires T.S.N. analysis and is not auto-generated.

waitingPeriods.duration: The order shall be entered not later than the 30th day after the date of acquittal. There is no waiting period; the constraint runs the other way.
No waiting period. The ordinary ex parte petition under art. 55A.251 remains available once the 30-day window has closed.
Article 102.0061(c) requires the fee to be waived where the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal and art. 55A.151 does not apply.

units.label: Request to the trial court within 30 days of acquittal, art. 55A.201
units.description: Applies where the acquittal is recent enough that the 30-day window is open. LegalEase generates a written request to the trial court under art. 55A.201, with notice to the state, together with the complete art. 55A.253 information package that art. 55A.201(c) requires the requesting party to provide, and the agency and entity list. LegalEase does not generate the order itself: art. 55A.201(d) assigns preparation to the acquitted person's attorney where the person was represented and otherwise to the attorney representing the state. The fee must be waived on this route under art. 102.0061(c) where art. 55A.151 does not apply, and the packet says so.

units.label: Ordinary ex parte petition where the window closed or the court did not act, art. 55A.251
units.description: Applies where the 30-day window has closed or the trial court did not enter the order. LegalEase generates the ordinary verified ex parte Petition for Expunction drafted to art. 55A.253 and the proposed Order of Expunction drafted to art. 55A.301, filed in a district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence. Article 55A.251 lists art. 55A.002 among the qualifying entitlements, so the fallback is a full petition route rather than a second request.

tracks.venue: In-window: the trial court if it is a district, justice or municipal court of record, or a district court in the county where the trial court sits (art. 55A.201(a)). Out-of-window: a district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence under art. 55A.251, or a justice or municipal court of record under art. 55A.252 for a fine-only arrest. Statewide across all 254 counties.

destination.name: The trial court within the window, otherwise a district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence
destination.detail: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable. On this track specifically, art. 102.0061(c) requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. selfHelpBoundaries: The state opposes the petition, or seeks retention of records under art. 55A.302.

The arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes. State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated.
A felony from the same transaction is present or arguable, which moves the wait to three years and can defeat the petition.
The applicable limitations period is contested, or the participant wants full rather than partial expunction and the limitations analysis is not clear.

There is any absconding or bail-jumping history. Article 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible under arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054, and a participant may not self-identify the fact.
The arrest may have been made on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
Venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence occurred in different counties.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
Any companion conviction or live charge from the same criminal episode, which art. 55A.151 makes an outright bar.
Any multi-count indictment with a mixed verdict.
The participant was represented at trial, in which case the trial attorney prepares the order on the in-window route.

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.
scopeRestrictions: TexasLawHelp forms carry non-commercial site terms and may not be filled and delivered inside a paid product. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 that texaslawhelp.org is operated by the Texas Legal Services Center as a legal-aid self-help site and that its expunction forms are neither promulgated nor mandatory nor statewide court forms. The Texas Justice Court Training Center forms are training aids for justice and municipal courts published by Texas State University, likewise not statewide court forms. County and district clerk packets are local only. LegalEase drafts its own petition and order to arts. 55A.253 and 55A.301 and uses none of these as a form.

Separately, whether the $25 per-non-electronic-entity charge applies twice for the same agency, once under art. 55A.254(f) and again under art. 55A.351(b-3), is supported by the text and unconfirmed in practice; it changes the participant's total by a multiple of the agency count.

tracks.publicName: Clear a conviction after a pardon for actual innocence
tracks.mechanism: A person tried, convicted and then pardoned or otherwise granted relief on the basis of actual innocence, where the pardon or order says so on its face, is entitled to expunction. The order is entered not later than the 30th day after the court receives notice of the pardon or grant of relief. Under art. 55A.204 the attorney representing the state prepares the order and must notify the Texas Department of Criminal Justice if the person is in custody, and art. 55A.205 prescribes the order's content including the agency listing and specific DPS and TDCJ index-deletion directives. Under art. 55A.202(b) the person provides the information required in an art. 55A.253 petition. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 that art. 55A.251 does not list art. 55A.003 among its petition grounds, though art. 55A.252 does for a fine-only offence, so for an ordinary case the automatic-entry route is the route.
exclusions: A pardon granted for a reason other than actual innocence, which is the art. 55A.004 route and is modelled separately.
A pardon or order that does not say on its face that it was granted on the basis of actual innocence.
The underlying clemency or habeas proceeding itself, which is outside scope.

waitingPeriods.duration: Not later than the 30th day after the court receives notice of the pardon or grant of relief. There is no participant waiting period.

tracks.venue: Statewide in scope with county-level filing. An ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred (art. 55A.251) — not the county of residence. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

destination.name: A district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, filed through the district clerk
destination.detail: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. selfHelpBoundaries: The state opposes the petition, or seeks retention of records under art. 55A.302.

The arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes. State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated.
A felony from the same transaction is present or arguable, which moves the wait to three years and can defeat the petition.
The applicable limitations period is contested, or the participant wants full rather than partial expunction and the limitations analysis is not clear.

There is any absconding or bail-jumping history. Article 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible under arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054, and a participant may not self-identify the fact.
The arrest may have been made on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
Venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence occurred in different counties.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
The pardon does not say on its face that it was granted on the basis of actual innocence.
