packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

scopeRestrictions: TexasLawHelp forms carry non-commercial site terms and may not be filled and delivered inside a paid product. The Texas Justice Court Training Center forms are training aids for justice and municipal courts published by Texas State University, likewise not statewide court forms. County and district clerk packets are local only. LegalEase drafts its own petition and order to arts. 55A.253 and 55A.301 and uses none of these as a form.

tracks.legalName: Expunction after a pardon granted for a reason other than actual innocence, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 55A.004
tracks.publicName: Clear a conviction after a pardon
tracks.mechanism: A person tried and convicted, then pardoned for a reason other than actual innocence, is entitled to expunction. This is a conviction-based expunction and it uses the ordinary ex parte petition route at art. 55A.251, or art. 55A.252 where the offence was fine-only. It does not use the art. 55A.202 automatic route, which covers only art. 55A.003 actual-innocence pardons. No waiting period is stated.
exclusions: A pardon granted on the basis of actual innocence, which is the art. 55A.003 route with its own automatic-entry procedure.
Anything short of a pardon. A commutation, a restoration of rights or a certificate is not a pardon for these purposes.
The art. 55A.051 threshold conditions where they apply.

waitingPeriods.duration: None stated in art. 55A.004.
Set not earlier than the 30th day following the date the petition is filed.

tracks.venue: Statewide in scope with county-level filing. An ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred (art. 55A.251) — not the county of residence. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

destination.name: A district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, filed through the district clerk
destination.detail: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.item: Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253 requires the petition to be verified. Both a notarial block and an unsworn declaration are provided; the participant executes whichever the county accepts.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

manualCompletionItems.item: Petition may not list an agency twice or list divisions separately (55A.253(b), 55A.256(c-1)).
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.

selfHelpBoundaries: The state opposes the petition, or seeks retention of records under art. 55A.302.

The arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes. State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated.
A felony from the same transaction is present or arguable, which moves the wait to three years and can defeat the petition.
The applicable limitations period is contested, or the participant wants full rather than partial expunction and the limitations analysis is not clear.

There is any absconding or bail-jumping history. Article 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible under arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054, and a participant may not self-identify the fact.
The arrest may have been made on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
Venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence occurred in different counties.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
The document is not a pardon, or its type cannot be confirmed.
packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.
participantQuestions: District clerk publishes the agency and e-mail list under 55A.253(c).
Confirm the pardon document type before generating. Volume on this track is low and a commutation or restoration of rights is not a pardon.
scopeRestrictions: TexasLawHelp forms carry non-commercial site terms and may not be filled and delivered inside a paid product. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 that texaslawhelp.org is operated by the Texas Legal Services Center as a legal-aid self-help site and that its expunction forms are neither promulgated nor mandatory nor statewide court forms. The Texas Justice Court Training Center forms are training aids for justice and municipal courts published by Texas State University, likewise not statewide court forms. County and district clerk packets are local only. LegalEase drafts its own petition and order to arts. 55A.253 and 55A.301 and uses none of these as a form.

provenance.sourceHeading: 2.1 Chapter 55A expunction: no mandatory statewide form
provenance.sourceStatement: Finding: Texas has no mandatory or statewide-approved expunction petition form. The Texas State Law Library states that Texas has very few official legal forms and that official forms, where they exist, appear on the court or clerk website. Article 55A.253 prescribes the contents of the petition instead. Consequence: expunction is a custom_pleading jurisdiction. Do not classify it as official_pdf_fill merely because unofficial fillable PDFs circulate.

Open question blocks release (participant_instructions): What an expunction petition costs to file today, county by county. Read at source on 2026-08-06: art. 102.0061 replaced the repealed art. 102.006 effective 2026-01-01 and sets the district-court fee as the ordinary civil filing fee for an ex parte petition, which varies by county and is not a flat statutory amount, plus a flat $100 in justice or municipal court. That resolves which provision governs but not the county figure. Separately, whether the $25 per-non-electronic-entity charge applies twice for the same agency, once under art. 55A.254(f) and again under art. 55A.351(b-3), is supported by the text and unconfirmed in practice; it changes the participant's total by a multiple of the agency count.

Harris, Dallas, Bexar, Tarrant and Travis practice should be pulled. This is a packet-formatting question on a known pleading, not a question about what the pleading must contain.

tracks.legalName: Expunction of a pre-2021 unlawful carrying of a handgun conviction, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 55A.005
tracks.publicName: Clear an old unlawful-carry conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person tried and convicted of an offence committed before 2021-09-01 under Penal Code 46.02(a), as that section existed before that date, is entitled to expunction. This is a mandatory expunction of a conviction arising from the 2021 permitless-carry change, and it runs on the ordinary ex parte petition route at art. 55A.251, or art. 55A.252 where the offence was fine-only. No waiting period is stated. It is missing from the internal reference and from the TexasLawHelp toolkit entirely, which is why a participant is unlikely to know it exists.
exclusions: An offence committed on or after 2021-09-01.
A conviction under a subsection of Penal Code 46.02 other than 46.02(a) as it existed before 2021-09-01.
Any conviction where the offence date and the statutory subsection cannot be confirmed from court records.

waitingPeriods.duration: None stated in art. 55A.005.
The offence must have been committed before 2021-09-01. This is an eligibility cut-off rather than a waiting period.
Set not earlier than the 30th day following the date the petition is filed.

tracks.venue: Statewide in scope with county-level filing. An ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred (art. 55A.251) — not the county of residence. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

destination.name: A district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, filed through the district clerk
destination.detail: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Ask for it by name. The clerk is not responsible for the list being complete, so it is a starting point rather than an answer, and every e-mail address on it saves the participant $25 per stage.

Obtain Court file and cause number from the county of arrest or prosecution. Ask the clerk for the court file and cause number. Some counties also want a certified disposition attached; ask when you call about the agency list.

The petitioner signs and the petition must be verified under art. 55A.253. Both a notarial verification block and an unsworn declaration under penalty of perjury are provided, and county practice chooses between them.

Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

selfHelpBoundaries: The state opposes the petition, or seeks retention of records under art. 55A.302.

The arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes. State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated.
A felony from the same transaction is present or arguable, which moves the wait to three years and can defeat the petition.
The applicable limitations period is contested, or the participant wants full rather than partial expunction and the limitations analysis is not clear.

There is any absconding or bail-jumping history. Article 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible under arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054, and a participant may not self-identify the fact.
The arrest may have been made on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
Venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence occurred in different counties.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
The offence date or the statutory subsection cannot be confirmed from court records.
packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.
Requires the conviction date and the pre-2021 statutory subsection to be confirmed from court records, not from the participant's memory.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

provenance.sourceHeading: 2.1 Chapter 55A expunction: no mandatory statewide form
provenance.sourceStatement: Finding: Texas has no mandatory or statewide-approved expunction petition form. The Texas State Law Library states that Texas has very few official legal forms and that official forms, where they exist, appear on the court or clerk website. Article 55A.253 prescribes the contents of the petition instead. Consequence: expunction is a custom_pleading jurisdiction. Do not classify it as official_pdf_fill merely because unofficial fillable PDFs circulate.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: TexasLawHelp forms carry non-commercial site terms and may not be filled and delivered inside a paid product. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 that texaslawhelp.org is operated by the Texas Legal Services Center as a legal-aid self-help site and that its expunction forms are neither promulgated nor mandatory nor statewide court forms. The Texas Justice Court Training Center forms are training aids for justice and municipal courts published by Texas State University, likewise not statewide court forms. County and district clerk packets are local only. LegalEase drafts its own petition and order to arts. 55A.253 and 55A.301 and uses none of these as a form.

tracks.legalName: Expunction on mistaken identity or identity theft, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. arts. 55A.006 and 55A.256
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest that was not yours
tracks.mechanism: Where a person was arrested solely because identifying information was inaccurate due to clerical error, or another arrested person falsely gave the applicant's identifying information without consent and that deception is the only reason the applicant's information is in the records, relief is available. Article 55A.006 operates notwithstanding the art. 55A.001 arrest requirement, so the applicant need not have been arrested at all. This is not a petition. The applicant files a verified application, including authenticated fingerprint records, with the attorney representing the state in the prosecution of felonies in the county where the applicant resides or where the offence was alleged to have occurred. Article 55A.256(b) prescribes the application's contents. After verifying the allegations the prosecutor supplements missing arrest information, forwards the application to the district court with the agency list attached, and requests the order, and the court enters a final order without a hearing. The effect differs from ordinary expunction: under art. 55A.354 agencies obliterate the applicant's identifying information and substitute the arrested person's information rather than returning or destroying the file, and index references are not deleted. The S.B. 1667 anti-duplication rules apply to the application under art. 55A.256(c-1).
exclusions: Any case where the applicant was in fact the arrested person.
Any case where the applicant's information is in the records for a reason other than the clerical error or the deception.
Any dispute about whether the applicant is the arrested person, which is outside self-help.

Ordinary expunction relief. Under art. 55A.354 the records are not returned or destroyed; the applicant's identifying information is obliterated and the arrested person's substituted, and index references remain.

tracks.venue: Statewide in scope with county-level filing. An ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred (art. 55A.251) — not the county of residence. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

destination.name: A district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, filed through the district clerk
destination.detail: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

selfHelpStopConditions: The state opposes the petition, or seeks retention of records under art. 55A.302.

The arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes. State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated.
A felony from the same transaction is present or arguable, which moves the wait to three years and can defeat the petition.
The applicable limitations period is contested, or the participant wants full rather than partial expunction and the limitations analysis is not clear.

There is any absconding or bail-jumping history. Article 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible under arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054, and a participant may not self-identify the fact.
The arrest may have been made on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
Venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence occurred in different counties.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
Any dispute about whether the applicant is in fact the arrested person.
The prosecutor declines to verify the application, which stops the matter before it reaches any court.
The applicant cannot obtain authenticated fingerprint records.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

provenance.sourceHeading: 2.1 Chapter 55A expunction: no mandatory statewide form
provenance.sourceStatement: Finding: Texas has no mandatory or statewide-approved expunction petition form. The Texas State Law Library states that Texas has very few official legal forms and that official forms, where they exist, appear on the court or clerk website. Article 55A.253 prescribes the contents of the petition instead. Consequence: expunction is a custom_pleading jurisdiction. Do not classify it as official_pdf_fill merely because unofficial fillable PDFs circulate.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: TexasLawHelp forms carry non-commercial site terms and may not be filled and delivered inside a paid product. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 that texaslawhelp.org is operated by the Texas Legal Services Center as a legal-aid self-help site and that its expunction forms are neither promulgated nor mandatory nor statewide court forms. The Texas Justice Court Training Center forms are training aids for justice and municipal courts published by Texas State University, likewise not statewide court forms. County and district clerk packets are local only. LegalEase drafts its own petition and order to arts. 55A.253 and 55A.301 and uses none of these as a form.

tracks.legalName: Streamlined expunction order after a specialty court dismissal, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 55A.203
tracks.publicName: Clear a case dismissed after a veterans or mental health court programme
tracks.mechanism: Where a case was dismissed following successful completion of a veterans treatment court programme under Government Code Chapter 124 or a mental health court programme under Chapter 125, a district court may, with the consent of the attorney representing the state, enter an expunction order not later than the 30th day after the dismissal or after it receives the dismissal information. Article 55A.203(c) forbids the court charging any fee or assessing any cost for such an order, and art. 102.0061(d) separately requires waiver of the district-court filing fee for an entitlement under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B). Article 55A.203(d), added by S.B. 1667, requires the person to provide the court with the information required in an art. 55A.253 petition. A person may receive only one expunction on each ground and must file an affidavit attesting to that fact. The prosecutor's consent makes the streamlined route discretionary in practice even though the underlying art. 55A.053 entitlement is mandatory; where consent is withheld or the window closes, the ordinary petition route under art. 55A.053 remains open, because the entitlement lives there rather than in art. 55A.203. Unlike art. 55A.201, art. 55A.203 is limited to district courts.
exclusions: A dismissal following anything other than a veterans treatment court programme under Government Code Chapter 124 or a mental health court programme under Chapter 125.
A second expunction on the same specialty-court ground. Each is available once, and the affidavit attests to it.
A court other than a district court. Article 55A.203 is limited to district courts, unlike art. 55A.201.
Any case where the attorney representing the state does not consent, which closes the streamlined route and sends the participant to the ordinary art. 55A.053 petition.

waitingPeriods.duration: Not later than the 30th day after the dismissal or after the court receives the dismissal information. There is no participant waiting period; the constraint is a window rather than a wait.
None. Article 55A.203(c) forbids any fee or cost for an order entered under the article, and art. 102.0061(d) requires waiver of the district-court filing fee on this entitlement.

tracks.venue: Statewide in scope with county-level filing. An ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred (art. 55A.251) — not the county of residence. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

destination.name: A district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, filed through the district clerk
destination.detail: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

releaseBlockers.question: What an expunction petition costs to file today, county by county. Read at source on 2026-08-06: art. 102.0061 replaced the repealed art. 102.006 effective 2026-01-01 and sets the district-court fee as the ordinary civil filing fee for an ex parte petition, which varies by county and is not a flat statutory amount, plus a flat $100 in justice or municipal court. That resolves which provision governs but not the county figure. Separately, whether the $25 per-non-electronic-entity charge applies twice for the same agency, once under art. 55A.254(f) and again under art. 55A.351(b-3), is supported by the text and unconfirmed in practice; it changes the participant's total by a multiple of the agency count.

tracks.legalName: Discretionary expunction on appellate acquittal or prosecutor recommendation, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 55A.101
tracks.publicName: Discretionary expunction: when the court may, but need not, clear a record
tracks.mechanism: A court may expunge where the person was convicted at trial and then acquitted by the Court of Criminal Appeals, or by a court of appeals once the period for granting discretionary review has expired, or where the office of the attorney representing the state authorised by law to prosecute the offence recommends the expunction to the court before the person is tried, whether or not a charging instrument was presented. Relief is discretionary: the court may expunge. A justice court or municipal court of record may act under the article only on fine-only arrests. Article 55A.151 bars relief where the acquitted offence arose out of a criminal episode in which the person was convicted of, or remains subject to prosecution for, another offence.
exclusions: A trial court acquittal, which is the mandatory art. 55A.002 route and is modelled separately.
An acquitted offence arising out of a criminal episode where the person was convicted of, or remains subject to prosecution for, another offence in that episode.
A justice court or municipal court of record acting on anything other than a fine-only arrest.
This track produces no packet. It is outside the current LegalEase self-help scope.

tracks.legalName: Automatic order of nondisclosure after deferred adjudication for a nonviolent misdemeanour, Tex. Gov't Code 411.072
tracks.publicName: Automatic sealing after deferred adjudication for a nonviolent misdemeanour
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Where a person receives a discharge and dismissal under art. 42A.111 after deferred adjudication community supervision for a misdemeanour, and satisfies Gov't Code 411.074, the court that placed the person on deferred adjudication shall issue an order of nondisclosure. The court itself determines whether the 411.074 requirements are satisfied. No petition exists and none is required: the participant's only obligations are to present to the court any evidence necessary to establish eligibility, and to pay a $28 fee to the clerk before the court issues the order. Section 411.0716(b) limits the section to a discharge and dismissal received on or after 2017-09-01. The court must issue at discharge and dismissal where that occurs on or after the 180th day after placement on deferred adjudication, and otherwise as soon as practicable on or after the 180th day. Section 411.072 is the only provision in either Texas scheme with no prosecutor role at all: no consent, no certification, no notice, no opportunity to be heard and no objection right, and the 411.0745(e) notice-and-hearing machinery applies only on receipt of a petition and so does not reach it. Where the court did not act, OCA publishes a model letter, expressly not a petition, that the person submits to the court presenting evidence of entitlement with the $28 fee. Section 411.072 was last amended in 2019 and was not touched in 2021, 2023, 2025 or 2026.
exclusions: A discharge and dismissal received before 2017-09-01, under Gov't Code 411.0716(b).
Fewer than 180 days served on deferred adjudication. The court cannot issue the order before the 180th day after placement.
A court affirmative finding under art. 42A.105(f) that automatic nondisclosure is not in the best interest of justice. Section 411.072(d) routes that person to the 411.0725 petition instead.
Felony deferred adjudication.
DWI under Penal Code 49.04, BWI under 49.06, or any misdemeanour under Penal Code Chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43, 46 or 71.
Any prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than a fine-only traffic offence. This section is for first-time offenders only.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

waitingPeriods.duration: The court cannot issue the order until the person has served a minimum of 180 days on deferred adjudication. The clock runs from placement on deferred adjudication, not from discharge.
At discharge and dismissal where that occurs on or after the 180th day after placement, and otherwise as soon as practicable on or after the 180th day. There is no post-discharge waiting period.
None as such.

units.label: The order the court owes automatically, and how to verify it issued
units.description: The ordinary path, and the one that must be checked before anything is sold. The court determines eligibility when it grants discharge and dismissal and issues the order without any petition. LegalEase confirms the discharge and dismissal date is on or after 2017-09-01, confirms 180 days were served on deferred adjudication, screens the offence exclusions and the first-time-offender condition, and directs the participant to pull their DPS criminal history to see whether the record is already sealed. If it is sealed, there is nothing to buy and nothing to file. Automating a petition here would be the single most expensive error available in Texas, because it would sell a paid petition packet to someone entitled to a free automatic order.

The participant submits it to the court that placed them on deferred adjudication, with the $28 fee under 411.072(c) or a Rule 145 Statement of Inability. OCA's own instructions state that a person eligible under 411.072 does not have to file a petition or pay filing fees.

generationRequirements.question: Which court sentenced you or placed you on community supervision? That is where this is filed — not the county where you were arrested.
What is the cause number?
What was the offence, and what level was it?
Were you placed on deferred adjudication, or were you convicted and placed on probation, or neither? Texas splits nearly every nondisclosure section on this line.
On what date did you complete everything the sentence or supervision required, including any confinement and all fines, costs and restitution?
Did the court ever make a finding that the offence involved family violence, or was family violence alleged anywhere in the case?
List every other conviction and every other deferred adjudication you have ever had, with dates, other than fine-only traffic offences.
Do you want to ask the court to waive the filing costs because you cannot afford them?

tracks.legalName: Order of nondisclosure after deferred adjudication, felonies and certain misdemeanours, Tex. Gov't Code 411.0725
tracks.publicName: Seal a record after completing deferred adjudication
tracks.mechanism: Deferred adjudication community supervision resulting in discharge and dismissal, where the person does not qualify under Gov't Code 411.072. Read at source on 2026-08-06 the waiting periods are: on the discharge and dismissal for a misdemeanour not listed in the section's subdivision (2); the second anniversary of discharge and dismissal for a misdemeanour under Penal Code Chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43 or 46; and the fifth anniversary of discharge and dismissal for a felony. Penal Code Chapter 71 is not on that list — it appears in the 411.072 automatic exclusions and in the 411.073 and 411.0735 offence exclusions. Unlike 411.072, a prior conviction or deferred adjudication does not by itself defeat eligibility under 411.0725(c), subject to the 411.074 bars. The court shall issue the order after notice to the state, an opportunity for a hearing, and a determination of entitlement and best interest of justice. Section 411.0725 was last amended in 2019 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.
exclusions: A person who qualifies under Gov't Code 411.072, which must be ruled out first because that route is automatic and nearly free.
DWI under Penal Code 49.04 or BWI under 49.06, which route to Gov't Code 411.0726.
A person who was convicted rather than placed on deferred adjudication.
A case where no discharge and dismissal was received.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

Gov't Code 411.0745(c) and (d) do direct OCA to prescribe and publish a form for petitions filed electronically or by mail, and every county and district clerk website must link to it, so these sit closer to a statutorily authorised statewide model than to a sample. Nothing in Subchapter E-1 makes the OCA form mandatory or forbids a differently drafted petition, and the packet does not assert that it is mandatory.

tracks.legalName: Order of nondisclosure after deferred adjudication for DWI or BWI, Tex. Gov't Code 411.0726
tracks.publicName: Seal a DWI or BWI record after completing deferred adjudication
tracks.mechanism: Class B misdemeanour DWI under Penal Code 49.04 or BWI under 49.06, placed on deferred adjudication and discharged and dismissed, with no art. 42A.105(f) affirmative finding, and never previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for another offence other than a fine-only traffic offence. The waiting period is the second anniversary of completion of deferred adjudication and discharge and dismissal. Section 411.0726(c) expressly requires the petition to include evidence that the person is entitled to file it. Under 411.0726(e) a court may not issue the order if the attorney representing the state presents evidence sufficient to the court demonstrating that the offence resulted in a motor vehicle collision involving another person, including a passenger in the vehicle operated by the person seeking the order. The section was last amended in 2023 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.
exclusions: Any offence other than Penal Code 49.04 DWI or 49.06 BWI.
A case with no deferred adjudication, or no discharge and dismissal.
Any prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than a fine-only traffic offence. This section is for first-time offenders only.
An offence that caused a motor vehicle accident involving another person, including a passenger, even without injury.
A person who held a commercial driver's licence or commercial learner's permit at the time, or whose alcohol concentration was 0.15 or more.
Punishment enhanced under Penal Code 49.09.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

waitingPeriods.duration: The second anniversary of completion of the deferred adjudication and the discharge and dismissal.
Required unless the state does not request one before the 45th day after receiving notice and the court finds entitlement and best interest of justice.

tracks.venue: Statewide in scope with court-level filing. The petition is filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, including deferred adjudication community supervision — not the county of arrest. This is the single biggest venue difference from expunction, and it matters because a person with both an expunction and a nondisclosure may be filing in two different courts.

generationRequirements.question: Which court sentenced you or placed you on community supervision? That is where this is filed — not the county where you were arrested.
What is the cause number?
What was the offence, and what level was it?
Were you placed on deferred adjudication, or were you convicted and placed on probation, or neither? Texas splits nearly every nondisclosure section on this line.
On what date did you complete everything the sentence or supervision required, including any confinement and all fines, costs and restitution?
Did the court ever make a finding that the offence involved family violence, or was family violence alleged anywhere in the case?
List every other conviction and every other deferred adjudication you have ever had, with dates, other than fine-only traffic offences.
Do you want to ask the court to waive the filing costs because you cannot afford them?
Did the offence result in a motor vehicle collision involving another person, including a passenger in the vehicle you were driving, even if nobody was hurt?
Was your alcohol concentration 0.15 or more?
Did you hold a commercial driver's licence or commercial learner's permit at the time?

tracks.legalName: Order of nondisclosure after successful completion of a veterans treatment court programme, Tex. Gov't Code 411.0727
tracks.publicName: Seal a record after completing veterans treatment court
tracks.mechanism: Successful completion of a veterans treatment court programme as defined by Government Code Chapter 124 or former law. The waiting period is the second anniversary of the date of successful completion, and a felony conviction at any time during those two years defeats it. Under 411.0727(e) the section is not available where entry into the programme arose from an offence involving operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated. A prior conviction for any offence on the section's own exclusion list also defeats it. Section 411.0727 was last amended in 2017 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026. The overlap with expunction is decisive and is routing logic rather than an optimisation: a veterans treatment court dismissal may also support expunction under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) with the streamlined 30-day order under art. 55A.203 and no fee, and expunction is the stronger remedy because it destroys rather than seals.
exclusions: Entry into the programme because of an offence involving operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated.

A prior conviction for any offence on the 411.0727 exclusion list, which includes first-degree criminal solicitation, murder, capital murder, aggravated kidnapping, trafficking of persons, indecency with a child under Penal Code 21.11(a)(1), sexual assault, aggravated sexual assault, first-degree injury to a child where the victim is a child, aggravated robbery, certain first-degree burglary with intent to commit an enumerated sexual felony, compelling prostitution, sexual performance by a child, certain enhanced Health and Safety Code Chapter 481 offences, certain 481.1123 offences, and any sexually violent offence as defined by Code of Criminal Procedure art. 62.001.
Conviction of a felony at any time during the two years following successful completion.

generationRequirements.question: Which court sentenced you or placed you on community supervision? That is where this is filed — not the county where you were arrested.
What is the cause number?
What was the offence, and what level was it?
Were you placed on deferred adjudication, or were you convicted and placed on probation, or neither? Texas splits nearly every nondisclosure section on this line.
On what date did you complete everything the sentence or supervision required, including any confinement and all fines, costs and restitution?
Did the court ever make a finding that the offence involved family violence, or was family violence alleged anywhere in the case?
List every other conviction and every other deferred adjudication you have ever had, with dates, other than fine-only traffic offences.
Do you want to ask the court to waive the filing costs because you cannot afford them?
Has the expunction route been checked first? A veterans court dismissal may qualify for expunction, which destroys the record rather than sealing it, on a 30-day streamlined order with no fee.
Did you enter the programme because of a driving while intoxicated offence? That closes this route.

packetInstructions: The OCA nondisclosure documents are statewide MODEL forms, not mandatory and not promulgated. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 from the Texas Judicial Branch nondisclosure forms page and from the document footers themselves, which read OCA MODEL PETITION and are dated February 2022, with the Overview dated February 2024. Gov't Code 411.0745(c) and (d) do direct OCA to prescribe and publish a form for petitions filed electronically or by mail, and every county and district clerk website must link to it, so these sit closer to a statutorily authorised statewide model than to a sample. Nothing in Subchapter E-1 makes the OCA form mandatory or forbids a differently drafted petition, and the packet does not assert that it is mandatory.
An order of nondisclosure applies to one offence. Multiple offences require multiple orders, and that is a cost and packet multiplier the participant must be told about before paying.

Nondisclosure seals rather than destroys. The record remains available to the criminal justice and noncriminal justice agencies listed in Gov't Code 411.0765, which include school districts, charter and private schools, education service centres and commercial transportation companies, and the person may not deny the matter in those contexts.
The engine must test the expunction route first and only fall back to 411.0727. Expunction is the stronger remedy and the overlap rule is mandatory routing logic, not an optimisation.

tracks.legalName: Order of nondisclosure after community supervision following a misdemeanour conviction, Tex. Gov't Code 411.073
tracks.publicName: Seal a misdemeanour conviction after successfully completing probation
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of a misdemeanour and placed on community supervision under a Chapter 42A provision other than Subchapter C — straight probation rather than deferred adjudication, including split sentences — who successfully completed it. The waiting period is immediate on completion of community supervision, except that a misdemeanour under Penal Code Chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43 or 46 waits until the second anniversary of completion. Completion means the full supervision period including any term of confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution. This is the ordinary route for a probated misdemeanour conviction and is probably the highest-volume conviction track in the state. Section 411.073 was last amended in 2017 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.
exclusions: Straight time served, or deferred adjudication. Those route to Gov't Code 411.0735 and 411.0725 respectively.
Community supervision that was revoked.
Failure to complete the supervision period, including any term of confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, other than a fine-only traffic offence, between placement on community supervision and expiration of any applicable waiting period.
Alcoholic Beverage Code 106.041, and Penal Code 49.04, 49.05, 49.06 and 49.065, and any offence under Penal Code Chapter 71.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

rules.fees: Under Gov't Code 411.0745(b) the petition must be accompanied by payment of a fee that generally applies to the filing of a civil case. tracks.legalName: Order of nondisclosure after community supervision following a DWI conviction, Tex. Gov't Code 411.0731
tracks.publicName: Seal a DWI conviction after successfully completing probation
tracks.mechanism: A conviction for DWI punishable as a Class B misdemeanour under Penal Code 49.04, other than an offence punishable under 49.04(d), followed by community supervision under a Chapter 42A provision other than Subchapter C which the person completed. The waiting period is the second anniversary of completing community supervision where the person successfully complied with a condition requiring an ignition interlock device for six months or longer, and otherwise the fifth anniversary. Section 411.0731(c) expressly requires the petition to include evidence that the person is entitled to file it. Under 411.0731(e) a court may not issue the order if the attorney representing the state presents evidence sufficient to the court demonstrating that the offence resulted in a motor vehicle collision involving another person, including a passenger. The person remains eligible if the court waived all or part of the fine and costs. The section was last amended in 2023 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.
exclusions: DWI as a Class A misdemeanour or higher, an offence punishable under Penal Code 49.04(d), or an alcohol concentration of 0.15 or more.
Deferred adjudication rather than post-conviction community supervision, which routes to Gov't Code 411.0726.

Community supervision that was revoked, or not completed including confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution. Waiver of all or part of the fine and costs by the court does not disqualify.
Any prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than a fine-only traffic offence. This section is for first-time offenders only.
An offence that resulted in a motor vehicle accident involving another person, including a passenger, even without injury.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

packetInstructions: The OCA nondisclosure documents are statewide MODEL forms, not mandatory and not promulgated. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 from the Texas Judicial Branch nondisclosure forms page and from the document footers themselves, which read OCA MODEL PETITION and are dated February 2022, with the Overview dated February 2024. Gov't Code 411.0745(c) and (d) do direct OCA to prescribe and publish a form for petitions filed electronically or by mail, and every county and district clerk website must link to it, so these sit closer to a statutorily authorised statewide model than to a sample. Nothing in Subchapter E-1 makes the OCA form mandatory or forbids a differently drafted petition, and the packet does not assert that it is mandatory.
An order of nondisclosure applies to one offence. Multiple offences require multiple orders, and that is a cost and packet multiplier the participant must be told about before paying.

Nondisclosure seals rather than destroys. The record remains available to the criminal justice and noncriminal justice agencies listed in Gov't Code 411.0765, which include school districts, charter and private schools, education service centres and commercial transportation companies, and the person may not deny the matter in those contexts.
The petition must include evidence showing entitlement to file. The section says so expressly, so the packet carries the supporting record rather than relying on the petition's assertions alone.
Interlock duration of six months or longer under 411.0731 and 411.0736 is a supporting document the participant obtains. The judgment and conditions of community supervision are what establish it.
participantQuestions: Nondisclosure venue is the sentencing court, not the county of arrest.

Accident-involving-another-person bar under 411.0726, 411.0731 and 411.0736 is a participant question with a hard stop. A court may not issue the order if the attorney representing the state presents evidence sufficient to the court that the offence resulted in a motor vehicle collision involving another person, including a passenger in the vehicle operated by the person seeking the order.
scopeRestrictions: TexasLawHelp forms carry non-commercial site terms and may not be filled and delivered inside a paid product. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 that texaslawhelp.org is operated by the Texas Legal Services Center as a legal-aid self-help site and that its expunction forms are neither promulgated nor mandatory nor statewide court forms. The Texas Justice Court Training Center forms are training aids for justice and municipal courts published by Texas State University, likewise not statewide court forms. County and district clerk packets are local only. LegalEase drafts its own petition and order to arts. 55A.253 and 55A.301 and uses none of these as a form.

tracks.legalName: Order of nondisclosure after a misdemeanour conviction without community supervision, Tex. Gov't Code 411.0735
tracks.publicName: Seal a misdemeanour conviction where you were not put on probation
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of a misdemeanour who was not placed on community supervision of any kind and whose sentence is complete, and who is not eligible under Gov't Code 411.073. The waiting period is the date of completion of the sentence where the misdemeanour was punishable by fine only, and otherwise the second anniversary of completion. Under 411.0735(c-1) the court may not issue the order if it determines the offence, other than a Penal Code 22.01 offence, was violent or sexual in nature — a conviction for assault under 22.01 may still qualify. Section 411.0735 was last amended in 2017 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.
exclusions: Felonies.
Alcoholic Beverage Code 106.041, Penal Code Chapter 71, and Penal Code 49.04, 49.05, 49.06 and 49.065.
A person who was placed on community supervision, including deferred adjudication.
A person who qualifies under Gov't Code 411.073, which must be ruled out first.
A sentence not completed, including any confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution.
An offence the court determines was violent or sexual in nature, other than a Penal Code 22.01 offence.
Any prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than a fine-only traffic offence. This section is for first-time offenders only.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

waitingPeriods.duration: Immediately on completion of the sentence.

tracks.venue: Statewide in scope with court-level filing. The petition is filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, including deferred adjudication community supervision — not the county of arrest. This is the single biggest venue difference from expunction, and it matters because a person with both an expunction and a nondisclosure may be filing in two different courts.

tracks.legalName: Order of nondisclosure after a DWI conviction without qualifying community supervision, Tex. Gov't Code 411.0736
tracks.publicName: Seal a DWI conviction where probation was revoked or never imposed
tracks.mechanism: A conviction under Penal Code 49.04 for DWI punishable as a Class B misdemeanour, other than an offence punishable under 49.04(d), where the person does not qualify under Gov't Code 411.0731 — typically because community supervision was revoked or none was imposed. The waiting period is the third anniversary of completing the sentence where the person successfully complied with a sentence condition requiring an ignition interlock device for six months or longer, and otherwise the fifth anniversary. Section 411.0736(c) expressly requires the petition to include evidence that the person is entitled to file it. Under 411.0736(e) a court may not issue the order if the attorney representing the state presents evidence sufficient to the court that the offence resulted in a motor vehicle collision involving another person, including a passenger, regardless of injury or death. Waiver of the fine and costs by the court does not disqualify. The section was last amended in 2023 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.
exclusions: Class A misdemeanour DWI or higher, an offence punishable under Penal Code 49.04(d), or an alcohol concentration of 0.15 or more.
A person who qualifies under Gov't Code 411.0731, which must be ruled out first.
A sentence not completed, including confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution. Waiver of the fine and costs by the court does not disqualify.
Any prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than a fine-only traffic offence.
A DWI that resulted in a motor vehicle accident involving another person, including a passenger, regardless of injury or death.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

generationRequirements.question: Which court sentenced you or placed you on community supervision? That is where this is filed — not the county where you were arrested.
What is the cause number?
What was the offence, and what level was it?
Were you placed on deferred adjudication, or were you convicted and placed on probation, or neither? Texas splits nearly every nondisclosure section on this line.
On what date did you complete everything the sentence or supervision required, including any confinement and all fines, costs and restitution?
Did the court ever make a finding that the offence involved family violence, or was family violence alleged anywhere in the case?
List every other conviction and every other deferred adjudication you have ever had, with dates, other than fine-only traffic offences.
Do you want to ask the court to waive the filing costs because you cannot afford them?
Did the offence result in a motor vehicle collision involving another person, including a passenger in the vehicle you were driving, even if nobody was hurt?
Were you required to have an ignition interlock device, and for how long? Six months or longer shortens the wait substantially.
Was your alcohol concentration 0.15 or more?

tracks.publicName: Seal a record after completing a veterans reemployment programme
tracks.mechanism: A misdemeanour for which the person was placed on community supervision, including deferred adjudication, who successfully completed all conditions and successfully completed a court-approved veterans reemployment programme under Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 42A, Subchapter H-1, after committing the offence, and who is a veteran of the United States Armed Forces including reserves, national guard or state guard. Read at source on 2026-08-06: the court shall enter the order after notice to the state and a hearing on whether issuance is in the best interest of justice, and the statute names no filing party — there is no petition requirement in the section. Under 411.0729(b) the section applies regardless of whether the defendant meets the other eligibility criteria in the subchapter, so the Gov't Code 411.074 basic conditions do not gate it. There is no waiting period. OCA nonetheless publishes a model petition and instructions for the section, because in practice courts may require a petition or may not hold the hearing. The section was last amended in 2019 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.

The OCA nondisclosure documents are statewide MODEL forms, not mandatory and not promulgated. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 from the Texas Judicial Branch nondisclosure forms page and from the document footers themselves, which read OCA MODEL PETITION and are dated February 2022, with the Overview dated February 2024. Gov't Code 411.0745(c) and (d) do direct OCA to prescribe and publish a form for petitions filed electronically or by mail, and every county and district clerk website must link to it, so these sit closer to a statutorily authorised statewide model than to a sample. Nothing in Subchapter E-1 makes the OCA form mandatory or forbids a differently drafted petition, and the packet does not assert that it is mandatory.
An order of nondisclosure applies to one offence. Multiple offences require multiple orders, and that is a cost and packet multiplier the participant must be told about before paying.

tracks.legalName: Automatic deletion of traffic offense records, Utah Code 77-40a-202
tracks.publicName: Utah deletes old traffic cases automatically
tracks.mechanism: The court deletes traffic offense records on its own initiative. A traffic offense means an infraction or class B or C misdemeanour under Title 41 Chapter 6a, Title 53 Chapter 3 Part 2 and Title 73 Chapter 18, plus substantially similar local ordinances. Title 41 Chapter 6a Part 5, driving under the influence and reckless driving, and Sections 73-18-13 through 73-18-13.6 are expressly not traffic offenses, so DUI is not a traffic offense in Utah. Deletion follows an acquittal on all charges, a dismissal with prejudice other than one resulting from successful completion of a plea in abeyance, or adjudication plus five years for class C misdemeanours and infractions or six years for class B misdemeanours. Where the qualifying event occurred on or after 2020-05-01 the court deletes on identification; where it occurred before that date the court deletes within one year of identification. The court deletes and BCI neither receives nor indexes expunged traffic offenses, so traffic expungement enquiries go to the court rather than to BCI. The duty is mandatory.
exclusions: Driving under the influence and reckless driving under Title 41 Chapter 6a Part 5, and the boating equivalents at Sections 73-18-13 through 73-18-13.6, together with substantially similar local ordinances. DUI is not a traffic offense in Utah.
A dismissal with prejudice resulting from successful completion of a plea in abeyance.
Offences above class B misdemeanour, which fall outside the traffic offense definition entirely.
