tracks.legalName: Automatic expungement after acquittal or dismissal with prejudice, Utah Code 77-40a-206
tracks.publicName: Utah clears acquittals and dismissals automatically
tracks.mechanism: Where a person is acquitted on all charges the court expunges the case 60 days after the acquittal. Where the case is dismissed with prejudice the court expunges 180 days after the day of dismissal if no appeal was filed, or after a final non-appealable order if one was. A case dismissed with prejudice as a result of successful completion of a plea in abeyance agreement is excluded, as is a case in which the person was found not guilty by reason of insanity. Since 2026-01-01 the identification duty at 77-40a-204(3) puts the work on the court's own initiative and form 1200EX is retired. The duty is mandatory once the case is identified. Section 77-40a-204 does not preclude filing a petition for a case that is eligible for automatic expungement where the automatic expungement has not occurred, which is what makes the petition tracks a genuine fallback rather than a duplicate.
exclusions: A case dismissed with prejudice as a result of successful completion of a plea in abeyance agreement.
A case in which the person was found not guilty by reason of insanity.
A dismissal without prejudice, which is not within 77-40a-206 at all and routes to UT-PET-03.
This track offers no participant filing. Where the automatic expungement has not occurred, the fallback is the UT-PET-02 or UT-PET-04 petition.

tracks.legalName: Clean Slate automatic expungement of convictions, Utah Code 77-40a-205
tracks.publicName: Utah's Clean Slate: some convictions clear themselves
tracks.mechanism: Every conviction in the case must be a misdemeanour for possession of a controlled substance under Subsection 58-37-8(2)(a)(i), a class B misdemeanour, a class C misdemeanour, or an infraction. The waiting periods run from the day the individual is adjudicated: five years for class C misdemeanours and infractions, six years for class B misdemeanours, and seven years for class A misdemeanour possession of a controlled substance under 58-37-8(2)(a)(i). The prosecuting agency receives notice and may object; if 35 days pass without a written objection the court proceeds. Since 2026-01-01 the court identifies eligible cases on its own initiative under 77-40a-204(3), and form 1200EX is retired. For cases adjudicated on or after 2020-05-01 that are not traffic offenses the target is expungement within 30 days of the court determining requirements are satisfied; for cases adjudicated or dismissed before that date, within one year of identification. In practice the process can take up to 120 days because the court runs the job monthly and must allow the objection window.
exclusions: A pending misdemeanour or felony proceeding.
Incarceration, probation or parole as of 2025-01-01 for an individual seeking automatic expungement on and after that date.
A not-guilty-by-reason-of-insanity finding.
Unsatisfied state debt, or a criminal accounts receivable entered as a civil judgment and transferred to the Office of State Debt Collection.
Conviction counts exceeding the 77-40a-303(4) or (5) limits.

Any plea in abeyance or conviction for a felony; a class A misdemeanour other than drug possession; a capital felony; a first degree felony; a violent felony under 76-3-203.5(1)(c)(i); felony DUI; a registerable sex offence; a registerable child abuse offence; an offence against a person under Title 76 Chapter 5; a weapons offence under Title 76 Chapter 10 Part 5; sexual battery; lewdness; DUI or reckless driving; damage to or interruption of a communication device; or domestic violence.
This track offers no participant filing. Where the case is not eligible, or the wait has not run, the paid petition tracks are the alternative.

releaseBlockers.question: Resolved on 2026-08-06 and recorded rather than carried as open. S.B. 303 of the 2026 General Session failed: the House struck its enacting clause on 2026-03-06 and it does not appear in the passed-bills table. Its substance nevertheless became law through H.B. 110, 6th Substitute, Chapter 452 of the 2026 General Session, which amended 77-40a-303 effective 2026-05-06 to add civil protective orders to the certificate bars and to broaden the bar to any qualifying order against the petitioner. Two further 2026 acts touch the chapter: Chapter 291 (S.B. 323, 1st Substitute) amended 77-40a-101 and 77-40a-403 effective 2026-07-01, and Chapter 362 (H.B. 301, 1st Substitute) amended 77-40a-205 effective 2026-05-06. What remains open is the section-by-section effect of Chapter 291 on the 77-40a-101 definitions, which the eligibility branch depends on and which was not diffed.

provenance.sourceStatement: Did S.B. 303 (2026) pass? ... The last recorded action found was 2026-03-03, first reading in House Rules, and no enactment was located. releaseBlockers.question: Sections 77-40a-205(1)(a) and 77-40a-206(1)(a) still condition the court's automatic expungement order on the individual having submitted a form on and after 2024-10-01 but before 2026-01-01, and those conditions were not conformed to the 77-40a-204(3) cutover under which the court identifies eligible cases on its own initiative on and after 2026-01-01. selfHelpStopConditions: The prosecuting agency objects to a clean slate expungement.
The case meets every published criterion but has not been expunged well past the timeline, including the practical 120-day allowance.
The conviction count is anywhere near the 77-40a-303(4) or (5) limits, which run on total criminal history across all states including previously expunged cases.
There is an unsatisfied state debt or a transferred criminal accounts receivable and the participant cannot establish whether it is cleared.
The participant is not a US citizen and is asking about the consequences of clearing a record.

tracks.legalName: Expungement of an arrest where no charges were filed, Utah Code 77-40a-302(1)
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest where you were never charged
tracks.mechanism: Where a person was arrested or charged and the prosecutor made a final decision not to file charges, the arrest, investigation and detention records may be expunged on petition, at least 30 days after the arrest, on a certificate of eligibility from BCI. Because no case exists, venue is the district court in the county where the arrest occurred. The petition, the proposed order and the certificate are filed together; the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney, who has 35 days to respond, and the court waits 60 days before acting.
exclusions: Any case in which charges were in fact filed, which routes to the dismissal or acquittal tracks instead.
A case where the prosecutor has not made a final decision, as distinct from one merely not yet charged.
An unfinished case. Nothing is available on any petition track while the case is still open.
Unpaid fines, fees, restitution or interest on the case.
A pending criminal case other than a traffic case.
Current incarceration, probation or parole.
A civil protective order, a criminal protective order or a criminal stalking injunction against the petitioner that is in effect, whether or not it relates to the case being cleared.

waitingPeriods.duration: At least 30 days since the arrest.
Valid 180 days from issuance and must be valid on the filing date.
60 days, to allow the prosecutor 35 days and the victim 60 days to respond.

units.label: Stage one: BCI application for a certificate of eligibility
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History, and the BCI Third Party Release where the certificate is to be sent to someone other than the petitioner, together with the fee waiver request where one is asked for. The participant submits the application to the Bureau of Criminal Identification with the application fee. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases, may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction, and then issues a certificate of eligibility, offers a special certificate, or denies. LegalEase does not determine eligibility and does not assert that BCI will issue.

units.label: Stage two: expungement petition in the district court where the arrest occurred
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the statewide Utah Courts packet: civil cover sheet 1044XX, petition 1000EX, proposed order 1020EX complete but for the judge's signature, and the Acceptance of Service 1146XX and Consent and Waiver of Hearing 1148XX. The participant files the packet with the certificate of eligibility attached, within the certificate's 180-day life, in the court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

tracks.venue: The court that decided the criminal case, district or justice court. If that court no longer exists, the court that would have jurisdiction if the case were filed today. If charges were never filed, the district court in the county where the arrest occurred, or for a traffic matter, the court where the citation was received.

destination.name: Stage one, the Utah DPS Bureau of Criminal Identification; stage two, the court that decided the case
destination.detail: Two destinations in a fixed legal sequence. The participant first applies to BCI, which decides eligibility and issues a certificate valid for 180 days. The participant then files the expungement petition, with the certificate attached and still valid, in the district or justice court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

components.conditionDescription: Only where the certificate is to be sent to someone other than the petitioner, such as a clinic or partner organisation.

Where a victim or prosecutor statement is filed and the petitioner wishes to respond within 14 days.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certificate of eligibility issued by BCI. Submit the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History with the application fee, or with a fee waiver request. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases and may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction. If eligible, BCI issues the certificate on payment of the issuance fee. File the court packet within 180 days of issuance.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Utah Department of Public Safety, Bureau of Criminal Identification

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "If BCI has already issued your certificate of eligibility, what date did it issue? It is valid for 180 days and must still be valid on the day you file." against Certificate of eligibility issued by BCI, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a current balance on the case, and check with the Office of State Debt Collection if any balance was entered as a civil judgment and transferred. An unpaid balance defeats the petition and will also defeat the BCI certificate.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that handled the case, and the Office of State Debt Collection where a criminal accounts receivable was transferred

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have all fines, fees, interest and restitution on this case been paid in full?" against Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The participant's own case history for every case in every state, including previously expunged cases. Assemble the full list before applying to BCI. BCI assesses eligibility against total criminal history in all states, including cases that were previously expunged, so an incomplete list produces a denial rather than a certificate.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Court clerks in each jurisdiction and state criminal history repositories

The packet is the civil cover sheet, the petition, the proposed order and the BCI certificate of eligibility, with the filing fee or a fee waiver request. rules.notice: The court sends a copy of the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The prosecutor has 35 days to file an objection or statement, including on a victim's behalf; the victim has 60 days. The court must wait 60 days from filing before acting. The petitioner may reply to a prosecutor or victim statement within 14 days of receiving it. The court may order Adult Probation and Parole to file a written response, which AP&P serves on the petitioner, the prosecutor and the victim, and to which the petitioner may reply within 14 days.

Utah says expungement, but under 77-40a-101 to expunge means to seal or otherwise restrict access to the record held by an agency. It is not destruction, and BCI retains an expungement file released only on court order. Two things changed from the text the controlling review worked from: civil protective orders were added, and the scope broadened from an order in effect for the case to any such order against the petitioner. An unrelated protective order now bars a certificate, and the screening question is asked accordingly.

tracks.legalName: Expungement of a case dismissed with prejudice, Utah Code 77-40a-302(1)
tracks.publicName: Clear a case that was dismissed for good
tracks.mechanism: A case dismissed with prejudice may be expunged on petition at least 30 days after the arrest, on a certificate of eligibility from BCI. The same disposition is separately eligible for automatic expungement 180 days after dismissal under 77-40a-206, so the petition is the faster paid route to the same result and the free route must be disclosed before payment. Where the case came through a plea in abeyance, the case must actually have been dismissed; in some courts a Motion to Dismiss must be filed first using the general motions forms, which is a prerequisite step outside the expungement packet.
exclusions: A dismissal without prejudice, which routes to UT-PET-03 and carries different conditions.
A plea in abeyance that has not yet resulted in an actual dismissal. The dismissal must exist before this track opens.
An unfinished case. Nothing is available on any petition track while the case is still open.
Unpaid fines, fees, restitution or interest on the case.
A pending criminal case other than a traffic case.
Current incarceration, probation or parole.
A civil protective order, a criminal protective order or a criminal stalking injunction against the petitioner that is in effect, whether or not it relates to the case being cleared.

waitingPeriods.duration: At least 30 days since the arrest.
Automatic expungement under 77-40a-206 occurs 180 days after the dismissal where no appeal was filed. The petition is the faster paid route.
Valid 180 days from issuance and must be valid on the filing date.
60 days, to allow the prosecutor 35 days and the victim 60 days to respond.

units.label: Stage one: BCI application for a certificate of eligibility
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History, and the BCI Third Party Release where the certificate is to be sent to someone other than the petitioner, together with the fee waiver request where one is asked for. The participant submits the application to the Bureau of Criminal Identification with the application fee. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases, may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction, and then issues a certificate of eligibility, offers a special certificate, or denies. LegalEase does not determine eligibility and does not assert that BCI will issue.

units.label: Stage two: expungement petition in the court that decided the case
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the statewide Utah Courts packet: civil cover sheet 1044XX, petition 1000EX, proposed order 1020EX complete but for the judge's signature, and the Acceptance of Service 1146XX and Consent and Waiver of Hearing 1148XX. The participant files the packet with the certificate of eligibility attached, within the certificate's 180-day life, in the court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

tracks.venue: The court that decided the criminal case, district or justice court. If that court no longer exists, the court that would have jurisdiction if the case were filed today. If charges were never filed, the district court in the county where the arrest occurred, or for a traffic matter, the court where the citation was received.

destination.name: Stage one, the Utah DPS Bureau of Criminal Identification; stage two, the court that decided the case
destination.detail: Two destinations in a fixed legal sequence. The participant first applies to BCI, which decides eligibility and issues a certificate valid for 180 days. The participant then files the expungement petition, with the certificate attached and still valid, in the district or justice court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

The packet is the civil cover sheet, the petition, the proposed order and the BCI certificate of eligibility, with the filing fee or a fee waiver request. rules.notice: The court sends a copy of the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The prosecutor has 35 days to file an objection or statement, including on a victim's behalf; the victim has 60 days. The court must wait 60 days from filing before acting. The petitioner may reply to a prosecutor or victim statement within 14 days of receiving it. The court may order Adult Probation and Parole to file a written response, which AP&P serves on the petitioner, the prosecutor and the victim, and to which the petitioner may reply within 14 days.

tracks.legalName: Expungement of a case dismissed without prejudice, Utah Code 77-40a-302(1) and 77-40a-306(2)
tracks.publicName: Clear a case that was dismissed without prejudice
tracks.mechanism: A case dismissed without prejudice may be expunged on petition at least 30 days after the arrest, and either the prosecutor consents in writing to the expungement or at least 180 days have passed since the dismissal. Under 77-40a-306(2) a prosecutor opposing expungement of a case dismissed without prejudice, or without condition, must have a good faith basis for intending to refile, and the court must consider how often that basis has been asserted. If the court denies on that ground, the petitioner may apply again for a certificate if charges are not refiled within 180 days after the denial.
exclusions: A dismissal with prejudice, which routes to UT-PET-02 and does not carry the refiling condition.
A case where charges have in fact been refiled, which is a pending case and defeats every petition track.
An unfinished case. Nothing is available on any petition track while the case is still open.
Unpaid fines, fees, restitution or interest on the case.
A pending criminal case other than a traffic case.
Current incarceration, probation or parole.
A civil protective order, a criminal protective order or a criminal stalking injunction against the petitioner that is in effect, whether or not it relates to the case being cleared.

waitingPeriods.duration: At least 30 days since the arrest.

waitingPeriods.condition: After a denial on the intent-to-refile ground

units.label: Stage one: BCI application for a certificate of eligibility
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History, and the BCI Third Party Release where the certificate is to be sent to someone other than the petitioner, together with the fee waiver request where one is asked for. The participant submits the application to the Bureau of Criminal Identification with the application fee. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases, may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction, and then issues a certificate of eligibility, offers a special certificate, or denies. LegalEase does not determine eligibility and does not assert that BCI will issue.

units.label: Stage two: expungement petition in the court that decided the case
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the statewide Utah Courts packet: civil cover sheet 1044XX, petition 1000EX, proposed order 1020EX complete but for the judge's signature, and the Acceptance of Service 1146XX and Consent and Waiver of Hearing 1148XX. The participant files the packet with the certificate of eligibility attached, within the certificate's 180-day life, in the court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

tracks.venue: The court that decided the criminal case, district or justice court. If that court no longer exists, the court that would have jurisdiction if the case were filed today. If charges were never filed, the district court in the county where the arrest occurred, or for a traffic matter, the court where the citation was received.

destination.name: Stage one, the Utah DPS Bureau of Criminal Identification; stage two, the court that decided the case
destination.detail: Two destinations in a fixed legal sequence. The participant first applies to BCI, which decides eligibility and issues a certificate valid for 180 days. The participant then files the expungement petition, with the certificate attached and still valid, in the district or justice court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

rules.filing: Filed in the court that decided the case, district or justice court, under Utah Code 77-40a-305. The packet is the civil cover sheet, the petition, the proposed order and the BCI certificate of eligibility, with the filing fee or a fee waiver request. The certificate must still be valid on the filing date. Certified copies of a granted order must be requested within 28 days after the order is granted (URCrP 42).

rules.notice: The court sends a copy of the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The prosecutor has 35 days to file an objection or statement, including on a victim's behalf; the victim has 60 days. The court must wait 60 days from filing before acting. The petitioner may reply to a prosecutor or victim statement within 14 days of receiving it. The court may order Adult Probation and Parole to file a written response, which AP&P serves on the petitioner, the prosecutor and the victim, and to which the petitioner may reply within 14 days.

tracks.mechanism: An acquittal may be expunged on petition at least 30 days after the arrest, on a certificate of eligibility from BCI. Automatic expungement under 77-40a-206 should occur 60 days after the acquittal, so the petition is the fallback where it did not, and the free route must be checked and disclosed first. Acquittal by reason of insanity is expressly excluded from the automatic track and is treated as out of scope for the petition track until confirmed.

Current incarceration, probation or parole.
A civil protective order, a criminal protective order or a criminal stalking injunction against the petitioner that is in effect, whether or not it relates to the case being cleared.

units.label: Stage one: BCI application for a certificate of eligibility
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History, and the BCI Third Party Release where the certificate is to be sent to someone other than the petitioner, together with the fee waiver request where one is asked for. The participant submits the application to the Bureau of Criminal Identification with the application fee. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases, may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction, and then issues a certificate of eligibility, offers a special certificate, or denies. LegalEase does not determine eligibility and does not assert that BCI will issue.

units.label: Stage two: expungement petition in the court that decided the case
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the statewide Utah Courts packet: civil cover sheet 1044XX, petition 1000EX, proposed order 1020EX complete but for the judge's signature, and the Acceptance of Service 1146XX and Consent and Waiver of Hearing 1148XX. The participant files the packet with the certificate of eligibility attached, within the certificate's 180-day life, in the court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

tracks.venue: The court that decided the criminal case, district or justice court. If that court no longer exists, the court that would have jurisdiction if the case were filed today. If charges were never filed, the district court in the county where the arrest occurred, or for a traffic matter, the court where the citation was received.

The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

tracks.legalName: Expungement where the statute of limitations has expired, Utah Code 77-40a-302(1)
tracks.publicName: Clear a case the State can no longer bring
tracks.mechanism: Expiry of the statute of limitations on all charges in the case is a qualifying event under 77-40a-302(1), and BCI lists failure to meet it as a denial reason under 77-40a-302(1)(b)(v). A certificate of eligibility is required, which means BCI applies the limitations screen at the certificate stage. That is a meaningful protection in product terms: LegalEase does not have to compute a limitations period to route this track, because BCI will refuse the certificate if the period has not run.
exclusions: Any case in which the limitations period has not expired on every charge. The certificate stage is where that is decided.
An offence with no limitations period.
An unfinished case. Nothing is available on any petition track while the case is still open.
Unpaid fines, fees, restitution or interest on the case.
A pending criminal case other than a traffic case.
Current incarceration, probation or parole.
A civil protective order, a criminal protective order or a criminal stalking injunction against the petitioner that is in effect, whether or not it relates to the case being cleared.

waitingPeriods.duration: The limitations period must have expired on every charge in the case. BCI applies this screen at the certificate stage.
Valid 180 days from issuance and must be valid on the filing date.

units.label: Stage one: BCI application for a certificate of eligibility
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History, and the BCI Third Party Release where the certificate is to be sent to someone other than the petitioner, together with the fee waiver request where one is asked for. The participant submits the application to the Bureau of Criminal Identification with the application fee. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases, may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction, and then issues a certificate of eligibility, offers a special certificate, or denies. LegalEase does not determine eligibility and does not assert that BCI will issue.

units.label: Stage two: expungement petition in the court that decided the case, or the district court in the county of arrest where no case was filed
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the statewide Utah Courts packet: civil cover sheet 1044XX, petition 1000EX, proposed order 1020EX complete but for the judge's signature, and the Acceptance of Service 1146XX and Consent and Waiver of Hearing 1148XX. The participant files the packet with the certificate of eligibility attached, within the certificate's 180-day life, in the court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

tracks.venue: The court that decided the criminal case, district or justice court. If that court no longer exists, the court that would have jurisdiction if the case were filed today. If charges were never filed, the district court in the county where the arrest occurred, or for a traffic matter, the court where the citation was received.

destination.name: Stage one, the Utah DPS Bureau of Criminal Identification; stage two, the court that decided the case
destination.detail: Two destinations in a fixed legal sequence. The participant first applies to BCI, which decides eligibility and issues a certificate valid for 180 days. The participant then files the expungement petition, with the certificate attached and still valid, in the district or justice court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

rules.filing: Filed in the court that decided the case, district or justice court, under Utah Code 77-40a-305. The packet is the civil cover sheet, the petition, the proposed order and the BCI certificate of eligibility, with the filing fee or a fee waiver request. The certificate must still be valid on the filing date. Certified copies of a granted order must be requested within 28 days after the order is granted (URCrP 42).

rules.notice: The court sends a copy of the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The prosecutor has 35 days to file an objection or statement, including on a victim's behalf; the victim has 60 days. The court must wait 60 days from filing before acting. The petitioner may reply to a prosecutor or victim statement within 14 days of receiving it. The court may order Adult Probation and Parole to file a written response, which AP&P serves on the petitioner, the prosecutor and the victim, and to which the petitioner may reply within 14 days.
rules.service: The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case: the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The Proof of Service form appears in the published packet only as an optional form, used where the prosecutor's office will not accept service. tracks.legalName: Expungement of a conviction on a certificate of eligibility, Utah Code 77-40a-303
tracks.publicName: Expunge a conviction
tracks.mechanism: A conviction may be expunged on petition where all fines and interest are paid in full, all restitution is paid in full, and the applicable waiting period has elapsed, counted from the date the case finished, release from incarceration, or the end of probation or parole, whichever is most recent. The periods are ten years for a misdemeanour under 41-6a-501(2) and a felony under 58-37-8(2)(g); seven years for a felony; five years for a class A misdemeanour and for felony drug possession; four years for a class B misdemeanour; and three years for any other misdemeanour or infraction. Capital felonies, first degree felonies, violent felonies under 76-3-203.5(1)(c)(i), felony automobile homicide, felony DUI under 41-6a-501(2), registerable sex offences under 77-41-102 and registerable child abuse offences under 77-43-102(2) are permanently ineligible. The conviction-count bars at 77-40a-303(4) and (5) are measured against the entire criminal history including previously expunged and out-of-state convictions, with a separate allowance of up to four drug possession offences and a mixed-episode counting rule at 77-40a-303(6). Relief is discretionary in the sense that the court must find by clear and convincing evidence that expungement is not contrary to the public interest, and the petition form itself asks the petitioner to explain why.
exclusions: Capital felony; first degree felony; a felony conviction of a violent felony as defined in Subsection 76-3-203.5(1)(c)(i); a felony conviction described in Subsection 41-6a-501(2); and an offence, or a combination of offences, requiring registration as a sex offender, kidnap offender or child abuse offender under Title 53, Chapter 29, at the time of sentencing or at the time of the application for the certificate. Read at source on 2026-08-06. The controlling review listed felony automobile homicide as a separate permanent bar; the current statute does not, and that item is corrected out here rather than carried. The review's registry citations to 77-41-102 and 77-43-102(2) are likewise superseded by Title 53, Chapter 29.

The 77-40a-303(2)(a) bars do not apply to a conviction for a qualifying sexual offence as defined in Section 76-3-209 committed at age 14 through 17, unless the petitioner was convicted by a district court as an adult under Title 80, Chapter 6, Part 5.
Two or more felony convictions, other than drug possession, from separate criminal episodes.
Any combination of three or more convictions including two class A misdemeanours, other than drug possession.
Any combination of four or more convictions including three class B misdemeanours, other than drug possession.
Five or more convictions of any degree, other than drug possession.
Three or more felony drug possession convictions, or five or more drug possession convictions of any degree.
A pending or investigated proceeding under 77-40a-303(2)(b).
An unfinished case. Nothing is available on any petition track while the case is still open.
Unpaid fines, fees, restitution or interest on the case.
A pending criminal case other than a traffic case.
Current incarceration, probation or parole.
A civil protective order, a criminal protective order or a criminal stalking injunction against the petitioner that is in effect, whether or not it relates to the case being cleared.

units.label: Stage one: BCI application for a certificate of eligibility
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History, and the BCI Third Party Release where the certificate is to be sent to someone other than the petitioner, together with the fee waiver request where one is asked for. The participant submits the application to the Bureau of Criminal Identification with the application fee. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases, may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction, and then issues a certificate of eligibility, offers a special certificate, or denies. LegalEase does not determine eligibility and does not assert that BCI will issue.

units.label: Stage two: expungement petition in the court that entered the conviction
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the statewide Utah Courts packet: civil cover sheet 1044XX, petition 1000EX, proposed order 1020EX complete but for the judge's signature, and the Acceptance of Service 1146XX and Consent and Waiver of Hearing 1148XX. The participant files the packet with the certificate of eligibility attached, within the certificate's 180-day life, in the court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

tracks.venue: The court that decided the criminal case, district or justice court. If that court no longer exists, the court that would have jurisdiction if the case were filed today. If charges were never filed, the district court in the county where the arrest occurred, or for a traffic matter, the court where the citation was received.

destination.name: Stage one, the Utah DPS Bureau of Criminal Identification; stage two, the court that decided the case
destination.detail: Two destinations in a fixed legal sequence. The participant first applies to BCI, which decides eligibility and issues a certificate valid for 180 days. The participant then files the expungement petition, with the certificate attached and still valid, in the district or justice court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

rules.filing: Filed in the court that decided the case, district or justice court, under Utah Code 77-40a-305. The packet is the civil cover sheet, the petition, the proposed order and the BCI certificate of eligibility, with the filing fee or a fee waiver request. rules.notice: The court sends a copy of the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The prosecutor has 35 days to file an objection or statement, including on a victim's behalf; the victim has 60 days. The court must wait 60 days from filing before acting. The petitioner may reply to a prosecutor or victim statement within 14 days of receiving it. The court may order Adult Probation and Parole to file a written response, which AP&P serves on the petitioner, the prosecutor and the victim, and to which the petitioner may reply within 14 days.

The participant is asking to expunge appellate records.
The conviction count is anywhere near the 77-40a-303(4) or (5) limits, which run on the entire criminal history across all states including previously expunged convictions.
A criminal episode contains both a drug possession offence and a non-drug offence, so the 77-40a-303(6) mixed-episode counting rule has to be applied.

The public-interest explanation needs to be argued rather than stated.

tracks.legalName: Expungement on a special certificate, Utah Code 77-40a-304(1)(c) and Utah Admin. Code R722-350-4(4)
tracks.publicName: Expunge a record where BCI could not complete the history
tracks.mechanism: Where BCI cannot obtain disposition information for a criminal episode, or cannot determine whether the petitioner meets the requirements, after reasonable research, it offers a special certificate per criminal episode on payment of the issuance fee. The consequence is that the court rather than BCI makes the final eligibility determination and the evidentiary burden shifts to the petitioner at the hearing. Where the petitioner requested a fee waiver, BCI does not charge an issuance fee for the special certificate; if the court then finds the petitioner not indigent, the issuance fee must be paid before BCI will process the expungement order. The special certificate track uses a different petition and order from the certificate-of-eligibility track, which is why it is a distinct track rather than a variant.
exclusions: Any case where BCI issued an ordinary certificate of eligibility, which routes to the ordinary petition tracks and their 1000EX and 1020EX forms.
A case the participant wants to run without the special certificate BCI actually offered.
An unfinished case. Nothing is available on any petition track while the case is still open.
Unpaid fines, fees, restitution or interest on the case.
A pending criminal case other than a traffic case.
Current incarceration, probation or parole.
A civil protective order, a criminal protective order or a criminal stalking injunction against the petitioner that is in effect, whether or not it relates to the case being cleared.

waitingPeriods.duration: Offered per criminal episode after BCI's reasonable research fails to establish disposition or eligibility. It carries the same 180-day life and must be valid on the filing date.
60 days, to allow the prosecutor 35 days and the victim 60 days to respond.

units.label: Stage one: BCI application for a certificate of eligibility
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History, and the BCI Third Party Release where the certificate is to be sent to someone other than the petitioner, together with the fee waiver request where one is asked for. The participant submits the application to the Bureau of Criminal Identification with the application fee. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases, may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction, and then issues a certificate of eligibility, offers a special certificate, or denies. LegalEase does not determine eligibility and does not assert that BCI will issue.

units.label: Stage two: special certificate expungement petition in the court that decided the case
units.description: LegalEase completes the participant portions of the statewide Utah Courts packet: civil cover sheet 1044XX, petition 1001EX, proposed order 1021EX complete but for the judge's signature, and the Acceptance of Service 1146XX and Consent and Waiver of Hearing 1148XX. The participant files the packet with the certificate of eligibility attached, within the certificate's 180-day life, in the court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

tracks.venue: The court that decided the criminal case, district or justice court. If that court no longer exists, the court that would have jurisdiction if the case were filed today. If charges were never filed, the district court in the county where the arrest occurred, or for a traffic matter, the court where the citation was received.

destination.name: Stage one, the Utah DPS Bureau of Criminal Identification; stage two, the court that decided the case
destination.detail: Two destinations in a fixed legal sequence. The participant first applies to BCI, which decides eligibility and issues a certificate valid for 180 days. The participant then files the expungement petition, with the certificate attached and still valid, in the district or justice court that decided the case. The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.

rules.filing: Filed in the court that decided the case, district or justice court, under Utah Code 77-40a-305. The packet is the civil cover sheet, the petition, the proposed order and the BCI certificate of eligibility, with the filing fee or a fee waiver request. The certificate must still be valid on the filing date. Certified copies of a granted order must be requested within 28 days after the order is granted (URCrP 42).

rules.notice: The court sends a copy of the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The prosecutor has 35 days to file an objection or statement, including on a victim's behalf; the victim has 60 days. The court must wait 60 days from filing before acting. The petitioner may reply to a prosecutor or victim statement within 14 days of receiving it. The court may order Adult Probation and Parole to file a written response, which AP&P serves on the petitioner, the prosecutor and the victim, and to which the petitioner may reply within 14 days.

tracks.legalName: Traffic conviction expungement petition, Utah Code 77-40a-305
tracks.publicName: Clear an old traffic conviction now instead of waiting
tracks.mechanism: Section 77-40a-305 excuses the certificate of eligibility requirement for the traffic conviction petition, and BCI expressly directs traffic expungement enquiries to the court and states that no BCI application is needed. Eligible records are traffic offense convictions as defined at 77-40a-101 — infractions and class B or C misdemeanours under Title 41 Chapter 6a, Title 53 Chapter 3 Part 2 and Title 73 Chapter 18, plus substantially similar local ordinances — excluding driving under the influence and reckless driving under Title 41 Chapter 6a Part 5 and the boating equivalents. The track exists because a petition is faster than waiting five or six years for automatic deletion under 77-40a-202, at the cost of a filing fee. The packet is the civil cover sheet 1044XX, petition 1002EX, order 1022EX, and the 1146XX and 1148XX forms.
exclusions: Driving under the influence and reckless driving under Title 41 Chapter 6a Part 5, and the boating equivalents at Sections 73-18-13 through 73-18-13.6. DUI is not a traffic offense in Utah and does not reach this track.
Any offence above class B misdemeanour, which falls outside the traffic offense definition.
A traffic offense case pending against the petitioner, under 77-40a-305(3)(b).
A plea in abeyance for a traffic offense case pending against the petitioner, under 77-40a-305(3)(c).
A petitioner currently on probation for a traffic offense case, under 77-40a-305(3)(d).
An unfinished case. Nothing is available on any petition track while the case is still open.
Unpaid fines, fees, restitution or interest on the case.
A pending criminal case other than a traffic case.
Current incarceration, probation or parole.
A civil protective order, a criminal protective order or a criminal stalking injunction against the petitioner that is in effect, whether or not it relates to the case being cleared.

waitingPeriods.condition: Class C misdemeanour or infraction traffic case
waitingPeriods.duration: At least three years after the day on which the case was adjudicated or dismissed, under 77-40a-305(3)(a)(i). Read at source on 2026-08-06. The controlling review recorded no waiting period on this track; the current statute imposes one, and it is corrected here.
At least four years after the day on which the case was adjudicated or dismissed, under 77-40a-305(3)(a)(ii).

Three or four years on the petition, against five years for a class C misdemeanour or infraction and six years for a class B misdemeanour on the free automatic deletion under 77-40a-202. The petition is faster, not instant.
60 days, to allow the prosecutor 35 days and the victim 60 days to respond.

tracks.legalName: Cannabis possession conviction expungement petition, Utah Code 77-40a-305 and 77-40a-306(1)
tracks.publicName: Clear a cannabis possession conviction
tracks.mechanism: Sections 77-40a-305 and 77-40a-306(1) allow a petition for a conviction related to cannabis possession without a certificate of eligibility, where the petition makes the required showing. The petitioner must show a qualifying condition at the time of the arrest or citation; that the cannabis was in a form allowed by law, meaning tablet, capsule, concentrated liquid or viscous oil, liquid suspension, topical, transdermal, sublingual, gelatinous cube or lozenge, resin or wax, or unprocessed flower in a compliant container, or a form measured in grams, milligrams or millilitres; and that the amount did not exceed the medicinal amount, up to 113 grams by weight of unprocessed cannabis in a medicinal dosage form, or 20 grams of total composite tetrahydrocannabinol in a cannabis product in medicinal dosage form. The citation question the controlling review left open is resolved: section 77-40a-305(4)(a), read at its official locator on 2026-08-06, itself cites Section 26B-4-201, which defines a qualifying condition by reference to Section 26B-4-203 where the conditions are listed. Title 26 Chapter 61a, which Utah Courts materials still cite, publishes no current version on the Legislature's site. The packet is cover sheet 1044XX, petition 1003EX, order 1023EX, and the 1146XX and 1148XX forms.
exclusions: Any cannabis conviction where the participant did not have a qualifying condition at the time of the arrest or citation.
Cannabis in a form not allowed by law under 26-61a-102.

An amount exceeding the medicinal amount — more than 113 grams by weight of unprocessed cannabis in a medicinal dosage form, or more than 20 grams of total composite tetrahydrocannabinol in a cannabis product in medicinal dosage form.
Distribution, cultivation or possession-with-intent offences, which are not possession convictions and are not on this track.
An unfinished case. Nothing is available on any petition track while the case is still open.
Unpaid fines, fees, restitution or interest on the case.
A pending criminal case other than a traffic case.
Current incarceration, probation or parole.
A civil protective order, a criminal protective order or a criminal stalking injunction against the petitioner that is in effect, whether or not it relates to the case being cleared.

tracks.venue: The court that decided the criminal case, district or justice court. If that court no longer exists, the court that would have jurisdiction if the case were filed today. If charges were never filed, the district court in the county where the arrest occurred, or for a traffic matter, the court where the citation was received.

destination.name: The district or justice court that entered the cannabis conviction
destination.detail: Single-stage. No BCI certificate is required, so there is no agency stage: the participant files the petition, proposed order and cover sheet directly in the court that entered the conviction, with the filing fee or a fee waiver request. The three statutory showings are made in the petition on the participant's own facts.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Medical records or a clinician's letter establishing the qualifying condition at the time of the arrest or citation. Ask the clinician who treated the condition for records covering the date of the arrest or citation. LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates these records and does not judge whether they establish the condition — the participant attaches them and the court weighs them.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The participant's own treating clinician or medical provider

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Did you have a qualifying medical condition at the time of the arrest or citation? If so, which one?" against Medical records or a clinician's letter establishing the qualifying condition at the time of the arrest or citation, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Charging document, police report or laboratory report describing the form and amount. Ask the clerk or the arresting agency for the charging document and any laboratory report. These are usually the only contemporaneous record of the form and quantity, which is why the review flags the showing as an evidentiary question about a years-old arrest.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that entered the conviction, or the arresting agency

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "How much was it, by weight or by total composite THC? Obtain Certified copy of the judgment of conviction. Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the judgment. It carries the conviction date and the offence as charged.

A court filing fee set by Utah Code 78A-2-301 applies. The Utah Courts page directs filers to the cover sheet for the current amount rather than publishing a figure, so the packet does not quote one. The exact current amount is an open release-blocking question.

The court fee waiver process applies to the filing fee, and the published packet includes the fee waiver route. BCI separately operates an indigency-linked waiver and will issue without the issuance fee where the court is likely to waive the filing fee; if the court then finds the petitioner not indigent, the BCI issuance fee must be paid before BCI will process the expungement order.

rules.notice: The court sends a copy of the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The prosecutor has 35 days to file an objection or statement, including on a victim's behalf; the victim has 60 days. The court must wait 60 days from filing before acting. The petitioner may reply to a prosecutor or victim statement within 14 days of receiving it. The court may order Adult Probation and Parole to file a written response, which AP&P serves on the petitioner, the prosecutor and the victim, and to which the petitioner may reply within 14 days.

selfHelpBoundaries: The participant is not a US citizen. The Utah Courts self-help page itself tells non-citizens to consult an immigration lawyer before expunging, because the FBI may retain records of an expunged case. This is a hard stop, not a caveat.
The prosecutor or a victim objects, or the court schedules a hearing.
BCI offers a special certificate instead of a certificate of eligibility, because the court rather than BCI then decides eligibility.
The public-interest showing has to be argued rather than simply stated.
Any conviction-counting question near the 77-40a-303(4) or (5) limits, including out-of-state and previously expunged convictions.
An active protective order or stalking injunction.
The participant is asking to expunge appellate records.
The participant cannot establish that they had a qualifying condition at the time of the arrest or citation.
The form or amount of the cannabis is genuinely in doubt, which the review flags as an evidentiary question about a years-old arrest.
The offence was distribution, cultivation or possession with intent rather than possession.

tracks.legalName: Motion to remove the link between personal identifying information and a dismissed criminal case, Utah Code 77-40a-105
tracks.publicName: Break the link between your name and a dismissed case
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06. An individual whose criminal case is dismissed may move the court for an order removing the link between the individual's personal identifying information and the dismissed case in any publicly searchable database of the Utah state courts. Personal identifying information means a current name, former name, nickname or alias, together with date of birth. The court shall grant the motion if 30 days have passed from the day the case was dismissed, no appeal was filed within that 30-day period, and no charge in the case was a domestic violence offence as defined in Section 77-36-1. Relief is ministerial rather than discretionary once those three conditions are met. Two express limits define what the remedy is worth: under subsection (3) removing the link does not affect a prosecuting, arresting or other agency's records, and under subsection (4) the case history, unless expunged under the chapter, remains public and accessible through a search by case number. The remedy therefore breaks the name-to-case search path in the state courts' public database and does nothing else. The companion provision at Utah Code 78B-7-1002.1 gives the same relief to a person against whom a civil protective order or civil stalking injunction was sought and denied; that branch is a civil matter outside the record-clearing product scope and is not built here.
exclusions: Any case in which a charge was a domestic violence offence as defined in Section 77-36-1. This is an absolute bar under 77-40a-105(2)(b)(iii).
Any case dismissed fewer than 30 days ago.
Any case in which an appeal was filed within the 30-day period following dismissal.

A denied request for a civil protective order or a civil stalking injunction. That branch is governed by Utah Code 78B-7-1002.1, is a civil matter, and is outside the record-clearing product scope even though the same form covers it.
Agency records. Subsection (3) is explicit that removing the link does not affect a prosecuting, arresting or other agency's records, so this track is not a substitute for expungement.
An unfinished case. Nothing is available on any petition track while the case is still open.
Unpaid fines, fees, restitution or interest on the case.
A pending criminal case other than a traffic case.
Current incarceration, probation or parole.
A civil protective order, a criminal protective order or a criminal stalking injunction against the petitioner that is in effect, whether or not it relates to the case being cleared.

tracks.legalName: Appellate record expungement, Utah Supreme Court Standing Order No. 12
tracks.publicName: Expunging appellate court records
tracks.mechanism: Standing Order No. 12 governs expungement of appellate court records. The prerequisite is an existing district court order expunging the entire trial court record and the records held by other government entities. What is filed with the Utah Supreme Court, and served on the Utah Attorney General, is a written petition, a copy of the district court expungement petition, a certified copy of the district court expungement order, and a proposed redacted appellate opinion replacing the petitioner's name with initials or a pseudonym and redacting address, birthdate and government identification numbers. The Attorney General has 30 days from service to object to the expungement or to the proposed redaction. If granted, appellate records including briefs are sealed, the published opinion is replaced with the redacted version, and the appellate courts notify LexisNexis and Westlaw; other publishers are not legally required to redact. Utah Courts states expressly that there are no forms for this.

tracks.legalName: Motion to reduce conviction under Utah Code 76-3-402, adjacent non-relief routing node
tracks.publicName: Not eligible yet? Reducing the conviction level may open a route
tracks.mechanism: This node produces no record-clearing relief and no packet of its own. A motion to reduce a conviction, commonly called a 402 motion, is not a record-clearing mechanism, but Utah Courts routes ineligible petitioners to it and a reduction can convert an ineligible conviction into an eligible one by changing the offence level and therefore both the applicable waiting period and the conviction-counting math under 77-40a-303 and 77-40a-205. The adopted counsel structure places it in the Utah decision tree as an adjacent non-relief routing node — a not yet, but here is the path branch — and expressly not as a relief track.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Police and Court Records of a Non-Conviction, Va. Code § 19.2-392.2(A)
tracks.publicName: Expunge a Virginia charge that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06 in the version effective until December 1, 2026, § 19.2-392.2(A) allows a person charged with a crime, a civil offence or any offence defined in Title 18.2 who is acquitted, or against whom a nolle prosequi is taken or the charge is otherwise dismissed including dismissal by accord and satisfaction under § 19.2-151, to petition for expungement of the police and court records relating to the charge, and provides that no court fees or costs are payable. Subsection C fixes venue in the circuit court of the county or city where the case was disposed of, prescribes the petition contents, and requires the petitioner to request that the CCRE electronically forward a copy of the petitioner's Virginia criminal history record to that court. Subsection D gives the attorney for the Commonwealth twenty-one days to object, answer or give written notice of no objection. Subsection F applies the manifest injustice standard but adds a presumption the controlling review could not verify: where the petitioner has no prior criminal record and the arrest was for a misdemeanor violation or the charge was a civil offence, the petitioner is entitled to expungement in the absence of good cause shown to the contrary by the Commonwealth. Subsection F also allows the court to enter the order without a hearing where the Commonwealth gives written notice of no objection and, for a felony charge, stipulates manifest injustice. Subsection K makes State Police validate the accuracy of the record but not its eligibility. Subsection L makes an order voidable within three years. Subsection M keeps the petition and any responsive pleadings under seal.
exclusions: A charge dismissed after a finding of facts sufficient for guilt, and a deferred or first-offender disposition such as a § 18.2-251 drug dismissal. Under Commonwealth v. Dotson 'otherwise dismissed' is read narrowly and this population routes to sealing instead. Exception recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research: a dismissal under § 19.2-298.02 that all parties agreed to treat as otherwise dismissed under subsection D of that section (version in force on 2026-09-06) is evaluated under this route rather than excluded automatically; eligibility is not an order granting expungement, the agreement is never inferred, and an absent, ambiguous or disputed agreement goes to human legal review.
Convictions, other than those reached by the pardon and actual-innocence subsections, which are their own tracks.
Records where another person used the petitioner's identity, which is § 19.2-392.2(B) and a different track with a fingerprint requirement.
Juvenile records, which are a separate regime.
Federal records; Virginia relief reaches Virginia records only.

researchDeferredDispositionException.requiredDistinction: Agreement to a deferred case disposition, agreement that the dismissal qualifies for expungement treatment under subsection D, and the prosecutor's later response to an expungement petition are three different facts and are never collapsed into one checkbox. The record may identify the agreement in the final disposition order; the statute does not make that order the only possible evidence, so the product captures the document or reference actually establishing the agreement and sends ambiguous evidence to review.
researchDeferredDispositionException.implementation: The route record, the packet's election gate (runtime) and the participant text change together; prose is never changed while the runtime still rejects the branch, and the branch is never opened merely because the form contains it. The opposition stop, every remaining § 19.2-392.2 requirement, and the no-generated-consent rule stay. No attorney's consent or signature is generated.

researchParticipantText.text: A deferred dismissal needs a closer check. A dismissal after a plea, a stipulation, or deferred proceedings does not automatically qualify. A dismissal under Virginia Code §19.2-298.02 may qualify where all parties agreed to the treatment described in subsection D. Check the court record and the agreement before selecting the dismissal ground. If the legal basis or agreement is unclear, obtain legal review before filing. Do not assume the same rule covers a dismissal under another first-offender statute.

releaseBlockers.question: Chapter 23.2 and § 19.2-392.2 both carry future versions that the controlling review predates and does not record. Read at source on 2026-08-06: § 19.2-392.2 exists in two versions, one effective until December 1, 2026 and one effective December 1, 2026, the later of which broadens subsection A to any person 'arrested, charged, summonsed, or indicted' who 'is not ultimately convicted' provided no stipulation or judicial finding of facts sufficient to find guilt and no deferred adjudication, codifies the Dotson limit in the statute itself, and adds a new subsection C sentence permitting a single petition to cover multiple charges arising out of SEPARATE transactions or occurrences. Section 19.2-392.6 likewise carries an A subsection effective until July 1, 2027 and a second effective July 1, 2027, and its historical citation now includes 2026, Sp. Sess. I, c. 1, which the review did not have. The review's open question about a 2026 amendment is therefore answered in the affirmative. Every Virginia track must be re-read before 2026-12-01 and again before 2027-07-01.

releaseBlockers.question: What the December 1, 2026 version of § 19.2-392.2 does to this track. Read at source on 2026-08-06, the later version replaces the subsection A gateway with any person 'arrested, charged, summonsed, or indicted' for an infraction, crime or civil offence who 'is not ultimately convicted, provided that no stipulation of facts sufficient to find guilt was entered or the court did not determine the facts sufficient to find guilt but deferred adjudication or disposition to a later date'. That codifies the Dotson limit in the statute, extends the route to infractions, and adds a sentence to subsection C permitting a single petition to cover multiple charges arising out of separate transactions or occurrences, which the current version does not allow. It also provides that unavailability of the arrest information alone is not a basis for refusing expungement, and requires an objecting Commonwealth's Attorney to state the basis. The packet must be rebuilt for that version before it takes effect.

tracks.legalName: Expungement of Police and Court Records After an Absolute Pardon, Va. Code § 19.2-392.2(I)
tracks.publicName: Clear a Virginia conviction the Governor has absolutely pardoned
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 19.2-392.2(I) provides that, notwithstanding any other provision of the section, upon receiving a copy pursuant to § 2.2-402 of an absolute pardon for the commission of a crime that a person did not commit, the court shall enter an order requiring expungement of the police and court records relating to the charge and conviction, and that the order shall state that the expungement is ordered pursuant to that subsection. The trigger is the court's receipt of the pardon copy, not a petition, and the outcome is mandatory. Subsection K then routes the order to State Police, who validate the accuracy of the record but expressly not its eligibility. There is no waiting period, no fee, no fingerprint step and no manifest injustice showing on this subsection.
exclusions: A conditional or partial pardon. Subsection (I) reaches an absolute pardon for the commission of a crime the person did not commit.
A simple pardon granted as an act of clemency rather than on innocence grounds, where the subsection's own words may not be satisfied.
The pardon application to the Governor itself, which is a separate executive process outside the adopted product scope.
Non-conviction charges, which are § 19.2-392.2(A) and a different track.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Section 19.2-392.2(I) imposes no waiting period; the duty arises on the court's receipt of the pardon copy.

tracks.legalName: Expungement of Police and Court Records After a Writ of Actual Innocence, Va. Code § 19.2-392.2(J)
tracks.publicName: Clearing a Virginia conviction vacated by a writ of actual innocence
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 19.2-392.2(J) provides that upon receiving a copy of a writ vacating a conviction pursuant to § 19.2-327.5 or § 19.2-327.13, the court shall enter an order requiring expungement of the police and court records relating to the charge and conviction, and the order shall state that the expungement is ordered pursuant to that subsection. The trigger is the court's receipt of the writ. No petition, no application, no waiting period and no fee are prescribed, and nothing is left for the participant to submit. The two cited sections are the biological-evidence and non-biological-evidence writs of actual innocence, both of which are litigated in the Court of Appeals or the Supreme Court of Virginia by a petitioner who is represented by the time the writ issues.
exclusions: The writ litigation itself under § 19.2-327.5 or § 19.2-327.13, which is appellate post-conviction litigation and is outside the adopted product scope.
Any conviction not vacated by one of those two writs.
Non-conviction charges, which are § 19.2-392.2(A).

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement Where Another Person Used the Petitioner's Identity, Va. Code § 19.2-392.2(B)
tracks.publicName: Clear a Virginia record created when someone else used your name
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, the exact subsection is § 19.2-392.2(B): if any person whose name or other identification has been used without his consent or authorisation by another person who has been charged or arrested using such name or identification, he may file a petition with the court disposing of the charge for relief under the section, without paying any court fees or costs, and the petition shall include one complete set of the petitioner's fingerprints obtained from a law-enforcement agency. Subsection E prescribes the proof route the controlling review could not verify: the petitioner obtains the fingerprint set from a law-enforcement agency and gives that agency a copy of the petition; the agency submits the fingerprints to the CCRE with the petition attached; the CCRE forwards the criminal history and the fingerprint set to the court under seal; on completion of the hearing the court returns the fingerprint card, and where no hearing was held the card is destroyed unless the petitioner asks for it back within thirty days or supplies a stamped self-addressed envelope. Subsection H supplies a distinct and faster route where the charge is dismissed because the court finds the person arrested or charged is not the person named in the summons, warrant, indictment or presentment: the dismissing court, on motion of the person improperly charged, enters the expungement order.
exclusions: Records the participant's own conduct created. This route is for records created by another person's use of the participant's identity.
Charges the participant was in fact arrested for under an alias of their own.
Records outside Virginia.

Code 19.2-392.2(A): it is the petition for expungement this source names.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal an Enumerated Offence After Seven Clean Years, Va. Code § 19.2-392.12:1(A)
tracks.publicName: Seal an eligible minor Virginia conviction after seven clean years
tracks.mechanism: A free-standing petition track, not a backstop. Section 19.2-392.12:1(A) reaches an exhaustive list of offence provisions — a violation of § 4.1-305; a misdemeanor violation of § 18.2-96 or § 18.2-103; a violation of § 18.2-119, § 18.2-120 or § 18.2-134; a misdemeanor violation of § 18.2-248.1; a violation of subsection A of § 18.2-265.3; or a violation of § 18.2-415 — whether the disposition was a conviction or a deferred and dismissed charge, with an offence date on or after 1 January 1986. The single test is seven years since the date of conviction or of dismissal of the deferred charge with no conviction in that period of any law requiring a report to the CCRE under § 19.2-390(A), or of any other state, the District of Columbia, the United States or any territory, excluding Title 46.2 traffic infractions. What is not required is the whole of what makes § 19.2-392.12 hard: no manifest injustice, no rehabilitation showing, no restitution criterion, no felony-history bars, and no lifetime cap, subsection E confirming both that there is no limit on the number of petitions and that grants here do not count against the two-petition cap in § 19.2-392.12. Subsection I makes the outcome mandatory on the two findings. Subsection D carries a same-date rule: the petition may not seek sealing where the charge, conviction or ancillary matter was finalised on the same date as a conviction or deferred dismissal that is not eligible under the section. One petition may cover multiple charges, convictions and ancillary matters provided all are eligible.
exclusions: Any offence outside the exhaustive list in § 19.2-392.12:1(A).
Any offence date before 1 January 1986.
Any case where a reportable conviction occurred during the seven-year period, anywhere, other than a Title 46.2 traffic infraction.
Any charge, conviction or ancillary matter finalised on the same date as a conviction or deferred dismissal that is not eligible under the section, § 19.2-392.12:1(D).

waitingPeriods.duration: Seven years since the date of conviction or of dismissal of the deferred charge, with no reportable conviction anywhere during that period, excluding Title 46.2 traffic infractions.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal an Ancillary Matter Left Behind by Automatic Sealing, Va. Code § 19.2-392.12:1(B) and (J)
tracks.publicName: Seal the probation violation or failure to appear left behind when your charge was sealed
tracks.mechanism: Section 19.2-392.12:1(B) lets a person whose conviction or offence was automatically sealed under § 19.2-392.7 or § 19.2-392.11, with an offence date on or after 1 January 1986, or under § 19.2-392.6:1 regardless of offence date, petition to seal a specifically identified ancillary matter left behind — a probation or parole violation, a contempt, a failure to appear, or a bail appeal tied to the charge. Subsection J directs the court to enter the order if the underlying charge or conviction has been sealed, which makes the outcome close to ministerial. There is no lifetime cap and no fee. The § 19.2-392.6:1 branch, for former marijuana possession offences sealed without any court order, applies regardless of the offence date, which is the one place in the chapter where the 1986 floor does not bite.
exclusions: Any ancillary matter whose underlying charge or conviction has not in fact been sealed. Subsection J's test is that the underlying matter is sealed.
Any ancillary matter tied to a § 19.2-392.7 or § 19.2-392.11 sealing where the offence date is before 1 January 1986. The § 19.2-392.6:1 branch is the exception and carries no date floor.
Ancillary matters not specifically identified in the petition; the statute requires specific identification.

waitingPeriods.duration: None of its own. The precondition is that the underlying charge or conviction has been sealed, which in practice means waiting for the automatic process to reach the record.

Retrieval was attempted at the official Virginia Judicial System circuit-court form library on 2026-08-06 at every plausible CC-1201 and CC-1203 path and every one returned HTTP 404, while CC-1473 retrieved successfully from the same library, so the series is published under a path this pass could not locate rather than being absent. releaseBlockers.question: Chapter 23.2 and § 19.2-392.2 both carry future versions that the controlling review predates and does not record. Read at source on 2026-08-06: § 19.2-392.2 exists in two versions, one effective until December 1, 2026 and one effective December 1, 2026, the later of which broadens subsection A to any person 'arrested, charged, summonsed, or indicted' who 'is not ultimately convicted' provided no stipulation or judicial finding of facts sufficient to find guilt and no deferred adjudication, codifies the Dotson limit in the statute itself, and adds a new subsection C sentence permitting a single petition to cover multiple charges arising out of SEPARATE transactions or occurrences. Section 19.2-392.6 likewise carries an A subsection effective until July 1, 2027 and a second effective July 1, 2027, and its historical citation now includes 2026, Sp. Sess. I, c. 1, which the review did not have. The review's open question about a 2026 amendment is therefore answered in the affirmative. Every Virginia track must be re-read before 2026-12-01 and again before 2027-07-01.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal a Misdemeanour Conviction or Deferred Dismissal, Va. Code § 19.2-392.12
tracks.publicName: Seal a Virginia misdemeanour conviction after seven clean years
tracks.mechanism: Petition sealing under § 19.2-392.12 reaching a conviction of, or a charge deferred and dismissed for, a misdemeanor, with an offence date on or after 1 January 1986. Seven years must have passed with no reportable conviction, and the clock runs from the latest of five events, not two: dismissal of the deferred charge, conviction, release from incarceration, a finding that the person violated a suspended sentence, probation or parole, or release from incarceration following such a finding. A probation violation therefore restarts the clock. Three felony-history bars apply: never convicted of a Class 1 or 2 felony or any other felony punishable by life; no Class 3 or 4 felony conviction within the past twenty years; and no other felony conviction within the past ten years from the date the petition was filed. Four further criteria the internal reference omits entirely: rehabilitation demonstrated where the records indicate the occurrence involved the use of or dependence upon alcohol, a narcotic drug or any other self-administered intoxicant; court-ordered restitution on any charge, conviction or ancillary matter in the petition paid in full; not previously having obtained sealing of two other deferrals or convictions arising out of different sentencing events; and manifest injustice, which is a statutory condition of sealing and not merely of expungement. Subsection C caps the section at two petitions granted in a lifetime and confines one petition to charges arising out of the same transaction or occurrence, ancillary matters not counting as separate transactions. Subsection L carries a nineteen-subdivision exclusion list of enumerated Code sections. There is no fee, the Commonwealth has thirty days, a written notice of no objection stipulating eligibility and manifest injustice permits an order without a hearing, and subsection J makes an order voidable on motion within two years.
exclusions: The nineteen subdivisions of § 19.2-392.12(L), which must be encoded by Code section rather than by theme.
Subdivision L.19: any offence where the victim was a family or household member as defined in § 16.1-228.
Subdivision L.4: any non-violent felony where the person used a firearm as part of the transaction, unless firearm rights have been restored under § 18.2-308.2.
Subdivision L.16 excludes Article 3 of Chapter 8 of Title 18.2 with the exception of § 18.2-346, former subsection A of § 18.2-346, and § 18.2-347, so prostitution itself remains sealable.
Any offence date before 1 January 1986.
Any petitioner barred by the three felony-history bars.
Any petitioner who has already been granted two petitions under this section, or who has already obtained sealing of two other deferrals or convictions arising out of different sentencing events.
Any petitioner with unpaid court-ordered restitution on a matter in the petition.
Felony convictions, which are the § 19.2-392.12 felony track.

waitingPeriods.duration: Seven years with no reportable conviction, running from the latest of: dismissal of the deferred charge, conviction, release from incarceration, a finding of violation of a suspended sentence, probation or parole, or release from incarceration following such a finding.
