rules.filing: File the petition in the circuit court of the county or city in which the case was disposed of. District court charges are filed in that locality's circuit court. Multiple charges may go on one petition only if they all arose out of the same transaction or occurrence and all are eligible; ancillary matters are not counted as separate transactions.
rules.fees: none. Sections 19.2-392.12(B) and 19.2-392.12:1(C) provide that no court fees or costs are charged for a sealing petition, and the 2025 acts repealed the Sealing Fee Fund. The CCRE charges its own fee for the participant's own copy of their criminal history record, which is a separate cost.
rules.feeWaiver: none — no court fee is charged, so there is nothing to waive.
rules.notice: The petitioner delivers or first-class mails a copy of the petition to the attorney for the Commonwealth of the city or county where it is filed. That office has thirty days to object, answer, or give written notice of no objection. Where the notice of no objection also stipulates eligibility, and under § 19.2-392.12 also stipulates manifest injustice, the court may enter the order without a hearing.
rules.service: Delivery or first-class mail to the attorney for the Commonwealth of the filing locality. The Commonwealth is a party to the proceeding.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition.
rules.notarization: none stated in § 19.2-392.12 or § 19.2-392.12:1 for the petition.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and the full name you used at the time of arrest?
What is your date of birth?
In which Virginia county or city was the case disposed of?
Was the case in general district court, juvenile and domestic relations court, or circuit court?
What was the charge, and which Code section was it under?
On what date were you arrested, and which agency arrested you?
How did the case end, and on what date?
On what date did the offence happen?
Was the offence date on or after 1 January 1986?
Have you been convicted of anything since, anywhere? Virginia traffic infractions under Title 46.2 do not count.
Did a court ever find that you violated a suspended sentence, probation or parole on this case, and when?
If you served time on this case, on what date were you released?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where a sentence of incarceration was served, because release is one of the five events the clock runs from.

generationRequirements.question: Have you ever been convicted of a felony? If so, what class, and when?
Did the offence involve the use of, or dependence on, alcohol, a narcotic drug or another self-administered intoxicant?
Was court-ordered restitution ordered on any charge, conviction or ancillary matter you want sealed, and is it paid in full?
Have you ever had a Virginia record sealed by petition before, and how many times?
Was the victim a family or household member — a spouse, former spouse, someone you have a child with, a parent, child, sibling, or someone you lived with?
Was a firearm used as part of what happened?
Are you asking about more than one charge, and did they all come out of the same incident?
In your own words, what harm does this record cause you now — work, housing, licensing, family?

participantFilingRequirements.name: The participant's own Virginia criminal history record from the CCRE
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Virginia State Police, Central Criminal Records Exchange
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own copy from the CCRE for the fee they charge. This is a different thing from the court's copy: you must separately ask the CCRE to forward a copy electronically to the circuit court as part of the petition. The Norfolk clerk's guidance is that the case is established with the court first and the State Police request comes second, so the sequence matters.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal a Class 5 or 6 Felony or an 18.2-95 Larceny Felony, Va. Code § 19.2-392.12
tracks.publicName: Seal an eligible Virginia felony conviction after ten clean years
tracks.mechanism: Petition sealing under § 19.2-392.12 reaching a conviction of, or a deferred and dismissed charge for, a Class 5 or 6 felony, or a violation of § 18.2-95 or any other felony offence in which the defendant is deemed guilty of larceny and punished as provided in § 18.2-95, with an offence date on or after 1 January 1986. Ten years must have passed with no reportable conviction, and the clock runs from the latest of five events, not two: dismissal of the deferred charge, conviction, release from incarceration, a finding that the person violated a suspended sentence, probation or parole, or release from incarceration following such a finding. A probation violation therefore restarts the clock. Three felony-history bars apply: never convicted of a Class 1 or 2 felony or any other felony punishable by life; no Class 3 or 4 felony conviction within the past twenty years; and no other felony conviction within the past ten years from the date the petition was filed. Four further criteria the internal reference omits entirely: rehabilitation demonstrated where the records indicate the occurrence involved the use of or dependence upon alcohol, a narcotic drug or any other self-administered intoxicant; court-ordered restitution on any charge, conviction or ancillary matter in the petition paid in full; not previously having obtained sealing of two other deferrals or convictions arising out of different sentencing events; and manifest injustice, which is a statutory condition of sealing and not merely of expungement. Subsection C caps the section at two petitions granted in a lifetime and confines one petition to charges arising out of the same transaction or occurrence, ancillary matters not counting as separate transactions. Subsection L carries a nineteen-subdivision exclusion list of enumerated Code sections. There is no fee, the Commonwealth has thirty days, a written notice of no objection stipulating eligibility and manifest injustice permits an order without a hearing, and subsection J makes an order voidable on motion within two years.
exclusions: The nineteen subdivisions of § 19.2-392.12(L), which must be encoded by Code section rather than by theme.
Subdivision L.19: any offence where the victim was a family or household member as defined in § 16.1-228.
Subdivision L.4: any non-violent felony where the person used a firearm as part of the transaction, unless firearm rights have been restored under § 18.2-308.2.
Subdivision L.16 excludes Article 3 of Chapter 8 of Title 18.2 with the exception of § 18.2-346, former subsection A of § 18.2-346, and § 18.2-347, so prostitution itself remains sealable.
Any offence date before 1 January 1986.
Any petitioner barred by the three felony-history bars.
Any petitioner who has already been granted two petitions under this section, or who has already obtained sealing of two other deferrals or convictions arising out of different sentencing events.
Any petitioner with unpaid court-ordered restitution on a matter in the petition.
Any felony other than a Class 5 or 6 felony or an § 18.2-95 larceny felony.

rules.filing: File the petition in the circuit court of the county or city in which the case was disposed of. District court charges are filed in that locality's circuit court. Multiple charges may go on one petition only if they all arose out of the same transaction or occurrence and all are eligible; ancillary matters are not counted as separate transactions.
rules.fees: none. Sections 19.2-392.12(B) and 19.2-392.12:1(C) provide that no court fees or costs are charged for a sealing petition, and the 2025 acts repealed the Sealing Fee Fund. rules.feeWaiver: none — no court fee is charged, so there is nothing to waive.
rules.notice: The petitioner delivers or first-class mails a copy of the petition to the attorney for the Commonwealth of the city or county where it is filed. That office has thirty days to object, answer, or give written notice of no objection. Where the notice of no objection also stipulates eligibility, and under § 19.2-392.12 also stipulates manifest injustice, the court may enter the order without a hearing.

rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition.
rules.notarization: none stated in § 19.2-392.12 or § 19.2-392.12:1 for the petition.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and the full name you used at the time of arrest?
What is your date of birth?
In which Virginia county or city was the case disposed of?
Was the case in general district court, juvenile and domestic relations court, or circuit court?
What was the charge, and which Code section was it under?
On what date were you arrested, and which agency arrested you?
How did the case end, and on what date?
On what date did the offence happen?
Was the offence date on or after 1 January 1986?
Have you been convicted of anything since, anywhere? Virginia traffic infractions under Title 46.2 do not count.
Did a court ever find that you violated a suspended sentence, probation or parole on this case, and when?
If you served time on this case, on what date were you released?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where a sentence of incarceration was served, because release is one of the five events the clock runs from.

generationRequirements.question: Have you ever been convicted of a felony? If so, what class, and when?
Did the offence involve the use of, or dependence on, alcohol, a narcotic drug or another self-administered intoxicant?
Was court-ordered restitution ordered on any charge, conviction or ancillary matter you want sealed, and is it paid in full?
Have you ever had a Virginia record sealed by petition before, and how many times?
Was the victim a family or household member — a spouse, former spouse, someone you have a child with, a parent, child, sibling, or someone you lived with?
Was a firearm used as part of what happened?
Are you asking about more than one charge, and did they all come out of the same incident?
In your own words, what harm does this record cause you now — work, housing, licensing, family?

packetInstructions: Two-petition lifetime cap under section 19.2-392.12. It must be disclosed before payment, and the participant must be told they are spending one of two.

Waiting period runs from the latest of five events including a probation violation finding: dismissal of the deferred charge, conviction, release from incarceration, a finding that the person violated a suspended sentence, probation or parole, or release from incarceration following such a finding. A probation violation restarts the clock.
CCRE electronic forwarding request, not fingerprints, for sealing.
Sealing restricts access, expungement removes.

The prostitution carve-back at L.16: subdivision L.16 excludes Article 3 of Chapter 8 of Title 18.2, with the exception of section 18.2-346, former subsection A of 18.2-346, and section 18.2-347. Prostitution itself remains sealable, and for a product serving trafficking survivors this is the difference between a route and a dead end.

The Commonwealth's Attorney gets 30 days, and there is a no-hearing consent route: if the attorney for the Commonwealth gives written notice of no objection and stipulates eligibility, and for 19.2-392.12 also stipulates manifest injustice, the court may enter the sealing order without a hearing. It is the single most valuable thing a participant can obtain.
participantQuestions: Family or household member victim exclusion at L.19. Subdivision L.19 bars sealing of any offense where the victim was a family or household member as defined in section 16.1-228, which is far broader than the reference's assault of a family member.

Firearm-use exclusion at L.4. Subdivision L.4 bars any non-violent felony where the person used a firearm as part of the transaction, unless firearm rights have been restored under section 18.2-308.2.
Restitution paid in full.
Offense-date floor of 1986-01-01.
scopeRestrictions: Always test section 19.2-392.12:1(A) before section 19.2-392.12, because the same conduct may qualify there without a cap or a manifest injustice showing.
Two-year voidability for failure to strictly comply. Use the official forms.

Subdivision L.12 bars conspiracy, attempt, solicitation, and accessory or principal-in-the-second-degree liability where the completed substantive offense would be a Class 1, 2, 3, or 4 felony or punishable by more than 10 years, with an express exception for section 18.2-95 larceny offenses.

releaseBlockers.question: Chapter 23.2 and § 19.2-392.2 both carry future versions that the controlling review predates and does not record. Read at source on 2026-08-06: § 19.2-392.2 exists in two versions, one effective until December 1, 2026 and one effective December 1, 2026, the later of which broadens subsection A to any person 'arrested, charged, summonsed, or indicted' who 'is not ultimately convicted' provided no stipulation or judicial finding of facts sufficient to find guilt and no deferred adjudication, codifies the Dotson limit in the statute itself, and adds a new subsection C sentence permitting a single petition to cover multiple charges arising out of SEPARATE transactions or occurrences. Section 19.2-392.6 likewise carries an A subsection effective until July 1, 2027 and a second effective July 1, 2027, and its historical citation now includes 2026, Sp. Sess. I, c. 1, which the review did not have. The review's open question about a 2026 amendment is therefore answered in the affirmative. Every Virginia track must be re-read before 2026-12-01 and again before 2027-07-01.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Sealing of Enumerated Misdemeanour Convictions, Va. Code §§ 19.2-392.6 and 19.2-392.7
tracks.publicName: Some minor Virginia convictions seal themselves after seven clean years
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 19.2-392.6(A) lists the convictions ordered to be automatically sealed in the manner set out in § 19.2-392.7 where the offence date is on or after 1 January 1986: a misdemeanor violation of § 18.2-96 or § 18.2-103; § 18.2-119, § 18.2-120 or § 18.2-134; a misdemeanor violation of § 18.2-248.1; or § 18.2-415. Subsection B requires seven years since the conviction date with no conviction during that period of any law requiring a CCRE report under § 19.2-390(A), or of any other state, the District of Columbia, the United States or any territory, excluding Title 46.2 traffic infractions. Subsection C blocks automatic sealing where, on the date of the conviction, the person was convicted of another offence not eligible for automatic sealing. Subsection D preserves the right to petition under § 19.2-392.12 or § 19.2-392.12:1. The section carries a second version of subsection A effective 1 July 2027 substituting 'former § 18.2-248.1', and its historical citation now includes 2026, Sp. Sess. I, c. 1.
exclusions: Any offence outside the seven provisions in § 19.2-392.6(A). In particular § 4.1-305 and subsection A of § 18.2-265.3 are on the § 19.2-392.12:1(A) petition list but NOT on the automatic list, so they can only be reached by petition.
Any offence date before 1 January 1986.
Any case where the person was convicted of an ineligible offence on the same date, § 19.2-392.6(C).
Any case where a reportable conviction occurred during the seven years.

waitingPeriods.duration: Seven years since the date of the conviction with no reportable conviction anywhere during that period, excluding Title 46.2 traffic infractions.

tracks.publicName: Virginia charges that ended without a conviction can seal themselves
tracks.mechanism: Offences resulting in acquittal, nolle prosequi or dismissal are reached by the automatic-sealing machinery in §§ 19.2-392.8 and 19.2-392.10. This overlaps the expungement track: where automatic sealing reaches the record the person gets restricted access at no cost and with no filing, but sealing restricts rather than removes, and § 19.2-392.13 preserves the use of sealed records for firearm eligibility determinations and NICS, fingerprint comparison in AFIS, research by the Sentencing Commission, Crime Commission and JLARC, and access by law enforcement employees. Expungement under § 19.2-392.2 remains available and remains the stronger remedy for a participant who wants the record removed. The choice between them is a real one and the packet presents it honestly rather than steering.
exclusions: Convictions of any kind.
Any record the participant wants removed rather than restricted, where expungement is the better remedy.
Charges dismissed after a stipulation or judicial finding of facts sufficient for guilt, which are not expungeable under Dotson but which sealing may still reach.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Sealing of Misdemeanour Non-Convictions for People With Otherwise Clean Records, Va. Code § 19.2-392.11
tracks.publicName: A Virginia misdemeanour charge that ended without a conviction, for someone with no other record
tracks.mechanism: Section 19.2-392.11 reaches misdemeanour offences resulting in acquittal, nolle prosequi or dismissal for a person with no convictions and no deferred and dismissed offences on their criminal history record. State Police identify finalised dispositions and provide an electronic list to the Office of the Executive Secretary and to circuit court clerks whose case management systems interface with State Police under § 17.1-502(B1), and the Executive Secretary provides lists to participating circuit court clerks on at least an annual basis. The mechanism matters to the participant because the annual cadence and the interface requirement together mean the same record may seal at different times in different courts, and there is no participant-facing status portal for this before the State Police verification portal is built.
exclusions: Any person with any conviction, or any deferred and dismissed offence, on their criminal history record. The section is confined to an otherwise clean record.
Felony non-convictions.
Convictions of any kind.

tracks.legalName: Marijuana Possession and Traffic Infractions Sealed Without a Court Order, Va. Code §§ 19.2-392.6:1 and 19.2-392.17
tracks.publicName: Old Virginia marijuana possession charges and traffic infractions are already sealed
tracks.mechanism: Section 19.2-392.6:1 seals former possession of marijuana offences without entry of any court order, and § 19.2-392.17 deems traffic infractions sealed. Both operate by force of statute: there is no petition, no order and no fee, and nothing for the participant to submit. One consequence is worth surfacing: § 19.2-392.12:1(B) allows an ancillary matter attached to a § 19.2-392.6:1 sealed offence to be petitioned separately, and unlike the other ancillary route it applies regardless of the offence date, which is the one place in Chapter 23.2 where the 1 January 1986 floor does not bite.
exclusions: Anything other than a former marijuana possession offence under § 19.2-392.6:1 or a traffic infraction under § 19.2-392.17.
Ancillary matters attached to those offences, which are not sealed by operation of law and are petitioned for under § 19.2-392.12:1(B).

tracks.legalName: Expungement of a conviction for conduct no longer prohibited, 13 V.S.A. § 7602(a)(1) and (b)
tracks.publicName: Expunge a conviction for something that is no longer a crime
tracks.mechanism: A person may petition the Criminal Division of the Superior Court for expungement where the person was convicted of an offence for which the underlying conduct is no longer prohibited by law or designated as a criminal offence. The court shall grant the petition where the person completed any sentence or supervision for the offence and any restitution and surcharges ordered by the court are paid in full, subject to the § 7282 surcharge waiver. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 7602(b) carries no waiting period and no interests-of-justice escape hatch — the contrast with the sealing subsections at (c), (d) and (e) is deliberate. After Act 60 of 2025, effective 2025-07-01, this is the only surviving expungement route in chapter 230; everything else that formerly led to expungement now leads to sealing. Section 7602(a)(5) disapplies the entire section to a commercial driver's licence or commercial permit holder seeking to clear a misdemeanour or felony committed in a motor vehicle.
exclusions: Any conviction where the underlying conduct is still prohibited or still designated as a criminal offence. The petitioner must prove decriminalisation; the offence being old is not enough.
A commercial driver's licence or commercial learner's permit holder seeking to clear a misdemeanour or felony committed in a motor vehicle, under § 7602(a)(5), which disapplies the whole section.
Any case where restitution or surcharges ordered on any conviction remain unpaid, unless the surcharge was waived under § 7282.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere, under § 7604.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Section 7602(b) imposes no clock beyond completion of the sentence or supervision.
At least two years before another petition, unless the court authorises a shorter period (§ 7605).

packetInstructions: After 2025-07-01 Vermont is a sealing state, not an expungement state. Participant-facing copy must not use expungement as the umbrella term: expungement removes records from any accessible database and destroys the paper file, sealing moves them into a confidential file without destroying them, and after Act 60 expungement survives only for conduct that is no longer criminal.

The stipulation is a request, not an entitlement, and the prosecutor's refusal converts a paper decision into a hearing the participant must attend. A Vermont packet must say that plainly before the participant pays, and it must not describe a stipulation as though signature were a formality.
Separate petition per offense where offenses are unrelated or in different counties.
Denial carries a 2-year refiling bar.

Expunged and sealed records may still appear in a federal criminal background check. Vermont relief does not reach federal records even though VCIC notifies the FBI's National Crime Information Center.

tracks.legalName: Expungement on discharge from a deferred sentence, 13 V.S.A. § 7041(e)
tracks.publicName: Records cleared after completing a deferred sentence
tracks.mechanism: On fulfilment of the terms of probation and of the deferred sentence agreement, the court shall strike the adjudication of guilt and discharge the person. Except as provided in subsection (h), the record of the criminal proceedings shall be expunged on discharge from probation, absent a finding of good cause by the court, and the court shall issue an order to expunge all records and files related to the arrest, citation, investigation, charge, adjudication of guilt, criminal proceedings and probation. Copies go to each agency, department or official named, and thereafter the court, law enforcement officers, agencies and departments reply that no record exists. Notwithstanding the subsection, the record is not expunged until restitution has been paid in full. Read at source on 2026-08-06: § 7041 sits in chapter 221, was not amended by Act 60, and its relief is court-driven — no petition is required and the participant files nothing to obtain it. Subsection (h) requires VCIC to retain a confidential special index of deferred sentences for sex offences requiring registration, accessible only by the VCIC director and one designated staff person for presentence investigation purposes.
exclusions: Any deferred sentence not yet fulfilled, or probation not yet discharged.
Any case where restitution has not been paid in full. The statute bars expungement until it is.
A sex offence requiring registration, to the extent of the § 7041(h) confidential VCIC special index, which survives the expungement.
Cases for which deferred adjudication is unavailable, including certain serious sexual offences against children, which forecloses this route entirely.
A court finding of good cause against expungement.

waitingPeriods.duration: Discharge from probation on fulfilment of the terms of probation and of the deferred sentence agreement. There is no separate waiting period.

units.label: The expungement the court owes on discharge, and how to verify it happened
units.description: The ordinary and intended path. Section 7041(e) makes expungement the court's duty on discharge from probation, absent a finding of good cause, and nothing is filed by the participant. LegalEase confirms that the person was discharged and the adjudication of guilt struck, confirms restitution is paid in full, and explains how to check whether the expungement order issued. Anyone who completed a deferred sentence should not be sold a petition packet, and this unit is why.

units.label: Written request to the court where the expungement order did not issue
units.description: Applies only where the person was discharged, restitution is paid, and the order nevertheless did not issue. LegalEase generates a controlled written request to the Criminal Division of the Superior Court that entered the deferred sentence, identifying the docket, stating the date of discharge and the date restitution was satisfied, citing § 7041(e), and asking the court to enter the expungement order the statute requires absent a finding of good cause. There is no Judiciary form for this request; the statute supplies the destination, the court, the operative facts and the relief, which is what makes a controlled pleading supportable rather than a guess.

tracks.legalName: Sealing of a qualifying misdemeanour conviction, 13 V.S.A. § 7602(a)(2) and (c)
tracks.publicName: Seal a misdemeanour conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of a qualifying misdemeanour, or of qualifying misdemeanours arising out of the same incident or occurrence, may petition the Criminal Division of the Superior Court for sealing. Under § 7601(4)(A), read at source on 2026-08-06, a qualifying crime means all misdemeanour offences except sixteen enumerated exclusions, the first of which is a listed crime as defined in 13 V.S.A. § 5301(7). The waiting period is at least three years since the date the person completed the terms and conditions of the sentence. Restitution and surcharges ordered for any crime of which the person has been convicted must be paid in full, subject to the § 7282 waiver. The merits condition is drafted against the State: the court shall grant where the respondent has failed to show that sealing would be contrary to the interests of justice. Where the petitioner and the respondent stipulate, § 7602(a)(4) requires the court to grant the petition without hearing.
exclusions: A listed crime as defined in 13 V.S.A. § 5301(7). This cross-reference is the whole misdemeanour screen and must be encoded in full rather than paraphrased.
Sexual exploitation of children under chapter 64.
Violation of an abuse prevention order, an order against stalking or sexual assault, or a protective order concerning contact with a child under § 1030.
Abuse, neglect and exploitation of a vulnerable adult under chapter 28.
Voyeurism under § 2605(b) or (c).
Cruelty to animals under § 352(1) through (10).
Failure to comply with sex offender registry requirements under § 5409.
Hate-motivated crimes under § 1455.
Cruelty to a child under § 1304(a).
Cruelty by a person having custody of another under § 1305.
Mistreatment of persons with impaired cognitive function under § 1306.
Female genital mutilation under § 3151.
Sexual exploitation of a minor under § 3258(b).
Violation of an extreme risk protection order under § 4058(b)(1).
An offence committed in a motor vehicle as defined in 23 V.S.A. § 4 by a commercial driver's licence or commercial permit holder.
Any offence requiring sex offender registration under chapter 167, subchapter 3.
A commercial driver's licence or commercial permit holder seeking to seal a misdemeanour or felony committed in a motor vehicle, under § 7602(a)(5), which disapplies the whole section.
Any case where restitution or surcharges on any conviction remain unpaid, unless waived under § 7282.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere, under § 7604.

waitingPeriods.duration: At least three years since the date the person completed the terms and conditions of the sentence.

Any restitution and surcharges ordered for any crime of which the person has been convicted must be paid in full, except that surcharges are not required if the court waived them under 13 V.S.A. § 7282. Note the breadth: restitution on any conviction, not only the one being cleared.
Under § 7604 the court shall not act on the petition until any pending criminal charge is disposed of.
At least two years before another petition, unless a shorter duration is authorised by the court (§ 7605).

tracks.publicName: Seal a qualifying felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: Only four categories of felony qualify, and § 7601(4)(B) is an exhaustive inclusion list rather than a category. Read at source on 2026-08-06 they are: burglary under 13 V.S.A. § 1201, excluding burglary into an occupied dwelling unless the person was 25 years of age or younger at the time of the offence and did not carry a dangerous or deadly weapon during its commission; designated felony property offences as defined at § 7601(5), a list of twenty-five enumerated sections; offences relating to possessing, cultivating, selling, dispensing or transporting regulated drugs, specified at subsection level across 18 V.S.A. §§ 4230, 4231, 4232, 4233, 4233a, 4234, 4234a, 4234b, 4235 and 4235a; and any offence for which the person has been granted an unconditional pardon from the Governor. The waiting period is at least seven years since completion of the terms and conditions of the sentence.
exclusions: Any felony not expressly within one of the four § 7601(4)(B) categories. The list is an exhaustive inclusion list: if the exact section is not on it, the felony does not qualify.
Burglary into an occupied dwelling, unless the person was 25 years of age or younger at the time of the offence and did not carry a dangerous or deadly weapon during its commission.
A regulated-drug felony whose exact subsection is not among those enumerated at § 7601(4)(B)(iii). The statute qualifies only parts of each section, so subsection-level encoding is required.
A commercial driver's licence or commercial permit holder seeking to seal a misdemeanour or felony committed in a motor vehicle, under § 7602(a)(5).
Any case where restitution or surcharges on any conviction remain unpaid, unless waived under § 7282.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere, under § 7604.

waitingPeriods.duration: At least seven years since the date the person completed the terms and conditions of the sentence.

Any restitution and surcharges ordered for any crime of which the person has been convicted must be paid in full, except that surcharges are not required if the court waived them under 13 V.S.A. § 7282. Note the breadth: restitution on any conviction, not only the one being cleared.
Under § 7604 the court shall not act on the petition until any pending criminal charge is disposed of.
At least two years before another petition, unless a shorter duration is authorised by the court (§ 7605).

tracks.legalName: Sealing of a qualifying DUI misdemeanour conviction, 13 V.S.A. § 7602(a)(2) and (e)
tracks.publicName: Seal a DUI conviction
tracks.mechanism: A qualifying DUI misdemeanour may be sealed at least ten years after completion of the terms and conditions of the sentence, and only where the person is not the holder of a commercial driver's licence or commercial driver's permit under 23 V.S.A. chapter 39. The commercial-licence bar reaches further than this track: § 7601(4)(A)(xv) excludes from the qualifying-crime definition any offence committed in a motor vehicle by a commercial licence or permit holder, and § 7602(a)(5) disapplies the entire section to such a holder seeking to seal a misdemeanour or felony committed in a motor vehicle. A DUI committed before age 25 should be tested against the 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g) route first, and a DUI committed at 18 to 21 against § 7609, since both beat the ten-year clock by a wide margin.
exclusions: A person who holds a commercial driver's licence or commercial driver's permit under 23 V.S.A. chapter 39. This is an express condition of § 7602(e) and is separately reinforced by § 7601(4)(A)(xv) and § 7602(a)(5).
Any case where restitution or surcharges on any conviction remain unpaid, unless waived under § 7282.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere, under § 7604.
A record mixing qualifying and nonqualifying offences, where the participant is being routed to § 7609 instead.

waitingPeriods.duration: At least ten years since the date the person completed the terms and conditions of the sentence.

Under § 7604 the court shall not act on the petition until any pending criminal charge is disposed of.

This is the one Vermont track with a filing fee. rules.filing: Filed with the Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court in the county that handled the case. Offences arising from the same incident or occurrence may go on one petition. Offences not related to the same incident, or offences in more than one county, require a separate petition for each offence. That is a per-offence cost and packet multiplier, not a per-county one.
rules.fees: This is the one Vermont track with a filing fee. Under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e), read at source on 2026-08-06, the $90 filing fee applies only to a motion to seal a criminal history record of a violation of 23 V.S.A. § 1201(a) and does not apply to any other motion to seal or expunge under 13 V.S.A. § 7602, 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g) or other records-clearance provisions. Two currency problems attach and are carried as a release blocker rather than resolved: § 1431(e) still cross-references 13 V.S.A. § 7602(a)(1)(C), a subdivision Act 60 eliminated, and the Judiciary's own gloss that the fee applies where the offence was committed at 25 or older has no anchor in the current § 7602 text. The packet therefore states that a fee applies on this track and directs the participant to the Judiciary fee page rather than asserting an amount or an age condition. Research disposition 2026-09-06: on this route, and on no other Vermont route, the packet states the $90 filing fee as due under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e) for a motion to seal a 23 V.S.A. § 1201(a) conviction, as the Judiciary's own 200-00130A instructions state it; no age condition is asserted, and the stale § 7602(a)(1)(C) cross-reference and the Judiciary's 25-or-older gloss are recorded as currency notes rather than carried into the packet.
rules.feeWaiver: Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs, form 600-00228 (revision 04/2026), the Vermont Judiciary's single statewide fee-waiver application. Use it only if you are asking the court to waive the filing fee; if you are paying the fee, you do not need it. It supports whatever you are already filing and is not a separate request to seal or expunge anything, so it does not change what you are asking the court to do. The packet names the form by its number and title and links the Judiciary's current fee-waiver page. The waiver form number is 600-00228 at revision 04/2026, the object the Judiciary's own fee-waiver page serves; the number printed in the Judiciary's expungement narrative is a typo for the same document (vt-600-00228-source-identity-resolution) and is not carried.
rules.notice: The court notifies the prosecuting office. Under § 7608 the respondent, not the participant and not the court, must give notice of the petition to any victim of the offence known to the respondent, and the victim has the right to offer a statement to the respondent before any stipulation or to offer one to the court. The respondent's inability to locate a victim after reasonable effort — first-class mail, telephone and email to the last known contact details — is not a bar to granting the petition.
rules.service: The participant does not serve the prosecutor with process. Where a stipulation is used, the Judiciary directs the participant to take or send the stipulation form to the prosecutor and to ask whether the prosecutor will file it or return it signed for the participant to file. Under § 7602(a)(4) the respondent files the stipulation.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. On a stipulation form the petitioner signs and the State's Attorney signs separately; LegalEase neither obtains nor asserts the prosecutor's signature.
rules.notarization: Not required by chapter 230 or by the Judiciary's published petition forms.

tracks.legalName: Sealing of a criminal history record where there was no conviction, 13 V.S.A. § 7603
tracks.publicName: Clear a case that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Read in full at source on 2026-08-06. Section 7603 provides one remedy — sealing — reachable by three distinct routes, and Act 60 repealed subsections (c), (d), (e), (f) and (h), so no expungement route survives on a no-conviction record. Under (a)(1), unless either party objects in the interests of justice, the court shall issue a sealing order within 60 days after final disposition if the court did not make a probable cause determination at arraignment, the charge was dismissed before trial with or without prejudice, or the defendant was acquitted; nothing is filed and the duty runs to the court. Under (a)(2) the court may seal at any time if the prosecuting attorney and the defendant stipulate. Under (g) a person may petition at any time, and the court shall grant and issue the order if it finds that sealing serves the interests of justice or if the parties stipulate. Under (b), where a party objects the court schedules a hearing, and the defendant and the prosecuting attorney are the only parties. The burden on the (g) route is affirmative on the petitioner, unlike the § 7602 conviction tracks where the respondent must show the contrary.
exclusions: Any case that ended in a conviction, which routes to the § 7602 tracks instead.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere. Under § 7604 the court shall not act until the new charge is disposed of.

Expungement. Act 60 repealed § 7603(e), (f) and (h), so a no-conviction record can be sealed but not expunged, and automatic conversion of a sealed record to an expunged record after eight years no longer exists.

units.label: Automatic court-initiated sealing within 60 days, and how to verify it happened
units.description: The ordinary path and the one that must be checked before anything is sold. Under § 7603(a)(1) the court shall seal within 60 days of final disposition where there was no probable cause determination at arraignment, the charge was dismissed before trial with or without prejudice, or the defendant was acquitted, unless either party objects in the interests of justice. The participant files nothing: there is no petition, no form, no fee and no application step. LegalEase confirms the disposition is one of the three triggers, confirms 60 days have run, and explains how to check whether the record still appears.

units.label: Stipulated sealing at any time, § 7603(a)(2)
units.description: Applies where the automatic route did not run or does not reach the disposition, and the prosecuting attorney will agree. LegalEase completes the participant portions of Petition to Seal Criminal History 200-00130 and of Stipulation to Seal Criminal History Record 200-00132, leaving the State's Attorney's signature block and the order page blank. The participant takes or sends the stipulation to the prosecutor and asks whether the office will file it or return it signed. This route is available at any time and carries no waiting period.

units.label: Ordinary contested petition at any time, § 7603(g)
units.description: Applies where the automatic route did not run and the prosecutor will not stipulate. LegalEase completes the participant portions of Petition to Seal Criminal History 200-00130. The court shall grant if it finds that sealing serves the interests of justice. The interests-of-justice statement is a participant-authored field with prompts and never generated argument, because on this route the burden is affirmative on the petitioner rather than on the State.

packetInstructions: After 2025-07-01 Vermont is a sealing state, not an expungement state. Participant-facing copy must not use expungement as the umbrella term: expungement removes records from any accessible database and destroys the paper file, sealing moves them into a confidential file without destroying them, and after Act 60 expungement survives only for conduct that is no longer criminal.
Non-conviction records should seal on their own within 60 days. Do not sell a petition for a disposition that should have sealed itself, without first checking.

Section 7603 subsections (c) through (f) and (h) are repealed. Act 60 gutted the old non-conviction expungement scheme and left sealing, so anyone working from an older Vermont packet will look for provisions that no longer exist.

The stipulation is a request, not an entitlement, and the prosecutor's refusal converts a paper decision into a hearing the participant must attend. A Vermont packet must say that plainly before the participant pays, and it must not describe a stipulation as though signature were a formality.
Denial carries a 2-year refiling bar.

Expunged and sealed records may still appear in a federal criminal background check. Vermont relief does not reach federal records even though VCIC notifies the FBI's National Crime Information Center.
participantQuestions: Pending charge anywhere freezes the petition.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether victims receive notice on the § 7603(a)(1) court-initiated route. Section 7608 requires the respondent to notify any known victim at the time a petition is filed, and by its terms that duty does not attach where no petition is filed. The chapter is silent and no official Judiciary statement addressing it was located on 2026-08-06. It does not change what is generated, because nothing is generated on the automatic route, but it bears on what the participant is told to expect.

openLegalQuestions.question: Whether a § 7602(a)(4) or § 7603 stipulation waives the waiting periods that otherwise apply. Section 7602(a)(4) is drafted as a flat command not expressly subordinated to the § 7602(b) to (e) clocks, and the statute is silent. On the § 7603 routes no waiting period applies in any event, so the question does not bite here, but it is recorded because the same stipulation provision is merged into the § 7602 conviction tracks.

Open question blocks release (notice_or_service): Whether victims receive notice on the § 7603(a)(1) court-initiated route. tracks.legalName: Sealing of criminal history records of a person 18 to 21 years of age, 13 V.S.A. § 7609
tracks.publicName: Seal a record from when you were 18 to 21
tracks.mechanism: A person who was 18 to 21 years of age at the time they committed a qualifying crime may petition the Criminal Division of the Superior Court for sealing 30 days after completing the terms and conditions of the sentence. Read at source on 2026-08-06: the section heading and the operative text both fix the band at 18 to 21, and § 7609 contains no reference to age 25 anywhere. The conditions are that restitution and surcharges ordered for any crime of which the person has been convicted are paid in full, subject to the § 7282 waiver, and that the respondent has failed to show that sealing would be contrary to the interests of justice. Subsection (b)(1) is a hard bar: a criminal history record that includes both qualifying and nonqualifying offences is not eligible for sealing under this section. Order, notice and effect comply with § 7607(a) and (b). This is Vermont's fastest route by a wide margin, thirty days against three, seven or ten years, so the age question must be asked of every participant regardless of what else they say.
exclusions: A criminal history record that includes both qualifying and nonqualifying offences. Section 7609(b)(1) makes this an absolute bar, and it is the condition that most often closes this route.

An offence committed outside the 18 to 21 age band. A person under 18 falls outside chapter 230 entirely; a person over 21 runs on the ordinary § 7602 clocks, and an offence committed before age 25 should be tested against 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g).
Any offence that is not a qualifying crime under § 7601(4).
A commercial driver's licence or commercial permit holder seeking to seal an offence committed in a motor vehicle.
Any case where restitution or surcharges on any conviction remain unpaid, unless waived under § 7282.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere, under § 7604.

waitingPeriods.duration: At least 30 days since the date the person completed the terms and conditions of the sentence.

Any restitution and surcharges ordered for any crime of which the person has been convicted must be paid in full, except that surcharges are not required if the court waived them under 13 V.S.A. § 7282. Note the breadth: restitution on any conviction, not only the one being cleared.
Under § 7604 the court shall not act on the petition until any pending criminal charge is disposed of.
At least two years before another petition, unless a shorter duration is authorised by the court (§ 7605).

packetInstructions: After 2025-07-01 Vermont is a sealing state, not an expungement state. Participant-facing copy must not use expungement as the umbrella term: expungement removes records from any accessible database and destroys the paper file, sealing moves them into a confidential file without destroying them, and after Act 60 expungement survives only for conduct that is no longer criminal.

On the § 7602 conviction tracks and on § 7609 the statute is drafted against the State: the court shall grant if the respondent has failed to show that sealing would be contrary to the interests of justice. This is not a petitioner-side public-interest burden and the packet must not write it as one.

Separate petition per offense where offenses are unrelated or in different counties.
Denial carries a 2-year refiling bar.

tracks.legalName: Sealing of records of an offence committed before age 25, 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g)
tracks.publicName: Seal a record from an offence you committed before you turned 25
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06. On application of a person who has pleaded guilty to or been convicted of a crime under Vermont law committed prior to attaining 25 years of age, or on the motion of the court having jurisdiction, and after notice to all parties of record and hearing, the court shall order the sealing of all files and records related to the proceeding if it finds that two years have elapsed since the final discharge of the person; that the person has not been convicted of a listed crime as defined in 13 V.S.A. § 5301 or adjudicated delinquent for such an offence for ten years prior to the application or motion, and no new proceeding is pending seeking such a conviction or adjudication; and that the person's rehabilitation has been attained to the satisfaction of the court. Subsection (m) bars sealing where restitution and surcharges are owed. Subsection (k) provides that the court shall provide assistance to persons who seek to file an application for sealing under the section. This provision sits outside chapter 230, was not amended by Act 60, and is procedurally unlike anything in that chapter: it uses an application rather than a petition, it is dual-initiated, it mandates notice to all parties of record and a hearing, it runs on a two-year clock from final discharge, and it places an affirmative rehabilitation burden on the participant. Under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e) no filing fee applies to a § 5119(g) motion.
exclusions: Any offence committed on or after the person attained 25 years of age.
A person convicted of a listed crime as defined in 13 V.S.A. § 5301, or adjudicated delinquent for such an offence, within the ten years prior to the application or motion.
A person with a new proceeding pending seeking such a conviction or adjudication.
A case where fewer than two years have elapsed since final discharge.
A case where restitution or surcharges remain owed, under § 5119(m).

tracks.legalName: Court-initiated expungement after successful completion of adult post-charge court diversion, 3 V.S.A. § 164(f)(5)
tracks.publicName: Records cleared after completing court diversion on a charge
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Within 30 days after the two-year anniversary of a successful completion of adult post-charge diversion, the court shall provide notice to all parties of record of the court's intention to order the expungement of all court files and records, law enforcement records, fingerprints and photographs. The court shall give the State's Attorney an opportunity for a hearing to contest the expungement, and shall expunge if it finds that two years have elapsed since successful completion, that there has been no subsequent felony or misdemeanour conviction during the two-year period and no proceeding is pending seeking one, and that the participant owes no restitution related to the case. The participant files nothing: the duty runs to the court. Section 164 is titled Adult court diversion program and its subsection (f) is captioned Records; deletion and expungement. It was amended by 2023 Act 180, effective 2025-07-01, and by 2025 Act 64, effective 2025-07-02, not by Act 60.
exclusions: Any diversion not successfully completed.

Pre-charge diversion, which runs on the separate deletion scheme at § 164(f)(1) to (4) and is modelled separately.

tracks.legalName: Automatic deletion of records after successful completion of adult pre-charge court diversion, 3 V.S.A. § 164(f)(1) to (4)
tracks.publicName: Records deleted after completing pre-charge diversion
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Within 10 days of successful completion of pre-charge diversion the programme notifies the victim, law enforcement and the State's Attorney, payment of restitution being required for successful completion. Within 30 days after the two-year anniversary of notifying the State's Attorney's office of the successful completion, the Attorney General shall provide notice that all records held by the diversion programme shall be deleted, and correspondingly for law enforcement and State's Attorney public records. Subsection (f)(4), captioned Deletion applicability, limits the scheme: the process of automatically deleting records as provided in the section applies only to those persons who completed pre-charge diversion on or after 2025-07-01. Valcour and similar non-public law-enforcement databases are exempt from deletion. The participant files nothing on this route; the duty runs to the Attorney General and the holding agencies.
exclusions: A person who completed pre-charge diversion before 2025-07-01. Subsection (f)(4) limits the automatic deletion scheme to completions on or after that date.
Valcour and similar non-public law enforcement databases, which are expressly exempt from deletion.
Any diversion not successfully completed. Payment of restitution is required for successful completion.
Post-charge diversion, which runs on the separate court-initiated expungement scheme at § 164(f)(5) and is modelled separately.
This track offers no participant filing. The duty runs to the Attorney General and the holding agencies.

tracks.legalName: Sealing after an unconditional pardon, 13 V.S.A. § 7601(4)(B)(iv) and § 7602(d)
tracks.publicName: Seal a record after a Governor's pardon
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Section 7601(4)(B)(iv) makes any offence for which the person has been granted an unconditional pardon from the Governor a qualifying felony. The pardon therefore changes the offence's status rather than its disposition, and it leads to sealing rather than expungement. Because the pardon route sits in the qualifying-felony subsection, the seven-year clock at § 7602(d) appears to apply even to a pardoned misdemeanour; whether a pardoned misdemeanour instead runs on the three-year clock at § 7602(c) is not resolved by the text. A pardon is not itself record relief in Vermont: it makes the offence a qualifying crime for sealing, and the sealing petition is still required.
exclusions: A conditional pardon. Section 7601(4)(B)(iv) reaches only an unconditional pardon from the Governor.
A commercial driver's licence or commercial permit holder seeking to seal an offence committed in a motor vehicle, under § 7602(a)(5).
Any case where restitution or surcharges on any conviction remain unpaid, unless waived under § 7282.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere, under § 7604.

packetInstructions: After 2025-07-01 Vermont is a sealing state, not an expungement state. Participant-facing copy must not use expungement as the umbrella term: expungement removes records from any accessible database and destroys the paper file, sealing moves them into a confidential file without destroying them, and after Act 60 expungement survives only for conduct that is no longer criminal.

On the § 7602 conviction tracks and on § 7609 the statute is drafted against the State: the court shall grant if the respondent has failed to show that sealing would be contrary to the interests of justice. This is not a petitioner-side public-interest burden and the packet must not write it as one.

The stipulation is a request, not an entitlement, and the prosecutor's refusal converts a paper decision into a hearing the participant must attend. A Vermont packet must say that plainly before the participant pays, and it must not describe a stipulation as though signature were a formality.
Separate petition per offense where offenses are unrelated or in different counties.
Denial carries a 2-year refiling bar.

Expunged and sealed records may still appear in a federal criminal background check. Vermont relief does not reach federal records even though VCIC notifies the FBI's National Crime Information Center.

At least four versions of the 200-00130A instruction guide have been live on vtcourts.gov, including 07/2017, 01/2018 and 02/2020 revisions that predate Act 60 and describe expungement categories that no longer exist. Only the version linked from the live expungement page may be used, and any archived copy in the LegalEase library is superseded until its revision date is checked against the live link.
A pardon is not itself record relief in Vermont. It makes the offence a qualifying crime for sealing, and the sealing petition is still required.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Vacate a Misdemeanour or Gross Misdemeanour Conviction, RCW 9.96.060(2)
tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington misdemeanour conviction after three clean years
tracks.mechanism: Washington vacates; it does not expunge adult convictions. On a granted petition the court permits withdrawal of the guilty plea and entry of a not guilty plea, or sets aside the guilty verdict, then dismisses the charging document and vacates the judgment and sentence. The applicant must have completed all terms of sentence including satisfaction of financial obligations; at least three years must have passed since the later of release from supervision or probation, release from total and partial confinement as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, or the sentencing date; and there must be no new crime in this state, another state or federal or tribal court in the three years before the application. Since 2024 c 296 the three-year clock no longer restarts on the date legal financial obligations are paid off, and the court may be asked to cancel or reduce some of them. Relief is discretionary: the court may in its discretion vacate even where every requirement is met, which makes Washington unusual and means no outcome may be promised. On vacation the person is released from all penalties and disabilities, the conviction is not included in criminal history for later sentencing, and for all purposes including employment and housing the person may state they were never convicted.
exclusions: Any pending charge in Washington, another state, or federal or tribal court.
A violent offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, or an attempt.
DUI, physical control, railroad intoxication, or an RCW 46.61.5055 prior offence, subject to the ten-year rule.
Any misdemeanour or gross misdemeanour violation or attempt under chapter 9.68, chapter 9.68A or chapter 9A.44 RCW, except failure to register under RCW 9A.44.132.
Convictions meeting the RCW 9.96.060(2)(f) domestic violence conditions, which are the separate DV track.
The protection order conditions at RCW 9.96.060(2)(i).
Felony convictions, which run under RCW 9.94A.640.

Vacation does not restore firearm rights, which run through RCW 9.41.041.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Vacate a Domestic Violence Misdemeanour or Gross Misdemeanour Conviction, RCW 9.96.060(2)(f)
tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington domestic violence misdemeanour after five years
tracks.mechanism: The domestic violence branch of the misdemeanour vacation statute, separate because it has a different waiting period, an added notice requirement, a count limitation, an affidavit trap and a different legal effect. The DV trigger does not require a RCW 10.99.020 designation: the court may determine, after reviewing the court file and the totality of the records including any prior RCW 10.99.020 convictions or comparable out-of-state or federal offences and the damage to person or property, that the offence involved domestic violence, so an agent screening only for a DV tag will misroute. Four disqualifying factors each block relief: the applicant has not given written notification of the vacation petition to the prosecuting attorney's office that prosecuted the offence, or has not given that notification to the court; the applicant has two or more DV convictions stemming from different incidents, with the favourable rule that where the current application covers more than one conviction arising from a single incident none of those counts as a previous conviction; the applicant signed an affidavit under penalty of perjury affirming no previous DV conviction and a criminal history check reveals one; or less than five years have elapsed since completion of the terms of the original conditions of sentence including any ordered treatment but excluding payment of financial obligations. The distinct effect is valuable and concrete: on vacation the state may not use the conviction in a later prosecution except for violating a restraining, no-contact or protection order, stalking under RCW 9A.46.110, or a domestic violence or vulnerable adult protection order under chapter 7.105 RCW, and the vacated conviction is not a conviction of such an offence for the purposes of 27 C.F.R. 478.11.
exclusions: Two or more domestic violence convictions stemming from different incidents.
Any case where written notification has not been given both to the prosecuting attorney's office that prosecuted the offence and to the court.
Any case where less than five years have elapsed since completion of the original conditions of sentence including any ordered treatment.
The ordinary RCW 9.96.060(2) bars, which continue to apply.
Felony domestic violence convictions, which run under RCW 9.94A.640.

packetInstructions: Written notice to the prosecuting attorney is a DV eligibility condition, not a courtesy.

Where the current application covers more than one conviction arising out of a single incident, none of those convictions counts as a previous DV conviction. That is a favorable rule and it changes how a packet should be bundled.

RCW 9.96.060(8)(b) states that a vacated DV conviction is not considered a conviction of such an offense for the purposes of 27 C.F.R. 478.11, and bars the state from using it in a later prosecution except for three enumerated categories. It should be stated precisely, because it is one of the few concrete wins vacation delivers.
Vacation does not make the court record private, or remove the case from court indexes and public court websites. Never call Washington vacation expungement.
Vacation does not restore firearm rights, which run through RCW 9.41.041.

Vacated convictions still count for recidivist charging. RCW 9.96.060(8)(c) provides that a conviction vacated on or after 2019-07-28 qualifies as a prior conviction for the purpose of charging a present recidivist offense committed on or after that date.
Local county superior court rules may require additional documents. Every packet carries a local-check instruction rather than assuming the pattern form set is complete.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Vacate a Misdemeanour Cannabis Conviction, RCW 9.96.060(5)
tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington misdemeanour cannabis conviction
tracks.mechanism: A mandatory sub-route inside the misdemeanour vacation statute. A person convicted of a misdemeanour cannabis offence who was twenty-one years of age or older at the time of the offence may apply, and if the applicant qualifies the court shall vacate. The covered offences are any offence under RCW 69.50.4014 from 1 July 2004 onward, its predecessor statutes including former RCW 69.50.401(e) from 21 March 1979 to 1 July 2004 and former RCW 69.50.401(d) from 21 May 1971 to 21 March 1979, and any offence under an equivalent municipal ordinance, with cannabis taking the RCW 69.50.101 meaning. No waiting period is stated. This is not Blake relief: Blake concerns a conviction that is void, and this route concerns a lawful conviction the legislature has decided to clear.
exclusions: Any person under twenty-one years of age at the time of the offence.
Any offence outside the enumerated cannabis statutes and their equivalent municipal ordinances.
Felony cannabis convictions.
Cases that were not cannabis only, where another offence in the same case needs its own route.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Vacate a Drug Conviction After a Substance Use Disorder Programme, RCW 9.96.060(6)
tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington drug conviction after treatment or a recovery programme
tracks.mechanism: Added by 2023 sp.s. c 1 s 11 as part of the post-Blake drug legislation and absent from the internal reference altogether. A person convicted under RCW 69.50.4011(1)(b) or (c), 69.50.4013, 69.50.4014, or 69.41.030(2)(b) or (c) qualifies on either of two paths: completing a substance use disorder programme and filing proof of completion with the court; or obtaining an assessment from a recovery navigator programme under RCW 71.24.115, an arrest and jail alternative programme under RCW 36.28A.450, or a law enforcement assisted diversion programme under RCW 71.24.589, together with six months of substantial compliance with recommended treatment or services and progress toward recovery goals as reflected by a written status update. There is no waiting period; the six months of compliance is the only clock and only on the second path. The outcome is mandatory: upon verification the court must vacate the conviction or convictions. Subsection (6) is drafted as a standalone route and does not on its face incorporate the subsection (2) exclusion list.
exclusions: Any conviction outside the six enumerated statutes.
Any participant who has neither completed a substance use disorder programme nor obtained a qualifying assessment with six months of substantial compliance.
Nothing else on the face of the subsection. Whether the subsection (2) bars nonetheless apply is an open question and is treated as a stop rather than as an assumption either way.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Proof of completion filed with the court is the trigger.
Six months of substantial compliance with recommended treatment or services and progress toward recovery goals, reflected in a written status update.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Washington State Patrol criminal history record. The $11 WATCH name and date-of-birth check online gives conviction information immediately and is enough to start routing. The non-conviction record is a different and slower product: it needs a fingerprint card plus $12, or an in-person record review at no fee with fingerprints and limited inspection time. tracks.legalName: Application to Vacate a Pre-1975 Treaty Indian Fishing Rights Conviction, RCW 9.96.060(4)
tracks.publicName: Vacate a pre-1975 Washington fishing conviction where a treaty right was being exercised
tracks.mechanism: A mandatory route reaching misdemeanour, gross misdemeanour and felony convictions alike, notwithstanding RCW 9.94A.640, which is broader than the internal reference's footnote treatment. It applies to a conviction before 1 January 1975 of violating any statute or rule regarding the regulation of fishing activities, including the enumerated former fisheries and game statutes, where the person claimed to be exercising a treaty Indian fishing right. The court must find two things: that the applicant is a member of a tribe that may exercise treaty Indian fishing rights at the location where the offence occurred; and that the state has been enjoined from enforcing the statute or rule to the extent it interferes with a treaty Indian fishing right as determined under United States v. Washington or Sohappy v. Smith and any post-trial orders, or any other state supreme court or federal court decision. On those findings the court shall vacate. The person may apply, or, if the person is deceased, a family member or an official representative of the tribe of which the person was a member may apply on their behalf.
authority: United States v. Washington, 384 F. Supp. 312 (W.D. Wash. 1974)
Sohappy v. Smith, 302 F. Supp. 899 (D. Or. 1969)
exclusions: Any conviction on or after 1 January 1975.
Any conviction not for violating a statute or rule regulating fishing activities.
Any case where the person was not claiming to be exercising a treaty Indian fishing right.
Any case where the applicant is not, and the subject was not, a member of a tribe that may exercise treaty Indian fishing rights at the location of the offence.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. The route turns on the pre-1975 offence date and the two findings, not on any elapsed period.

tracks.venue: The sentencing court. Because the route reaches felonies as well as misdemeanours, that may be a superior court.

destination.name: Clerk of the sentencing court
destination.detail: File the application in the sentencing court. Where the subject of the conviction has died, the applicant may be a family member or an official representative of the tribe, and the packet is prepared in that person's name.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Court docket from the sentencing court. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for the docket. It supplies the cause number, the exact RCW, the offence class, the sentencing date and the supervision and release dates. Every Washington waiting period runs from one of those dates and none of them is reliably on the $11 WATCH check.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the district, municipal or superior court that sentenced the participant

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "What is the sentencing date, the date you were released from any confinement, and the date any supervision or probation ended?" against Court docket from the sentencing court, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof of tribal membership. Ask the tribe for written confirmation of membership. The court must find that the person is a member of a tribe that may exercise treaty Indian fishing rights at the location where the offence occurred, and the tribe is the only source for the first half of that.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The tribe of which the person was a member

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Which tribe was the person a member of, and does that tribe exercise treaty fishing rights at the place where this happened?" against Proof of tribal membership, and correct the packet if they disagree.

researchApplicantVictimDistinction.statute: RCW 9.96.060(7) authorises a family member to apply to the sentencing court on behalf of a deceased homicide victim with a prostitution conviction under RCW 9A.88.030; it adds no trafficking finding, estate appointment or waiting period. Municipal-ordinance convictions or disputed family relationships go to narrower review rather than a silent broadening of the listed offense.
researchApplicantVictimDistinction.pleading: The applicant is the living family member; the defendant in the original caption is the deceased person. A declaration states the applicant's own identity and relationship in the first person and describes the deceased person's conviction and homicide status in the third person with a factual source identified. The applicant never adopts a living defendant's personal conviction history as their own, and the general CrRLJ vacatur forms' first-person defendant affidavit is not signed by a relative.
researchApplicantVictimDistinction.kitsapLocalForm: Kitsap District Court Form 950780, revised 08/08/2024, three pages (petition, declaration, instructions): page one keeps the defendant caption and introduces the applicant separately; page two separates the applicant's name and relationship from the defendant's convictions and homicide status; its instructions name notice form 950790, same-day copies of the petition and notice to the prosecutor, and hearing attendance, and say the applicant does NOT prepare a proposed order because the judge prepares it at the hearing. It applies within Kitsap District Court only and is not promoted statewide; no mandatory proposed-order task is inserted into the Kitsap branch. The form contains a citation missing the 'A' in one reference to the prostitution statute; the original bytes are preserved when acquired and the discrepancy recorded; LegalEase's own instructions and pleadings cite RCW 9A.88.030.
researchApplicantVictimDistinction.nonKitsap: Outside Kitsap, a custom pleading only through the actual court's accepted vehicle and the repository's applicable design approval, with the handoff's content outline (applicant, relationship, deceased defendant, court and cause number, exact RCW 9A.88.030 conviction, records supporting death and homicide-victim status, relief under subsection (7)); the supporting declaration states relationship, basis of knowledge, record sources and authentication facts the applicant can truthfully supply; the court decides whether the applicant qualifies; no particular death or relationship certificate is stated as universally mandated.
researchApplicantVictimDistinction.remaining: Outside Kitsap: local scheduling and service, accepted declaration execution, proposed-order practice and the custom filing vehicle; the Kitsap form's bytes are not yet held and must be acquired and bound before that branch is built.

tracks.legalName: Victim and Survivor Vacation of a Misdemeanour or Gross Misdemeanour, RCW 9.96.080
tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington misdemeanour you were convicted of because of what was being done to you
tracks.mechanism: Invoked through RCW 9.96.060(3), this route lets the victim, or the prosecutor on behalf of the state, petition to vacate a misdemeanour or gross misdemeanour committed as a result of being a victim of sex trafficking, prostitution or commercial sexual abuse of a minor, sexual assault, or domestic violence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030. The statute states expressly that a prosecutor preparing or filing the petition is not providing legal advice or assistance to the victim but is performing an administrative function on behalf of the state. The requirements per the controlling review are an affidavit proving by a preponderance of the evidence that the offence was committed as a result of the victimisation; no pending charges other than prostitution; new-conviction rules; and victim penalty assessment and restitution requirements unless exceptions apply. A conviction vacated through RCW 9.96.080 is subject to RCW 9.96.060(7) and (8), so it carries the same effect and the same limits as any other vacation.
exclusions: Any conviction not committed as a result of one of the three qualifying kinds of victimisation.
Any pending charge other than prostitution.
Felony convictions, which run under RCW 9.94A.648.
Any case where the new-conviction rules are not met.

waitingPeriods.duration: None stated as a fixed period. The new-conviction rules apply and were not read at source in the controlling review's pass, so the packet asks for the conviction history rather than computing a clock.

Read the WSP fee table live rather than relying on a stored figure.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Vacate a Felony Conviction, RCW 9.94A.640
tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington class B or class C felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: Felony vacation in the sentencing superior court. The applicant generally must first have been discharged under RCW 9.94A.637, and the certificate of discharge is a separate process and the most common blocker. Class A felonies are not available on this route. A class B felony requires at least ten years since the later of release from community custody, release from full and partial confinement, or the sentencing date, and no new crime in this state, another state or federal court in the ten years before the application. A class C felony requires five years on the same three-event latest-of test with a five-year clean period, except that a class C felony described in RCW 46.61.502(6) or 46.61.504(6) is carved out of that rule by subsection (2)(f) and then barred outright by subsection (2)(g). The bars are pending charges in this state, another state or federal court; a violent offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030 OR a crime against persons as defined in RCW 43.43.830, which are two different and separately encoded lists; and any felony described in RCW 46.61.502 or 46.61.504. Three narrow exceptions to the violent and person-crime bar exist, available only where the conviction did not include a firearm, deadly weapon or sexual motivation enhancement: assault in the second degree under RCW 9A.36.021; assault in the third degree under RCW 9A.36.031 when not committed against a law enforcement officer or peace officer; and robbery in the second degree under RCW 9A.56.210.
exclusions: Class A felonies.
Any pending charge in this state, another state or federal court.
A violent offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, subject only to the three narrow exceptions.
A crime against persons as defined in RCW 43.43.830, which is a separate and longer list from the violent offence list and must be encoded separately.
Any felony described in RCW 46.61.502 or RCW 46.61.504, including the class C felonies described in RCW 46.61.502(6) and 46.61.504(6).
Any conviction that included a firearm, deadly weapon or sexual motivation enhancement, which closes the three narrow exceptions.
Assault in the third degree committed against a law enforcement officer or peace officer, which the exception does not reach.

tracks.legalName: Victim and Survivor Vacation of a Class B or C Felony, RCW 9.94A.648
tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington felony you were convicted of because of what was being done to you
tracks.mechanism: Invoked through RCW 9.94A.640(3), this route reaches class B or class C felony convictions committed as a result of being a victim of sex trafficking, prostitution or commercial sexual abuse of a minor, sexual assault, or domestic violence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030. The victim may apply, or the prosecutor of the county of sentencing may exercise discretion to apply on behalf of the state. The requirements per the controlling review are an affidavit under penalty of perjury stating the specific facts and circumstances proving by a preponderance of the evidence that the offence was committed as a result of the victimisation; no pending charges in any court of this state, another state or federal court for any offence other than prostitution; and, for a class C felony, no new offence in this state, another state, or federal or tribal court in the five years prior to the application, with a ten-year rule for class B. If the court finds the application meets the requirements, the court may decide whether to grant it, so the outcome is discretionary.
exclusions: Class A felonies.
Any pending charge in any court of this state, another state or federal court for any offence other than prostitution.
Any conviction not committed as a result of one of the three qualifying kinds of victimisation.
Misdemeanour convictions, which run under RCW 9.96.080.
