tracks.legalName: Dismissal After Probation and Vacation of a Pre-1984 Conviction, RCW 9.95.240
tracks.publicName: Clear an older Washington conviction after you finished probation
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, RCW 9.95.240 is one of only four routes RCW 9.94A.030(11)(b) recognises for removing a conviction from criminal history, and it has two distinct limbs. Subsection (1): every defendant who has fulfilled the conditions of probation for the entire period, or who was discharged from probation before the period ended, may at any time before the maximum period of punishment for the offence expires be permitted in the court's discretion to withdraw a guilty plea and enter a plea of not guilty, or, where convicted after a plea of not guilty, have the verdict set aside, and the court may then dismiss the information or indictment, after which the person is released from all penalties and disabilities resulting from the offence. The probationer is to be informed of this right in their probation papers. A proviso preserves the conviction for pleading and proof in any subsequent prosecution for any other offence, with the same effect as if probation had not been granted. Subsection (2)(a): after the period of probation has expired, the defendant may apply to the sentencing court for vacation of the record of conviction under RCW 9.94A.640, and the court may in its discretion clear the record if it finds the defendant has met the equivalent of the RCW 9.94A.640(2) tests as those tests would be applied to a person convicted of a crime committed before 1 July 1984. That fixes the scope the controlling review could not: this is the pre-Sentencing Reform Act route. Subsection (2)(b) carries the same clerk transmittal to the Washington State Patrol identification section and any local police agency, the same immediate-update and FBI transmittal duties, and the same bar on dissemination except to criminal justice enforcement agencies.
exclusions: On the subsection (1) limb, any application made after the maximum period of punishment for the offence has expired.
On the subsection (1) limb, any defendant who did not fulfil the conditions of probation for the entire period and was not discharged early.
On the subsection (2)(a) limb, any offence committed on or after 1 July 1984, for which RCW 9.94A.640 or RCW 9.96.060 applies directly.
Any expectation that the conviction disappears for later prosecutions: the subsection (1) proviso preserves it for pleading and proof in any subsequent prosecution for any other offence.

waitingPeriods.duration: None, but there is a deadline instead: the application must be made at any time before the maximum period of punishment for the offence expires.
After the period of probation has expired, and then the equivalent of the RCW 9.94A.640(2) tests as applied to a pre-1 July 1984 offence.

packetInstructions: RCW 9.94A.030(11)(b) states that a conviction may be removed from a defendant's criminal history only if it is vacated under RCW 9.96.060, 9.94A.640, 9.95.240, or a similar out-of-state statute, or by a governor's pardon. Section 9.95.240 is one of only four routes the sentencing statute recognizes.

In any subsequent prosecution for any other offence, a conviction dismissed under RCW 9.95.240(1) may still be pleaded and proved, and has the same effect as if probation had not been granted or the information or indictment dismissed.
Vacation does not make the court record private, or remove the case from court indexes and public court websites. Never call Washington vacation expungement.
Vacation does not restore firearm rights, which run through RCW 9.41.041.

Vacated convictions still count for recidivist charging. RCW 9.96.060(8)(c) provides that a conviction vacated on or after 2019-07-28 qualifies as a prior conviction for the purpose of charging a present recidivist offense committed on or after that date.
Local county superior court rules may require additional documents. Every packet carries a local-check instruction rather than assuming the pattern form set is complete.

tracks.legalName: Request to Delete Non-Conviction Criminal History Record Information, RCW 10.97.060
tracks.publicName: Ask the Washington State Patrol to delete a record of a case that did not end in conviction
tracks.mechanism: The only real deletion mechanism in Washington, and it does not touch convictions. Non-conviction criminal history record information is subject to deletion from generally searched criminal justice agency files where two years or more have passed since a favourable disposition, or three years from arrest, citation or warrant for an offence where no conviction was obtained. The request goes to the Washington State Patrol rather than to a court: it is an agency request, not a petition. Two bars apply outright, the person being a fugitive and the case remaining under active prosecution. Beyond those the agency retains discretion to refuse on three common grounds: the disposition was a deferred prosecution or similar diversion; the person has a prior felony or gross misdemeanour conviction; or the person has been arrested for or charged with another crime during the intervening period. WashingtonLawHelp states directly that it is hard for information to qualify as non-conviction data under the rules, which makes deletion hard to obtain, and that expectation must be set before anyone pays. Where deletion is refused there is a fallback: RCW 10.97.040 requires agencies to check with the WSP for the most current and complete information before reporting a conviction, and RCW 10.97.110 supports a suit, potentially with attorney fees, against an agency that violates the requirement.
exclusions: Convictions of any kind. This route reaches non-conviction data only.
Any person who is a fugitive.
Any case remaining under active prosecution.
Records that do not qualify as non-conviction data under RCW 10.97.030(2), which WashingtonLawHelp warns is a harder test than it looks.

Not an exclusion but a discretion: the agency may refuse where the disposition was a deferred prosecution or similar diversion, where the person has a prior felony or gross misdemeanour conviction, or where the person was arrested for or charged with another crime in the intervening period.

waitingPeriods.duration: Two years or more since the favourable disposition.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Vacate a Void Drug Possession Conviction and Refund Paid Legal Financial Obligations, State v. Blake
tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington drug possession conviction that is void, and get your money back
tracks.mechanism: Blake relief rests on the conviction being unconstitutionally void rather than on any waiting period or clean record. It covers convictions based on RCW 69.50.4013 or RCW 69.50.4014, their predecessor statutes, similar local ordinances, and certain inchoate offences, which the Blake order forms state are unconstitutionally void and must be vacated, with legal financial obligations and accrued interest paid pursuant to those convictions refunded. The relief available is vacation, refund of paid legal financial obligations, waiver of unpaid balances, and full or partial case vacatur, in superior, district and municipal courts alike. The refund is the part participants most often do not know about. Blake is not the same as the RCW 9.96.060(6) treatment route: Blake is about a void conviction and the treatment route is about treatment or programme participation, and the same person may qualify for both, so both questions are asked.
exclusions: Convictions not based on RCW 69.50.4013, RCW 69.50.4014, their predecessors, a similar local ordinance, or a covered inchoate offence.
Convictions for offences other than simple possession, including possession with intent to deliver and delivery.
Any expectation that the refund is automatic; it is claimed.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Eligibility turns on the void conviction category, not on any elapsed period.

tracks.legalName: Application for a Certificate of Restoration of Opportunity, RCW 9.97.020
tracks.publicName: Get a Washington court certificate that stops most licensing bodies disqualifying you for your record
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06. A certificate of restoration of opportunity is a court-issued instrument that operates on the collateral consequences of a conviction rather than on the record itself, and RCW 9.94A.030(11) treats issued certificates as part of the criminal history a sentencing court sees, which confirms it is a recognised instrument rather than an informal document. Its operative effect is at RCW 9.97.020(1): no state, county or municipal department, board, officer or agency authorised to assess the qualifications of an applicant for a licence, certificate of authority, qualification to engage in a profession or business, or admission to a qualifying examination may disqualify a qualified applicant solely on the basis of criminal history where the applicant holds a certificate and meets all other statutory and regulatory requirements, except as required by federal law or as exempted. The exemptions are extensive and must be encoded: criminal justice agencies as defined in RCW 10.97.030 and the Washington State Bar Association are exempt outright, and the section does not apply to the licensing, certification or qualification of accountants, bail bond agents, escrow agents, nursing home administrators, nursing, physicians and physician assistants, private investigators, receivers, teachers, notaries public, real estate brokers and salespersons, security guards, and vulnerable adult care providers who are not home care aides or contracted providers or licensees as defined in RCW 43.20A.715. The Department of Social and Health Services and its contracted providers and licensees retain sole discretion whether to consider a certificate when hiring or licensing for positions caring for or having unsupervised access to vulnerable adults or children. Nothing in the section restores or creates a means to restore firearm rights or eligibility for a firearm dealer licence under RCW 9.41.110, and nothing requires the removal of a protection order. Eligibility is set by the RCW 9.97.010(1) definition of qualified applicant, on a graduated scale: one year from sentencing for a misdemeanour or gross misdemeanour probation, deferred or other noncustodial sentence; eighteen months from release from confinement on such an offence; two years from sentencing, or from release from confinement, for a class B or C felony; and five years from sentencing, or from release, for a violent offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030. The applicant must also be in compliance with or have completed all sentencing requirements, including having paid legal financial obligations in full, being fully compliant with a payment plan, or being out of compliance with a payment plan but having established good cause with the court. And the applicant must never have been convicted of a class A felony or an attempt, solicitation or conspiracy to commit one, a sex offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, a crime including sexual motivation under RCW 9.94A.835, RCW 13.40.135 or RCW 9.94A.535(3)(f), or extortion in the first degree, among the further bars in that subsection. The procedural half of the section was read at source on 2026-08-08 and is carried here. RCW 9.97.010(2) defines a qualified court as any Washington superior court in the county where the applicant resides or that sentenced or adjudicated them, and provides that where the sentencing or adjudicating court was a court of limited jurisdiction the qualified court is the superior court in the county of conviction or adjudication; a district or municipal court is therefore never itself a qualified court. RCW 9.97.020(2) gives a qualified court jurisdiction to issue a certificate to a qualified applicant, and RCW 9.97.020(2)(a) leaves it to that court's discretion whether the certificate applies to all past criminal history or only to the convictions or adjudications in the jurisdiction of the court. The application is filed as a civil action under RCW 9.97.020(7). Under RCW 9.97.020(6) the applicant must notify the prosecutor in the county where the certificate is sought, and must also notify the prosecuting attorney in any other jurisdiction that sentenced the applicant in the five years preceding the application; the prosecutor in the county of application supplies the court with a report of the applicant's criminal history. Under RCW 9.97.020(8) a superior court in the county in which the applicant resides may decline to consider the application, in which case it must dismiss without prejudice, state the reason on the order, and the applicant may refile in another qualified court, while the superior court in the county of the applicant's conviction or adjudication may not decline to consider the application; a court of either county that finds the applicant not qualified must likewise dismiss without prejudice and state the reasons on the order. The section provides no transfer procedure: the remedy for a declining court is dismissal and refiling by the applicant, not transfer by the court. Under RCW 9.97.020(9) the court decides without a hearing on the application and the prosecutor's pleadings unless it determines a hearing is necessary, and under RCW 9.97.020(10) the clerk of the granting court transmits the certificate to the Washington State Patrol identification section. RCW 9.97.020(11) directs the Administrative Office of the Courts to develop instructions, forms and an informational brochure, including at least a sample standard application and a form order, distributed to all county clerks and superior courts and translated into the state's significant non-English-speaking languages.
exclusions: Any person who has ever been convicted of a class A felony, or an attempt, criminal solicitation of, or criminal conspiracy to commit a class A felony.

Any person who has ever been convicted of a sex offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, or a crime that includes sexual motivation under RCW 9.94A.835, RCW 13.40.135 or RCW 9.94A.535(3)(f), or extortion in the first degree.
Any applicant who has not reached the applicable point on the RCW 9.97.010(1)(a) scale.

Any applicant not in compliance with sentencing requirements including legal financial obligations, unless on a compliant payment plan or with good cause established with the court for non-compliance.

The professions and bodies the section does not reach: criminal justice agencies and the Washington State Bar Association, and the licensing, certification or qualification of accountants, bail bond agents, escrow agents, nursing home administrators, nursing, physicians and physician assistants, private investigators, receivers, teachers, notaries public, real estate brokers and salespersons, security guards, and the vulnerable adult care providers the section carves out.
Firearm rights and firearm dealer licence eligibility, which the section expressly does not restore.
Removal of a protection order, which the section expressly does not require.

tracks.venue: A qualified court, and RCW 9.97.010(2) closes the set: a Washington superior court in the county where the applicant resides, or the superior court of the county that sentenced or adjudicated them. Where the sentencing or adjudicating court was a court of limited jurisdiction, the qualified court is the superior court of that county of conviction or adjudication; the district or municipal court that convicted the applicant is never itself a qualified court. Because the set is closed and statutory, one statewide packet serves the whole state as to venue and the county is a participant answer rather than a routing branch. The packet routes to the superior court of the county of the applicant's conviction or adjudication, because RCW 9.97.020(8) provides that court may not decline to consider the application.

destination.name: The superior court of a qualified county under RCW 9.97.010(2)
destination.detail: Filed as a civil action under RCW 9.97.020(7), at the superior court clerk's office of the chosen qualified county, with the notice to each prosecuting attorney RCW 9.97.020(6) requires. The packet routes to the superior court of the county of conviction or adjudication because RCW 9.97.020(8) provides that it may not decline to consider the application. The superior court of the county where the applicant resides remains statutorily available and may be nearer, and a participant who prefers it may use it, but that court may decline to consider the application; if it does, it must dismiss without prejudice, must state the reason on the order, and the applicant may refile in another qualified court. There is no statutory transfer procedure: the remedy is refiling by the applicant, not transfer by the court. Confirming intake with the clerk is prudent practice and not a legal prerequisite, and it is not a condition of generating this packet; which counties require additional accompanying documents under local superior court rules is a separate open filing-instruction question.

tracks.legalName: Execution of a Court-Ordered Expungement by Certificate of Discharge (Wis. Stat. § 973.015(1m)(b))
tracks.publicName: Complete an expungement the judge already ordered
tracks.mechanism: Where the sentencing court ordered at the time of sentencing that the record be expunged upon successful completion of the sentence, and the sentence included probation, jail or prison, relief is executed administratively. A person has successfully completed the sentence if the person has not been convicted of a subsequent offense and, if on probation, the probation has not been revoked and the probationer has satisfied the conditions of probation. Upon successful completion the detaining or probationary authority shall issue a certificate of discharge which shall be forwarded to the court of record and which shall have the effect of expunging the record. There is no petition and no separate court motion in the ordinary case.
exclusions: Any case where the sentencing court did not order expungement at the time of sentencing. Wisconsin has no general later route, and State v. Matasek limits the decision to the sentencing proceeding while State v. Arberry forecloses reaching it afterwards through sentence modification.
Any case where the person was convicted of a subsequent offense before completion.
Any case where probation was revoked, or probation conditions were not satisfied.

Information maintained by the Department of Transportation regarding a conviction required to be included in a record kept under Wis. Stat. § 343.23(2)(a), which § 973.015(1m)(a)1 expressly places outside the subsection.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records.

Where it was never issued or never forwarded, the participant's own written request is produced by the wi_exp_certificate_of_discharge_followup supporting action rather than by this route.

packetInstructions: Department of Transportation records are outside the statute. Section 973.015(1m)(a)1 states expressly that the subsection does not apply to information maintained by the DOT regarding a conviction required to be included in a record kept under § 343.23(2)(a). This is a limit written into the eligibility provision itself and belongs in the participant-facing script, not only in a never-promise list.

Expungement does not vacate the conviction and does not reach DOJ, police or prosecutor records. Quote the CR-266 warning language, because the state's own form is more credible on the limits than we are.

This route covers only the authority-issued certificate of discharge, for which nothing is filed. The participant's written request for issuance is generated on the wi_exp_certificate_of_discharge_followup supporting action, which is a supporting node on the same source slot and not a second record-clearing remedy.
participantQuestions: Ask whether the participant was under 25 at the time of the offence.
Ask whether the maximum period of imprisonment for the offence was six years or less. This requires an offence-class lookup rather than a participant's estimate.
Ask about successful completion, including whether any subsequent conviction occurred before completion and whether probation was revoked. Either answer is a hard stop.
scopeRestrictions: Adult expungement must have been ordered at sentencing. This is the first screening question, and where the answer is no the participant should be told immediately, told why, and pivoted to DOJ record correction, fair employment protections and a pardon referral rather than run through a long intake to reach a dead end.

Do not charge petition-level pricing on this track. The realistic work is verification and a follow-up letter, and for the large majority of Wisconsin adults with a conviction there is nothing to sell at all, which should be said quickly and kindly.

The two readings produce opposite answers and OWI is high volume.

tracks.legalName: Participant Request that the Supervising or Detaining Authority Issue and Forward the Certificate of Discharge (Wis. Stat. § 973.015(1m)(b))
tracks.publicName: Ask for the certificate that completes your expungement
tracks.mechanism: Section 973.015(1m)(b) makes issuance mandatory rather than discretionary: upon successful completion of the sentence the detaining or probationary authority SHALL issue a certificate of discharge, which shall be forwarded to the court of record and which shall have the effect of expunging the record. The triggering event is successful completion — no subsequent conviction and, where the person was on probation, no revocation and satisfied conditions. Where that mandatory certificate was not issued, or was issued but never forwarded to the clerk, the participant may write to the supervising or detaining authority asking that it be issued and forwarded. No statute or rule prescribes the contents of that request and Wisconsin publishes no official participant form for it, so the correspondence is drafted. The letter supports implementation of an expungement the court already ordered; it does not itself change legal status, and the certificate remains the authority's document.
exclusions: Any case where the sentencing court did not order expungement at the time of sentencing. There is nothing to ask the supervising authority to certify.
Any case where the sentence included neither probation nor incarceration, which has no supervising or detaining authority and routes to the CR-266 petition track instead.

Any case where the person was convicted of a subsequent offense before completion, or where probation was revoked or its conditions unsatisfied — the certificate is not owed and the request would misstate the position.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records.

tracks.mechanism: Where the sentencing court ordered at the time of sentencing that the record be expunged upon successful completion, and the sentence included no probation and no incarceration, there is no supervising or detaining authority to issue a certificate of discharge. The person therefore asks the court directly, on statewide circuit court form CR-266 with proposed order CR-267, filed in the same circuit court criminal case. CR-266 executes an expungement the judge already ordered; it does not create one.

A Class I felony where the person has in their lifetime been convicted of a prior felony, or where the felony is a violent offense as defined in § 301.048(2)(bm), or is a violation of § 948.23(1)(a).
Department of Transportation records required to be kept under Wis. Stat. § 343.23(2)(a).
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records.

tracks.mechanism: The court shall order at the time of sentencing that the record be expunged upon successful completion of the sentence if the offense was a violation of Wis. Stat. § 942.08(2)(b), (c) or (d) or (3), and the person was under the age of 18 when he or she committed it. This is the only place in § 973.015 where the sentencing court has no discretion, and it uses a different age threshold — under 18 — from the general under-25 rule. Execution follows the ordinary route: a certificate of discharge where the sentence included supervision or confinement, or CR-266 where it did not.
exclusions: Any offence other than a violation of Wis. Stat. § 942.08(2)(b), (c) or (d) or (3).
Any person aged 18 or older when the offence was committed.
Any case where the person was convicted of a subsequent offense before completion, or where probation was revoked or its conditions unsatisfied.
Department of Transportation records required to be kept under Wis. Stat. § 343.23(2)(a).
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records.

tracks.legalName: Trafficking Survivor Vacatur or Expungement of a Prostitution Record (Wis. Stat. § 973.015(2m))
tracks.publicName: Clear a prostitution record that resulted from trafficking
tracks.mechanism: At any time after a person has been convicted, adjudicated delinquent, or found not guilty by reason of mental disease or defect for a violation of Wis. Stat. § 944.30, a court may, upon the motion of the person, vacate the conviction, adjudication or finding, or order that the record be expunged, if the person was a victim of trafficking for the purposes of a commercial sex act and committed the violation as a result of that trafficking, and the motion complies with § 971.30 and contains a statement of facts. The motion may include certified court records, immigration-related certifications, official government documentation or other relevant and probative evidence. This is the only adult route in Wisconsin that operates after sentencing.
exclusions: Any offence other than a violation of Wis. Stat. § 944.30.
Any case where the violation did not result from being a victim of trafficking for the purposes of a commercial sex act.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records.

tracks.legalName: Wisconsin DOJ Fingerprint and Arrest Record Removal (form DJ-LE-250B; Wis. Stat. § 165.84)
tracks.publicName: Remove a non-conviction arrest from your state criminal record
tracks.mechanism: A person who was arrested and released without charge, found not guilty, had charges dismissed by the court or prosecutor, or against whom no charges were filed may request removal of the fingerprint and arrest record from the Wisconsin criminal history repository, using DOJ form DJ-LE-250B with fingerprints and supporting documentation. All charges arising from the arrest event must be cleared; a conviction on any charge from the same fingerprint event may block removal. There is no fee for the removal request. Where the removed Wisconsin arrest information had been forwarded to the FBI, DOJ contacts the FBI to remove it from the FBI record.
authority: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Information Bureau fingerprint record removal process
exclusions: Any arrest event where a charge arising from the same fingerprint event resulted in a conviction, which may block removal.
Convictions ordered expunged by a court, which per the DOJ position cannot be removed from the Wisconsin criminal history repository because the conviction disqualifies that arrest from removal.
Federal and out-of-state records, except that DOJ contacts the FBI where the removed Wisconsin arrest information had been forwarded to it.
Tribal records.

waitingPeriods.condition: Non-conviction disposition of every charge arising from the arrest event

exclusions: Records that are accurate. This route corrects the record; it does not clear it.

tracks.legalName: Conditional Discharge for Possession or Attempted Possession as a First Offence (Wis. Stat. § 961.47)
tracks.publicName: Drug possession first-offence conditional discharge
tracks.mechanism: Where a person has not previously been convicted of any offense under Wis. Stat. ch. 961, or of any comparable federal, state or county ordinance offense relating to controlled substances, and pleads guilty to or is found guilty of possession or attempted possession under § 961.41(3g)(b), the court may, without entering a judgment of guilt and with the consent of the accused, defer further proceedings and place the person on probation on terms and conditions. On fulfillment of the terms and conditions the court shall discharge the person and dismiss the proceedings. Discharge and dismissal is without adjudication of guilt and is not a conviction for purposes of disqualifications or disabilities imposed by law upon conviction of a crime, including the § 961.48 second-or-subsequent-offense penalties. There may be only one discharge and dismissal under the section with respect to any person. Within 20 days after probation is granted the clerk of court notifies the Department of Justice.
exclusions: Any person previously convicted of an offense under Wis. Stat. ch. 961, or of any statute of the United States or of any state or any county ordinance relating to controlled substances or controlled substance analogs, narcotic drugs, marijuana or stimulant, depressant or hallucinogenic drugs.
Any person who has already had one discharge and dismissal under the section; the statute permits only one with respect to any person.
Any charge other than possession or attempted possession under Wis. Stat. § 961.41(3g)(b).
Any case where a term or condition was violated and the court entered an adjudication of guilt.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records.

waitingPeriods.condition: Fulfilment of the terms and conditions of the probation imposed under the section
waitingPeriods.duration: the probation period set by the court; the statute sets no separate clock

buildBlockers.question: Counsel flagged as a build blocker whether § 961.47 contains its own expungement provision, or whether completion simply produces a non-conviction that routes to DOJ removal. The section has now been read in full at the official Wisconsin Legislature publication: subsections (1) and (2) contain no expungement provision of any kind. Completion produces a discharge and dismissal without adjudication of guilt that is not a conviction, and nothing more. The routing into the DOJ fingerprint removal track is therefore the correct and only model. Reading the section also supplied two facts the review did not carry: only one discharge and dismissal is available per person, and the clerk must notify the Department of Justice within 20 days after probation is granted.

tracks.legalName: Shared Non-Conviction Expungement Procedure and Threshold Screen, W. Va. Code § 61-11-25
tracks.publicName: Before you file: what West Virginia checks on a non-conviction expungement
tracks.mechanism: This node produces no relief and no packet of its own. It is the shared § 61-11-25 procedure and threshold screen that both West Virginia non-conviction tracks run on, modelled separately because the adopted counsel structure directs that the two shared procedure nodes be modelled rather than distributed. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 61-11-25 supplies: a civil petition filed in the circuit court in which the charges were filed, even where the case was heard in magistrate or municipal court; a bar on filing sooner than 60 days after the order of acquittal or dismissal; no filing fees or costs of any kind; a discretionary hearing, which the court need not set and which triggers notice to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting agency only if it does; a standard under which the court, on finding no current charges or proceedings pending relating to the matter, may grant the petition, seal court records and expunge agency records including law enforcement records; a 60-day agency certification duty; sealing of the enforcing orders themselves; an effect provision under which the proceedings are considered never to have occurred, the court and agencies reply that no record exists, and the person need not disclose the record on an application for employment, credit or other type of application; and a two-route later-inspection rule. Two threshold bars decide the whole section rather than a single charge: any prior felony conviction disqualifies the person from filing at all, and criminal investigation reports together with all records relating to § 15-12-1 offences are exempt only because the person was found not guilty by reason of mental illness, intellectual disability or addiction. The § 61-11-25(b) duty to advise obliges any court entering an order of acquittal or dismissal to inform the person of the right to petition.
exclusions: Any prior felony conviction. This bars the person from filing under § 61-11-25 at all, whatever the disposition of the case being cleared, and is screened before anything is generated on either non-conviction track.
A dismissal given in exchange for a guilty plea to another offence resulting in a conviction.

Criminal investigation reports, and all records relating to offences subject to § 15-12-1 et seq. because the person was found not guilty by reason of mental illness, intellectual disability or addiction. This is a narrow not-guilty-by-reason-of carve-out and is not a general sex-offence exclusion.
Any Division of Motor Vehicles record, which may not be expunged by virtue of any order entered pursuant to § 17C-5-2b.

Charges dismissed by way of full and successful completion of a deferred adjudication, for violations of § 61-2-28(a), § 61-2-28(b), § 61-2-9(a), § 61-2-9a, § 61-2-9(b) or § 61-2-9(c) where the alleged victim is a family or household member as defined in § 48-27-204.
This node offers no relief of its own and generates no petition. It screens and routes.

packetInstructions: No record in the Division of Motor Vehicles may be expunged by virtue of any order entered pursuant to section 17C-5-2b. The criminal record can be cleared; the driving record cannot, and that belongs in the participant-facing script.
Non-conviction expungement under section 61-11-25 is free. There are no filing fees charged and no costs assessed, and the participant should be told so before payment.

Under section 61-11-25(d) all orders enforcing the expungement procedure are themselves sealed, and under subsection (f) the sealed records may later be inspected only on a motion by the subject of the records or on a prosecutor's petition showing the records are necessary to an investigation or prosecution.
Section 61-11-25 relief is discretionary in form: if the court finds no current charges or proceedings pending, the court may grant the petition. The packet copy must not describe this as automatic.

Under section 61-11-25(e) the person need not disclose the record on an application for employment, credit, or other application, with no stated law-enforcement-employment exception. The law-enforcement and legally-required-background-check exceptions come from section 61-11-26 and must not be applied to section 61-11-25 relief.

It is the shared § 61-11-26 procedure, the complete statutory exclusion screen, and the once-per-lifetime bundling counsel that all four West Virginia conviction tracks run on, modelled separately because the adopted counsel structure directs it. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 61-11-26 supplies: a petition to the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred; a petition verified under oath carrying the twelve content items at subsection (d), including every name and alias, every address from the date of the offence to the date of the petition, the rehabilitation account and the prior-expungement disclosure; service by the petitioner on five recipients at subsection (e), namely the Superintendent of the State Police, the prosecuting attorney of the county or counties of conviction, the chief law-enforcement officer of the arresting agency, the superintendent, warden or Commissioner of Corrections of any institution of confinement, and the circuit, magistrate or municipal court that disposed of the charge; service on identified victims by the prosecuting attorney rather than by the petitioner, at subsection (f); a 30-day opposition window and a 30-day reply window at subsection (g); a clear-and-convincing burden on six elements at subsection (h); a 60-day court-action deadline with four permitted outcomes at subsection (i); sealing and a 60-day agency certification duty at subsection (k); an effect provision at subsection (l) that is narrower than the § 61-11-25 effect, because an applicant for a position involving the prevention, detection, investigation, prosecution or incarceration of law violators must disclose expunged convictions and entities required by state or federal law to obtain criminal history checks may learn of them; a fee provision at subsection (n) tying the circuit clerk's charge to the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action fee and adding a $100 State Police processing fee on grant; and, at subsection (o), the rule that a person may obtain the relief afforded by §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a only once. Section 61-11-26b independently bars any court from expunging a motor vehicle traffic control conviction for a person who held a commercial driver's licence or was operating a commercial motor vehicle, from masking such a charge, and from expunging any DUI conviction.
exclusions: § 61-11-26(c)(1): any felony offence of violence against the person as defined in subsection (p)(2), or any misdemeanour involving the intentional infliction of physical injury to a minor or law-enforcement officer.
§ 61-11-26(c)(2): any felony offence in which the victim of the crime was a minor as defined in subsection (p)(3).
§ 61-11-26(c)(3): any violation of § 61-8B-1 et seq.
§ 61-11-26(c)(4): any offence in which the petitioner used or exhibited a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument.

§ 61-11-26(c)(5): any violation of § 61-2-28, or any offence violating § 61-2-9(b) or § 61-2-9(c) in which the victim was a spouse, a person with whom the petitioner had a child in common, or with whom the petitioner ever cohabited prior to the offence, or a violation of § 61-2-28(c).
§ 61-11-26(c)(7): any offence of driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance.
§ 61-11-26(c)(8): any offence which violates § 17B-4-3.
§ 61-11-26(c)(9): any offence which violates § 61-8-12 or § 61-8-19.
§ 61-11-26(c)(10): any violation of § 61-2-9a.
§ 61-11-26(c)(12): any violation of § 61-3-11 involving a structure regularly used as a dwelling. Burglary of a building that is not a dwelling is expungeable.
§ 61-11-26(c)(13): any conviction for which the sentencing judge made a written finding that the offence was sexually motivated.
§ 61-11-26(c)(14): any offence which violates § 17E-1-13(g).
§ 61-11-26(c)(15): any offence of conspiracy or attempt to commit a felony set forth in subdivisions (1) through (11) and (13).

§ 61-11-26b: any motor vehicle traffic control conviction where the person held a commercial driver's licence or permit or was operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the offence; any action masking a charge or conviction from a commercial driving record; and any DUI conviction.
§ 61-11-26(o): a person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a. The relief is available only once.
This node offers no relief of its own and generates no petition. It screens, counsels bundling, and routes.

waitingPeriods.duration: One year after conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision, whichever is later in time.
Two years after the last conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision ordered for the last conviction, whichever is later in time.
Five years after conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision, whichever is later in time.

90 days of approved treatment or recovery compliance, or completion of an approved job readiness course, for a single misdemeanour; one year for multiple misdemeanours; three years for a nonviolent felony. Each measured after completion of any sentence of incarceration or period of supervision, whichever is later in time.

destination.detail: Nothing is submitted on this node. It runs the complete § 61-11-26(c) exclusion screen and the § 61-11-26b commercial-driving screen, establishes whether the participant has already spent the once-per-lifetime relief, inventories every conviction that could be bundled into the single petition, applies the applicable temporal requirement, and routes to wv_conv_single_misdemeanor, wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors, wv_conv_nonviolent_felony or wv_acc_treatment_job_readiness.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order for every conviction on the inventory. Ask the clerk of the county of disposition for a certified copy of the disposition, the judgment order and the sentencing order for each case. Most counties charge a per-copy fee. Ask for every case, not only the one you came in for, because the petition is once per lifetime.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Circuit or magistrate clerk of the county of disposition

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "List every West Virginia conviction on your record, however old, including traffic citations — not just the one you came here about. What was each offence, in which county, and on what date were you convicted?" against Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order for every conviction on the inventory, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof of supervision completion. Ask the probation office that supervised you for written confirmation of the date supervision ended, and the institution of confinement for the date of release. The waiting period runs from the later of conviction, release and end of supervision, so this date is usually the one that decides eligibility.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The supervising probation office, and the institution of confinement where applicable

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "For each conviction, on what date did you finish any jail or prison term and any probation, parole or other supervision?" against Proof of supervision completion, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Copy of any current restitution, protection, restraining or no-contact order. Ask the clerk of the court that entered the order for a copy. The statute requires a current order to be attached to the petition; a past order is disclosed but not attached.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Only where such an order is currently in force. Section 61-11-26(d)(7) requires a current order to be attached to the petition.

generationRequirements.question: Has any court in West Virginia, another state, or a federal court ever granted you an expungement or similar relief for a criminal conviction?

List every West Virginia conviction on your record, however old, including traffic citations — not just the one you came here about. What was each offence, in which county, and on what date were you convicted?
Of the convictions you want cleared, are they a single misdemeanour, more than one misdemeanour, or a felony?
For each conviction, on what date did you finish any jail or prison term and any probation, parole or other supervision?

Did any of these convictions involve violence to a person, a minor victim, a sexual offence, a deadly weapon, a domestic or household-member victim, strangulation, driving under the influence, driving while your licence was revoked for DUI, or burglary of a home?
At the time of any traffic offence on your list, did you hold a commercial driver's licence or permit, or were you driving a commercial vehicle?

Do you have a medically documented history of substance abuse and successful compliance with an approved treatment or recovery and counselling programme, or have you graduated from a West Virginia Department of Education approved job readiness adult training course?
Do you have any criminal charges pending against you right now?
Is there now, or has there ever been, an order for restitution, protection, a restraining order or another no-contact order stopping you contacting a victim in any of these cases?
Did a West Virginia court ever enter a criminal offence reduction order in your case under the old sentence-reduction law?

packetInstructions: Conviction expungement under sections 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a is available once in a lifetime. That must be said before money changes hands, and it should drive bundling advice.
The circuit clerk civil filing fee applies, and a $100 State Police processing fee is due on grant, unless the petition is under section 61-11-26a.

Expunged convictions must still be disclosed for jobs involving the prevention, detection, investigation, prosecution, or incarceration of law violators, and legally required background checks may still reveal them.
The court has 60 days to act, agencies have 60 days to certify, and a victim or prosecutor may oppose within 30 days.

The complete section 61-11-26 exclusion list was read at source on 2026-08-06 and is recorded here verbatim in fifteen subdivisions, closing the review's build blocker for the exclusion screen. A DUI conviction does not automatically block expungement of an unrelated otherwise expungeable felony if the DUI conviction is at least five years old when the petition is filed.
participantQuestions: If a conviction petition is available, inventory everything eligible first. One petition, one lifetime. The counseling job is to make sure the participant spends it on the whole record they can clear, not the first record they thought of.
CDL holders and commercial vehicle operators are barred from the DUI deferral route and from certain traffic expungements. Participant question with a hard stop.

releaseBlockers.question: Venue on a multi-county conviction petition. The controlling review states that S.B. 562 (2020) allows a person seeking expungement of convictions in more than one county to file in his or her county of residence. Section 61-11-26 was read in full at source on 2026-08-06 and the current text does not contain a residence-county venue option: subsections (a)(1) and (a)(2) both say 'petition the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred', the subsection (d) proviso requires a multiple-misdemeanour petition to 'identify and group such information by circuit court, as applicable', and § 61-11-26a(a) says 'may petition the circuit court or circuit courts in which the conviction or convictions occurred'. Read together the current text supports one petition covering several counties, grouped by circuit court and served on the prosecuting attorney of each county of conviction, but it does not name a residence-county forum. Venue for the single-county case is unaffected and unambiguous. Until counsel resolves this, the packet directs a multi-county participant to the circuit court of conviction and adds a local-check instruction rather than promising a residence-county filing.

provenance.sourceHeading: HEADLINE FINDING / Corrections to what is there
provenance.sourceStatement: Venue for conviction expungement is not only the county of conviction. S.B. 562 (2020) allows a person seeking expungement of convictions in multiple counties to file the petition in his or her county of residence, with notice to the prosecuting attorney in every county of conviction.
provenance.counselQuestion: Section 61-11-26 as currently codified says only 'the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred' and § 61-11-26a says 'the circuit court or circuit courts in which the conviction or convictions occurred'; neither names a county of residence. Where does the county-of-residence venue option for a multi-county petition come from, and does it survive in the current text? Until answered, may LegalEase direct multi-county participants to the circuit court of conviction rather than to their county of residence?

releaseBlockers.question: Whether relief under § 60A-4-407 or § 17C-5-2b counts against the once-per-lifetime limit in § 61-11-26. Section 61-11-26(o) by its terms reaches only §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a, and neither § 60A-4-407 nor § 17C-5-2b cross-references it; both were read in full at source on 2026-08-06 and neither contains a limit referring to § 61-11-26. The textual reading is therefore that they are separate limits in separate statutes, but a participant deciding whether to spend their one lifetime petition needs a settled answer rather than a textual inference.

provenance.sourceStatement: Does relief under section 60A-4-407 or section 17C-5-2b count against the once-per-lifetime limit in section 61-11-26? The limit by its terms applies to sections 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a. Release blocker, because a participant deciding whether to spend their one lifetime petition needs the right answer.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether the $200 circuit clerk civil filing fee under § 59-1-11(a)(1) is in practice charged in full on an expungement petition in every circuit, and whether any circuit applies an indigency waiver. The statutory amount and its statutory basis are now settled at source; the practice, and whether the ordinary civil indigency affidavit is accepted, is not.

openLegalQuestions.question: Section 61-11-26(r) provides that a person who had a sentence reduction under the repealed § 61-11B-1 et seq. 'may petition the court of record to have the criminal offense reduction order converted into an order of expungement', and that on verification the court shall enter an order of expungement. That is a participant-facing petition with mandatory relief on verification, and it is not inventoried as a mechanism in the controlling review, so it has no source slot and no node here. It is surfaced rather than modelled, because creating an eleventh relief track would break the adopted ten-slot structure.

provenance.sourceStatement: Every ordinary adult record-clearance mechanism was identified. Confirmed, with two newly added from the DUI statutes.
provenance.counselQuestion: Is the § 61-11-26(r) conversion of a repealed § 61-11B-1 criminal offence reduction order into an order of expungement a distinct record-clearing mechanism that West Virginia should offer, and if so should it be added to the source inventory as an eleventh slot in a future addendum rather than inside this normalization?

Open question blocks release (venue): Venue on a multi-county conviction petition. The controlling review states that S.B. 562 (2020) allows a person seeking expungement of convictions in more than one county to file in his or her county of residence. Section 61-11-26 was read in full at source on 2026-08-06 and the current text does not contain a residence-county venue option: subsections (a)(1) and (a)(2) both say 'petition the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred', the subsection (d) proviso requires a multiple-misdemeanour petition to 'identify and group such information by circuit court, as applicable', and § 61-11-26a(a) says 'may petition the circuit court or circuit courts in which the conviction or convictions occurred'. Read together the current text supports one petition covering several counties, grouped by circuit court and served on the prosecuting attorney of each county of conviction, but it does not name a residence-county forum. Venue for the single-county case is unaffected and unambiguous. Until counsel resolves this, the packet directs a multi-county participant to the circuit court of conviction and adds a local-check instruction rather than promising a residence-county filing.

Open question blocks release (eligibility_branch): Whether relief under § 60A-4-407 or § 17C-5-2b counts against the once-per-lifetime limit in § 61-11-26. Section 61-11-26(o) by its terms reaches only §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a, and neither § 60A-4-407 nor § 17C-5-2b cross-references it; both were read in full at source on 2026-08-06 and neither contains a limit referring to § 61-11-26. The textual reading is therefore that they are separate limits in separate statutes, but a participant deciding whether to spend their one lifetime petition needs a settled answer rather than a textual inference.

Open question blocks release (filing_process): Whether the $200 circuit clerk civil filing fee under § 59-1-11(a)(1) is in practice charged in full on an expungement petition in every circuit, and whether any circuit applies an indigency waiver. The statutory amount and its statutory basis are now settled at source; the practice, and whether the ordinary civil indigency affidavit is accepted, is not.

tracks.legalName: Civil Petition to Expunge Records of an Acquittal or Dismissal, W. Va. Code § 61-11-25(a)
tracks.publicName: Clear a West Virginia case that ended in a not-guilty verdict or a dismissal
tracks.mechanism: Any person charged with a criminal offence under West Virginia law who has been found not guilty, or against whom charges have been dismissed and not in exchange for a guilty plea to another offence resulting in a conviction, may file a civil petition in the circuit court in which the charges were filed to expunge all records relating to the arrest, charge, or other matters arising out of the arrest or charge. Records reached expressly include arrest records, fingerprints, photographs, index references and other data in documentary or electronic form. The petition may not be filed sooner than 60 days after the order of acquittal or dismissal. There are no filing fees or costs. A hearing is discretionary; if the court sets one it must notify the prosecuting attorney and the arresting agency and give them an opportunity to respond. If the court finds no current charges or proceedings pending relating to the matter, it may grant the petition, seal the court records and order every other agency, including law enforcement, to expunge, each certifying completion within 60 days. Relief is discretionary in form. A person previously convicted of a felony may not file under this section at all.
exclusions: Any prior felony conviction, which bars the person from filing under § 61-11-25 at all.
A dismissal given in exchange for a guilty plea to another offence resulting in a conviction.

Criminal investigation reports, and all records relating to offences subject to § 15-12-1 et seq. because the person was found not guilty by reason of mental illness, intellectual disability or addiction.
Any case in which criminal charges or proceedings relating to the matter are still pending.
Division of Motor Vehicles records, which are never reached by an expungement order entered under § 17C-5-2b.
Juvenile proceedings, which are governed by the § 49-5-104 confidentiality scheme and are outside core scope.

tracks.legalName: Civil Petition to Expunge Records Following Completion of a Pretrial Diversion or Deferred Adjudication, W. Va. Code § 61-11-25(a) with §§ 61-11-22 and 61-11-22a
tracks.publicName: Clear a West Virginia case that was dismissed after you completed diversion or a deferred adjudication
tracks.mechanism: Any person whose charges have been dismissed following full and successful completion of a pretrial diversion under § 61-11-22, or following full and successful completion of a deferred adjudication under § 61-11-22a, may file a civil petition in the circuit court for expungement of all charges originally brought, provided the charges sought to be expunged arose from the same transaction or occurrence. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 61-11-22 caps a diversion agreement at 24 months and excludes any person charged under § 17C-5-2, directing such a person instead to the § 17C-5-2b deferral; § 61-11-22a operates on an entered guilty plea whose acceptance the court defers, for up to three years on a felony and two years on a misdemeanour, and on compliance the defendant withdraws the plea and the matter is dismissed. Two provisos in § 61-11-25(a) bear directly on this route: no Division of Motor Vehicles record may be expunged by virtue of any order entered pursuant to § 17C-5-2b, and charges dismissed by way of full and successful completion of a deferred adjudication may not be expunged for violations of § 61-2-28(a), § 61-2-28(b), § 61-2-9(a), § 61-2-9a, § 61-2-9(b) or § 61-2-9(c) where the alleged victim is a family or household member as defined in § 48-27-204. The waiting period, absence of fees, discretionary hearing, sealing, certification, effect and later-inspection rules are those of the shared § 61-11-25 procedure.
exclusions: Any prior felony conviction, which bars the person from filing under § 61-11-25 at all.

On the deferred adjudication route only: violations of § 61-2-28(a), § 61-2-28(b), § 61-2-9(a), § 61-2-9a, § 61-2-9(b) or § 61-2-9(c) where the alleged victim is a family or household member as defined in § 48-27-204. This carve-out does not attach to the pretrial diversion route.
Charges that did not arise from the same transaction or occurrence as the charges being expunged.
Any Division of Motor Vehicles record, which is never reached by an order entered pursuant to § 17C-5-2b.
A deferred adjudication that ended in a plea to a lesser offence rather than dismissal, which is a conviction and is outside § 61-11-25 entirely.
Cases where the deferral period has not ended or compliance is disputed.
Criminal investigation reports, and records relating to § 15-12-1 offences where the person was found not guilty by reason of mental illness, intellectual disability or addiction.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether SCA-C903 is the right vehicle for a deferred-adjudication dismissal. The form was read at source on 2026-08-06: it is captioned 'for Reasons Other than Entry of a Plea', recites 'W.Va. Code § 61-11-25 (2000)', carries a single charge block with one free-text reason-for-dismissal field, has no same-transaction-or-occurrence paragraph and no diversion or deferred-adjudication paragraph, and requires the movant to state that the dismissal 'was not in exchange for a guilty plea to another offense'. Section 61-11-22a operates on an entered guilty plea which is withdrawn on compliance, so the movant's statement is literally true — the dismissal is not in exchange for a plea to another offence — but the caption and the missing paragraphs make the fit imperfect. The packet therefore generates the official form plus a supplemental pleading carrying the statutory basis, the same-transaction recital and the carve-out recital. Whether the Judiciary regards SCA-C903 as the correct form for this route, or whether a distinct form or a full custom petition is expected, is not established.

tracks.legalName: Verified Petition to Expunge a Single Misdemeanour Conviction, W. Va. Code § 61-11-26(a)(1) and (b)(1)
tracks.publicName: Clear one West Virginia misdemeanour conviction
tracks.mechanism: Subject to the limitations in the section, a person convicted of a misdemeanour offence may petition the circuit court in which the conviction occurred for expungement of the conviction and the records associated with it. Eligibility opens one year after conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision, whichever is later in time. The petition is verified under oath and must carry the twelve items at subsection (d). The petitioner serves five recipients; the prosecuting attorney serves identified victims. Opposing parties have 30 days to file a notice of opposition and the petitioner has 30 days after service to reply. The burden is on the petitioner to prove six matters by clear and convincing evidence. Within 60 days the circuit court must summarily grant, return the petition for missing information or obvious errors, set the matter for hearing, or summarily deny. On grant the court seals its records and orders every other agency to expunge, each certifying within 60 days. The relief afforded by §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a may be obtained only once.
exclusions: Every offence in the fifteen subdivisions of § 61-11-26(c), which the shared wv_common_conv_procedure node states verbatim and screens.

Any motor vehicle traffic control conviction where the person held a commercial driver's licence or permit or was operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the offence, and any DUI conviction, under § 61-11-26b.
A person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a. The relief is available only once.
A person with criminal charges pending.
More than one misdemeanour conviction, which is wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors and runs on a different clock and a different anchoring event.
Felony convictions, which are wv_conv_nonviolent_felony.

releaseBlockers.question: Which published form is the operative § 61-11-26 misdemeanour petition. The Judiciary Court Forms index was read at source on 2026-08-06 and publishes exactly five expungement forms. SCA-C900, captioned 'Instructions for Expungement of Records Petition' and revised 04/01/2021, is a five-page document whose pages 2 to 5 are themselves a petition, verification and certificate of service. That embedded petition is materially stale: it requires the petitioner to have been 'between eighteen and twenty-six years of age', requires 'no prior or subsequent convictions other than minor traffic violations', recites 'W. Va. Code §61-11-26 (2009)', and cross-references the exclusion list to '§61-11-26(i)', all of which are features of the pre-2019 section. The section in force places exclusions at subsection (c) and imposes no age limit. SCA-C906 matches the current subsection (c) and (d) structure and carries the § 61-11-26a elections, and is therefore used here. The packet must not generate the SCA-C900 embedded petition. Whether the Judiciary intends SCA-C900 to remain published in that form is not established.

tracks.legalName: Verified Petition to Expunge Multiple Misdemeanour Convictions, W. Va. Code § 61-11-26(a)(1) and (b)(2)
tracks.publicName: Clear several West Virginia misdemeanour convictions in one petition
tracks.mechanism: The same subsection (a)(1) mechanism as the single-misdemeanour route, on a different clock and a different anchoring event: a person is not eligible for expungement of multiple misdemeanours until two years after the last conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision ordered for the last conviction, whichever is later in time. The petition must account for every conviction in the group, and the subsection (d) proviso read at source on 2026-08-06 requires that a petition for the expungement of multiple misdemeanours 'identify and group such information by circuit court, as applicable, from which expungement of a particular conviction or convictions is being sought'. Because relief under §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a may be obtained only once, this is the route on which the bundling counsel matters most.
exclusions: Every offence in the fifteen subdivisions of § 61-11-26(c), which the shared wv_common_conv_procedure node states verbatim and screens. A single excluded conviction in the group does not bar the others, but it cannot itself be expunged.

Any motor vehicle traffic control conviction where the person held a commercial driver's licence or permit or was operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the offence, and any DUI conviction, under § 61-11-26b.
A person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a.
A person with criminal charges pending.
Felony convictions, which are wv_conv_nonviolent_felony and run on the five-year clock.

releaseBlockers.question: Where a multiple-misdemeanour group spans more than one county, which circuit court receives the single petition. Section 61-11-26 was read in full at source on 2026-08-06: subsection (a)(1) says 'the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred', and the subsection (d) proviso requires the petition to 'identify and group such information by circuit court, as applicable'. tracks.legalName: Verified Petition to Expunge a Nonviolent Felony Conviction, W. Va. Code § 61-11-26(a)(2) and (b)(3)
tracks.publicName: Clear a West Virginia nonviolent felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of a nonviolent felony offence, or of multiple nonviolent felony offences arising from the same transaction or series of transactions, may petition the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred for expungement. Eligibility opens five years after conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision, whichever is later in time. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 61-11-26(p)(5) defines a nonviolent felony as one that is not listed in subsection (c), does not involve the intentional infliction of serious bodily injury, and which the circuit court finds to be consistent with the purposes of the article and not to involve violence or potential violence to another person or the public. Two of those four limbs are express judicial findings, which is why the nonviolent determination is a legal conclusion and never a participant question. Subsection (p)(2) defines a felony crime of violence against the person by reference to §§ 61-2-1 et seq., 61-3E-1 et seq., 61-8B-1 et seq. and 61-8D-1 et seq.; subsection (p)(3) defines a felony in which the victim was a minor by reference to §§ 61-3C-14b, 61-8-1 et seq., 61-8A-1 et seq., 61-8C-1 et seq. and 61-8D-1 et seq. A DUI conviction does not preclude expungement of an unrelated and otherwise expungeable felony if the DUI conviction is at least five years old when the petition is filed.
exclusions: Every offence in the fifteen subdivisions of § 61-11-26(c), which the shared wv_common_conv_procedure node states verbatim and screens.
Any felony offence of violence against the person as defined by § 61-11-26(p)(2), and any felony in which the victim was a minor as defined by § 61-11-26(p)(3).
Any felony involving the intentional infliction of serious bodily injury, § 61-11-26(p)(5)(B).

Any felony the circuit court does not find consistent with the purposes of the article, or which it finds to involve violence or potential violence to another person or the public, § 61-11-26(p)(5)(C) and (D). This is a judicial finding and cannot be determined in advance.
Multiple felonies that did not arise from the same transaction or series of transactions.
A person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a.
A person with criminal charges pending.

Section 61-11-26(p)(5) was read at source on 2026-08-06 and makes two of the four limbs of 'nonviolent felony' express circuit-court findings, so the eligibility recital on SCA-C907 is one LegalEase must leave for the participant and their counsel. Both limbs were read at source and are clear on their own terms; how the packet should explain the difference to a participant who came in about a DUI is an instruction question.

tracks.legalName: Verified Petition for Accelerated Expungement with Approved Treatment, Recovery or Job Readiness, W. Va. Code § 61-11-26a
tracks.publicName: Clear a West Virginia conviction sooner using treatment or job-training completion
tracks.mechanism: Notwithstanding § 61-11-26 to the contrary, a person convicted of a nonviolent felony offence or multiple misdemeanours who would otherwise be eligible under § 61-11-26, and who has either a medically documented history of substance abuse and of successful compliance with a substance abuse treatment or recovery and counselling programme approved by the Secretary of the Department of Health, or who graduates from a West Virginia Department of Education approved job readiness adult training course, or both, may petition the circuit court or circuit courts in which the conviction or convictions occurred. Read at source on 2026-08-06, the section's own subdivisions set three accelerated clocks: subdivision (a)(1) reaches a person convicted of a single misdemeanour and opens eligibility on 90 days of compliance with an approved treatment and recovery and counselling programme or on completion of an approved job readiness course, after completion of any sentence of incarceration or period of supervision, whichever is later in time; subdivision (a)(2) sets one year for multiple misdemeanours; subdivision (a)(3) sets three years for a nonviolent felony. Subsection (b) adds two petition contents to the § 61-11-26(d) list — documentation of compliance with an approved programme, and a certificate of graduation from an approved job readiness course, as applicable. Subsection (c) waives the $100 State Police processing fee otherwise required by § 61-11-26(n). Relief under §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a may be obtained only once, combined.
exclusions: Every offence in the fifteen subdivisions of § 61-11-26(c). Section 61-11-26a reaches only convictions that would otherwise be eligible under § 61-11-26, so the whole exclusion screen applies unchanged.
Any motor vehicle traffic control conviction where the person held a commercial driver's licence or was operating a commercial motor vehicle, and any DUI conviction, under § 61-11-26b.
A person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a. The combined relief is available only once.
A person with criminal charges pending.

A treatment or recovery and counselling programme not approved by the Secretary of the Department of Health, or a job readiness adult training course not approved by the West Virginia Department of Education.

releaseBlockers.question: How the § 61-11-26a(a)(1) 90-day single-misdemeanour clock interacts with the § 61-11-26(b)(1) one-year clock where the participant relies on job readiness graduation rather than 90 days of treatment compliance. Subdivision (a)(1) was read at source on 2026-08-06 and makes eligibility turn on '90 days' of programme compliance 'or upon completion of an approved job readiness adult training course, or both, if applicable, but after the completion of any sentence of incarceration or completion of any period of supervision, whichever is later in time'. On the graduation branch there is no stated period at all beyond completion of sentence and supervision, which would make the route available immediately on graduation. The packet applies the text as written and records the question rather than reading a 90-day period into the graduation branch.

tracks.legalName: Application to Expunge Records of Arrest, Trial and Conviction After a First-Offence Controlled Substance Conditional Discharge, W. Va. Code § 60A-4-407(b)
tracks.publicName: Clear a first drug-possession case that ended in a conditional discharge
tracks.mechanism: A person who has not previously been convicted of any offence under chapter 60A or under any federal or state narcotics, marihuana, stimulant, depressant or hallucinogenic drug statute, and who pleads guilty to or is found guilty of possession of a controlled substance under § 60A-4-401(c), may with their consent have further proceedings deferred and be placed on probation without entry of a judgment of guilt. On fulfilment of the terms and conditions the court discharges the person and dismisses the proceedings without adjudication of guilt. The discharge is not a conviction for purposes of any disqualification or disability imposed by law, and its effect is to restore the person in contemplation of law to the status occupied before arrest and trial. There may be only one discharge and dismissal under the section with respect to any person. Read at source on 2026-08-06, subsection (b) supplies the relief this track generates: after a period of not less than six months, beginning to run immediately on the expiration of the term of probation, the person may apply to the court for an order to expunge from all official records all recordations of the arrest, trial and conviction, and if the court determines after a hearing that the person was not guilty of any serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation during probation or before the application, it shall order the expungement. Subsection (c) makes the person liable for the court costs assessable against a person convicted under § 60A-4-401(c), and payment may be a condition of probation.
exclusions: Any person previously convicted of an offence under chapter 60A or under any federal or state statute relating to narcotic drugs, marihuana, or stimulant, depressant or hallucinogenic drugs. The conditional discharge itself is unavailable to them.
Any person who has already had one discharge and dismissal under § 60A-4-407. Only one is allowed, ever.
Any person whose probation was revoked, or who was adjudicated guilty because the terms and conditions were not fulfilled.
Offences other than possession of a controlled substance under § 60A-4-401(c).
Applications made sooner than six months after the expiration of the term of probation.

waitingPeriods.duration: Not less than six months, beginning to run immediately upon the expiration of the term of probation. The clock runs from the end of probation, not from the date of dismissal.

tracks.venue: The court that entered the conditional discharge and imposed probation. Section 60A-4-407(b) directs the application to 'the court', which is the court whose probation expired.

tracks.legalName: Court-Ordered Dismissal and Expungement on Completion of the Test and Lock Program, W. Va. Code § 17C-5-2(j)(1)
tracks.publicName: An under-21 first alcohol-driving charge that the court clears itself when you finish the test and lock program
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17C-5-2(j)(1) provides that any person under the age of 21 who drives with an alcohol concentration of two hundredths of one percent or more but less than eight hundredths of one percent, for a first offence under that subsection, is guilty of a misdemeanour; that a person charged with a first offence under the subsection may move for a continuance of the proceedings, from time to time, to allow participation in the test and lock program under § 17C-5A-3a; and that 'Upon successful completion of the program, the court shall dismiss the charge against the person and expunge the person's record as it relates to the alleged offense.' If the person fails to complete the program the court proceeds to adjudication, and a motion for a continuance may not be construed as an admission or used as evidence. The expungement is mandatory, court-ordered and automatic on completion: the subsection describes no petition, no application, no waiting period and no participant submission of any kind after the continuance motion. This closes the controlling review's build blocker asking which subsection of § 17C-5-2 carries the test and lock dismissal and expungement and which offences it covers: the answer is subsection (j)(1), and the population is first offenders under 21 with a blood alcohol concentration between 0.02 and 0.08 percent.
exclusions: Any person aged 21 or over at the time of the offence.
Any blood alcohol concentration of eight hundredths of one percent or more, which is a § 17C-5-2(e) or (f) offence and not this subsection.
A second or subsequent offence under § 17C-5-2(j), for which the subsection provides no continuance and no expungement.
Any person who failed to complete or was removed from the test and lock program, in which case the court proceeds to adjudication of the alleged offence.

Any Division of Motor Vehicles record. The subsection reaches the person's record as it relates to the alleged offence, and § 61-11-26b independently bars masking a motor vehicle offence from a commercial driving record.
The continuance motion itself, which is charge-stage criminal defence and is expressly outside the adopted LegalEase product scope.
