tracks.legalName: Motion to Dismiss the Charges and Application to Expunge After a First-Offence DUI Deferral, W. Va. Code § 17C-5-2b(c) and (g)
tracks.publicName: Clear a first DUI that was deferred and dismissed after the test and lock program
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17C-5-2b operates on a person who pleads to or is found guilty of the offence defined in § 17C-5-2(e), has no prior DUI-type conviction, and notifies the court within 30 days of arrest of the intention to participate in a deferral. On those conditions the court, without entering a judgment of guilt, shall defer further proceedings and place the person on probation conditioned on successful completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program under § 17C-5A-3a, for at least 165 days after a 15-day licence suspension and completed within one year thereafter. The section then creates two separate participant-facing submissions. First, under subsection (c), when the defendant has satisfactorily completed the programme and complied with its conditions, the defendant may move the court for an order dismissing the charges; that motion must be supported by the defendant's affidavit and by certification of the Division of Motor Vehicles that the programme was successfully completed, and the prosecuting attorney has 30 days after service to advise the judge of objections, in the absence of which the court shall dismiss. Second, under subsection (g), after a period of not less than one year beginning to run immediately on the expiration of the term of probation, the person may apply to the court for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, except those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles, provided that a person previously convicted of a felony may not make that motion; objections are filed within 30 days of service, and if objections are filed the court holds a hearing and, if it determines there was no serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, it shall order the expungement. Only one discharge and dismissal is available under the section, and § 61-11-25(a) independently provides that no Division of Motor Vehicles record may be expunged by virtue of any order entered pursuant to § 17C-5-2b.
exclusions: Any prosecution in which any violation of any other provision of article 17C-5 has been charged, § 17C-5-2b(f)(1).
Any person who holds a commercial driver's licence or operates commercial motor vehicles, § 17C-5-2b(f)(2).

Any person who has previously had a licence to operate a motor vehicle revoked for an offence with the same elements under a municipal ordinance of this state or any other state, or a statute of the United States or any other state, § 17C-5-2b(f)(3).
Any person as to whom a court entered an order finding a refusal of the secondary chemical test under § 17C-5-7a, § 17C-5-2b(f)(4).
Any person previously convicted of a felony, who may not make the subsection (g) expungement motion.
Any person who has already had one discharge and dismissal under the section, § 17C-5-2b(e).
Any Division of Motor Vehicles record, which the expungement order expressly does not reach.
The deferral request itself, made within 30 days of arrest, which is charge-stage criminal defence and is expressly outside the adopted LegalEase product scope.

waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond satisfactory completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program and compliance with its conditions. The programme itself runs for at least 165 days after a 15-day licence suspension and must be completed within one year thereafter.
Not less than one year, beginning to run immediately upon the expiration of the term of probation. The clock runs from the expiration of probation, not from the dismissal.

units.label: Section 17C-5-2b(c) motion to dismiss the charges, with the defendant's affidavit
units.description: The dismissal stage. Once the participant has satisfactorily completed the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program and complied with its conditions, subsection (c) allows the defendant to move the court for an order dismissing the charges. The motion must be supported by the defendant's own affidavit and by the Division of Motor Vehicles certification of successful completion, and a copy must be served on the prosecuting attorney, who has 30 days to advise the judge of any objections. If none are filed in that period the court shall dismiss the charges. Legal effect: dismissal and discharge without adjudication of guilt, which is not a conviction for purposes of disqualifications or disabilities. This is a distinct submission from unit 2, made to the same court but on different required contents, with its own objection window and its own legal effect, and it must occur before unit 2 becomes available at all. No West Virginia Judiciary form exists for it; the Court Forms index was read at source on 2026-08-06 and publishes exactly five expungement forms, none for this section.

units.label: Section 17C-5-2b(g) application to expunge all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction
units.description: The expungement stage, which cannot be reached until unit 1 has produced a dismissal and discharge and a further year has run from the expiration of the probation term. Subsection (g)(1) allows the person to apply to the court for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, except those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles, and bars the motion outright to anyone previously convicted of a felony. Objections are filed within 30 days of service of the motion; if objections are filed the court holds a hearing at which all parties are heard, and if it determines the person was not guilty of any serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation during probation or before the application, it shall order the expungement. Legal effect: expungement of the criminal record, with the driving record expressly untouched. The required contents, the one-year clock measured from the expiration of probation rather than from dismissal, and the felony bar are all different from unit 1, which is why the two are modelled as separate units rather than as one filing.

tracks.venue: The court in which the § 17C-5-2(e) charge was brought and which deferred proceedings and imposed probation. Both units are filed in that court.

destination.name: Clerk of the court that deferred proceedings and imposed probation under § 17C-5-2b
destination.detail: Both units are filed with the clerk of the court that entered the deferral. Unit 1 is served on the prosecuting attorney, who has 30 days to object. Unit 2 is filed no sooner than one year after the probation term expired and is likewise served on the prosecuting attorney, who has 30 days to object, with a hearing if objections are filed. Neither order reaches any Division of Motor Vehicles record.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge the Record of a Conviction After a Full and Unconditional Pardon, W. Va. Code § 5-1-16a
tracks.publicName: Clear a West Virginia conviction after the Governor has pardoned you
tracks.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 5-1-16a provides that any person who has received a full and unconditional pardon from the Governor may petition the circuit court in the county where the conviction was had to have the record of that conviction expunged. The petition is served on the prosecuting attorney of the county where the petition is filed, and the petitioner must publish notice of the time and place the petition will be made as a Class I legal advertisement under article 3, chapter 59, with the publication area being the county where the petition is filed. On verification of the act of pardon and after a hearing to determine that good cause exists, the circuit court may enter an order directing that all public record of the conviction be expunged. A record expunged under the section may not be considered in an application to any educational institution in this state or in an application for any licensure required by any professional organisation in this state. Eligibility opens one year after the pardon and, separately, five years after discharge of the sentence for the pardoned conviction; both must be satisfied. First degree murder, treason, kidnapping and any felony defined in article 8B are excluded. The records of the Governor, the Legislature and the Secretary of State that pertain to a grant of pardon are not public record for this purpose and are not subject to an expungement order.
exclusions: A conditional pardon, or any pardon that is not full and unconditional.
First degree murder as defined in § 61-2-1.
Treason as defined in § 61-1-1.
Kidnapping as defined in § 61-2-14a.
Any felony defined in article 61-8B.
Any petition made sooner than one year after the pardon, or sooner than five years after discharge of the sentence for the pardoned conviction.
The records of the Governor, the Legislature and the Secretary of State that pertain to the grant of pardon, which are not subject to an expungement order.
The pardon application to the Governor itself, which is a separate executive process and is outside the adopted LegalEase product scope.

waitingPeriods.duration: One year after having been pardoned.
Five years after the discharge of the sentence upon the conviction for which the person was pardoned. Both this and the one-year period must be satisfied.

tracks.venue: The circuit court in the county where the conviction was had. The publication area for the Class I legal advertisement is the county where the petition is filed.

destination.name: Clerk of the circuit court of the county where the conviction was had
destination.detail: File the petition with the circuit clerk of the county of conviction. Serve it on the prosecuting attorney of that county. Separately arrange publication of the notice of the time and place the petition will be made, as a Class I legal advertisement in a qualified newspaper for that county, and obtain the publisher's affidavit of publication to file with the court. The court verifies the act of pardon and holds a hearing on good cause.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Arrest, Dismissal of Charges or Disposition (Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-1401)
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest or dismissed charge
tracks.mechanism: On a verified petition to the court in which the proceeding occurred or would have occurred, the court may expunge records of an arrest, a charge that was dismissed, or a disposition where the person was not convicted, provided at least 180 days have passed, no formal charges are pending, and no disposition under § 7-13-301, § 35-7-1037 or former § 7-13-203 was entered to any charge arising from the incident, including to a different or lesser charge. Expungement classifies the record at the Division of Criminal Investigation so it is not disseminated except to criminal justice agencies for criminal justice purposes; the court file is sealed and a certified order is transmitted to DCI.
exclusions: Any disposition under Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-301, § 35-7-1037 or former § 7-13-203 entered to any charge resulting from the incident, including a disposition to a different or lesser charge.
Formal charges pending against the person at the time the petition is filed.

Records that are not maintained in the state central repository at the Division of Criminal Investigation, including investigatory files of any local, state or federal criminal justice agency used solely for criminal justice purposes.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records, which Wyoming relief does not reach.

packetInstructions: Wyoming publishes no statewide expungement form. County clerks, municipal courts and circuit courts may have local templates or formatting requirements. Call the clerk of the court where the petition will be filed before finalizing, and use a local template where one exists. Never invent a statewide form number.

Adult expungement in Wyoming means classifying the record at DCI so it is not publicly disseminated. It does not destroy the record, criminal justice agencies retain access, and newspapers, private websites and private background-check databases are not reached. Nothing in Wyoming happens automatically, and DCI answers 'no' to whether adult arrests ever drop off a Wyoming record.
No order may issue before 20 days after service on the prosecuting attorney. Tell the participant that timing in the packet instructions rather than in the pleading.
participantQuestions: Ask whether any charge arising from the same incident ended in a disposition under § 7-13-301, § 35-7-1037 or former § 7-13-203, including a disposition to a different or lesser charge. That last clause is the one that catches people, and it decides whether this track is available at all.

Ask whether the participant was fingerprinted at arrest, because a Wyoming criminal history exists only where an arrest fingerprint card was submitted. A participant may have a court record with no DCI record, or the reverse, and that changes what expungement is worth to them.

releaseBlockers.question: Which unpublished local filing preferences apply in the court where this petition will be filed: local cover sheet, copy count, electronic versus paper filing, filing method, chambers copy, whether the proposed Order for Expungement is submitted with the initial filing or later, any unpublished local template, any unpublished additional service document, and other court-specific filing mechanics. This is the narrowed remainder of the original packet-assembly question, which asked which Wyoming courts publish local expungement templates. The published half is answered: Wyoming publishes no statewide petition form and no statewide proposed-order template, and Casper Municipal Court is the only publicly identified local-form exception, whose packets bind that court alone. What remains is unpublished preference, which is filing mechanics rather than the legal document, so it is release-level and does not block generation of the statewide verified petition and proposed order. It is owned by rcap-wy-local-template-and-handout-survey, which remains open: no Wyoming county has been telephoned and the survey must not be recorded as complete. Escalation: if a county's answer changes the statewide legal document rather than only how it is filed, that exact issue returns to legal design before release.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Conviction of Certain Misdemeanors (Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-1501)
tracks.publicName: Clear a misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person who has pled guilty or nolo contendere to, or been convicted of, a misdemeanor may petition the convicting court to expunge the records of conviction. The waiting period is at least five years for non-status offenses and at least one year for status offenses as defined by § 7-1-107(b)(iii), measured from expiration of the terms of sentence including probation and any court-ordered program. The offense must not have involved the use or attempted use of a firearm; a health care provider convicted of a § 6-2-313 offense against a patient in their care is ineligible. The court must find the petitioner is not a substantial danger to himself, any identifiable victim or society. One expungement under this section is permitted in a lifetime. Per the Wyoming Judicial Branch, the section includes cases of deferred adjudication and cases where the charge was later dismissed.
exclusions: Misdemeanors involving the use or attempted use of a firearm.
A health care provider who pled guilty or nolo contendere to, or was convicted of, an offense punishable under Wyo. Stat. § 6-2-313 committed against a patient under that provider's care.
Any person who has previously received an expungement of records of conviction under § 7-13-1501; the statute permits one in a lifetime.
Felony convictions, which are handled under § 7-13-1502.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records, which Wyoming relief does not reach.

A juvenile Child in Need of Supervision adjudication under Wyo. Stat. § 14-6-402(a)(iv) — habitual truancy as defined in § 21-4-101(a)(ii), running away from home, habitually disobeying the reasonable and lawful demands of a parent, guardian, custodian or other proper authority, or being ungovernable and beyond control. Section 7-13-1501(a) reaches only a person who has pled guilty or nolo contendere to, or been convicted of, a misdemeanor, and a CHINS adjudication is none of those three things. It is outside the section whichever waiting period the word "status" might suggest.

waitingPeriods.condition: Non-status misdemeanor offense. This is the default branch and it takes every offense the section reaches other than one the legislature has itself labelled a status offense. Wyo. Stat. § 7-1-107(b)(iii) expressly excludes a violation of § 12-6-101(b) or (c), or any similar municipal ordinance, from the definition, so an under-twenty-one alcohol conviction under § 12-6-101(c) — purchase, attempted purchase, solicitation, possession, consumption, a measurable alcohol concentration, unaccompanied presence in a designated off-premise sales area, or dispensing or selling — takes this five-year branch and not the one-year branch. Convictions under § 6-4-305(c) or (d) are ordinary misdemeanors by § 6-4-305(f) and take this branch too. The branch is decided from the Revised Statutes section of conviction shown on the judgment and sentence, never from the participant's age at the time, never from the case having been in juvenile court, and never from the offense merely being minor.
waitingPeriods.duration: At least 5 years since the expiration of the terms of the sentence imposed by the court, including any period of probation or completion of any program ordered by the court

waitingPeriods.condition: Status offense as defined by Wyo. Stat. § 7-1-107(b)(iii): an offense which, if committed by an adult, would not constitute an act punishable as a criminal offense by the laws of this state or a violation of a municipal ordinance, but which does not include a violation of W.S. 12-6-101(b) or (c) or any similar municipal ordinance. The one offense the Wyoming legislature has expressly labelled a status offense under that definition is W.S. 6-4-305(b) — a minor who knowingly disseminates a nude image of himself, or possesses a nude image of another minor at least eleven years of age, subject to the inadvertent-possession exception — because § 6-4-305(e) says so in terms and uses this same cross-reference. A conviction recorded under § 6-4-305(b) takes this one-year branch. This branch is the exception and must be justified from the charging section.
waitingPeriods.duration: At least 1 year since the expiration of the terms of the sentence imposed by the court, including any period of probation or completion of any program ordered by the court

selfHelpBoundaries: The participant cannot identify the Wyoming statute section of conviction from the judgment and sentence. The one-year and five-year branches under § 7-13-1501(a)(i) are decided from that section and from nothing else, so the packet fails closed rather than inferring the branch from the participant's age, from the offense sounding youthful, or from the word "status".
The participant has already received one expungement under § 7-13-1501; the statute allows one in a lifetime.
Any firearm use or attempted use in the offense.
The participant is a health care provider and the offense was committed against a patient in their care.
A plea was entered to a lesser charge arising from the same incident, which changes which statute applies.
The prosecuting attorney or an identifiable victim files an objection, or the court sets a contested hearing.
An identifiable victim is likely to object.
Facts indicating human trafficking or coercion, which route to the § 6-2-708 vacatur outside this track.
Any offense subject to sex offender registration.
Immigration consequences.

The underlying matter was a felony deferral rather than a misdemeanor one; § 7-13-1502 requires a conviction and there may be no route. Stop and refer.

The conviction is under a city or town ordinance in a municipal court rather than under a Wyoming statute. Whether such a conviction is a "misdemeanor" as W.S. 6-10-101 defines it for § 7-13-1501(m)(ii) is unresolved, so this route is not offered to that participant.

The matter was a juvenile Child in Need of Supervision adjudication — truancy, running away, disobedience or being ungovernable — rather than a misdemeanor plea or conviction. Section 7-13-1501 does not reach it, and it does not become reachable because it is commonly called a status offense.

Stop where the participant cannot identify the statute section of conviction, where the conviction is under a municipal ordinance rather than a Wyoming statute, or where the matter was a juvenile Child in Need of Supervision adjudication for truancy, running away, disobedience or being ungovernable. The first makes the branch undeterminable; the second is an open question about whether the section reaches the conviction at all; the third is outside § 7-13-1501 entirely, and is the mis-screen the word "status" most often causes.
Stop where a plea was entered to a lesser charge arising from the same incident, because that changes which statute applies.
packetInstructions: The waiting period is decided from the Revised Statutes section of conviction and from nothing else. One year applies where the section of conviction is W.S. 6-4-305(b), which § 6-4-305(e) expressly labels a status offense under § 7-1-107(b)(iii). Five years applies to every other offense the section reaches, including an under-twenty-one alcohol conviction under W.S. 12-6-101(c), which § 7-1-107(b)(iii) expressly excludes from the definition, and including W.S. 6-4-305(c) and (d), which § 6-4-305(f) makes ordinary misdemeanors. Both branches run from the expiration of the terms of sentence imposed by the court, including any period of probation and the completion of any program ordered by the court. Never route the branch on the participant's age at the time, on the case having been in juvenile court, or on the offense sounding minor.

The misdemeanor packet may not promise that any right is restored, and firearm rights in particular: § 7-13-1501 restores none by its own terms, the legislature removed the provision that once did, and § 7-13-1502(m) may not be read across. It may not promise an entitlement to answer an inquiry as though the conviction did not occur, because W.S. 7-13-1401(f) is confined to its own section. It may not describe the record as destroyed, erased or gone. It may say that the court file is placed under seal, that the Division of Criminal Investigation record is reclassified out of general dissemination, and that relief is discretionary.
Disclose before payment that Wyoming allows one misdemeanor expungement under § 7-13-1501 in a lifetime, and that the felony statute carries a separate once-per-lifetime limit.

Tell the participant to obtain and attach proof that probation and any court-ordered program were completed. The conviction clock runs from expiration of the terms of sentence, not from the conviction date, so the completion documents are the eligibility evidence.
Wyoming publishes no statewide expungement form. Call the clerk of the convicting court about local templates and formatting before finalizing, and never invent a statewide form number.
No order may issue before 30 days after service on the prosecuting attorney. State that timing in the packet instructions rather than in the pleading.
participantQuestions: Ask for the Wyoming statute section of conviction exactly as it appears on the judgment and sentence, and ask whether the conviction was under a city or town ordinance in a municipal court rather than under a Wyoming statute. The first decides the waiting-period branch; the second decides whether the section reaches the conviction at all. LegalEase must not supply either answer from the participant's age, from the court the case was in, or from the offense description.

Ask whether the matter was handled through deferred prosecution, first-offender treatment, probation before judgment or a dismissal after probation, and whether the underlying matter was a misdemeanor or a felony. A completed misdemeanor deferral routes here rather than to § 7-13-1401 or to manual review; a completed felony deferral is a stop condition. This encodes the routing correction the review requires.
Ask whether the offense involved the use or attempted use of a firearm. LegalEase must not assert that no firearm was used.

buildBlockers.question: Is a conviction under a city or town ordinance a "misdemeanor" as W.S. 6-10-101 defines it for the purposes of § 7-13-1501(m)(ii), and so can a minor-only municipal offense such as curfew be expunged under the section at all? The conduct satisfies the status-offense definition, because an adult doing it violates neither a state criminal law nor a municipal ordinance, but § 6-10-101 classifies crimes by the punishment authorized and does not say whether a municipal ordinance violation is a crime for that purpose. This is prior to the clock rather than part of it, and it decides whether a whole class of participants has a route. Answering it would take reading municipal ordinances and the law of municipal court jurisdiction, which no integrated Wyoming decision reaches.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The waiting period is decided from the Revised Statutes section of conviction and from nothing else. One year applies where the section of conviction is W.S. 6-4-305(b), which § 6-4-305(e) expressly labels a status offense under § 7-1-107(b)(iii). Five years applies to every other offense the section reaches, including an under-twenty-one alcohol conviction under W.S. 12-6-101(c), which § 7-1-107(b)(iii) expressly excludes from the definition, and including W.S. 6-4-305(c) and (d), which § 6-4-305(f) makes ordinary misdemeanors. Both branches run from the expiration of the terms of sentence imposed by the court, including any period of probation and the completion of any program ordered by the court. Never route the branch on the participant's age at the time, on the case having been in juvenile court, or on the offense sounding minor.

provenance.sourceStatement: The one-year branch is real but narrow. It has exactly one statutorily identified occupant that can produce a live misdemeanour conviction needing expungement: W.S. 6-4-305(b). ... For any Wyoming misdemeanour a participant is likely to bring, the clock is five years from the expiration of the terms of sentence including any period of probation and the completion of any court-ordered programme. ... What drives the branch: the Revised Statutes section the person was convicted under, taken from the court record.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Ask for the Wyoming statute section of conviction exactly as it appears on the judgment and sentence, and ask whether the conviction was under a city or town ordinance in a municipal court rather than under a Wyoming statute. The first decides the waiting-period branch; the second decides whether the section reaches the conviction at all. LegalEase must not supply either answer from the participant's age, from the court the case was in, or from the offense description.

provenance.sourceStatement: The one input that decides the clock is the Revised Statutes section of conviction, taken from the judgment and sentence. If the memo does not already ask for it in that form, it should.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The misdemeanor packet may not promise that any right is restored, and firearm rights in particular: § 7-13-1501 restores none by its own terms, the legislature removed the provision that once did, and § 7-13-1502(m) may not be read across. It may not promise an entitlement to answer an inquiry as though the conviction did not occur, because W.S. 7-13-1401(f) is confined to its own section. It may not describe the record as destroyed, erased or gone. It may say that the court file is placed under seal, that the Division of Criminal Investigation record is reclassified out of general dissemination, and that relief is discretionary.

provenance.sourceStatement: Must not state: That any right is restored. Section 7-13-1501 restores none by its own terms and the legislature removed the provision that once did. That firearm rights are restored. ... That the participant may answer an inquiry as though the conviction did not occur. That the record is destroyed, erased or gone.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Stop where the participant cannot identify the statute section of conviction, where the conviction is under a municipal ordinance rather than a Wyoming statute, or where the matter was a juvenile Child in Need of Supervision adjudication for truancy, running away, disobedience or being ungovernable. The first makes the branch undeterminable; the second is an open question about whether the section reaches the conviction at all; the third is outside § 7-13-1501 entirely, and is the mis-screen the word "status" most often causes.

provenance.sourceStatement: This is the single most likely mis-screen on this track. A participant who says "I had a truancy case as a kid" is describing a juvenile matter that 7-13-1501 does not reach, and the packet must not route them into the one-year branch on the strength of the word.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Ask whether the matter was handled through deferred prosecution, first-offender treatment, probation before judgment or a dismissal after probation, and whether the underlying matter was a misdemeanor or a felony. A completed misdemeanor deferral routes here rather than to § 7-13-1401 or to manual review; a completed felony deferral is a stop condition. This encodes the routing correction the review requires.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Conviction of Certain Felonies (Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-1502)
tracks.publicName: Clear a felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of a felony, or of felonies subject to expungement under the section arising out of the same occurrence or related course of events, may petition the convicting court to expunge the records of conviction. At least ten years must have passed since expiration of the terms of sentence including probation; any court-ordered program must be complete and court-ordered restitution paid in full; the petitioner must have no other felony plea, nolo plea or conviction; the offense must not have involved the use or attempted use of a firearm except certain Title 23 offenses; and the offense must not appear on the statutory exclusion list. The court must find eligibility and that the petitioner is not a substantial danger to himself, any identifiable victim or society. One expungement under this section is permitted in a lifetime. Under subsection (m) the expungement restores any rights removed as a result of the conviction.
exclusions: Violent felonies under Wyo. Stat. § 6-1-104(a)(xii).
Aggravated homicide by vehicle; drug-induced homicide.
Sexual assault and related sexual offenses under Wyo. Stat. §§ 6-2-301 through 6-2-320.
Certain domestic battery offenses; child abuse; endangering children with controlled substances; incest; sexual exploitation of children.
Aggravated assault or battery on a corrections or detention officer; disarming a peace officer; escape from official detention and violent or armed escape.
Bribery.
Weapons offenses under Wyo. Stat. §§ 6-8-101 and 6-8-102.
Any offense subject to sex offender registration under Wyo. Stat. §§ 7-19-302(g) through (j).
Felonies involving the use or attempted use of a firearm, except certain Title 23 offenses.
Any petitioner who has previously pled guilty or nolo contendere to, or been convicted of, a felony other than the felony or felonies being expunged.
Any person who has previously received an expungement of records of conviction under § 7-13-1502; the statute permits one in a lifetime.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records, which Wyoming relief does not reach.

A completed deferral under Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-301 that ended in discharge and dismissal. Section 7-13-1502 opens "A person convicted of a felony", and Lynch v. State, 2026 WY 8 holds at ¶18 that a person who completed a deferral has no conviction and does not qualify.

selfHelpBoundaries: The felony may appear on the § 7-13-1502 exclusion list. The list is long and statute-specific and is not encoded; route to attorney review.
The participant has any other felony plea, nolo plea or conviction anywhere, since the other-felony bar looks at the entire record.
Any firearm use or attempted use, including where the participant believes a Title 23 carve-out applies.
Any offense subject to sex offender registration under §§ 7-19-302(g) through (j).
The participant has already received one expungement under § 7-13-1502; the statute allows one in a lifetime.

A completed felony deferral rather than a conviction. There is no Wyoming route: § 7-13-1401(a)(i) is barred by the deferral disposition itself, § 7-13-1502 requires a conviction the participant does not have, § 7-13-301 contains no record-clearing provision and § 7-13-307 forbids construing §§ 7-13-301 through 7-13-306 to authorize expunging the record. Stop and say so plainly rather than offering either section. Where the Division of Criminal Investigation record misdescribes the disposition, a W.S. 7-19-109 application to purge, modify or supplement inaccurate or incomplete criminal history record information is the only thing available — it corrects the record to say what actually happened and is not expungement, and it is not a track this packet offers.
The prosecuting attorney files an objection, or the court sets a contested hearing.
An identifiable victim is likely to object.
Facts indicating human trafficking or coercion, which route to the § 6-2-708 vacatur outside this track.
Immigration consequences.
Federal, tribal or out-of-state records.

A completed felony deferral has no Wyoming route, and the packet says so plainly rather than guessing. Section 7-13-1401(a)(i) is barred by the deferral disposition itself, § 7-13-1502 requires a conviction the participant does not have, § 7-13-301 carries no record-clearing provision, and § 7-13-307 forbids construing §§ 7-13-301 through 7-13-306 to authorize expunging the record. Neither conviction section may be offered to that participant. Stop and refer.
packetInstructions: Tell the participant the felony track takes at least ninety days after service before an order can issue, making it a four-month engagement at minimum.

Tell the participant to obtain and attach proof that court-ordered restitution was paid in full, and that probation and any court-ordered program were completed. The ten-year clock runs from expiration of the terms of sentence.

Disclose before payment that § 7-13-1502 allows one felony expungement in a lifetime, and that DCI, its employees and prosecuting attorneys are immune from liability under § 7-13-1502(j) for actions, inactions or omissions under the section.
Recite the restoration-of-rights effect under § 7-13-1502(m) in the proposed order, and make no assertion about the effect of expungement on firearm rights beyond that statutory restoration language.
Wyoming publishes no statewide expungement form. Call the clerk of the convicting court about local templates and formatting before finalizing, and never invent a statewide form number.

Where a participant completed a felony deferral, say that nothing in Wyoming law clears that record and name the reason, rather than implying that some other route might be found. The only thing available is a W.S. 7-19-109 application to the district court to purge, modify or supplement inaccurate or incomplete criminal history record information, which corrects the record to show the deferral, discharge and dismissal and leaves the corrected record in place and disseminable. Never describe it as expungement, never offer it as a packet, and do not model it as a Wyoming track without its own legal-design decision.

The restoration sentence belongs to this track alone. Section 7-13-1502(m) restores any rights removed as a result of the expunged conviction and may be recited in the proposed order; § 7-13-1501 restores nothing, the provision that once did was removed by 2009 ch. 67, and the two conviction tracks may not share this copy. Neither track may promise an entitlement to answer an inquiry as though the conviction did not occur: W.S. 7-13-1401(f) gives that on the non-conviction route only and is confined to its own section.
participantQuestions: Ask whether the petitioner has any other felony plea, nolo plea or conviction anywhere. The other-felony bar looks at the entire record, and LegalEase must not assert that the petitioner has no other felony.
Ask whether the offense involved the use or attempted use of a firearm, including where a Title 23 carve-out may apply. LegalEase must not assert that no firearm was used.

Ask whether the matter was a deferred prosecution or deferred sentencing the participant completed, after which the charge was dismissed, rather than a conviction; and ask for the Wyoming statute section of conviction exactly as it appears on the judgment and sentence. The first drives a fail-closed screen that neither the offense description nor the case number can drive. The second is what attorney review needs to place the offense against the exclusion list, and it is the input a subparagraph-level encoding will run on when one exists.
scopeRestrictions: This track carries a mandatory attorney-review gate before the packet is offered, because the restoration-of-rights payoff makes it worth doing properly once. The gate remains necessary now that the deferral rule is encoded: it was never standing in for that answer alone. Two of its three reasons are untouched — the exclusion list is still unencoded and the other-felony bar still looks at the entire record — and the third does not depend on any encoding.

releaseBlockers.question: Does anything outside § 7-13-1502 entitle a person whose felony conviction is expunged to answer an inquiry as though it did not occur? Subsection (m) restores rights removed as a result of the conviction, which is a different thing. W.S. 7-13-1401(f) supplies the answer-as-if entitlement on the non-conviction route and is confined to its own section by its own words, so the safe copy on this track is silence about it. Whether some other Wyoming provision supplies it has not been searched and is not asserted in either direction.

provenance.sourceStatement: On both conviction routes the packet may say what the order does to the division of criminal investigation record and to the court file, and may not tell the participant they are entitled to answer an inquiry as though the conviction did not occur. That entitlement exists on the non-conviction route and, by their own terms, on the two nicotine sections. It does not exist on 7-13-1501 or 7-13-1502.

openLegalQuestions.question: Should Wyoming model a W.S. 7-19-109 application to purge, modify or supplement inaccurate or incomplete criminal history record information as a route of its own? It is the only thing available to a person who completed a felony deferral, and the Supreme Court pointed at it in terms, saying at ¶18 that the record should be corrected to accurately reflect the deferred sentencing disposition and the ultimate dismissal. It is a different remedy with a different promise, it is correction rather than expungement, and it must not be folded into this or any other expungement track. It bears on neither this packet's selection, content, geography, filing instructions nor warnings, which is why it is recorded as a research note rather than as a blocker.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Vacate Conviction under Wyo. Stat. § 6-2-708(c) (human-trafficking victim)
tracks.publicName: Human-trafficking victim vacatur — W.S. 6-2-708

controllingAuthority.summary: Wyo. Stat. § 6-2-708(c) expressly allows a motion at any time after entry of conviction, in the court where the conviction was entered, concerning the defendant's participation resulting from trafficking. The court may vacate; relief is discretionary, never written as mandatory. Government documentation of trafficking status creates a presumption but is not mandatory. Subsection (a) (defense to liability), subsection (b) (minors) and subsection (c) (post-conviction motion) are distinct; an unresolved pending charge is never routed into a conviction-vacatur instrument. The subsection adds no sentence-completion requirement, extra waiting period, trafficker conviction, automatic record destruction, $300 filing fee, or the 90-day DCI-notice process of the separate felony-expungement route.

effectiveDates.note: Recorded 2026-09-06 from the research handoff; statute read at the official Wyoming channel by the researcher.

eligibleRecordTypes: conviction entered in a Wyoming court
exclusions: A pending, unresolved charge (not a conviction).

waitingPeriods.condition: Any time after entry of conviction
waitingPeriods.duration: None under § 6-2-708(c).

geography.venue: The court where the conviction was entered.

destination.name: The Wyoming court that entered the conviction
destination.detail: The person convicted files a custom Motion to Vacate Conviction under Wyo. Stat. § 6-2-708(c) under the original case caption in the court where the conviction was entered. The custom title implements the statutory motion; Wyoming publishes no form with that title. Recorded 2026-09-06 from the research handoff.

components.notes: Motion to Vacate Conviction under Wyo. Stat. § 6-2-708(c) by the person convicted, under the original caption: copy the caption and case number; identify the precise conviction and its entry date from the record; state the statutory ground; the defendant's own facts explaining trafficking status and its connection to participation in that offense; request vacatur of the specifically identified conviction, not erasure of every record held by every agency.
An execution-compliant supporting affidavit or declaration; identified supporting materials attached where available; a government certificate is never required as the only evidentiary route.

components.conditionDescription: Where locally requested.

rules.filing: File the motion in the court that entered the conviction, under the original caption, at any time after entry of conviction.
rules.fees: No statutory fee is set by § 6-2-708(c); the $300 felony-expungement fee of § 7-13-1502 does not apply; the clerk states any filing fee.
rules.feeWaiver: Not established for this motion.
rules.notice: Not established; the actual court's current service and scheduling procedure is bound before filing instructions are released.
rules.service: Not established; the prosecutor or current party list supported by the actual court's procedure is used, not the separate § 7-13-1502 expungement service list.
rules.participantSignature: The movant signs the motion and the supporting affidavit or declaration.
rules.notarization: As the affidavit or declaration form the court accepts requires.

researchParticipantText.text: File the motion in the court that entered the conviction. Explain, using your own facts and available evidence, how your participation in the offense resulted from trafficking. Government documentation can assist, but the statute does not make it mandatory. The judge decides whether to vacate the conviction. Do not assume this motion also seals all court and law-enforcement records.

selfHelpStopConditions: A pending, unresolved charge rather than an entered conviction.
